Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Fecit * mihi magna qui potens est, et sanctum Nomen ejus, allelúja.
Ant 1.eng: He That is mighty * hath done to me great things, and holy is His Name, alleluia.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Dedit se, * ut liberáret pópulum, et acquíreret sibi nomen ætérnum, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: He gave Himself * to deliver His people, and to get Himself an everlasting Name. Alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Vocábis * nomen ejus Jesum; ipse enim salvum fáciet pópulum suum a peccátis eórum, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: Thou shalt call His Name Jesus, * for He shall save His people from their sins, alleluia.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Fratres: Christus humiliávit semetípsum, factus obédiens usque ad mortem, mortem autem crucis. Propter quod et Deus exaltávit illum, et donávit illi nomen, quod est super omne nomen, ut in nómine Jesu omne genu flectátur.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: He humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death, even to the death of the cross. For which cause God also hath exalted him, and hath given him a name which is above all names: That in the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those that are in heaven, on earth, and under the earth.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Omne quodcúmque fácitis in verbo, aut in ópere: ómnia in nómine Dómini Jesu Christi fácite, grátias agéntes Deo et Patri per ipsum.
Capitulum Nona.eng: All whatsoever you do in word or in work, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, giving thanks to God and the Father by him.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: In nómine Jesu omne genu flectátur cæléstium, terréstrium, et infernórum: et omnis lingua confiteátur, quia Dóminus Jesus Christus in glória est Dei Patris.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: That in the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those that are in heaven, on earth, and under the earth: And that every tongue should confess that the Lord Jesus Christ is in the glory of God the Father.

Hymnus Laudes.label: Hymn
Hymnus Laudes.title: Jesu decus angélicum
Hymnus Laudes.lat:
Jesu decus angélicum,
In aure dulce cánticum,
In ore mel miríficum,
In corde nectar cǽlicum.

Qui te gustant, esúriunt;
Qui bibunt, adhuc sítiunt;
Desideráre nésciunt,
Nisi Jesum, quem díligunt.

O Jesu mi dulcíssime,
Spes suspirántis ánimæ!
Te quærunt piæ lácrimæ,
Te clamor mentis íntimæ.

Mane nobíscum, Dómine,
Et nos illústra lúmine;
Pulsa mentis calígine,
Mundum reple dulcédine.

Jesu, flos Matris Vírginis,
Amor nostræ dulcédinis,
Tibi laus, honor nóminis,
Regnum beatitúdinis.
Amen.
Hymnus Laudes.eng:
O Jesu, Thou the Beauty art
Of Angel worlds above;
Thy name is music to the heart,
Enchanting it with love.

Celestial Sweetness unalloyed!
Who eat thee hunger still;
Who drink of thee still feel a void,
Which naught but Thou can fill.

O my sweet Jesu! hear the sigh,
Which unto thee I send;
To thee mine inmost spirit cries
My being's hope and end!

Stay with us, Lord, and with thy light
Illume the soul's abyss;
Scatter the darkness of our night,
And fill the world with bliss.

O Jesu, spotless Virgin flower,
Our life and joy: to thee
Be praise, beatitude, and power,
Through all eternity.
Amen.

Hymnus Matutinum.label: Hymn
Hymnus Matutinum.title: Jesu, Rex admirábilis
Hymnus Matutinum.lat:
Jesu, Rex admirábilis,
Et triumphátor nóbilis,
Dulcédo ineffábilis,
Totus desiderábilis.

Quando cor nostrum vísitas,
Tunc lucet ei véritas,
Mundi viléscit vánitas,
Et intus fervet cáritas.

Jesu, dulcédo córdium,
Fons vivus, lumen méntium,
Excédens omne gáudium,
Et omne desidérium.

Jesum omnes agnóscite,
Amórem ejus póscite:
Jesum ardénter quǽrite,
Quæréndo inardéscite.

Te nostra, Jesu, vox sonet,
Nostri te mores éxprimant,
Te corda nostra díligant,
Et nunc, et in perpétuum.
Amen.
Hymnus Matutinum.eng:
O Jesu, King most wonderful
Thou conqueror renowned,
Thou sweetness most ineffable,
In whom all joys are found!

When once Thou visitest the heart,
Then truth begins to shine;
Then earthly vanities depart;
Then kindles love divine.

O Jesu, light of all below,
Thou fount of life and fire,
Surpassing all the joys we know,
And all we can desire:

May every heart confess thy Name,
And ever thee adore;
And, seeking thee, itself inflame
To seek thee more and more.

Thee may our tongues forever bless;
Thee may we love alone;
And ever in our lives express
The image of thine own.
Amen.

Hymnus Vespera.label: Hymn
Hymnus Vespera.title: Jesu, dulcis memória
Hymnus Vespera.lat:
Jesu, dulcis memória,
Dans vera cordis gáudia:
Sed super mel, et ómnia,
Ejus dulcis præséntia.

Nil cánitur suávius,
Nil audítur jucúndius,
Nil cogitátur dúlcius,
Quam Jesus Dei Fílius.

Jesu, spes pœniténtibus,
Quam pius es peténtibus!
Quam bonus te quæréntibus!
Sed quid inveniéntibus?

Nec lingua valet dícere,
Nec líttera exprímere:
Expértus potest crédere,
Quid sit Jesum dilígere.

Sis, Jesu, nostrum gáudium,
Qui es futúrus prǽmium:
Sit nostra in te glória,
Per cuncta semper sǽcula.
Amen.
Hymnus Vespera.eng:
Jesu, the very thought of thee
With sweetness fills my breast;
But sweeter far thy face to see,
And in thy presence rest.

Nor voice can sing, nor heart can frame,
Nor can the memory find,
A sweeter sound than thy blest Name,
O Saviour of mankind!

O Hope of every contrite heart,
O Joy of all the meek,
To those who fall, how kind Thou art!
How good to those who seek!

But what to those who find? Ah! this
Nor tongue nor pen can show:
The love of Jesus, what it is
None but his loved ones know.

Jesu, our only joy be Thou,
As Thou our prize wilt be;
Jesu, be Thou our glory now,
And through eternity.
Amen.

Invit.label: Antiphon
Invit.lat: Admirábile nomen Jesu, quod est super omne nomen, * Veníte, adorémus.
Invit.eng: The Name which shall be called Wonderful, the Name of Jesus is the Name which is above every name. * O come, let us worship Him.

Lectio Prima.label: Lectio brevis
Lectio Prima.lat: Omne quodcúmque fácitis in verbo, aut in ópere: ómnia in nómine Dómini Jesu Christi fácite, grátias agéntes Deo et Patri per ipsum.
Lectio Prima.eng: All whatsoever you do in word or in work, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, giving thanks to God and the Father by him.

Nocturn 1 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 1 Versum.lat: ℣. Propter nomen tuum, Dómine, propitiáberis peccáto meo.
Nocturn 1 Versum.eng: ℣. For thy Name's sake, O Lord, pardon mine iniquity.
Nocturn 1 Versum.engR: ℟. For it is great.

Nocturn 2 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 2 Versum.lat: ℣. Propter glóriam nóminis tui, Dómine, líbera nos.
Nocturn 2 Versum.latR: ℟. Et propítius esto peccátis nostris propter nomen tuum.
Nocturn 2 Versum.eng: ℣. For the glory of thy Name, deliver us, O Lord.
Nocturn 2 Versum.engR: ℟. And forgive our sins, for thy Name's sake.

Nocturn 3 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 3 Versum.latR: ℟. Afférte Dómino glóriam nómini ejus.
Nocturn 3 Versum.eng: ℣. Give unto the Lord glory and honour.
Nocturn 3 Versum.engR: ℟. Give unto the Lord the glory due unto His Name.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui unigénitum Fílium tuum constituísti humáni géneris Salvatórem, et Jesum vocári jussísti: concéde propítius; ut, cujus sanctum nomen venerámur in terris, ejus quoque aspéctu perfruámur in cælis.
Oratio.eng: O God, Who hast appointed thine Only-begotten Son to be the Saviour of mankind, and hast commanded that His Name should be called Jesus, mercifully grant that we who here on earth do worship that most Holy Name may be made glad in heaven by His Presence.

Responsory Breve Nona.lat:
℟.br. Magnificáte Dóminum mecum, * Allelúja, allelúja.
℣. Et exaltémus nomen ejus in idípsum.
℟. Allelúja, allelúja.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Magnificáte Dóminum mecum, * Allelúja, allelúja.
Responsory Breve Nona.eng:
℟.br. O magnify the Lord with me, * Alleluia, alleluia.
℣. And let us exalt His Name together.
℟. Alleluia, alleluia.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. O magnify the Lord with me, * Alleluia, alleluia.

Responsory Breve Sexta.label: Responsorium Breve
Responsory Breve Sexta.lat:
℟.br. Afférte Dómino glóriam et honórem, * Allelúja, allelúja.
℣. Afférte Dómino glóriam nómini ejus.
℟. Allelúja, allelúja.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Afférte Dómino glóriam et honórem, * Allelúja, allelúja.
Responsory Breve Sexta.eng:
℟.br. Give unto the Lord glory and honour, * Alleluia, alleluia.
℣. Give unto the Lord the glory due unto His Name.
℟. Alleluia, alleluia.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. Give unto the Lord glory and honour, * Alleluia, alleluia.

Responsory Breve Tertia.label: Responsorium Breve
Responsory Breve Tertia.lat:
℟.br. Sit nomen Dómini benedíctum, * Allelúja, allelúja.
℣. Ex hoc nunc et usque in sǽculum.
℟. Allelúja, allelúja.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Sit nomen Dómini benedíctum, * Allelúja, allelúja.
Responsory Breve Tertia.eng:
℟.br. Blessed be the Name of the Lord, * Alleluia, alleluia.
℣. From this time forth, and for evermore.
℟. Alleluia, alleluia.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. Blessed be the Name of the Lord, * Alleluia, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Oleum effúsum * nomen tuum, ídeo adolescéntulæ dilexérunt te.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Thy Name is as oil * poured forth, therefore do the virgins love thee.

Ant Laudes.ant: Scitóte, * quia Dóminus ipse est Deus, cujus nomen in ætérnum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Know ye that the Lord He is God, * and His Name endureth for ever.

Ant Laudes.ant: Sitívit * ánima mea ad nomen sanctum tuum, Dómine.
Ant Laudes.antEng: My soul thirsteth * for thy Holy Name, O Lord.

Ant Laudes.ant: Benedíctum * nomen glóriæ tuæ sanctum, et laudábile, et superexaltátum in sǽcula.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Blessed * is the Holy Name of thy glory, and worthy to be praised, and exalted above all for ever.

Ant Laudes.ant: Júvenes et vírgines, * senes cum junióribus laudáte nomen Dómini, quia exaltátum est nomen ejus solíus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Young men and maidens, * old men and children, praise the Name of the Lord, for His Name alone is exalted.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O Lord our Lord, * how admirable is thy name in the whole earth!

Ant Matutinum.ant: In nómine Jesu * omne genu flectátur cæléstium, terréstrium, et infernórum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: At the Name of Jesus, * let every knee bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Confitémini * Dómino, et invocáte nomen ejus: mementóte, quóniam excélsum est nomen ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Praise the Lord, * and call upon His Name; remember that His Name is exalted.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Mémores erunt * nóminis tui, Dómine, in omni generatióne et generatiónem.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: They shall be mindful * of thy Name, O Lord, unto all generations.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Magnificáte * Dóminum mecum, et exaltémus nomen ejus in idípsum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O magnify * the Lord with me, and let us exalt His Name together.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Omnes gentes, * quascúmque fecísti, vénient, et adorábunt coram te, Dómine, et glorificábunt nomen tuum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: All nations * whom Thou hast made, shall come and worship before thee, O Lord, and shall glorify thy Name.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Cantáte Dómino * et benedícite nómini ejus: annuntiáte de die in diem salutáre ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Sing unto the Lord, * and bless His Name show forth His salvation from day to day.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Secúndum nomen tuum, * Deus, sic et laus tua in fines terræ: justítia plena est déxtera tua.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: According to thy Name, O God, * so is thy praise unto the ends of the earth; thy right hand is full of righteousness.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Cantáte Deo, * psalmum dícite nómini ejus: iter fácite ei, qui ascéndit super occásum, Dóminus nomen illi.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Sing unto God, * sing praises to His Name; spread a path before Him That rideth upon the heavens the Lord is His Name.

Ant Vespera.ant: Omnis * qui invocáverit nomen Dómini, salvus erit.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Whosoever shall call * on the name of the Lord shall be saved.

Ant Vespera.ant: Sanctum et terríbile * nomen ejus, inítium sapiéntiæ timor Dómini.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Holy and terrible * is His Name; the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.

Ant Vespera.ant: Ego autem * in Dómino gaudébo, et exsultábo in Deo Jesu meo.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Yet will I rejoice * in the Lord I will joy in the God of my salvation.

Ant Vespera.ant: A solis ortu * usque ad occásum laudábile nomen Dómini.
Ant Vespera.antEng: From the rising of the sun * unto the going down of the same the Lord's Name is to be praised.

Ant Vespera.ant: Sacrificábo * hóstiam laudis, et nomen Dómini invocábo.
Ant Vespera.antEng: I will offer * the sacrifice of thanksgiving, and will call upon the Name of the Lord.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Propter nímiam * caritátem suam, qua diléxit nos Deus, Fílium suum misit in similitúdinem carnis peccáti, allelúja.
Ant 1.eng: God, for His great love * wherewith He loved us, sent His Own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh. Alleluia.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Mirábile mystérium * declarátur hódie: innovántur natúræ, Deus homo factus est: id quod fuit permánsit, et quod non erat assúmpsit; non commixtiónem passus, neque divisiónem.
Ant 2.eng: This day is set forth a wonderful mystery, * a new thing hath been created in the earth: God is made man. That which He was, He remaineth; and that which He was not, He taketh; suffering therein neither confusion nor division.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Magnum * hereditátis mystérium: templum Dei factus est úterus nesciéntis virum: non est pollútus ex ea carnem assúmens; omnes gentes vénient dicéntes: Glória tibi, Dómine.
Ant 3.eng: Herein is a great mystery * of heirship; the womb of her that knew not a man is become the temple of God; in taking of her flesh, He was not defiled; all nations shall come and say: Glory be to thee, O Lord!

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Appáruit grátia Dei Salvatóris nostri ómnibus homínibus, erúdiens nos, ut abnegántes impietátem, et sæculária desidéria, sóbrie, et juste, et pie vivámus in hoc sǽculo.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: The grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men, teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly in this present world.

Nocturn 3 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 3 Versum.latR: ℟. Salutáre suum, allelúja.
Nocturn 3 Versum.eng: ℣. The Lord hath made known, alleluia.
Nocturn 3 Versum.engR: ℟. His salvation, alleluia.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui salútis ætérnæ, beátæ Maríæ virginitáte fecúnda, humáno géneri prǽmia præstitísti: tríbue, quǽsumus; ut ipsam pro nobis intercédere sentiámus, per quam merúimus auctórem vitæ suscípere, Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum Fílium tuum:
Oratio.eng: O God, Who, by the fruitful virginity of the Blessed Mary, hast given unto mankind the rewards of everlasting life; grant, we beseech thee, that we may continually feel the might of her intercession, through whom we have worthily received the Author of our life, our Lord Jesus Christ, thy Son:

Versum 1.eng: ℣. The Word was made flesh, alleluia.
Versum 1.engR: ℟. And dwelt among us, alleluia.

Versum 2.label: Versicle

Versum 2.eng: ℣. The Word was made flesh, alleluia.
Versum 2.engR: ℟. And dwelt among us, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: O admirábile commércium: * Creátor géneris humáni, animátum corpus sumens, de Vírgine nasci dignátus est; et procédens homo sine sémine, largítus est nobis suam Deitátem.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O wondrous interchange! * the Creator of mankind, taking upon him a living body, vouchsafed to be born of a pure Virgin: and by his Humanity, which was begotten in no earthly wise, hath made us partakers of his Divinity.

Ant Laudes.ant: Quando natus es * ineffabíliter ex Vírgine, tunc implétæ sunt Scriptúræ: sicut plúvia in vellus descendísti, ut salvum fáceres genus humánum: te laudámus, Deus noster.
Ant Laudes.antEng: When thou wast born * all ineffably of a Virgin, then were the Scriptures fulfilled; thou camest down like the dew upon the fleece of wool, to bring salvation unto all mankind; we praise thee, O our God.

Ant Laudes.ant: Rubum, quem víderat Móyses * incombústum, conservátam agnóvimus tuam laudábilem virginitátem: Dei Génetrix, intercéde pro nobis.
Ant Laudes.antEng: In the bush which Moses saw * unconsumed, we recognize the preservation of thy glorious virginity: holy Mother of God, intercede for us.

Ant Laudes.ant: Germinávit radix Jesse, * orta est stella ex Jacob: Virgo péperit Salvatórem; te laudámus, Deus noster.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Root of Jesse hath budded, * the Star hath come out of Jacob, the Virgin hath borne the Saviour: we praise thee, O our God.

Ant Laudes.ant: Ecce María génuit * nobis Salvatórem, quem Joánnes videns, exclamávit, dicens: Ecce Agnus Dei, ecce qui tollit peccáta mundi, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Lo, Mary hath brought forth * the Saviour of whom when John saw him, he did proclaim: Behold the Lamb of God that taketh away the sins of the world, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dóminus dixit * ad me: Fílius meus es tu, ego hódie génui te.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord hath said unto Me: Thou art My Son, * this day have I begotten thee.

Ant Matutinum.ant: In sole pósuit * tabernáculum suum: et ipse tamquam sponsus procédens de thálamo suo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: In the sun hath He set His tabernacle * and He is as a bridegroom coming out of his chamber.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Elevámini, * portæ æternáles, et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Be ye lift up, ye everlasting doors, * and the King of glory shall come in.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Speciósus forma * præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Thou art fairer than the children of men, * grace is poured into thy lips.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Homo natus est * in ea, et ipse fundávit eam Altíssimus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: This man was born in her, * and the Highest Himself hath established her.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Exsultábunt ómnia ligna * silvárum ante fáciem Dómini, quóniam venit.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: All the trees of the wood shall rejoice * before the Lord, for He cometh.

Ant Matutinum.ant: In princípio, * et ante sǽcula Deus erat Verbum, et ipse natus est hódie Salvátor mundi.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: In the beginning, * and before the worlds, the Word was God, and this day is He born the Saviour of the world.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ante lucíferum génitus, * et ante sǽcula, Dóminus Salvátor noster hódie nasci dignátus est.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord our Saviour, * begotten before the daystar, and before the worlds, hath this day vouchsafed to be born.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Nato Dómino, * Angelórum chorus canébat, dicens: Salus Deo nostro, sedénti super thronum, et Agno.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: When the Lord was born the Angels sang together, * saying: Salvation to our God, Which sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb.

Ant Vespera.ant: O admirábile commércium: * Creátor géneris humáni, animátum corpus sumens, de Vírgine nasci dignátus est; et procédens homo sine sémine, largítus est nobis suam Deitátem.
Ant Vespera.antEng: O wondrous interchange! * the Creator of mankind, taking upon him a living body, vouchsafed to be born of a pure Virgin: and by his Humanity, which was begotten in no earthly wise, hath made us partakers of his Divinity.

Ant Vespera.ant: Quando natus es * ineffabíliter ex Vírgine, tunc implétæ sunt Scriptúræ: sicut plúvia in vellus descendísti, ut salvum fáceres genus humánum: te laudámus, Deus noster.
Ant Vespera.antEng: When thou wast born * all ineffably of a Virgin, then were the Scriptures fulfilled; thou camest down like the dew upon the fleece of wool, to bring salvation unto all mankind; we praise thee, O our God.

Ant Vespera.ant: Rubum, quem víderat Móyses * incombústum, conservátam agnóvimus tuam laudábilem virginitátem: Dei Génetrix, intercéde pro nobis.
Ant Vespera.antEng: In the bush which Moses saw * unconsumed, we recognize the preservation of thy glorious virginity: holy Mother of God, intercede for us.

Ant Vespera.ant: Germinávit radix Jesse, * orta est stella ex Jacob: Virgo péperit Salvatórem; te laudámus, Deus noster.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The Root of Jesse hath budded, * the Star hath come out of Jacob, the Virgin hath borne the Saviour: we praise thee, O our God.

Ant Vespera.ant: Ecce María génuit * nobis Salvatórem, quem Joánnes videns, exclamávit, dicens: Ecce Agnus Dei, ecce qui tollit peccáta mundi, allelúja.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Lo, Mary hath brought forth * the Saviour of whom when John saw him, he did proclaim: Behold the Lamb of God that taketh away the sins of the world, alleluia.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Propter nímiam * caritátem suam, qua diléxit nos Deus, Fílium suum misit in similitúdinem carnis peccáti, allelúja.
Ant 1.eng: God, for His great love * wherewith He loved us, sent His Own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh. Alleluia.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Mirábile mystérium * declarátur hódie: innovántur natúræ, Deus homo factus est: id quod fuit permánsit, et quod non erat assúmpsit; non commixtiónem passus, neque divisiónem.
Ant 2.eng: This day is set forth a wonderful mystery, * a new thing hath been created in the earth: God is made man. That which He was, He remaineth; and that which He was not, He taketh; suffering therein neither confusion nor division.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Magnum * hereditátis mystérium: templum Dei factus est úterus nesciéntis virum: non est pollútus ex ea carnem assúmens; omnes gentes vénient dicéntes: Glória tibi, Dómine.
Ant 3.eng: Herein is a great mystery * of heirship; the womb of her that knew not a man is become the temple of God; in taking of her flesh, He was not defiled; all nations shall come and say: Glory be to thee, O Lord!

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Appáruit grátia Dei Salvatóris nostri ómnibus homínibus, erúdiens nos, ut abnegántes impietátem, et sæculária desidéria, sóbrie, et juste, et pie vivámus in hoc sǽculo.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: The grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men, teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly in this present world.

Nocturn 3 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 3 Versum.latR: ℟. Salutáre suum, allelúja.
Nocturn 3 Versum.eng: ℣. The Lord hath made known, alleluia.
Nocturn 3 Versum.engR: ℟. His salvation, alleluia.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui salútis ætérnæ, beátæ Maríæ virginitáte fecúnda, humáno géneri prǽmia præstitísti: tríbue, quǽsumus; ut ipsam pro nobis intercédere sentiámus, per quam merúimus auctórem vitæ suscípere, Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum Fílium tuum:
Oratio.eng: O God, Who, by the fruitful virginity of the Blessed Mary, hast given unto mankind the rewards of everlasting life; grant, we beseech thee, that we may continually feel the might of her intercession, through whom we have worthily received the Author of our life, our Lord Jesus Christ, thy Son:

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dóminus dixit * ad me: Fílius meus es tu, ego hódie génui te.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord hath said unto Me: Thou art My Son, * this day have I begotten thee.

Ant Matutinum.ant: In sole pósuit * tabernáculum suum: et ipse tamquam sponsus procédens de thálamo suo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: In the sun hath He set His tabernacle * and He is as a bridegroom coming out of his chamber.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Elevámini, * portæ æternáles, et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Be ye lift up, ye everlasting doors, * and the King of glory shall come in.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Speciósus forma * præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Thou art fairer than the children of men, * grace is poured into thy lips.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Homo natus est * in ea, et ipse fundávit eam Altíssimus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: This man was born in her, * and the Highest Himself hath established her.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Exsultábunt ómnia ligna * silvárum ante fáciem Dómini, quóniam venit.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: All the trees of the wood shall rejoice * before the Lord, for He cometh.

Ant Matutinum.ant: In princípio, * et ante sǽcula Deus erat Verbum, et ipse natus est hódie Salvátor mundi.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: In the beginning, * and before the worlds, the Word was God, and this day is He born the Saviour of the world.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ante lucíferum génitus, * et ante sǽcula, Dóminus Salvátor noster hódie nasci dignátus est.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord our Saviour, * begotten before the daystar, and before the worlds, hath this day vouchsafed to be born.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Nato Dómino, * Angelórum chorus canébat, dicens: Salus Deo nostro, sedénti super thronum, et Agno.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: When the Lord was born the Angels sang together, * saying: Salvation to our God, Which sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb.

Oratio.lat: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui primítias Mártyrum in beáti Levítæ Stéphani sánguine dedicásti: tríbue quǽsumus; ut pro nobis intercéssor exsístat, qui pro suis étiam persecutóribus exorávit Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum Fílium tuum:
Oratio.eng: O Almighty and everlasting God, Who hast dedicated the first-fruits of Thy Martyrs with the blood of the Blessed Stephen; grant, we beseech Thee, that the same may pray for us also, who prayed even for his murderers to our Lord Jesus Christ Thy Son:

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Puer Jesus * proficiébat ætáte et sapiéntia coram Deo et homínibus.
Ant 1.eng: And Jesus advanced in wisdom * and age, and grace with God and men.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Dum médium siléntium * tenérent ómnia, et nox in suo cursu médium iter perágeret, omnípotens Sermo tuus, Dómine, a regálibus sédibus venit, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: While all things were in quiet silence * and that night was in the midst of her swift course, thine Almighty Word, O Lord, leapt down out of thy Royal Throne.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Fratres: Quanto témpore heres párvulus est, nihil differt a servo, cum sit dóminus ómnium: sed sub tutóribus et actóribus est usque ad præfínitum tempus a patre.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Brothers: As long as the heir is a child, he differeth nothing from a servant, though he be lord of all; But is under tutors and governors until the time appointed by the father.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Itaque jam non est servus, sed fílius: quod si fílius, et hæres per Deum.
Capitulum Nona.eng: Therefore now he is not a servant, but a son. And if a son, an heir also through God.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: At ubi venit plenitúdo témporis, misit Deus Fílium suum factum ex mulíere, factum sub lege, ut eos, qui sub lege erant, redímeret, ut adoptiónem filiórum reciperémus.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent his Son, made of a woman, made under the law: That he might redeem them who were under the law: that we might receive the adoption of sons.

Hymnus Laudes.label: Hymn
Hymnus Laudes.title: A solis ortus cárdine
Hymnus Laudes.lat:
A solis ortus cárdine
Ad usque terræ límitem,
Christum canámus Príncipem,
Natum María Vírgine.

Beátus auctor sǽculi
Servíle corpus índuit:
Ut carne carnem líberans,
Ne pérderet quos cóndidit.

Castæ Paréntis víscera
Cæléstis intrat grátia:
Venter Puéllæ bájulat
Secréta, quæ non nóverat.

Domus pudíci péctoris
Templum repénte fit Dei:
Intácta nésciens virum,
Concépit alvo Fílium.

Enítitur puérpera,
Quem Gábriel prædíxerat,
Quem ventre Matris géstiens,
Baptísta clausum sénserat.

Fœno jacére pértulit:
Præsépe non abhórruit:
Et lacte módico pastus est,
Per quem nec ales ésurit.

Gaudet chorus cæléstium,
Et Angeli canunt Deo;
Palámque fit pastóribus
Pastor, Creátor ómnium.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
Hymnus Laudes.eng:
From lands that see the sun arise
To earth's remotest boundaries,
The Virgin-born today we sing,
The Son of Mary, Christ the King.

Blest Author of this earthly frame,
To take a servant's form He came,
That, liberating flesh by flesh,
Whom He had made might live afresh.

In that chaste parent's holy womb
Celestial grace hath found its home;
And she, as earthly bride unknown,
Yet calls that Offspring blest her own.

The mansion of the modest breast
Becomes a shrine where God shall rest:
The pure and undefilèd one
Conceived in her womb the Son.

That Son, that Royal Son she bore,
Whom Gabriel's voice had told afore;
Whom, in His mother yet concealed,
The infant Baptist had revealed.

The manger and the straw He bore,
The cradle did He not abhor;
By milk in infant portions fed,
Who gives e'en fowls their daily bread.

The heavenly chorus filled the sky,
The Angels sang to God on high,
What time to shepherds, watching lone,
They made creation's Shepherd known.

All honor, laud, and glory be,
O Jesu, Virgin-born to thee:
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.

Hymnus Matutinum.label: Hymn
Hymnus Matutinum.title: Jesu, Redémptor ómnium
Hymnus Matutinum.lat:
Jesu, Redémptor ómnium,
Quem lucis ante oríginem
Parem patérnæ glóriæ
Pater suprémus édidit.

Tu lumen, et splendor Patris,
Tu spes perénnis ómnium,
Inténde quas fundunt preces
Tui per orbem sérvuli.

Meménto, rerum Cónditor,
Nostri quod olim córporis,
Sacráta ab alvo Vírginis
Nascéndo, formam súmpseris.

Testátur hoc præsens dies,
Currens per anni círculum,
Quod solus e sinu Patris
Mundi salus advéneris.

Hunc astra, tellus, ǽquora,
Hunc omne, quod cælo subest,
Salútis auctórem novæ
Novo salútat cántico.

Et nos, beáta quos sacri
Rigávit unda sánguinis,
Natális ob diem tui
Hymni tribútum sólvimus.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
Hymnus Matutinum.eng:
Jesus, the Ransomer of man,
Who, ere created light began,
Didst from the sovereign Father spring,
His power and glory equalling.

The Father’s Light and Splendor Thou,
Their endless hope to Thee that bow;
Accept the prayers and praise to-day
That through the world Thy servants pay.

Salvation’s Author, call to mind
How, taking form of humankind,
Born of a Virgin undefiled,
Thou in man’s flesh becam’st a Child.

Thus testifies the present day,
Through every year in long array,
That Thou, salvation’s source alone,
Proceedest from the Father’s throne.

The heavens above, the rolling main
And all that earth’s wide realms contain,
With joyous voice now loudly sing
The glory of their new-born King.

And we who, by Thy precious Blood
From sin redeemed, are marked for God,
On this the day that saw Thy birth,
Sing the new song of ransomed earth.

O Lord, the Virgin-born, to Thee
Eternal praise and glory be,
Whom with the Father we adore
And Holy Ghost forevermore.
Amen.

Invit.label: Antiphon
Invit.lat: Christus natus est nobis: * Veníte, adorémus.
Invit.eng: Unto us a Christ is born, * O come, let us worship Him.

Lectio Prima.label: Lectio brevis
Lectio Prima.lat: Itaque jam non est servus, sed fílius: quod si fílius, et hæres per Deum.
Lectio Prima.eng: Therefore now he is not a servant, but a son. And if a son, an heir also through God.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, dírige actus nostros in beneplácito tuo: ut in nómine dilécti Fílii tui mereámur bonis opéribus abundáre:
Oratio.eng: O Almighty and everlasting God, do Thou order all our actions in conformity with thy good pleasure, that through the name of thy well-beloved Son, we may worthily abound in all good works.

Versum 1.label: Versicle
Versum 1.eng: ℣. The Lord hath made known, alleluia.
Versum 1.engR: ℟. His salvation, alleluia.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Magi vidéntes * stellam, dixérunt ad ínvicem: Hoc signum magni Regis est: eámus et inquirámus eum, et offerámus ei múnera, aurum, thus, et myrrham, allelúja.
Ant 1.eng: When the wise men saw the star * they said one unto another: This is the sign of the Great King; let us go and search diligently for Him, and present unto Him gifts, gold, and frankincense, and myrrh. Alleluia.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Hódie * cælésti Sponso juncta est Ecclésia, quóniam in Jordáne lavit Christus ejus crímina: currunt cum munéribus Magi ad regáles núptias, et ex aqua facto vino lætántur convívæ, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: This day is the Church joined unto the Heavenly Bridegroom, * since Christ hath washed away her sins in Jordan; the wise men hasten with gifts to the marriage supper of the King; and they that sit at meat together make merry with water turned into wine. Alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Tribus miráculis * ornátum diem sanctum cólimus: hódie stella Magos duxit ad præsépium: hódie vinum ex aqua factum est ad núptias: hódie in Jordáne a Joánne Christus baptizári vóluit, ut salváret nos, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: This day we keep a holiday in honour of three wonders, * this day a star led the wise men to the manger; this day at the marriage, water was made wine; this day was Christ, for our salvation, pleased to be baptized of John in Jordan. Alleluia.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Surge, illumináre Jerúsalem, quia venit lumen tuum, et glória Dómini super te orta est.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Arise, be enlightened, O Jerusalem: for thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Omnes de Saba vénient, aurum et thus deferéntes, et laudem Dómino annuntiántes.
Capitulum Nona.eng: All they from Saba shall come, bringing gold and frankincense: and shewing forth praise to the Lord.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Leva in circúitu óculos tuos, et vide: omnes isti congregáti sunt, venérunt tibi: fílii tui de longe vénient, et fíliæ tuæ de látere surgent.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: Lift up thy eyes round about, and see: all these are gathered together, they are come to thee: thy sons shall come from afar.

Hymnus Laudes.label: Hymn
Hymnus Laudes.title: O sola magnárum úrbium
Hymnus Laudes.lat:
O sola magnárum úrbium
Major Bethlem, cui cóntigit
Ducem salútis cǽlitus
Incorporátum gígnere.

Quem stella, quæ solis rotam
Vincit decóre, ac lúmine;
Venísse terris núntiat
Cum carne terréstri Deum.

Vidére postquam illum Magi,
Eóa promunt múnera:
Stratíque votis ófferunt
Thus, myrrham, et aurum régium.

Regem Deúmque annúntiant
Thesáurus, et fragrans odor
Thuris Sabǽi, ac mýrrheus
Pulvis sepúlcrum prǽdocet.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui apparuísti géntibus,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
Hymnus Laudes.eng:
Bethlehem, of noblest cities
None can once with thee compare;
Thou alone the Lord from heaven
Didst for us incarnate bear.

Fairer than the sun at morning
Was the star that told His birth;
To the lands their God announcing,
Hid beneath a form of earth.

By its lambent beauty guided,
See, the eastern kings appear;
See them bend, their gifts to offer,
Gifts of incense, gold, and myrrh.

Amen.

Hymnus Matutinum.label: Hymn
Hymnus Matutinum.title: Crudélis Heródes, Deum
Hymnus Matutinum.lat:
Crudélis Heródes, Deum
Regem veníre quid times?
Non éripit mortália,
Qui regna dat cæléstia.

Ibant magi, quam víderant,
Stellam sequéntes prǽviam:
Lumen requírunt lúmine:
Deum faténtur múnere.

Lavácra puri gúrgitis
Cæléstis Agnus áttigit:
Peccáta, quæ non détulit,
Nos abluéndo sústulit.

Novum genus poténtiæ:
Aquæ rubéscunt hýdriæ,
Vinúmque jussa fúndere,
Mutávit unda oríginem.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui apparuísti géntibus,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
Hymnus Matutinum.eng:
Why, impious Herod, vainly fear
That Christ the Saviour cometh here?
He takes no earthly realms away
Who gives the crown that lasts for aye.

To greet His birth the Wise Men went,
Led by the star before them sent;
Called on by light, towards light they pressed,
And by their gifts their God confessed.

In holy Jordan's purest wave
The heavenly Lamb vouchsafed to lave;
That He, to whom was sin unknown,
Might cleanse His people from their own.

New miracle of power divine!
The water reddens into wine:
He spake the word: and poured the wave
In other streams than nature gave.

All glory, Lord, to thee we pay
For thine Epiphany to-day:
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.

Ant Laudes.ant: Ante lucíferum génitus, * et ante sǽcula, Dóminus Salvátor noster hódie mundo appáruit.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Lord our Saviour, * begotten before the day-star, and before the ages, is this day made manifest in the world.

Ant Laudes.ant: Venit lumen tuum * Jerúsalem, et glória Dómini super te orta est, et ambulábunt gentes in lúmine tuo, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O Jerusalem, * thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee, and the Gentiles shall walk in thy light. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Apértis thesáuris suis * obtulérunt Magi Dómino aurum, thus, et myrrham, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: When the wise men * had opened their treasures, they presented unto the Lord gold, frankincense, and myrrh. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Mária et flúmina * benedícite Dómino: hymnum dícite fontes Dómino, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O ye seas and floods, * bless ye the Lord. O ye wells, bless ye the Lord. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Stella ista * sicut flamma corúscat, et Regem regum Deum demónstrat: Magi eam vidérunt, et magno Regi múnera obtulérunt.
Ant Laudes.antEng: This star shineth * as a flame of fire, and pointeth out God, the King of kings: the Wise Men beheld it, and offered gifts unto the great King.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Afférte Dómino * fílii Dei, adoráte Dóminum in aula sancta ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Give unto the Lord, O ye sons of God, * worship the Lord in His holy courts.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Flúminis ímpetus * lætíficat, allelúja, civitátem Dei, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: It is a river, the streams whereof make glad, * alleluia, the city of God, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Psállite Deo nostro, * psállite: psállite Regi nostro, psállite sapiénter.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Sing praises to our God, sing praises * sing praises unto our King, sing ye praises with understanding.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Omnis terra adóret te, * et psallat tibi: psalmum dicat nómini tuo, Dómine.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Let all the earth worship thee, and sing unto thee * let them sing praises to thy name, O Lord.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Reges Tharsis * et ínsulæ múnera ófferent Regi Dómino.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The kings of Tarshish and the isles shall bring presents * unto the Lord the King.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Omnes gentes * quascúmque fecísti, vénient, et adorábunt coram te, Dómine.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: All nations whom Thou hast made shall come * and worship before thee, O Lord.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Veníte adorémus eum: * quia ipse est Dóminus Deus noster.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O come, let us worship Him: * for He is the Lord our God.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Adoráte Dóminum, * allelúja: in aula sancta ejus, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O worship the Lord, * alleluia, in His holy temple, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Adoráte Deum, * allelúja: omnes Angeli ejus, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Worship God, * alleluia, all ye His Angels, alleluia.

Ant Vespera.ant: Ante lucíferum génitus, * et ante sǽcula, Dóminus Salvátor noster hódie mundo appáruit.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The Lord our Saviour, * begotten before the day-star, and before the ages, is this day made manifest in the world.

Ant Vespera.antEng: O Jerusalem, * thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee, and the Gentiles shall walk in thy light. Alleluia.

Ant Vespera.ant: Apértis thesáuris suis * obtulérunt Magi Dómino aurum, thus, et myrrham, allelúja.
Ant Vespera.antEng: When the wise men * had opened their treasures, they presented unto the Lord gold, frankincense, and myrrh. Alleluia.

Ant Vespera.ant: Mária et flúmina * benedícite Dómino: hymnum dícite fontes Dómino, allelúja.
Ant Vespera.antEng: O ye seas and floods, * bless ye the Lord. O ye wells, bless ye the Lord. Alleluia.

Ant Vespera.ant: Stella ista * sicut flamma corúscat, et Regem regum Deum demónstrat: Magi eam vidérunt, et magno Regi múnera obtulérunt.
Ant Vespera.antEng: This star shineth * as a flame of fire, and pointeth out God, the King of kings: the Wise Men beheld it, and offered gifts unto the great King.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Magi vidéntes * stellam, dixérunt ad ínvicem: Hoc signum magni Regis est: eámus et inquirámus eum, et offerámus ei múnera, aurum, thus, et myrrham, allelúja.
Ant 1.eng: When the wise men saw the star * they said one unto another: This is the sign of the Great King; let us go and search diligently for Him, and present unto Him gifts, gold, and frankincense, and myrrh. Alleluia.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Hódie * cælésti Sponso juncta est Ecclésia, quóniam in Jordáne lavit Christus ejus crímina: currunt cum munéribus Magi ad regáles núptias, et ex aqua facto vino lætántur convívæ, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: This day is the Church joined unto the Heavenly Bridegroom, * since Christ hath washed away her sins in Jordan; the wise men hasten with gifts to the marriage supper of the King; and they that sit at meat together make merry with water turned into wine. Alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Tribus miráculis * ornátum diem sanctum cólimus: hódie stella Magos duxit ad præsépium: hódie vinum ex aqua factum est ad núptias: hódie in Jordáne a Joánne Christus baptizári vóluit, ut salváret nos, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: This day we keep a holiday in honour of three wonders, * this day a star led the wise men to the manger; this day at the marriage, water was made wine; this day was Christ, for our salvation, pleased to be baptized of John in Jordan. Alleluia.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Surge, illumináre Jerúsalem, quia venit lumen tuum, et glória Dómini super te orta est.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Arise, be enlightened, O Jerusalem: for thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Omnes de Saba vénient, aurum et thus deferéntes, et laudem Dómino annuntiántes.
Capitulum Nona.eng: All they from Saba shall come, bringing gold and frankincense: and shewing forth praise to the Lord.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Leva in circúitu óculos tuos, et vide: omnes isti congregáti sunt, venérunt tibi: fílii tui de longe vénient, et fíliæ tuæ de látere surgent.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: Lift up thy eyes round about, and see: all these are gathered together, they are come to thee: thy sons shall come from afar.

Hymnus Laudes.label: Hymn
Hymnus Laudes.title: O sola magnárum úrbium
Hymnus Laudes.lat:
O sola magnárum úrbium
Major Bethlem, cui cóntigit
Ducem salútis cǽlitus
Incorporátum gígnere.

Quem stella, quæ solis rotam
Vincit decóre, ac lúmine;
Venísse terris núntiat
Cum carne terréstri Deum.

Vidére postquam illum Magi,
Eóa promunt múnera:
Stratíque votis ófferunt
Thus, myrrham, et aurum régium.

Regem Deúmque annúntiant
Thesáurus, et fragrans odor
Thuris Sabǽi, ac mýrrheus
Pulvis sepúlcrum prǽdocet.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui apparuísti géntibus,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
Hymnus Laudes.eng:
Bethlehem, of noblest cities
None can once with thee compare;
Thou alone the Lord from heaven
Didst for us incarnate bear.

Fairer than the sun at morning
Was the star that told His birth;
To the lands their God announcing,
Hid beneath a form of earth.

By its lambent beauty guided,
See, the eastern kings appear;
See them bend, their gifts to offer,
Gifts of incense, gold, and myrrh.

Solemn things of mystic meaning:
Incense doth the God disclose;
Gold a royal child proclaimeth;
Myrrh a future tomb foreshows.

Holy Jesu, in thy brightness
To the Gentile world displayed,
With the Father and the Spirit,
Endless praise to thee be paid.
Amen.

Ant Laudes.ant: Ante lucíferum génitus, * et ante sǽcula, Dóminus Salvátor noster hódie mundo appáruit.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Lord our Saviour, * begotten before the day-star, and before the ages, is this day made manifest in the world.

Ant Laudes.ant: Venit lumen tuum * Jerúsalem, et glória Dómini super te orta est, et ambulábunt gentes in lúmine tuo, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O Jerusalem, * thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee, and the Gentiles shall walk in thy light. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Apértis thesáuris suis * obtulérunt Magi Dómino aurum, thus, et myrrham, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: When the wise men * had opened their treasures, they presented unto the Lord gold, frankincense, and myrrh. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Mária et flúmina * benedícite Dómino: hymnum dícite fontes Dómino, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O ye seas and floods, * bless ye the Lord. O ye wells, bless ye the Lord. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.antEng: This star shineth * as a flame of fire, and pointeth out God, the King of kings: the Wise Men beheld it, and offered gifts unto the great King.

Ant Matutinum.antEng: Give unto the Lord, O ye sons of God, * worship the Lord in His holy courts.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Flúminis ímpetus * lætíficat, allelúja, civitátem Dei, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: It is a river, the streams whereof make glad, * alleluia, the city of God, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Psállite Deo nostro, * psállite: psállite Regi nostro, psállite sapiénter.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Sing praises to our God, sing praises * sing praises unto our King, sing ye praises with understanding.

Ant Matutinum.antEng: Let all the earth worship thee, and sing unto thee * let them sing praises to thy name, O Lord.

Ant Matutinum.antEng: All nations whom Thou hast made shall come * and worship before thee, O Lord.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Homo natus est * in ea, et ipse fundávit eam Altíssimus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: This man was born in her, * and the Highest Himself hath established her.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Magi vidéntes * stellam, dixérunt ad ínvicem: Hoc signum magni Regis est: eámus et inquirámus eum, et offerámus ei múnera, aurum, thus, et myrrham, allelúja.
Ant 1.eng: When the wise men saw the star * they said one unto another: This is the sign of the Great King; let us go and search diligently for Him, and present unto Him gifts, gold, and frankincense, and myrrh. Alleluia.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Hódie * cælésti Sponso juncta est Ecclésia, quóniam in Jordáne lavit Christus ejus crímina: currunt cum munéribus Magi ad regáles núptias, et ex aqua facto vino lætántur convívæ, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: This day is the Church joined unto the Heavenly Bridegroom, * since Christ hath washed away her sins in Jordan; the wise men hasten with gifts to the marriage supper of the King; and they that sit at meat together make merry with water turned into wine. Alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Tribus miráculis * ornátum diem sanctum cólimus: hódie stella Magos duxit ad præsépium: hódie vinum ex aqua factum est ad núptias: hódie in Jordáne a Joánne Christus baptizári vóluit, ut salváret nos, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: This day we keep a holiday in honour of three wonders, * this day a star led the wise men to the manger; this day at the marriage, water was made wine; this day was Christ, for our salvation, pleased to be baptized of John in Jordan. Alleluia.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Surge, illumináre Jerúsalem, quia venit lumen tuum, et glória Dómini super te orta est.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Arise, be enlightened, O Jerusalem: for thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.

Capitulum Nona.lat: Omnes de Saba vénient, aurum et thus deferéntes, et laudem Dómino annuntiántes.
Capitulum Nona.eng: All they from Saba shall come, bringing gold and frankincense: and shewing forth praise to the Lord.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Leva in circúitu óculos tuos, et vide: omnes isti congregáti sunt, venérunt tibi: fílii tui de longe vénient, et fíliæ tuæ de látere surgent.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: Lift up thy eyes round about, and see: all these are gathered together, they are come to thee: thy sons shall come from afar.

Hymnus Laudes.label: Hymn
Hymnus Laudes.title: O sola magnárum úrbium
Hymnus Laudes.lat:
O sola magnárum úrbium
Major Bethlem, cui cóntigit
Ducem salútis cǽlitus
Incorporátum gígnere.

Quem stella, quæ solis rotam
Vincit decóre, ac lúmine;
Venísse terris núntiat
Cum carne terréstri Deum.

Vidére postquam illum Magi,
Eóa promunt múnera:
Stratíque votis ófferunt
Thus, myrrham, et aurum régium.

Regem Deúmque annúntiant
Thesáurus, et fragrans odor
Thuris Sabǽi, ac mýrrheus
Pulvis sepúlcrum prǽdocet.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui apparuísti géntibus,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
Hymnus Laudes.eng:
Bethlehem, of noblest cities
None can once with thee compare;
Thou alone the Lord from heaven
Didst for us incarnate bear.

Fairer than the sun at morning
Was the star that told His birth;
To the lands their God announcing,
Hid beneath a form of earth.

By its lambent beauty guided,
See, the eastern kings appear;
See them bend, their gifts to offer,
Gifts of incense, gold, and myrrh.

Solemn things of mystic meaning:
Incense doth the God disclose;
Gold a royal child proclaimeth;
Myrrh a future tomb foreshows.

Holy Jesu, in thy brightness
To the Gentile world displayed,
With the Father and the Spirit,
Endless praise to thee be paid.
Amen.

Hymnus Matutinum.label: Hymn
Hymnus Matutinum.title: Crudélis Heródes, Deum
Hymnus Matutinum.lat:
Crudélis Heródes, Deum
Regem veníre quid times?
Non éripit mortália,
Qui regna dat cæléstia.

Ibant magi, quam víderant,
Stellam sequéntes prǽviam:
Lumen requírunt lúmine:
Deum faténtur múnere.

Lavácra puri gúrgitis
Cæléstis Agnus áttigit:
Peccáta, quæ non détulit,
Nos abluéndo sústulit.

Novum genus poténtiæ:
Aquæ rubéscunt hýdriæ,
Vinúmque jussa fúndere,
Mutávit unda oríginem.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui apparuísti géntibus,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
Hymnus Matutinum.eng:
Why, impious Herod, vainly fear
That Christ the Saviour cometh here?
He takes no earthly realms away
Who gives the crown that lasts for aye.

To greet His birth the Wise Men went,
Led by the star before them sent;
Called on by light, towards light they pressed,
And by their gifts their God confessed.

In holy Jordan's purest wave
The heavenly Lamb vouchsafed to lave;
That He, to whom was sin unknown,
Might cleanse His people from their own.

New miracle of power divine!
The water reddens into wine:
He spake the word: and poured the wave
In other streams than nature gave.

All glory, Lord, to thee we pay
For thine Epiphany to-day:
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.

Ant 2.eng: There came wise men from the East to Bethlehem to worship the Lord * and when they had opened their treasures, they presented unto Him precious gifts; gold, as unto the Great King; frankincense as unto the true God; and myrrh for His burying. Alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon

Ant 3.eng: When the wise men saw the star, * they rejoiced with exceeding great joy; and when they were come into the house, they presented unto the Lord gold, frankincense, and myrrh. Alleluia.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Admóniti Magi * in somnis, per áliam viam revérsi sunt in regiónem suam.
Ant 1.eng: The wise men being warned * in a dream, departed into their own country another way.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Maniféste magnum est * pietátis sacraméntum, quod manifestátum est in carne, justificátum est in spíritu, appáruit Angelis, prædicátum est Géntibus, créditum est in mundo, assúmptum est in glória, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: Without controversy * great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifest in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen of Angels, preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory, alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Tribus miráculis * ornátum diem sanctum cólimus: hódie stella Magos duxit ad præsépium: hódie vinum ex aqua factum est ad núptias: hódie in Jordáne a Joánne Christus baptizári vóluit, ut salváret nos, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: This day we keep a holiday in honour of three wonders, * this day a star led the wise men to the manger; this day at the marriage, water was made wine; this day was Christ, for our salvation, pleased to be baptized of John in Jordan. Alleluia.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Surge, illumináre Jerúsalem, quia venit lumen tuum, et glória Dómini super te orta est.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Arise, be enlightened, O Jerusalem: for thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.

Hymnus Vespera.label: Hymn
Hymnus Vespera.title: Crudélis Heródes, Deum
Hymnus Vespera.lat:
Crudélis Heródes, Deum
Regem veníre quid times?
Non éripit mortália,
Qui regna dat cæléstia.

Ibant magi, quam víderant,
Stellam sequéntes prǽviam:
Lumen requírunt lúmine:
Deum faténtur múnere.

Lavácra puri gúrgitis
Cæléstis Agnus áttigit:
Peccáta, quæ non détulit,
Nos abluéndo sústulit.

Novum genus poténtiæ:
Aquæ rubéscunt hýdriæ,
Vinúmque jussa fúndere,
Mutávit unda oríginem.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui apparuísti géntibus,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
Hymnus Vespera.eng:
Why, impious Herod, vainly fear
That Christ the Saviour cometh here?
He takes no earthly realms away
Who gives the crown that lasts for aye.

To greet His birth the Wise Men went,
Led by the star before them sent;
Called on by light, towards light they pressed,
And by their gifts their God confessed.

In holy Jordan's purest wave
The heavenly Lamb vouchsafed to lave;
That He, to whom was sin unknown,
Might cleanse His people from their own.

New miracle of power divine!
The water reddens into wine:
He spake the word: and poured the wave
In other streams than nature gave.

All glory, Lord, to thee we pay
For thine Epiphany to-day:
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Remánsit puer Jesus * in Jerúsalem, et non cognovérunt paréntes ejus existimántes illum esse in comitátu: et requirébant eum inter cognátos et notos.
Ant 1.eng: The child Jesus * remained in Jerusalem; and his parents knew it not. And thinking that he was in the company, they came a day's journey, and sought him among their kinsfolks and acquaintance.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Remánsit puer Jesus * in Jerúsalem, et non cognovérunt paréntes ejus existimántes illum esse in comitátu: et requirébant eum inter cognátos et notos.
Ant 2.eng: The child Jesus * remained in Jerusalem; and his parents knew it not. And thinking that he was in the company, they came a day's journey, and sought him among their kinsfolks and acquaintance.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Fili, quid fecísti * nobis sic? Ego et pater tuus doléntes quærebámus te. Quid est quod me quærebátis? nesciebátis quia in iis, quæ Patris mei sunt, opórtet me esse?
Ant 3.eng: Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? Behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing. How is it that ye sought me? Wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Fratres: Obsécro vos per misericórdiam Dei, ut exhibeátis córpora vestra hóstiam vivéntem, sanctam, Deo placéntem, rationábile obséquium vestrum.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Brethren: I Beseech you, by the mercy of God, that you present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, pleasing unto God, your reasonable service

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Sicut enim in uno córpore multa membra habémus ómnia autem membra non eundem actum habent: ita multi unum corpus sumus in Christo sínguli autem alter altérius membra in Christo Jesu Dómino nostro.
Capitulum Nona.eng: For as in one body we have many members, but all the members have not the same office: So we being many, are one body in Christ, and every one members one of another.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Dico enim per grátiam quæ data est mihi ómnibus qui sunt inter vos non plus sápere quam opórtet sápere sed sápere ad sobrietátem unicuíque sicut Deus divísit mensúram fídei.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: For I say, by the grace that is given me, to all that are among you, not to be more wise than it behoveth to be wise, but to be wise unto sobriety, and according as God hath divided to every one the measure of faith

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Vota, quǽsumus, Dómine, supplicántis pópuli cælésti pietáte proséquere: ut et quæ agénda sunt, vídeant, et ad implénda quæ víderint, convaléscant.
Oratio.eng: Attend, O Lord, we beseech thee, of thy heavenly mercy, to the desires of thy suppliant people; and grant that they may both perceive what they ought to do, and may have strength to fulfill the same.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Concede, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut ad meliórem vitam Sanctórum tuórum exémpla nos próvocent; quátenus, quorum solémnia ágimus, étiam actus imitémur.
Oratio.eng: Grant, we beseech thee, O Almighty God, that the example of thy Saints may continually stir us up to amend our sinful lives, that as we do solemnly commemorate them, we may also sincerely strive to imitate them.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Euge, serve bone * et fidélis, quia in pauca fuísti fidélis, supra multa te constítuam, dicit Dóminus.
Ant 1.eng: Well done, thou good and faithful servant * thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things, saith the Lord.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Similábo eum * viro sapiénti, qui ædificávit domum suam supra petram.
Ant 2.eng: I will liken him unto a wise man, * which built his house upon a rock.

Versum 1.label: Versicle
Versum 1.eng: ℣. The mouth of the righteous speaketh wisdom.
Versum 1.engR: ℟. And his tongue talketh judgment.

Versum 2.label: Versicle
Versum 2.lat: ℣. Amávit eum Dóminus, et ornávit eum.
Versum 2.latR: ℟. Stolam glóriæ índuit eum.
Versum 2.eng: ℣. The Lord loved him and beautified him.
Versum 2.engR: ℟. He clothed him with a robe of glory.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Preces pópuli tui, quǽsumus, Dómine, cleménter exáudi: ut beáti Marcélli Mártyris tui atque Pontíficis méritis adjuvémur, cujus passióne lætámur.
Oratio.eng: O Lord, we pray thee, mercifully give ear unto the prayers of thy people who rejoice at the memory of the victory through suffering of thy blessed Martyr and Bishop Marcellus, and for his sake succour us.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Tu es pastor óvium, * Princeps Apostolórum, tibi tráditæ sunt claves regni cælórum.
Ant 1.eng: Thou art the Shepherd * of the sheep, and the Prince of the Apostles, and unto thee are given the keys of the kingdom of heaven.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Quodcúmque * ligáveris super terram, erit ligátum et in cælis; et quodcúmque sólveris super terram, erit solútum et in cælis: dicit Dóminus Simóni Petro.
Ant 2.eng: Thus saith the Lord * unto Simon Peter: Whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth, shall be bound in heaven; and whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth, shall be loosed in heaven.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Dum esset Summus Póntifex, * terréna non métuit, sed ad cæléstia regna gloriósus migrávit.
Ant 3.eng: While he was supreme Pontiff, * he feared not earthly powers, but gloriously went his way to the heavenly kingdom.

Hymnus Laudes.label: Hymn
Hymnus Laudes.title: Beáte Pastor, Petre, clemens áccipe
Hymnus Laudes.lat:
Beáte Pastor, Petre, clemens áccipe
Voces precántum, criminúmque víncula
Verbo resólve, cui potéstas trádita
Aperíre terris cælum, apértum cláudere.

Sit Trinitáti sempitérna glória,
Honor, potéstas atque jubilátio,
In unitáte, quæ gubérnat ómnia,
Per univérsa æternitátis sǽcula.
Amen.
Hymnus Laudes.eng:
Peter, blest shepherd, hearken to our cry,
And with a word unloose our guilty chain;
Thou! who hast power to open the gates on high
To men below, and power to shut them fast again.

Praise, blessing, majesty, through endless days,
Be to the Trinity immortal given;
Who in pure unity profoundly sways
Eternally alike all things in earth and heaven.
Amen.

Hymnus Matutinum.label: Hymn
Hymnus Matutinum.title: Quodcúmque in orbe néxibus revínxeris
Hymnus Matutinum.lat:
Quodcúmque in orbe néxibus revínxeris,
Erit revínctum, Petre, in arce síderum:
Et quod resólvit hic potéstas trádita,
Erit solútum cæli in alto vértice;
In fine mundi judicábis sǽculum.

Patri perénne sit per ævum glória,
Tibíque laudes concinámus ínclitas,
Ætérne Nate; sit, supérne Spíritus,
Honor tibi decúsque: sancta júgiter
Laudétur omne Trínitas per sǽculum.
Amen.

Hymnus Vespera.title: Quodcúmque in orbe néxibus revínxeris
Hymnus Vespera.lat:
Quodcúmque in orbe néxibus revínxeris,
Erit revínctum, Petre, in arce síderum:
Et quod resólvit hic potéstas trádita,
Erit solútum cæli in alto vértice;
In fine mundi judicábis sǽculum.

Patri perénne sit per ævum glória,
Tibíque laudes concinámus ínclitas,
Ætérne Nate; sit, supérne Spíritus,
Honor tibi decúsque: sancta júgiter
Laudétur omne Trínitas per sǽculum.
Amen.

Invit.label: Antiphon
Invit.lat: Tu es pastor óvium, Princeps Apostolórum: * Tibi trádidit Deus claves regni cælórum.
Invit.eng: Thou art the Shepherd of the sheep, and the Prince of the Apostles * and unto thee hath God given the keys of the kingdom of heaven.

Oratio Commemoratio.label: Commemoratio
Oratio Commemoratio.lat:
!Commemoratio S. Pauli Apostoli
v. Deus, qui multitúdinem géntium beáti Pauli Apóstoli prædicatióne docuísti: da nobis, quǽsumus; ut, cujus commemoratiónem cólimus, ejus apud te patrocínia sentiámus.
$Per Dominum
Oratio Commemoratio.eng:
!Commemoration of St. Paul the Apostle
v. O God, Who, through the preaching of the Blessed Apostle Paul, hast caused the light of the Gospel to shine throughout the world, grant, we beseech thee, that we, who do keep his memorial, may continually be helped by his intercession with thee.
$Per Dominum

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat:
Deus, qui beáto Petro Apóstolo tuo, collátis clávibus regni cæléstis, ligándi atque solvéndi pontifícium tradidísti: concéde; ut, intercessiónis ejus auxílio, a peccatórum nostrórum néxibus liberémur:
_
Oratio.eng:
O God, Who hast given unto thy Blessed Apostle Peter the keys of the kingdom of heaven, and the power to bind and to loose, loose us, we beseech thee, at his mighty intercession, from all the bands of our sins.
_

Versum 1.label: Versicle
Versum 1.latR: ℟. Et super hanc petram ædificábo Ecclésiam meam.
Versum 1.eng: ℣. You are Peter.
Versum 1.engR: ℟. And on this rock I am going to build my church.

Versum 2.label: Versicle
Versum 2.latR: ℟. Et in cáthedra seniórum laudent eum.
Versum 2.eng: ℣. Let them exalt Him in the congregation of the people.
Versum 2.engR: ℟. And praise Him in the assembly of the elders.

Versum 3.label: Versicle
Versum 3.lat: ℣. Elégit te Dóminus sacerdótem sibi.
Versum 3.latR: ℟. Ad sacrificándum ei hóstiam laudis.
Versum 3.eng: ℣. The Lord chose him as a priest unto himself.
Versum 3.engR: ℟. To offer unto him the Sacrifice of Thanksgiving.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Da, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui beátæ Priscæ Vírginis et Mártyris tuæ natalícia cólimus; et ánnua solemnitáte lætémur, et tantæ fídei proficiámus exémplo.
Oratio.eng: Grant, we beseech thee, Almighty God, unto all thy servants who do here keep the birthday of thy blessed Virgin and Martyr Prisca, and do year by year rejoice at her solemn commemoration, that they may have grace to follow after the pattern of her great faith.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Exáudi, Dómine, pópulum tuum cum Sanctórum tuórum patrocínio supplicántem: ut et temporális vitæ nos tríbuas pace gaudére; et ætérnæ reperíre subsídium.
Oratio.eng: Graciously hear, O Lord, the prayers of thy people who draw near unto thee under the protection of thy blessed Saints, granting us in this world thy peace, and in that which is to come life everlasting.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui ad illustrándam Ecclésiam tuam beátum Canútum regem martýrii palma et gloriósis miráculis decoráre dignátus es: concéde propítius; ut, sicut ipse Domínicæ passiónis imitátor fuit, ita nos, per ejus vestígia gradiéntes, ad gáudia sempitérna perveníre mereámur.
Oratio.eng: O God, who, for the greater glory of Thy Church, wast pleased to adorn blessed Canute the king with the palm of martyrdom and with glorious miracles: mercifully grant that, walking in the footsteps of him who followed our Lord in His sufferings, we may thereby deserve to attain to eternal joys.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Infirmitátem nostram réspice, omnípotens Deus: et, quia pondus própriæ actiónis gravat, beatórum Mártyrum tuórum Fabiáni et Sebastiáni intercéssio gloriósa nos prótegat.
Oratio.eng: Be mindful of our weakness, almighty God, and since the burden of our sins weighs heavily upon us, may the glorious intercession of thy holy Martyrs Fabian and Sebastian sustain us.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Beáta Agnes * in médio flammárum expánsis mánibus orábat: Te déprecor, omnípotens, adoránde, colénde, Pater metuénde, quia per sanctum Fílium tuum evási minas sacrílegi tyránni, et carnis spurcítias immaculáto calle transívi: et ecce vénio ad te, quem amávi, quem quæsívi, quem semper optávi.
Ant 1.eng: The blessed Agnes * stood in the midst of the fire, and stretched forth her hands, and prayed, saying O Father! Who Alone art Almighty! Who Alone art to be adored! Who Alone art to be worshipped! Who Alone art to be feared! I thank thee because that through thy Holy Son Thou hast delivered me from the threatenings of the godless tyrant, and hast made me to walk with clean feet over the filthy slough of fleshly sin and now, behold, I come unto thee, unto thee Whom I have loved, Whom I have sought, Whom I have ever desired.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Ecce, quod concupívi, * jam vídeo: quod sperávi, jam téneo: ipsi sum juncta in cælis, quem in terris pósita, tota devotióne diléxi.
Ant 2.eng: Behold, now I see that * which I have desired; now I possess that for which I have hoped now am I united in heaven to Him Whom I loved with my whole heart upon earth.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Stans beáta Agnes * in médio flammæ, expánsis mánibus orábat ad Dóminum: Omnípotens, adoránde, colénde, treménde, benedíco te, et glorífico nomen tuum in ætérnum.
Ant 3.eng: The blessed Agnes stood in the midst of the fire * and stretched forth her hands unto the Lord, and prayed, saying: O Thou Who Alone art Almighty! Who Alone art to be adored! Who Alone art to be worshipped! Who Alone art to be feared! I bless thee, and glorify thy Name for ever and ever!

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Confitébor tibi, Dómine, Rex, et collaudábo te Deum Salvatórem meum. Confitébor nómini tuo: quóniam adjútor et protéctor factus es mihi, et liberásti corpus meum a perditióne.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: I will give glory to thee, O Lord, O King, and I will praise thee, O God my Saviour. I will give glory to thy name: for thou hast been a helper and protector to me, and hast preserved my body from destruction.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Laudábit usque ad mortem ánima mea Dóminum, quóniam éruis sustinéntes te, et líberas eos de manu angústiæ, Dómine, Deus noster.
Capitulum Nona.eng: My soul shall praise the Lord even to death. How thou deliverest them that wait for thee, O Lord, and savest them out of the hands of the nations.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Liberásti me secúndum multitúdinem misericórdiæ nóminis tui a rugiéntibus, præparátis ad escam, de mánibus quæréntium ánimam meam, et de multis tribulatiónibus quæ circumdedérunt me.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: And thou hast delivered me, according to the multitude of the mercy of thy name, from them that did roar, prepared to devour. Out of the hands of them that sought my life, and from the gates of afflictions, which compassed me about.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui infírma mundi éligis, ut fórtia quæque confúndas: concéde propítius; ut, qui beátæ Agnétis Vírginis et Mártyris tuæ solémnia cólimus, ejus apud te patrocínia sentiámus.
Oratio.eng: O Almighty and everlasting God, Who hast chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty, mercifully grant unto us that we who keep the solemn feast of thy blessed Virgin and Martyr Agnes, may feel the power of her intercession with thee.

Ant Laudes.ant: Ingréssa Agnes * turpitúdinis locum, Angelum Dómini præparátum invénit.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Agnes entered * the place of shame, and found the Angel of the Lord ready.

Ant Laudes.ant: Mecum enim hábeo * custódem córporis mei, Angelum Dómini.
Ant Laudes.antEng: For I have with me * an Angel of the Lord to keep my body.

Ant Laudes.ant: Anulo suo * subarrhávit me Dóminus meus Jesus Christus, et tamquam sponsam decorávit me coróna.
Ant Laudes.antEng: My Lord Jesus Christ hath espoused me with His ring, * and hath set on my head a crown as the crown of a bride.

Ant Laudes.ant: Benedíco te, * Pater Dómini mei Jesu Christi, quia per Fílium tuum ignis exstínctus est a látere meo.
Ant Laudes.antEng: I bless thee, O Father of my Lord Jesus Christ, because through thy Son the fire is quenched around me.

Ant Laudes.ant: Congaudéte mecum * et congratulámini, quia cum his ómnibus lúcidas sedes accépi.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Rejoice with me * and make merry, because I also have received a throne in light among all these.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Discéde a me, * pábulum mortis, quia jam ab álio amatóre prævénta sum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Depart from me, prey of death, for I am prevented by another Lover.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Déxteram meam * et collum meum cinxit lapídibus pretiósis, trádidit áuribus meis inæstimábiles margarítas.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: My right hand and my neck hath He clasped with precious stones, and put pearls beyond price in mine ears.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Pósuit signum * in fáciem meam, ut nullum præter eum amatórem admíttam.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: He hath sealed me in my forehead that I may let in no other lover but Him.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Induit me Dóminus * cýclade auro texta, et imménsis monílibus ornávit me.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord hath clothed me with a vesture of wrought gold, and adorned me with a necklace of great price.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Mel et lac * ex ejus ore suscépi, et sanguis ejus ornávit genas meas.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I have sucked honey and milk out of His Mouth, and His Blood is red on my cheeks.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ipsi soli servo fidem, * ipsi me tota devotióne commítto.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I keep my troth to Him alone, and commit me altogether to Him.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Cujus pulchritúdinem * sol et luna mirántur, ipsi soli servo fidem.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I keep my troth to Him Alone, at Whose beauty the sun and the moon do wonder.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Christus circúmdedit me * vernántibus atque coruscántibus gemmis pretiósis.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Christ hath crowned me with the bright and priceless blossoms of the eternal spring-time.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ipsi sum desponsáta, * cui Angeli sérviunt, cujus pulchritúdinem sol et luna mirántur.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I am wedded to the Lord of Angels, at Whose beauty the sun and the moon do wonder.

Ant Vespera.antEng: Agnes entered * the place of shame, and found the Angel of the Lord ready.

Ant Vespera.ant: Mecum enim hábeo * custódem córporis mei, Angelum Dómini.

Ant Vespera.ant: Benedíco te, * Pater Dómini mei Jesu Christi, quia per Fílium tuum ignis exstínctus est a látere meo.
Ant Vespera.antEng: I bless thee, O Father of my Lord Jesus Christ, because through thy Son the fire is quenched around me.

Ant Vespera.ant: Congaudéte mecum * et congratulámini, quia cum his ómnibus lúcidas sedes accépi.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Rejoice with me * and make merry, because I also have received a throne in light among all these.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Adésto, Dómine, supplicatiónibus nostris: ut, qui ex iniquitáte nostra reos nos esse cognóscimus, beatórum Mártyrum tuórum Vincéntii et Anastásii intercessióne liberémur.
Oratio.eng: Let thy merciful ears, O Lord, be open unto our prayers, and whereas we do feel ourselves burdened by the guilt of our sins, do Thou graciously relieve us at the petition of thy blessed Martyrs, Vincent and Anastasius.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui beátum Raymúndum pœniténtiæ sacraménti insígnem minístrum elegísti, et per maris undas mirabíliter traduxísti: concéde; ut ejus intercessióne dignos pœniténtiæ fructus fácere, et ad ætérnæ salútis portum perveníre valeámus.
Oratio.eng: O God, Who didst choose the blessed Raymond to be an eminent minister of the Sacrament of Penance, and in a wonderful manner didst make him to pass over the waves of the sea, grant unto us, at his petition, the grace to bring forth fruits worthy of repentance, and in the end to attain unto the harbour of eternal salvation.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Vade, Anania, * et quære Saulum: ecce enim orat: quia vas electiónis est mihi, ut portet nomen meum coram géntibus, et régibus, et fíliis Israël.
Ant 1.eng: Ananias, go thy way * and seek Saul for, behold, he prayeth for he is a chosen vessel unto Me, to bear My name before the Gentiles, and kings, and the children of Israel.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Vos qui secúti estis me, * sedébitis super sedes, judicántes duódecim tribus Israël, dicit Dóminus.
Ant 2.eng: Thus saith the Lord: * Ye, which have followed Me, shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Sancte Paule Apóstole, * prædicátor veritátis et doctor géntium, intercéde pro nobis ad Deum, qui te elégit.
Ant 3.eng: O Holy Apostle Paul, * Preacher of the truth, and Teacher of the Gentiles, pray for us to God Who hath chosen thee.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Saulus autem adhuc spirans minárum et cædis in discípulos Dómini, accéssit ad príncipem sacerdótum, et pétiit ab eo epístolas in Damáscum ad synagógas: ut si quos invenísset hujus viæ viros ac mulíeres, vinctos perdúceret in Jerúsalem.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: And Saul, as yet breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, went to the high priest, and asked of him letters to Damascus, to the synagogues: that if he found any men and women of this way, he might bring them bound to Jerusalem.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Saulus autem multo magis convalescébat, et confundébat Judǽos qui habitábant Damásci, affírmans quóniam hic est Christus.
Capitulum Nona.eng: But Saul increased much more in strength, and confounded the Jews who dwelt at Damascus, affirming that this is the Christ.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Surréxit autem Saulus de terra, apertísque óculis nihil vidébat. Ad manus autem illum trahéntes, introduxérunt Damáscum. Et erat ibi tribus diébus non videns, et non manducávit neque bibit.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: And Saul arose from the ground; and when his eyes were opened, he saw nothing. But they leading him by the hands, brought him to Damascus. And he was there three days, without sight, and he did neither eat nor drink.

Hymnus Vespera.label: Hymn
Hymnus Vespera.title: Egrégie Doctor, Paule, mores ínstrue
Hymnus Vespera.lat:
Egrégie Doctor, Paule, mores ínstrue,
Et nostra tecum péctora in cælum trahe;
Veláta dum merídiem cernat fides,
Et solis instar sola regnet cáritas.

Sit Trinitáti sempitérna glória,
Honor, potéstas atque jubilátio,
In unitáte, quæ gubérnat ómnia,
Per univérsa æternitátis sǽcula.
Amen.
Hymnus Vespera.eng:
Our souls' great teacher, Paul, our guide in wisdom's ways,
Teach us, our fainting hearts, to heaven's glad clime to raise,
Till faith in clearest light her bright meridian gains,
And love with sun-like fire within each bosom reigns.

All honour, might, and power, and hymns of joy we bring,
While to the Trinity eternal praise we sing;
He rules the universe in wondrous Unity,
And shall, throughout the days of all eternity.
Amen.

Invit.label: Antiphon
Invit.lat: Laudémus Deum nostrum, * In conversióne Doctóris géntium.
Invit.eng: For the conversion of the Teacher of the Gentiles, * let us praise our God.

Lectio Prima.label: Lectio brevis
Lectio Prima.lat: Saulus autem multo magis convalescébat, et confundébat Judǽos qui habitábant Damásci, affírmans quóniam hic est Christus.
Lectio Prima.eng: But Saul increased much more in strength, and confounded the Jews who dwelt at Damascus, affirming that this is the Christ.

Oratio Commemoratio.label: Commemoratio
Oratio Commemoratio.lat:
!Commemoratio S. Petri Apostoli
v. Deus, qui beáto Petro Apóstolo tuo, collátis clávibus regni cæléstis, ligándi atque solvéndi pontifícium tradidísti: concéde; ut, intercessiónis ejus auxílio, a peccatórum nostrórum néxibus liberémur:
$Qui vivis
Oratio Commemoratio.eng:
!Commemoration of St. Peter the Apostle
v. O God, Who hast given unto thy Blessed Apostle Peter the keys of the kingdom of heaven, and the power to bind and to loose, loose us, we beseech thee, at his mighty intercession, from all the bands of our sins.
$Qui vivis

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat:
Deus, qui univérsum mundum beáti Pauli Apóstoli prædicatióne docuísti: da nobis, quǽsumus; ut, qui ejus hódie Conversiónem cólimus, per ejus ad te exémpla gradiámur.
_
Oratio.eng:
O God, Who, through the teaching of the Blessed Apostle Paul, hast caused the light of the Gospel to shine throughout the world, grant, we beseech thee, that we, having his wonderful conversion as on this day in remembrance, may show forth our thankfulness unto thee for the same, by following the holy example which he hath set.
_

Ant Laudes.ant: Ego plantávi, * Apóllo rigávit, Deus autem increméntum dedit. Allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: I have planted, * Apollos watered, but God gave the increase. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Libénter gloriábor * in infirmitátibus meis, ut inhábitet in me virtus Christi.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Most gladly therefore will I rather glory * in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.

Ant Laudes.ant: Grátia Dei * in me vácua non fuit, sed grátia ejus semper in me manet.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The grace of God which was bestowed upon me was not in vain, * but His grace abideth ever in me.

Ant Laudes.ant: Damásci, præpósitus * gentis Arétæ regis vóluit me comprehéndere: a frátribus per murum demíssus sum in sporta, et sic evási manus ejus in nómine Dómini.
Ant Laudes.antEng: In Damascus the governor under Aretas the king was desirous to apprehend me; by the brethren in a basket was I let down by the wall, and so escaped I his hands, in the name of the Lord.

Ant Laudes.ant: Ter virgis cæsus sum, * semel lapidátus sum, ter naufrágium pértuli pro Christi nómine.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Thrice was I beaten with rods, * once was I stoned, thrice I suffered shipwreck, for Christ's name's sake.
