Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Est secrétum, * Valeriáne, quod tibi volo dícere: Angelum Dei hábeo amatórem, qui nímio zelo custódit corpus meum.
Ant 1.eng: Valerian! there is a secret * which I wish to tell thee. I have an Angel of God for a lover, and he is very jealous to keep my body.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Dum auróra * finem daret, Cæcília exclamávit dicens: Eia, mílites Christi, abícite ópera tenebrárum et induímini arma lucis.
Ant 2.eng: As dawn was fading * into day, Cecilia cried and said: Arise, O soldiers of Christ, cast away the works of darkness, and put on the armour of light.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Virgo gloriósa * semper Evangélium Christi gerébat in péctore suo, et non diébus neque nóctibus a collóquiis divínis et oratióne cessábat.
Ant 3.eng: The glorious maiden * carried the Gospel of Christ always in her breast, and meditated therein day and night talking with God and praying.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui nos ánnua beátæ Cæcíliæ Vírginis et Mártyris tuæ solemnitáte lætíficas: da, ut, quam venerámur offício, étiam piæ conversatiónis sequámur exémplo.
Oratio.eng: O God, Who year by year dost gladden thy people by the solemn feast of thy blessed Virgin and Martyr Cecilia, grant unto us, we beseech thee, not only devoutly to observe the same, but also to follow after the pattern of her godly conversation.

Ant Laudes.ant: Cantántibus órganis, * Cæcília Dómino decantábat, dicens: Fiat cor meum immaculátum, ut non confúndar.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The musicians played, and Cecilia sang unto the Lord, * saying: Let my heart be undefiled, that I be not ashamed.

Ant Laudes.ant: Valeriánus * in cubículo Cæcíliam cum Angelo orántem invénit.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Valerian found Cecilia praying in her chamber, * and with her the Angel.

Ant Laudes.ant: Cæcília * fámula tua, Dómine, quasi apis tibi argumentósa desérvit.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Busy like a bee, * O Lord, did thine handmaiden Cecilia serve thee.

Ant Laudes.ant: Benedíco te, * Pater Dómini mei Jesu Christi, quia per Fílium tuum ignis exstínctus est a látere meo.
Ant Laudes.antEng: I bless thee, O Father of my Lord Jesus Christ, * that through thy Son the fire is gone out round about me.

Ant Laudes.ant: Triduánas * a Dómino popósci indúcias, ut domum meam ecclésiam consecrárem.
Ant Laudes.antEng: I have asked the Lord for three days, * that I may consecrate my house as a Church.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Cæcília virgo * Almáchium superábat: Tibúrtium et Valeriánum ad corónas vocábat.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Maiden Cecilia * overcame Almachius, and called Tiburtius and Valerian to crowns.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Expánsis mánibus * orábat ad Dóminum, ut eam eríperet de inimícis.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: She spread forth her hands * and prayed unto the Lord, that He would deliver her from her enemies.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Cilício * Cæcília membra domábat, Deum gemítibus exorábat.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Cecilia subdued her body with haircloth, * and besought God with loud crying.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dómine Jesu Christe, * seminátor casti consílii, súscipe séminum fructus, quos in Cæcília seminásti.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O Lord Jesus Christ, * Who hast said of abstaining from marriage: He that is able to receive it, let him receive it, accept now the fruits from this seed, which Thou didst sow in the heart of Cecilia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Beáta Cæcília * dixit ad Tibúrtium: Hódie te fáteor meum cognátum, quia amor Dei te fecit esse contemptórem idolórum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Blessed Cecilia * said unto Tiburtius: Today I call thee my brother, for the love of God hath made thee to cast away idols.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Fiat, Dómine, * cor meum et corpus meum immaculátum, ut non confúndar.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Lord, let my heart * and my body be undefiled, that I be not ashamed.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Crédimus Christum * Fílium Dei verum Deum esse, qui sibi talem elégit fámulam.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Christ, the Son of God, * Who hath chosen unto Himself such an handmaiden, Him we believe to be the true God.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Nos sciéntes * sanctum nomen ejus, omníno negáre non póssumus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: We that have known * His Holy Name can by no means deny Him.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Tunc Valeriánus * perréxit, et signo quod accéperat, invénit sanctum Urbánum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Then Valerian * went his way, and found the holy Urban, by the sign which had been given him.

Ant Vespera.antEng: I have asked the Lord for three days, * that I may consecrate my house as a Church.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dómine Jesu Christe, * seminátor casti consílii, súscipe séminum fructus, quos in Cæcília seminásti.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O Lord Jesus Christ, * Who hast said of abstaining from marriage: He that is able to receive it, let him receive it, accept now the fruits from this seed, which Thou didst sow in the heart of Cecilia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Beáta Cæcília * dixit ad Tibúrtium: Hódie te fáteor meum cognátum, quia amor Dei te fecit esse contemptórem idolórum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Blessed Cecilia * said unto Tiburtius: Today I call thee my brother, for the love of God hath made thee to cast away idols.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Fiat, Dómine, * cor meum et corpus meum immaculátum, ut non confúndar.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Lord, let my heart * and my body be undefiled, that I be not ashamed.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Crédimus Christum * Fílium Dei verum Deum esse, qui sibi talem elégit fámulam.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Christ, the Son of God, * Who hath chosen unto Himself such an handmaiden, Him we believe to be the true God.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Nos sciéntes * sanctum nomen ejus, omníno negáre non póssumus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: We that have known * His Holy Name can by no means deny Him.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Tunc Valeriánus * perréxit, et signo quod accéperat, invénit sanctum Urbánum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Then Valerian * went his way, and found the holy Urban, by the sign which had been given him.

Ant Vespera.ant: Cantántibus órganis, * Cæcília Dómino decantábat, dicens: Fiat cor meum immaculátum, ut non confúndar.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The musicians played, and Cecilia sang unto the Lord, * saying: Let my heart be undefiled, that I be not ashamed.

Ant Vespera.ant: Valeriánus * in cubículo Cæcíliam cum Angelo orántem invénit.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Valerian found Cecilia praying in her chamber, * and with her the Angel.

Ant Vespera.ant: Cæcília * fámula tua, Dómine, quasi apis tibi argumentósa desérvit.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Busy like a bee, * O Lord, did thine handmaiden Cecilia serve thee.

Ant Vespera.ant: Benedíco te, * Pater Dómini mei Jesu Christi, quia per Fílium tuum ignis exstínctus est a látere meo.
Ant Vespera.antEng: I bless thee, O Father of my Lord Jesus Christ, * that through thy Son the fire is gone out round about me.

Ant Vespera.ant: Triduánas * a Dómino popósci indúcias, ut domum meam ecclésiam consecrárem.
Ant Vespera.antEng: I have asked the Lord for three days, * that I may consecrate my house as a Church.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Cantántibus órganis, * Cæcília Dómino decantábat, dicens: Fiat cor meum immaculátum, ut non confúndar.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: The musicians played, and Cecilia sang unto the Lord, * saying: Let my heart be undefiled, that I be not ashamed.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Triduánas * a Dómino popósci indúcias, ut domum meam ecclésiam consecrárem.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: I have asked the Lord for three days, * that I may consecrate my house as a Church.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Orémus omnes * ad Dóminum Jesum Christum, ut Confessóribus suis fontis venam apériat.
Ant 1.eng: Let us all * pray Our Lord Jesus Christ to open a spring for those that own His Name.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Cum iter ad mare cepísset, * pópulus voce magna clamábat: Dómine Jesu Christe, salva illum; et Clemens cum lácrimis dicébat: Súscipe, Pater, spíritum meum.
Ant 2.eng: As he began to move toward the sea * the people cried out with a loud voice: O Lord Jesus Christ, deliver him! And Clement wept, and said: Father, receive my spirit!

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Dedísti, Dómine, * habitáculum Mártyri tuo Cleménti in mari, in modum templi marmórei angélicis mánibus præparátum: iter præbens pópulo terræ, ut enárrent mirabília tua.
Ant 3.eng: Lord, * Thou hast given unto thy Martyr Clement a tabernacle in the sea, after the fashion of a temple of marble, builded by the hands of Angels. And Thou givest a way thither unto the people on the land, that they may tell of thy marvellous works.

Ant Laudes.ant: Oránte * sancto Cleménte, appáruit ei Agnus Dei.
Ant Laudes.antEng: While St. Clement prayed, * there appeared unto him the Lamb of God.

Ant Laudes.ant: Non meis méritis * ad vos me misit Dóminus, vestris corónis partícipem fíeri.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Not for my own merits * hath the Lord sent me unto you, that I may share your crowns.

Ant Laudes.ant: Vidi supra montem * Agnum stantem, de sub cujus pede fons vivus emánat.
Ant Laudes.antEng: I saw on the mountain * the Lamb standing, from beneath whose foot flowed a fountain of living waters.

Ant Laudes.ant: De sub cujus pede * fons vivus emánat: flúminis ímpetus lætíficat civitátem Dei.
Ant Laudes.antEng: From beneath whose foot * a fountain of living waters flowed forth: the stream of the river that maketh glad the city of God.

Ant Laudes.ant: Omnes gentes * per gyrum credidérunt Christo Dómino.
Ant Laudes.antEng: All the nations * round about believed in Christ the Lord.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, beátæ Felicitátis Mártyris tuæ solémnia recenséntes, méritis ipsíus protegámur et précibus.
Oratio.eng: Grant, we beseech thee, O Almighty God, that in calling to mind the victory of thy blessed Martyr Felicity, we may find shelter both for her sake and in her prayers.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui sanctum Joánnem Confessórem tuum atque Doctórem perféctæ sui abnegatiónis et Crucis amatórem exímium effecísti: concéde; ut, ejus imitatióni júgiter inhæréntes, glóriam assequámur ætérnam.
Oratio.eng: O God, who didst give to blessed John, thy Confessor and Doctor, grace to shew forth a singular love of perfect self-denial and of bearing thy Cross: grant, we beseech thee; that we, cleaving steadfastly to his pattern, may attain to everlasting glory.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Adésto, Dómine, supplicatiónibus nostris: ut, qui ex iniquitáte nostra reos nos esse cognóscimus, beáti Chrysógoni Mártyris tui intercessióne liberémur.
Oratio.eng: Give ear, O Lord, unto our prayers, and grant that we who acknowledge ourselves guilty through our own iniquity, may be delivered at the petition of thy blessed Martyr Chrysogonus.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui dedísti legem Móysi in summitáte montis Sínai, et in eódem loco per sanctos Angelos tuos corpus beátæ Catharínæ Vírginis et Mártyris tuæ mirabíliter collocásti: præsta, quǽsumus; ut, ejus méritis et intercessióne, ad montem, qui Christus est, perveníre valeámus:
Oratio.eng: O God, Who didst give the Law unto Moses upon the top of Mount Sinai, and there didst cause the body of thy blessed Virgin and Martyr Catharine to be marvelously laid by thine holy Angels, grant unto us, we beseech thee, for her sake and at her prayers, that we may finally attain unto that mountain which is Christ.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Clementíssime Deus, qui sanctum Silvéstrum Abbátem, sǽculi hujus vanitátem in apérto túmulo pie meditántem, ad erémum vocáre, et præcláris vitæ méritis decoráre dignátus es: te súpplices exorámus; ut, ejus exémplo terréna despiciéntes, tui consórtio perfruámur ætérno.
Oratio.eng: Most merciful God, Who when the holy Abbot Sylvester was devoutly meditating upon the vanity of this world beside an open grave, graciously willed to call him into the desert and enrich him with unusual merits, we humbly pray that, following his example, despising the things of earth, we may thoroughly enjoy Thy everlasting presence.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Quǽsumus omnípotens Deus, ut beátus N. Apóstolus, cujus prævenímus festivitátem, tuum pro nobis implóret auxílium: ut a nostris reátibus absolúti a cunctis étiam perículis eruámur.
Oratio.eng: Grant, we beseech thee, O Almighty God, that the worshipful Feast of thy blessed Apostle, N. on the eve whereof we now stand, may avail us to the increase both of godliness toward thee, and of health to our own souls.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui nos beáti Saturníni Mártyris tui concédis natalício pérfrui: ejus nos tríbue méritis adjuvári.
Oratio.eng: O God, by Whose mercy we keep the birth-day of thy blessed martyr Saturninus, grant us also succour for his sake.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Unus ex duóbus, * qui secúti sunt Dóminum, erat Andréas, frater Simónis Petri, allelúja.
Ant 1.eng: One of the two * which followed the Lord was Andrew, Simon Peter's brother. Alleluia.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Concéde nobis * hóminem justum, redde nobis hóminem sanctum: ne interfícias hóminem Deo carum, justum, mansuétum et pium.
Ant 2.eng: Spare unto us * this just man, release unto us this holy one; slay not the friend of God, who is just, courteous, and godly.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Cum pervenísset * beátus Andréas ad locum, ubi crux paráta erat, exclamávit et dixit: O bona crux, diu desideráta, et jam concupiscénti ánimo præparáta: secúrus et gaudens vénio ad te, ita et tu exsúltans suscípias me discípulum ejus, qui pepéndit in te.
Ant 3.eng: When the blessed * Andrew came to the place where the cross was made ready, he cried and said: O precious cross, of a long time have I desired thee, and, now that thou art made ready for me, my soul is drawn to thee, and I come to thee in peace and gladness; thou also oughtest to welcome me with joy, for I am the disciple of Him Who hung on thee.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Fratres: Corde enim créditur ad justítiam, ore autem conféssio fit ad salútem. Dicit enim Scriptúra: Omnis, qui credit in illum, non confundétur.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Brothers: For, with the heart, we believe unto justice; but, with the mouth, confession is made unto salvation. For the scripture saith: Whosoever believeth in him, shall not be confounded.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Isaías enim dicit: Dómine, quis crédidit audítui nostro? Ergo fides ex audítu, audítus autem per verbum Christi. Sed dico: Numquid non audiérunt? Et quidem in omnem terram exívit sonus eórum, et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.
Capitulum Nona.eng: For Isaias saith: Lord, who hath believed our report? Faith then cometh by hearing; and hearing by the word of Christ. But I say: Have they not heard? Yes, verily, their sound hath gone forth into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the whole world.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Non enim est distínctio Judǽi et Græci: nam idem Dóminus ómnium, dives in omnes, qui ínvocant illum. Omnis enim, quicúmque invocáverit nomen Dómini, salvus erit.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: For there is no distinction of the Jew and the Greek: for the same is Lord over all, rich unto all that call upon him. For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord, shall be saved.

Lectio Prima.label: Lectio brevis
Lectio Prima.lat: Isaías enim dicit: Dómine, quis crédidit audítui nostro? Ergo fides ex audítu, audítus autem per verbum Christi. Sed dico: Numquid non audiérunt? Et quidem in omnem terram exívit sonus eórum, et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.
Lectio Prima.eng: For Isaias saith: Lord, who hath believed our report? Faith then cometh by hearing; and hearing by the word of Christ. But I say: Have they not heard? Yes, verily, their sound hath gone forth into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the whole world.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Majestátem tuam, Dómine, supplíciter exorámus: ut, sicut Ecclésiæ tuæ beátus Andréas Apóstolus éxstitit prædicátor et rector; ita apud te sit pro nobis perpétuus intercéssor.
Oratio.eng: O Lord, we humbly beseech thy Majesty, that even as Thou didst give thy blessed Apostle Andrew to thy Church to be a teacher and a ruler on earth, so, now that he is with thee, he may continually make intercession for us.

Ant Laudes.ant: Salve, crux pretiósa, * súscipe discípulum ejus, qui pepéndit in te magíster meus Christus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: God bless thee, precious cross, * be welcome to the follower of Him That hung on thee, even my Master Christ.

Ant Laudes.ant: Beátus Andréas * orábat, dicens: Dómine, Rex ætérnæ glóriæ, súscipe me pendéntem in patíbulo.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The blessed Andrew prayed and said: * O Lord, King of everlasting glory, receive me hanging on this gallows.

Ant Laudes.ant: Andréas Christi fámulus, * dignus Dei Apóstolus, germánus Petri, et in passióne sócius.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Andrew was the servant of Christ, * a worthy Apostle of God, the brother of Peter, and likened to Christ and to Peter in his death.

Ant Laudes.ant: Maximílla Christo amábilis * tulit corpus Apóstoli, óptimo loco cum aromátibus sepelívit.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Christ's dear handmaid Maximilla took the body * of the Apostle and buried it with spices in an honourable place.

Ant Laudes.ant: Qui persequebántur justum, * demersísti eos, Dómine, in inférno, et in ligno crucis dux justi fuísti.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O Lord, Thou hast caused them that persecuted the just to be swallowed up in hell, * but to the just Thou hast thyself shown the way on the tree of the cross.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Vidit Dóminus * Petrum et Andréam, et vocávit eos.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord saw Peter and Andrew, * and He called them.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Veníte post me, * dicit Dóminus, fáciam vos fíeri piscatóres hóminum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Follow Me, and I will make you fishers of men, * saith the Lord.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Relíctis rétibus suis, * secúti sunt Dóminum Redemptórem.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: And they left their nets, * and followed the Lord their Saviour.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dignum sibi Dóminus * computávit Mártyrem, quem vocávit Apóstolum, dum esset in mari, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Whom the Lord called to be His Apostle, * when he was by the sea, him also He counted worthy to be His martyr. Alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Diléxit Andréam * Dóminus in odórem suavitátis.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Andrew was to the Lord as a sweet savour, * which He loved exceedingly.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Bíduo vivens * pendébat in cruce beátus Andréas pro Christi nómine, et docébat pópulum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The blessed Andrew hung alive upon the cross for two days * for Christ's Name's sake, and, all the while, he taught the people.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Non me permíttas, Dómine, * fámulum tuum a te separári: tempus est ut commendétur terræ corpus meum, et me ad te veníre jubéas.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Suffer not thy servant, O Lord, to be parted from thee * the hour is come to lay my body in the earth, and for thee to bid me come unto thyself.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Andréas vero rogábat pópulum, * ut non impedíret passiónem ipsíus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: But Andrew besought the people * not to hinder his passion.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Accipe me ab homínibus * et redde me magístro meo: ut per te me recípiat, qui per te me redémit, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Welcome me from among men and join me again to my Master; * that, as by thee He redeemed me, so by thee also He may take me unto Himself. Alleluia.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, ómnium largítor bonórum, qui in fámula tua Bibiána cum virginitátis flore martýrii palmam conjunxísti: mentes nostras ejus intercessióne tibi caritáte conjúnge; ut, amótis perículis, prǽmia consequámur ætérna.
Oratio.eng: O God, the Giver of all good gifts, Who unto the lily of pure maidenhood in the hand of thy servant Bibiana, didst join the palm of a glorious martyrdom, grant us, we beseech thee, at her pleading, that our hearts and minds being joined to thee by thy love, we may escape all dangers which do presently beset us, and finally attain unto thine everlasting joy.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui Indiárum gentes beáti Francísci prædicatióne et miráculis Ecclésiæ tuæ aggregáre voluísti: concéde propítius; ut cujus gloriósa mérita venerámur, virtútum quoque imitémur exémpla.
Oratio.eng: O God, who wast pleased, by the preaching and miracles of blessed Francis, to add the nations of the Indies to thy Church; mercifully grant that, as we venerate his glorious merits, so we may also follow the example of his virtues.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui beátum Petrum Chrysólogum Doctórem egrégium, divínitus præmonstrátum, ad regéndam et instruéndam Ecclésiam tuam éligi voluísti: præsta, quǽsumus; ut, quem Doctórem vitæ habúimus in terris, intercessórem habére mereámur in cælis.
Oratio.eng: O God, who didst miraculously point out the glorious doctor Peter Chrysologus, and choose him to be a ruler and teacher of thy Church; grant, we beseech thee, that as on earth he taught us the way of life, so in heaven he may be our continual intercessor with thee.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui beátum Nicoláum Pontíficem innúmeris decorásti miráculis: tríbue, quǽsumus; ut ejus méritis et précibus a gehénnæ incéndiis liberémur.
Oratio.eng: O God, who didst glorify the blessed Bishop Nicholas with innumerable miracles; grant, we beseech thee, that, by his merits and prayers, we may be saved from the fires of hell.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Beátam me dicent * omnes generatiónes, quia fecit mihi magna, qui potens est, allelúja.
Ant 1.eng: All generations * shall call me blessed, because he that is mighty, hath done great things to me, alleluia.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Ait Dóminus Deus * ad serpéntem: Inimicítias ponam inter te et mulíerem, et semen tuum et semen illíus: ipsa cónteret caput tuum, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: The Lord God said * to the serpent: I will put enmities between thee and the woman, and thy seed and her seed: she shall crush thy head, alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Hódie egréssa est * virga de radíce Jesse: hódie sine ulla peccáti labe concépta est María: hódie contrítum est ab ea caput serpéntis antíqui, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: This day is a rod * sprung from the root of Jesse: this day is Mary conceived without any stain of sin: this day hath she bruised the head of the old serpent, alleluia.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Dóminus possédit me in inítio viárum suárum, ántequam quidquam fáceret a princípio. Ab ætérno ordináta sum, et ex antíquis ántequam terra fíeret. Nondum erant abýssi, et ego jam concépta eram.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his ways, before he made any thing from the beginning. I was set up from eternity, and of old before the earth was made. The depths were not as yet, and I was already conceived.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Signum magnum appáruit in cælo: Múlier amícta sole, et luna sub pédibus ejus, et in cápite ejus coróna stellárum duódecim.
Capitulum Nona.eng: And a great sign appeared in heaven: A woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Porta hæc clausa erit, non aperiétur, et vir non intrábit per eam, quóniam Dóminus Deus Israël ingréssus est per eam: erítque clausa príncipi. Princeps ipse sedébit in ea.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: This gate shall be shut, it shall not be opened, and no man shall pass through it: because the Lord the God of Israel hath entered in by it, and it shall be shut. For the prince, the prince himself, shall sit in it.

Hymnus Matutinum.label: Hymn
Hymnus Matutinum.title: Præclára custos Vírginum
Hymnus Matutinum.lat:
Præclára custos Vírginum,
Intácta mater Núminis,
Cæléstis aulæ jánua,
Spes nostra, cæli gáudium,

Inter rubéta lílium,
Colúmba formosíssima,
Virga e radíce gérminans
Nostro medélam vúlneri.

Turris dracóni impérvia,
Amíca stella náufragis,
Tuére nos a fráudibus,
Tuáque luce dírige.

Erróris umbras díscute,
Syrtes dolósas ámove,
Fluctus tot inter, déviis
Tutam reclúde sémitam.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
Hymnus Matutinum.eng:
Blest guardian of all virgin souls,
Portal of bliss to man forgiven,
Pure Mother of Almighty God,
Thou hope of earth and joy of heaven!

Fair Lily found among the thorn,
Most beauteous Dove with wings of gold,
Rod from whose tender root upsprang
That healing Flower so long foretold

Thou Tower against the dragon proof,
Thou Star to stormtossed voyagers dear;
Our course lies o'er a treacherous deep,
thine be the light by which we steer.

Scatter the mists that round us hang;
Keep far the fatal shoals away;
And while through darkling waves we sweep,
Open a path to light and day.

O Jesu, born of Virgin bright,
Immortal glory be to thee;
Praise to the Father infinite
And Holy Ghost eternally.
Amen.

Invit.label: Antiphon
Invit.lat: Immaculátam Conceptiónem Vírginis Maríæ celebrémus: * Christum ejus Fílium adorémus Dóminum.
Invit.eng: Let us celebrate the Immaculate Conception of the Virgin Mary: * Let us adore her Son, Christ the Lord.

Lectio Prima.label: Lectio brevis
Lectio Prima.lat: Signum magnum appáruit in cælo: Múlier amícta sole, et luna sub pédibus ejus, et in cápite ejus coróna stellárum duódecim.
Lectio Prima.eng: And a great sign appeared in heaven: A woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars.

Nocturn 1 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 1 Versum.eng: ℣. It is Almighty God That girdeth me with strength.
Nocturn 1 Versum.engR: ℟. And maketh my way perfect.

Nocturn 2 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 2 Versum.lat: ℣. In hoc cognóvi quóniam voluísti me.
Nocturn 2 Versum.latR: ℟. Quóniam non gaudébit inimícus meus super me.
Nocturn 2 Versum.eng: ℣. By this I know that Thou favourest me.
Nocturn 2 Versum.engR: ℟. Because mine enemy cannot triumph over me.

Nocturn 3 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 3 Versum.lat: ℣. Exaltábo te, Dómine, quóniam suscepísti me.
Nocturn 3 Versum.latR: ℟. Nec delectásti inimícos meos super me.
Nocturn 3 Versum.eng: ℣. I will extol thee, O Lord, for Thou hast lifted me up.
Nocturn 3 Versum.engR: ℟. And hast not made my foes to rejoice over me.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui per immaculátam Vírginis Conceptiónem dignum Fílio tuo habitáculum præparásti: quǽsumus; ut qui ex morte ejúsdem Fílii tui prævísa, eam ab omni labe præservásti, nos quoque mundos ejus intercessióne ad te perveníre concédas.
Oratio.eng: O God, by the Immaculate Conception of the Virgin, thou prepared a worthy habitation for thy Son; we beseech thee, that, as by the foreseen death of thy same Son thou preserved her from all stain of sin, so thou would grant us also, through her intercession, to come to thee with pure hearts.

Responsory Breve Nona.label: Responsorium Breve
Responsory Breve Nona.lat:
℟.br. Exaltábo te, Dómine, * Quóniam suscepísti me.
℣. Nec delectásti inimícos meos super me.
℟. Quóniam suscepísti me.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Exaltábo te, Dómine, * Quóniam suscepísti me.
Responsory Breve Nona.eng:
℟.br. I will extol thee, O Lord, * for Thou hast lifted me up.
℣. And hast not made my foes to rejoice over me.
℟. Thou hast lifted me up.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. I will extol thee, O Lord, * for Thou hast lifted me up.

Responsory Breve Sexta.label: Responsorium Breve
Responsory Breve Sexta.lat:
℟.br. In hoc cognóvi, * Quóniam voluísti me.
℣. Quóniam non gaudébit inimícus meus super me.
℟. Quóniam voluísti me.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. In hoc cognóvi, * Quóniam voluísti me.
Responsory Breve Sexta.eng:
℟.br. By this I know that * Thou favourest me.
℣. Because mine enemy shall not triumph over me.
℟. Thou favourest me.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. By this I know that * Thou favourest me.

Responsory Breve Tertia.label: Responsorium Breve
Responsory Breve Tertia.lat:
℟.br. Deus omnípotens * Præcínxit me virtúte.
℣. Et pósuit immaculátam viam meam.
℟. Præcínxit me virtúte.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Deus omnípotens * Præcínxit me virtúte.
Responsory Breve Tertia.eng:
℟.br. It is Almighty God * That girdeth me with strength.
℣. And maketh my way perfect.
℟. That girdeth me with strength.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. It is Almighty God * That girdeth me with strength.

Versum 1.label: Versicle
Versum 1.lat: ℣. Immaculáta Concéptio est hódie sanctæ Maríæ Vírginis.
Versum 1.latR: ℟. Quæ serpéntis caput virgíneo pede contrívit.
Versum 1.eng: ℣. This day is the Holy Virgin Mary conceived without sin.
Versum 1.engR: ℟. The Virgin's foot hath bruised the serpent's head.

Versum 2.label: Versicle
Versum 2.lat: ℣. Immaculáta Concéptio est hódie sanctæ Maríæ Vírginis.
Versum 2.latR: ℟. Quæ serpéntis caput virgíneo pede contrívit.
Versum 2.eng: ℣. This day is the Holy Virgin Mary conceived without sin.
Versum 2.engR: ℟. The Virgin's foot hath bruised the serpent's head.

Versum 3.label: Versicle
Versum 3.lat: ℣. Immaculáta Concéptio est hódie sanctæ Maríæ Vírginis.
Versum 3.latR: ℟. Quæ serpéntis caput virgíneo pede contrívit.
Versum 3.eng: ℣. This day is the Holy Virgin Mary conceived without sin.
Versum 3.engR: ℟. The Virgin's foot hath bruised the serpent's head.

Versum Nona.label: Versicle
Versum Nona.lat: ℣. Immaculáta Concéptio tua, Dei Génetrix Virgo.
Versum Nona.eng: ℣. Maiden Mother of God, thy stainless conception.
Versum Nona.engR: ℟. Was a message of joy to the whole world.

Versum Sexta.label: Versicle
Versum Sexta.lat: ℣. Exaltábo te, Dómine, quóniam suscepísti me.
Versum Sexta.latR: ℟. Nec delectásti inimícos meos super me.
Versum Sexta.eng: ℣. I will extol thee, O Lord, for Thou hast lifted me up.
Versum Sexta.engR: ℟. And hast not made my foes to rejoice over me.

Versum Tertia.lat: ℣. In hoc cognóvi quóniam voluísti me.
Versum Tertia.latR: ℟. Quóniam non gaudébit inimícus meus super me.

Versum Tertia.engR: ℟. Because mine enemy cannot triumph over me.

Ant Laudes.ant: Tota pulchra * es, María, et mácula originális non est in te.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Thou art all fair, O Mary, * there is no spot of original sin in thee.

Ant Laudes.ant: Vestiméntum tuum * cándidum quasi nix, et fácies tua sicut sol.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Thy raiment * is white as snow, and thy countenance as the sun.

Ant Laudes.ant: Tu glória Jerúsalem, * tu lætítia Israël, tu honorificéntia pópuli nostri.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Thou art the exaltation of Jerusalem, * thou art the great glory of Israel, thou art the great rejoicing of our nation.

Ant Laudes.ant: Benedícta es tu, * Virgo María, a Dómino Deo excélso præ ómnibus muliéribus super terram.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Virgin Mary, * blessed art thou of the Most High God, above all the women upon the earth.

Ant Laudes.ant: Trahe nos, * Virgo immaculáta, post te currémus in odórem unguentórum tuórum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Draw us, * Maiden undefiled, we will run after thee in the odour of thy perfumes.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Admirábile est * nomen tuum, Dómine, in univérsa terra, quia in Vírgine María dignum tibi habitáculum præparásti.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O Lord, how excellent is thy Name * in all the earth, Who hast made thee a worthy tabernacle in the Virgin Mary.

Ant Matutinum.ant: In sole pósuit * Deus tabernáculum suum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord hath set * His tabernacle in the sun.

Ant Matutinum.ant: In Conceptióne sua * accépit María benedictiónem a Dómino, et misericórdiam a Deo salutári suo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Even in her Conception * did Mary receive a blessing from the Lord, and mercy from the God of her salvation.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Diffúsa est * grátia in Conceptióne ejus, et speciósa appáruit inter fílias hóminum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Grace is poured into her Conception, * and she is fairer than the daughters of men.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Adjúvit eam * Deus mane dilúculo; sanctificávit tabernáculum suum Altíssimus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: God hath holpen her right early, * the Most High hath hallowed His tabernacle.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Gloriósa * dicta sunt de te, cívitas Dei: fundávit te Dóminus in móntibus sanctis.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Glorious things are spoken of thee, O City of God; * the Lord hath laid thy foundation in the holy mountains.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Sanctimónia et magnificéntia * in Conceptióne ejus: annuntiáte in ómnibus pópulis glóriam ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Holiness and beauty are in her Conception; * declare her glory among all people.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Lætámini, omnes, * in Dómino: et confitémini memóriæ sanctitátis ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Rejoice ye all in the Lord * and give thanks at the remembrance of His holiness.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Notum fecit * Dóminus opus suum: in conspéctu géntium revelávit glóriam Genetrícis suæ.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord hath made known His salvation; * the glory of His Mother hath He openly showed in the sight of the heathen.

Ant Vespera.ant: Tota pulchra * es, María, et mácula originális non est in te.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Thou art all fair, O Mary, * there is no spot of original sin in thee.

Ant Vespera.ant: Vestiméntum tuum * cándidum quasi nix, et fácies tua sicut sol.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Thy raiment * is white as snow, and thy countenance as the sun.

Ant Vespera.ant: Tu glória Jerúsalem, * tu lætítia Israël, tu honorificéntia pópuli nostri.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Thou art the exaltation of Jerusalem, * thou art the great glory of Israel, thou art the great rejoicing of our nation.

Ant Vespera.ant: Benedícta es tu, * Virgo María, a Dómino Deo excélso præ ómnibus muliéribus super terram.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Virgin Mary, * blessed art thou of the Most High God, above all the women upon the earth.

Ant Vespera.ant: Trahe nos, * Virgo immaculáta, post te currémus in odórem unguentórum tuórum.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Draw us, * Maiden undefiled, we will run after thee in the odour of thy perfumes.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Gloriósæ * Vírginis Maríæ ortum digníssimum recolámus, quæ et Genitrícis dignitátem obtínuit, et virginálem pudicítiam non amísit.
Ant 1.eng: Let us tell again * of the right worthy Birth of the glorious Virgin Mary, who gained the honour of Motherhood without losing the guilelessness of a Maid.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Conceptionem hodiernam * perpetuæ Virginis Genitricis Dei Mariæ solemniter celebremus, qua celsitudo throni processit, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: Let us this day keep solemnly * the Conception of Mary, Mother but still Maiden, her Birth, a step toward the loftiness of her throne. Alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Conceptio tua, * Dei Genitrix Virgo, gaudium annuntiavit universo mundo: ex te enim ortus est sol justitiæ, Christus Deus noster: qui solvens maledictionem, dedit benedictionem, et confundens mortem, donavit nobis vitam sempiternam.
Ant 3.eng: Thy Birth * O Virgin Mother of God, was a message of joy to the whole world, for out of thee rose the Sun of righteousness, even Christ our God. Who hath taken away the curse and brought a blessing, confounded death, and given unto us everlasting life.

Ant Matutinum 12.label: Antiphon
Ant Matutinum 12.lat: Angelus Dómini * nuntiávit Maríæ, et concépit de Spíritu Sancto. (Allelúja.)
Ant Matutinum 12.eng: The Angel of the Lord * announced unto Mary, and she conceived of the Holy Spirit. (Alleluia.)

Invit.label: Antiphon
Invit.lat: Conceptionem Virginis Mariæ celebremus: * Christum ejus Filium adoremus Dominum.
Invit.eng: Let us keep the Birthday of the Virgin Mary. * Let us worship Christ, her Son, and her Lord and ours.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Famulis tuis, quǽsumus Domine, cælestis gratiæ munus impertire: ut quibus beatæ Virginis partus exstitit salutis exordium, Conceptionis ejus votiva solemnitas pacis tribuat incrementum.
Oratio.eng: Grant unto us thy servants, we beseech thee, O Lord, the gift of thy heavenly grace, unto whom Thou didst give the first sight of a Saviour as the offspring of a Blessed Virgin, and grant that this Feast, which they keep in honour of the same Virgin, may avail them unto the increase of peace.

Versum 1.label: Versicle
Versum 1.lat: ℣. Conceptio est hodie sanctæ Mariæ Virginis.
Versum 1.latR: ℟. Cujus vita inclyta cunctas illustrat ecclesias.
Versum 1.eng: ℣. This day is the Conception of the holy Virgin Mary.
Versum 1.engR: ℟. Whose' famous life still sheddeth lustre upon all the Churches.

Versum 2.label: Versicle
Versum 2.lat: ℣. Conceptio est hodie sanctæ Mariæ Virginis.
Versum 2.latR: ℟. Cujus vita inclyta cunctas illustrat ecclesias.
Versum 2.eng: ℣. This day is the Conception of the holy Virgin Mary.
Versum 2.engR: ℟. Whose' famous life still sheddeth lustre upon all the Churches.

Versum 3.label: Versicle
Versum 3.lat: ℣. Conceptio est hodie sanctæ Mariæ Virginis.
Versum 3.latR: ℟. Cujus vita inclyta cunctas illustrat ecclesias.
Versum 3.eng: ℣. This day is the Conception of the holy Virgin Mary.
Versum 3.engR: ℟. Whose' famous life still sheddeth lustre upon all the Churches.

Ant Laudes.ant: Conceptio gloriosæ Virginis Mariæ * ex semine Abrahæ, ortæ de tribu Juda, clara ex stirpe David.
Ant Laudes.antEng: This day was conceived the glorious Virgin Mary, * a child of the seed of Abraham, a daughter of the tribe of Judah, a Princess of the lineage of David.

Ant Laudes.ant: Conceptio est hodie * sanctæ Mariæ Virginis cujus vita inclyta cunctas illustrat ecclesias.
Ant Laudes.antEng: This day is the Conception of the holy Virgin Mary, * whose famous life still sheddeth lustre upon all the Churches.

Ant Laudes.ant: Regali ex progenie * Maria exorta refulget: cujus precibus nos adjuvari mente et spiritu devotissime poscimus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Mary was a maiden of illustrious birth, * the daughter of a Kingly race. We earnestly entreat her to help our minds and souls by her prayers.

Ant Laudes.ant: Corde et animo * Christo canamus gloriam in hac sacra solemnitate præcelsæ Genitricis Dei Mariæ.
Ant Laudes.antEng: With all our heart and with all our soul let us sing praise to Christ * on this the solemn Feast-day of Mary, the mighty Mother of God.

Ant Laudes.ant: Cum jucunditate * Conceptionem beatæ Mariæ celebremus, ut ipsa pro nobis intercedat ad Dominum Jesum Christum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Let us keep with rejoicing the Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary, * that she may pray for us to our Lord Jesus Christ.

Ant Vespera.ant: Conceptio gloriosæ Virginis Mariæ * ex semine Abrahæ, ortæ de tribu Juda, clara ex stirpe David.
Ant Vespera.antEng: This day was conceived the glorious Virgin Mary, * a child of the seed of Abraham, a daughter of the tribe of Judah, a Princess of the lineage of David.

Ant Vespera.ant: Conceptio est hodie * sanctæ Mariæ Virginis cujus vita inclyta cunctas illustrat ecclesias.
Ant Vespera.antEng: This day is the Conception of the holy Virgin Mary, * whose famous life still sheddeth lustre upon all the Churches.

Ant Vespera.ant: Regali ex progenie * Maria exorta refulget: cujus precibus nos adjuvari mente et spiritu devotissime poscimus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Mary was a maiden of illustrious birth, * the daughter of a Kingly race. We earnestly entreat her to help our minds and souls by her prayers.

Ant Vespera.ant: Corde et animo * Christo canamus gloriam in hac sacra solemnitate præcelsæ Genitricis Dei Mariæ.
Ant Vespera.antEng: With all our heart and with all our soul let us sing praise to Christ * on this the solemn Feast-day of Mary, the mighty Mother of God.

Ant Vespera.ant: Cum jucunditate * Conceptionem beatæ Mariæ celebremus, ut ipsa pro nobis intercedat ad Dominum Jesum Christum.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Let us keep with rejoicing the Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary, * that she may pray for us to our Lord Jesus Christ.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Elégi et sanctificávi locum istum; * Ut sit ibi nomen meum, et permáneant óculi mei, et cor meum ibi cunctis diébus.
Ant 1.eng: I have chosen and made holy this place * That my name may be there, and mine eyes, and my heart may remain there for all the days.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Quasi arcus * refúlgens inter nébulas glóriæ, et quasi flos rosárum in diébus vernis.
Ant 2.eng: As the rainbow * giving light in the bright clouds of glory, and as the flower of roses in the spring of the year.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Leva in circúitu * óculos tuos, et vide: omnes isti congregáti sunt, venérunt tibi: fílii tui de longe vénient, et fíliæ tuæ de látere surgent.
Ant 3.eng: Lift up thine eyes * round about, and see: all they gather themselves together, they come to thee: thy sons shall come from far, and thy daughters shall rise up at thy side.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Beátus homo qui audit me, et qui vígilat ad fores meas cotídie, et obsérvat ad postes óstii mei. Qui me invénerit, invéniet vitam, et háuriet salútem a Dómino.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Blessed is the man that heareth me, and that watcheth daily at my gates, and waiteth at the posts of my doors.He that shall find me, shall find life, and shall have salvation from the Lord.

Hymnus Laudes.label: Hymn
Hymnus Laudes.title: !Ex S. Anselmo Ep. Cantuariensi
Hymnus Laudes.lat:
!Ex S. Anselmo Ep. Cantuariensi
Alma Parens, omni carens
Corruptélæ mácula,
Quam elégit qui confrégit
Diræ mortis víncula.

Clemens! præsta, ut, qui festa
Tua gaudent cólere,
Gratuléntur et læténtur,
Veræ lucis lúmine.

Primum quidem nobis fidem
Tuis auge précibus,
Spe labéntes firma mentes,
Caritáte róbora.

Mater Dei! nostræ spei
Causa et exórdium,
Aufer bella et flagélla,
Famem, pestem, gládium.

Egenórum et vinctórum
Consoláre gémitum;
Fave votis, dans ægrótis
Optátum remédium.

Pax et quies nostros dies
Fáciant lætíssimos;
Inimícos fac amícos,
Seda malos hómines.

O María, Mater pia,
Tuum da subsídium,
Ut regnémus et laudémus
Tuum semper Fílium.

Pater Deus, Fili Deus,
Deus alme Spíritus,
Per ætérna nos gubérna
Sæcla, Deus Trínitas.
Amen.
Hymnus Laudes.eng:
!From St. Anselm, Bishop of Canterbury
Kindly Mother like no other
Free from all corrupting stain,
Thou he preferred who death deterred
Breaking all its bonds in twain.

Mercifully give us fully
To rejoice in true light's light,
We who cling to thy feasts bring to
Them joy that is meet and right.

May we receive grace to believe,
Pray too that faith's power soar,
And that fragile minds be agile,
Strengthen hope and love still more.

Themes of dirges, war and scourges,
Hunger, plagues and massacres,
Far be removed that thou be proved
Dawn of hope for sufferers.

Consolation 'gainst frustration
May sad hearts and fetters feel,
Answer the prayers, also the cares
That all sense thy pow'r to heal.

Friendly be foe while here below,
Evil-do'rs likewise subdue,
Bringing peaceful indeed gleeful
Times to gladden hearts anew.

By thy passion and compassion
Grant us help in all our needs
That forever reigning, never
Cease our lauds for thy Son's deeds.

Father true God and Son true God,
God the Holy Spirit too,
Trinity God, Unity God,
Rule forever, as is due. Amen.

Hymnus Matutinum.label: Hymn
Hymnus Matutinum.title: Præclára custos Vírginum
Hymnus Matutinum.lat:
Præclára custos Vírginum,
Intácta mater Núminis,
Cæléstis aulæ jánua,
Spes nostra, cæli gáudium,

Inter rubéta lílium,
Colúmba formosíssima,
Virga e radíce gérminans
Nostro medélam vúlneri.

Turris dracóni impérvia,
Amíca stella náufragis,
Tuére nos a fráudibus,
Tuáque luce dírige.

Erróris umbras díscute,
Syrtes dolósas ámove,
Fluctus tot inter, déviis
Tutam reclúde sémitam.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
Hymnus Matutinum.eng:
Blest guardian of all virgin souls,
Portal of bliss to man forgiven,
Pure Mother of Almighty God,
Thou hope of earth and joy of heaven!

Fair Lily found among the thorn,
Most beauteous Dove with wings of gold,
Rod from whose tender root upsprang
That healing Flower so long foretold

Thou Tower against the dragon proof,
Thou Star to stormtossed voyagers dear;
Our course lies o'er a treacherous deep,
thine be the light by which we steer.

Scatter the mists that round us hang;
Keep far the fatal shoals away;
And while through darkling waves we sweep,
Open a path to light and day.

O Jesu, born of Virgin bright,
Immortal glory be to thee;
Praise to the Father infinite
And Holy Ghost eternally.
Amen.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui sub beatíssimæ Vírginis Maríæ singulári patrocínio constitútos perpétuis benefíciis nos cumulári voluísti: præsta supplícibus tuis; ut, cujus hódie commemoratióne lætámur in terris, ejus conspéctu perfruámur in cælis.
Oratio.eng: O God, who hast placed us under the special patronage of the most Blessed Virgin Mary, and hast been pleased to shower perpetual blessings upon us: grant to Thy suppliants; that, as we are brought joy on earth by the commemoration today, we may enjoy her sight in heaven.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Quia vidísti me * Thoma, credidísti: beáti qui non vidérunt, et credidérunt, allelúja.
Ant 1.eng: Because thou hast seen me, * Thomas, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen and have believed, alleluia.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Quia vidísti me * Thoma, credidísti: beáti qui non vidérunt, et credidérunt, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: Because thou hast seen me, * Thomas, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen and have believed, alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Quia vidísti me * Thoma, credidísti: beáti qui non vidérunt, et credidérunt, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: Because thou hast seen me, * Thomas, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen and have believed, alleluia.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Da nobis, quǽsumus, Dómine, beáti Apóstoli tui Thomæ solemnitátibus gloriári: ut ejus semper et patrocíniis sublevémur; et fidem cóngrua devotióne sectémur.
Oratio.eng: Grant us, Lord, we beseech thee, to glory in the solemnity of thy blessed Apostle Thomas, that we may ever be aided by his patronage, and follow his faith with true devotion.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Oriétur * sicut sol Salvátor mundi: et descéndet in úterum Vírginis, sicut imber super gramen, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: The Saviour of the world * shall rise like the sun, and come down into the womb of the Virgin as the showers upon the grass. Alleluia.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Paulus servus Jesu Christi, vocátus Apóstolus, segregátus in Evangélium Dei, quod ante promíserat per prophétas suos in Scriptúris sanctis de Fílio suo, qui factus est ei ex sémine David secúndum carnem.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, separated unto the gospel of God, which he had promised before, by his prophets, in the holy scriptures concerning his Son, who was made to him of the seed of David, according to the flesh.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Per quem accépimus grátiam, et apostolátum ad obediéndum fídei in ómnibus géntibus pro nómine ejus, in quibus estis et vos vocáti Jesu Christi Dómini nostri.
Capitulum Nona.eng: By whom we have received grace and apostleship for obedience to the faith, in all nations, for his name, among whom are you also the called of Jesus Christ.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Qui prædestinátus est Fílius Dei in virtúte secúndum spíritum sanctificatiónis, ex resurrectióne mortuórum Jesu Christi Dómini nostri.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: Who was predestinated the Son of God in power, according to the spirit of sanctification, by the resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ from the dead.

Invit.label: Antiphon
Invit.lat: Hódie sciétis quia véniet Dóminus: * Et mane vidébitis glóriam ejus.
Invit.eng: This day ye shall know that the Lord cometh * and in the morning, then ye shall see His glory.

Lectio Prima.label: Lectio brevis
Lectio Prima.lat: Per quem accépimus grátiam, et apostolátum ad obediéndum fídei in ómnibus géntibus pro nómine ejus, in quibus estis et vos vocáti Jesu Christi Dómini nostri.
Lectio Prima.eng: By whom we have received grace and apostleship for obedience to the faith, in all nations, for his name, among whom are you also the called of Jesus Christ.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui nos redemptiónis nostræ ánnua exspectatióne lætíficas: præsta; ut Unigénitum tuum, quem Redemptórem læti suscípimus, veniéntem quoque Júdicem secúri videámus, Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum Fílium tuum:
Oratio.eng: O God, thou Who gladden us year after year with the expectation of our redemption, grant that we, who now welcome with joy thy only-begotten Son as our Redeemer, may also gaze upon Him without fear when He comes as our judge, our Lord Jesus Christ.

Responsory Breve Nona.lat:
℟.br. Crástina * Erit vobis salus.
℣. Dicit Dóminus Deus exercítuum.
℟. Erit vobis salus.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Crástina * Erit vobis salus.
Responsory Breve Nona.eng:
℟.br. On the morrow * Ye shall be saved.
℣. Saith the Lord God of hosts.
℟. Ye shall be saved.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. On the morrow * Ye shall be saved.

Responsory Breve Sexta.label: Responsorium Breve
Responsory Breve Sexta.lat:
℟.br. Crástina die * Delébitur iníquitas terræ.
℣. Et regnábit super nos Salvátor mundi.
℟. Delébitur iníquitas terræ.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Crástina die * Delébitur iníquitas terræ.
Responsory Breve Sexta.eng:
℟.br. On the morrow * the sins of the earth shall be washed away.
℣. And the Saviour of the world will be our King.
℟. The sins of the earth shall be washed away.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. On the morrow * the sins of the earth shall be washed away.

Responsory Breve Tertia.label: Responsorium Breve

℟.br. Hódie sciétis * Quia véniet Dóminus.
℣. Et mane vidébitis glóriam ejus.

Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Hódie sciétis * Quia véniet Dóminus.

℟.br. This day ye shall know * That the Lord cometh.
℣. And in the morning, then ye shall see His glory.
℟. That the Lord cometh.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. This day ye shall know * That the Lord cometh.

Ant 1.eng: When the sun shall have risen * from heaven, ye shall see the King of kings proceeding from the Father, as a bridegroom from his chamber.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Glória in excélsis Deo, * et in terra pax homínibus bonæ voluntátis, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: Glory be to God in the highest; * and on earth, peace to men of good will, alleluia, alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Hódie * Christus natus est: hódie Salvátor appáruit: hódie in terra canunt Angeli, lætántur Archángeli: hódie exsúltant justi, dicéntes: Glória in excélsis Deo, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: This day the Christ is born this day the Saviour is appeared; * this day the Angels sing praise in the earth and the Archangels rejoice; this day the righteous are glad and say: Glory to God in the highest. Alleluia.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Multifáriam, multísque modis olim Deus loquens pátribus in prophétis: novíssime diébus istis locútus est nobis in Fílio, quem constítuit herédem universórum, per quem fecit et sǽcula.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: God, who, at sundry times and in diverse manners, spoke in times past to the fathers by the prophets, last of all, in these days hath spoken to us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the world.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Ipsi períbunt, tu autem permanébis; et omnes sicut vestiméntum veteráscent: et velut amíctum mutábis eos, et mutabúntur: tu autem idem ipse es, et anni tui non defícient.
Capitulum Nona.eng: They shall perish, but thou shalt continue: and they shall all grow old as a garment. And as a vesture shalt thou change them, and they shall be changed: but thou art the selfsame, and thy years shall not fail.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Et: Tu in princípio, Dómine, terram fundásti: et ópera mánuum tuárum sunt cæli.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: And: Thou in the beginning, O Lord, didst found the earth: and the works of thy hands are the heavens.

Capitulum Vespera 1.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Vespera 1.lat: Appáruit benígnitas, et humánitas Salvatóris nostri Dei: non ex opéribus justítiæ, quæ fécimus nos, sed secúndum suam misericórdiam salvos nos fecit.
Capitulum Vespera 1.eng: But when the goodness and kindness of God our Saviour appeared: Not by the works of justice, which we have done, but according to his mercy, he saved us.

Capitulum Vespera 3.label: Capitulum

Hymnus Laudes.label: Hymn
Hymnus Laudes.title: A solis ortus cárdine
Hymnus Laudes.lat:
A solis ortus cárdine
Ad usque terræ límitem,
Christum canámus Príncipem,
Natum María Vírgine.

Beátus auctor sǽculi
Servíle corpus índuit:
Ut carne carnem líberans,
Ne pérderet quos cóndidit.

Castæ Paréntis víscera
Cæléstis intrat grátia:
Venter Puéllæ bájulat
Secréta, quæ non nóverat.

Domus pudíci péctoris
Templum repénte fit Dei:
Intácta nésciens virum,
Concépit alvo Fílium.

Enítitur puérpera,
Quem Gábriel prædíxerat,
Quem ventre Matris géstiens,
Baptísta clausum sénserat.

Fœno jacére pértulit:
Præsépe non abhórruit:
Et lacte módico pastus est,
Per quem nec ales ésurit.

Gaudet chorus cæléstium,
Et Angeli canunt Deo;
Palámque fit pastóribus
Pastor, Creátor ómnium.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
Hymnus Laudes.eng:
From lands that see the sun arise
To earth's remotest boundaries,
The Virgin-born today we sing,
The Son of Mary, Christ the King.

Blest Author of this earthly frame,
To take a servant's form He came,
That, liberating flesh by flesh,
Whom He had made might live afresh.

In that chaste parent's holy womb
Celestial grace hath found its home;
And she, as earthly bride unknown,
Yet calls that Offspring blest her own.

The mansion of the modest breast
Becomes a shrine where God shall rest:
The pure and undefilèd one
Conceived in her womb the Son.

That Son, that Royal Son she bore,
Whom Gabriel's voice had told afore;
Whom, in His mother yet concealed,
The infant Baptist had revealed.

The manger and the straw He bore,
The cradle did He not abhor;
By milk in infant portions fed,
Who gives e'en fowls their daily bread.

The heavenly chorus filled the sky,
The Angels sang to God on high,
What time to shepherds, watching lone,
They made creation's Shepherd known.

All honor, laud, and glory be,
O Jesu, Virgin-born to thee:
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.

Hymnus Matutinum.label: Hymn
Hymnus Matutinum.title: Jesu, Redémptor ómnium
Hymnus Matutinum.lat:
Jesu, Redémptor ómnium,
Quem lucis ante oríginem
Parem patérnæ glóriæ
Pater suprémus édidit.

Tu lumen, et splendor Patris,
Tu spes perénnis ómnium,
Inténde quas fundunt preces
Tui per orbem sérvuli.

Meménto, rerum Cónditor,
Nostri quod olim córporis,
Sacráta ab alvo Vírginis
Nascéndo, formam súmpseris.

Testátur hoc præsens dies,
Currens per anni círculum,
Quod solus e sinu Patris
Mundi salus advéneris.

Hunc astra, tellus, ǽquora,
Hunc omne, quod cælo subest,
Salútis auctórem novæ
Novo salútat cántico.

Et nos, beáta quos sacri
Rigávit unda sánguinis,
Natális ob diem tui
Hymni tribútum sólvimus.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
Hymnus Matutinum.eng:
Jesus, the Ransomer of man,
Who, ere created light began,
Didst from the sovereign Father spring,
His power and glory equalling.

The Father’s Light and Splendor Thou,
Their endless hope to Thee that bow;
Accept the prayers and praise to-day
That through the world Thy servants pay.

Salvation’s Author, call to mind
How, taking form of humankind,
Born of a Virgin undefiled,
Thou in man’s flesh becam’st a Child.

Thus testifies the present day,
Through every year in long array,
That Thou, salvation’s source alone,
Proceedest from the Father’s throne.

The heavens above, the rolling main
And all that earth’s wide realms contain,
With joyous voice now loudly sing
The glory of their new-born King.

And we who, by Thy precious Blood
From sin redeemed, are marked for God,
On this the day that saw Thy birth,
Sing the new song of ransomed earth.

O Lord, the Virgin-born, to Thee
Eternal praise and glory be,
Whom with the Father we adore
And Holy Ghost forevermore.
Amen.

Invit.lat: Christus natus est nobis: * Veníte, adorémus.
Invit.eng: Unto us a Christ is born, * O come, let us worship Him.

Lectio Prima.label: Lectio brevis
Lectio Prima.lat: Ipsi períbunt, tu autem permanébis; et omnes sicut vestiméntum veteráscent: et velut amíctum mutábis eos, et mutabúntur: tu autem idem ipse es, et anni tui non defícient.
Lectio Prima.eng: They shall perish, but thou shalt continue: and they shall all grow old as a garment. And as a vesture shalt thou change them, and they shall be changed: but thou art the selfsame, and thy years shall not fail.

Ant Laudes.ant: Quem vidístis, * pastóres? dícite, annuntiáte nobis, in terris quis appáruit? Natum vídimus, et choros Angelórum collaudántes Dóminum, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O ye shepherds, speak, * and tell us what ye have seen; who is appeared in the earth? We saw the newborn Child, and angels singing praise to the Lord, alleluia, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Génuit puérpera * Regem, cui nomen ætérnum, et gáudia matris habens cum virginitátis honóre: nec primam símilem visa est, nec habére sequéntem, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Mother brought forth the King, * Whose name is called The Eternal; the joy of a Mother was hers, remaining a Virgin unsullied; neither before nor henceforth hath there been or shall be such another, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Angelus ad pastóres * ait: Annúntio vobis gáudium magnum: quia natus est vobis hódie Salvátor mundi, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Angel said unto the shepherds * I bring you good tidings of great joy; for unto you is born this day a Saviour of the world, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Facta est cum Angelo * multitúdo cæléstis exércitus laudántium Deum, et dicéntium: Glória in excélsis Deo, et in terra pax homínibus bonæ voluntátis, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: There was with the Angel a multitude of the heavenly host, * praising God, and saying Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, to men of good will, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Párvulus fílius * hódie natus est nobis: et vocábitur Deus, Fortis, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Unto us this day a little Child is born, * and His name shall be called the Mighty God, alleluia, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dóminus dixit * ad me: Fílius meus es tu, ego hódie génui te.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord hath said unto Me: * Thou art My Son, this day have I begotten thee.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Tamquam sponsus * Dóminus procédens de thálamo suo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord is as a bridegroom * coming out of his chamber.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Diffúsa est * grátia in lábiis tuis, proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Grace is poured into thy lips, * therefore God hath blessed thee for ever.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Suscépimus, * Deus, misericórdiam tuam in médio templi tui.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: We have drunk in thy loving-kindness, * O God, in the midst of thy temple.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Oriétur * in diébus Dómini abundántia pacis, et dominábitur.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: In the Lord's days * shall abundance of peace arise and flourish.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Véritas de terra * orta est, et justítia de cælo prospéxit.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Truth is sprung out of the earth, * and righteousness hath looked down from heaven.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ipse invocábit * me, allelúja: Pater meus es tu, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: He shall cry unto Me, alleluia, * Thou art My Father, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Læténtur cæli, * et exsúltet terra ante fáciem Dómini, quóniam venit.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Let the heavens rejoice, * and let the earth be glad before the Lord, for He cometh.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Notum fecit * Dóminus, allelúja, salutáre suum, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord hath made known, alleluia, * His salvation, alleluia.

Ant Vespera.ant: Rex pacíficus * magnificátus est, cujus vultum desíderat univérsa terra.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The King of Peace * is magnified, whose face the whole earth desireth.

Ant Vespera.ant: Magnificátus est * Rex pacíficus super omnes reges univérsæ terræ.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The Peaceful King * exceeded all the kings of the whole earth.

Ant Vespera.ant: Compléti sunt * dies Maríæ, ut páreret Fílium suum primogénitum.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The days of Mary * were accomplished that she should bring forth her first-born Son.

Ant Vespera.ant: Scitóte * quia prope est regnum Dei: amen dico vobis, quia non tardábit.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Know ye that the kingdom * of God is at hand? Amen, I say unto you, it will not tarry.

Ant Vespera.ant: Leváte cápita vestra: * ecce appropínquat redémptio vestra.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Lift up your heads; * behold, your redemption draweth nigh.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Tecum princípium * in die virtútis tuæ, in splendóribus sanctórum, ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: Thine shall be the dominion * in the day of thy power, amid the brightness of the saints, from the womb, before the day-star, have I begotten thee.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Redemptiónem * misit Dóminus pópulo suo: mandávit in ætérnum testaméntum suum.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: The Lord sent redemption * unto His people, He hath commanded His covenant for ever.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Exórtum est * in ténebris lumen rectis corde: miséricors, et miserátor, et justus Dóminus.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: Unto the upright there ariseth * light in the darkness; the Lord is gracious, and full of compassion, and righteous.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Apud Dóminum * misericórdia, et copiósa apud eum redémptio.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: With the Lord * there is mercy, and with Him is plenteous redemption.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: De fructu * ventris tui ponam super sedem tuam.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: Of the fruit * of thy body will I set upon thy throne.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Cum ortus fúerit * sol de cælo, vidébitis Regem regum procedéntem a Patre, tamquam sponsum de thálamo suo.
Ant 1.eng: When the sun shall have risen * from heaven, ye shall see the King of kings proceeding from the Father, as a bridegroom from his chamber.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Glória in excélsis Deo, * et in terra pax homínibus bonæ voluntátis, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: Glory be to God in the highest; * and on earth, peace to men of good will, alleluia, alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Hódie * Christus natus est: hódie Salvátor appáruit: hódie in terra canunt Angeli, lætántur Archángeli: hódie exsúltant justi, dicéntes: Glória in excélsis Deo, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: This day the Christ is born this day the Saviour is appeared; * this day the Angels sing praise in the earth and the Archangels rejoice; this day the righteous are glad and say: Glory to God in the highest. Alleluia.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Multifáriam, multísque modis olim Deus loquens pátribus in prophétis: novíssime diébus istis locútus est nobis in Fílio, quem constítuit herédem universórum, per quem fecit et sǽcula.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: God, who, at sundry times and in diverse manners, spoke in times past to the fathers by the prophets, last of all, in these days hath spoken to us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the world.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Ipsi períbunt, tu autem permanébis; et omnes sicut vestiméntum veteráscent: et velut amíctum mutábis eos, et mutabúntur: tu autem idem ipse es, et anni tui non defícient.
Capitulum Nona.eng: They shall perish, but thou shalt continue: and they shall all grow old as a garment. And as a vesture shalt thou change them, and they shall be changed: but thou art the selfsame, and thy years shall not fail.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Et: Tu in princípio, Dómine, terram fundásti: et ópera mánuum tuárum sunt cæli.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: And: Thou in the beginning, O Lord, didst found the earth: and the works of thy hands are the heavens.

Capitulum Vespera 1.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Vespera 1.lat: Appáruit benígnitas, et humánitas Salvatóris nostri Dei: non ex opéribus justítiæ, quæ fécimus nos, sed secúndum suam misericórdiam salvos nos fecit.
Capitulum Vespera 1.eng: But when the goodness and kindness of God our Saviour appeared: Not by the works of justice, which we have done, but according to his mercy, he saved us.

Capitulum Vespera 3.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Vespera 3.lat: Multifáriam, multísque modis olim Deus loquens pátribus in prophétis: novíssime diébus istis locútus est nobis in Fílio, quem constítuit herédem universórum, per quem fecit et sǽcula.
Capitulum Vespera 3.eng: God, who, at sundry times and in diverse manners, spoke in times past to the fathers by the prophets, last of all, in these days hath spoken to us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the world.

Hymnus Laudes.label: Hymn
Hymnus Laudes.title: A solis ortus cárdine
Hymnus Laudes.lat:
A solis ortus cárdine
Ad usque terræ límitem,
Christum canámus Príncipem,
Natum María Vírgine.

Beátus auctor sǽculi
Servíle corpus índuit:
Ut carne carnem líberans,
Ne pérderet quos cóndidit.

Castæ Paréntis víscera
Cæléstis intrat grátia:
Venter Puéllæ bájulat
Secréta, quæ non nóverat.

Domus pudíci péctoris
Templum repénte fit Dei:
Intácta nésciens virum,
Concépit alvo Fílium.

Enítitur puérpera,
Quem Gábriel prædíxerat,
Quem ventre Matris géstiens,
Baptísta clausum sénserat.

Fœno jacére pértulit:
Præsépe non abhórruit:
Et lacte módico pastus est,
Per quem nec ales ésurit.

Gaudet chorus cæléstium,
Et Angeli canunt Deo;
Palámque fit pastóribus
Pastor, Creátor ómnium.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
Hymnus Laudes.eng:
From lands that see the sun arise
To earth's remotest boundaries,
The Virgin-born today we sing,
The Son of Mary, Christ the King.

Blest Author of this earthly frame,
To take a servant's form He came,
That, liberating flesh by flesh,
Whom He had made might live afresh.

In that chaste parent's holy womb
Celestial grace hath found its home;
And she, as earthly bride unknown,
Yet calls that Offspring blest her own.

The mansion of the modest breast
Becomes a shrine where God shall rest:
The pure and undefilèd one
Conceived in her womb the Son.

That Son, that Royal Son she bore,
Whom Gabriel's voice had told afore;
Whom, in His mother yet concealed,
The infant Baptist had revealed.

The manger and the straw He bore,
The cradle did He not abhor;
By milk in infant portions fed,
Who gives e'en fowls their daily bread.

The heavenly chorus filled the sky,
The Angels sang to God on high,
What time to shepherds, watching lone,
They made creation's Shepherd known.

All honor, laud, and glory be,
O Jesu, Virgin-born to thee:
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.

Hymnus Matutinum.label: Hymn
Hymnus Matutinum.title: Jesu, Redémptor ómnium
Hymnus Matutinum.lat:
Jesu, Redémptor ómnium,
Quem lucis ante oríginem
Parem patérnæ glóriæ
Pater suprémus édidit.

Tu lumen, et splendor Patris,
Tu spes perénnis ómnium,
Inténde quas fundunt preces
Tui per orbem sérvuli.

Meménto, rerum Cónditor,
Nostri quod olim córporis,
Sacráta ab alvo Vírginis
Nascéndo, formam súmpseris.

Testátur hoc præsens dies,
Currens per anni círculum,
Quod solus e sinu Patris
Mundi salus advéneris.

Hunc astra, tellus, ǽquora,
Hunc omne, quod cælo subest,
Salútis auctórem novæ
Novo salútat cántico.

Et nos, beáta quos sacri
Rigávit unda sánguinis,
Natális ob diem tui
Hymni tribútum sólvimus.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
Hymnus Matutinum.eng:
Jesus, the Ransomer of man,
Who, ere created light began,
Didst from the sovereign Father spring,
His power and glory equalling.

The Father’s Light and Splendor Thou,
Their endless hope to Thee that bow;
Accept the prayers and praise to-day
That through the world Thy servants pay.

Salvation’s Author, call to mind
How, taking form of humankind,
Born of a Virgin undefiled,
Thou in man’s flesh becam’st a Child.

Thus testifies the present day,
Through every year in long array,
That Thou, salvation’s source alone,
Proceedest from the Father’s throne.

The heavens above, the rolling main
And all that earth’s wide realms contain,
With joyous voice now loudly sing
The glory of their new-born King.

And we who, by Thy precious Blood
From sin redeemed, are marked for God,
On this the day that saw Thy birth,
Sing the new song of ransomed earth.

O Lord, the Virgin-born, to Thee
Eternal praise and glory be,
Whom with the Father we adore
And Holy Ghost forevermore.
Amen.

Invit.label: Antiphon
Invit.lat: Christus natus est nobis: * Veníte, adorémus.
Invit.eng: Unto us a Christ is born, * O come, let us worship Him.

Lectio Prima.label: Lectio brevis
Lectio Prima.lat: Ipsi períbunt, tu autem permanébis; et omnes sicut vestiméntum veteráscent: et velut amíctum mutábis eos, et mutabúntur: tu autem idem ipse es, et anni tui non defícient.
Lectio Prima.eng: They shall perish, but thou shalt continue: and they shall all grow old as a garment. And as a vesture shalt thou change them, and they shall be changed: but thou art the selfsame, and thy years shall not fail.

!Commemoratio Octavæ Nativitatis
Ant. Hódie Christus natus est: hódie Salvátor appáruit: hódie in terra canunt Angeli, lætántur Archángeli: hódie exsúltant justi, dicéntes: Glória in excélsis Deo, allelúja.
_

R. Salutáre suum, allelúja.
_

v. Concéde, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut nos Unigéniti tui nova per carnem Natívitas líberet; quos sub peccáti jugo vetústa sérvitus tenet.

Ant Laudes.ant: Quem vidístis, * pastóres? dícite, annuntiáte nobis, in terris quis appáruit? Natum vídimus, et choros Angelórum collaudántes Dóminum, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O ye shepherds, speak, * and tell us what ye have seen; who is appeared in the earth? We saw the newborn Child, and angels singing praise to the Lord, alleluia, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Génuit puérpera * Regem, cui nomen ætérnum, et gáudia matris habens cum virginitátis honóre: nec primam símilem visa est, nec habére sequéntem, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Mother brought forth the King, * Whose name is called The Eternal; the joy of a Mother was hers, remaining a Virgin unsullied; neither before nor henceforth hath there been or shall be such another, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Angelus ad pastóres * ait: Annúntio vobis gáudium magnum: quia natus est vobis hódie Salvátor mundi, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Angel said unto the shepherds * I bring you good tidings of great joy; for unto you is born this day a Saviour of the world, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Facta est cum Angelo * multitúdo cæléstis exércitus laudántium Deum, et dicéntium: Glória in excélsis Deo, et in terra pax homínibus bonæ voluntátis, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: There was with the Angel a multitude of the heavenly host, * praising God, and saying Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, to men of good will, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Párvulus fílius * hódie natus est nobis: et vocábitur Deus, Fortis, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Unto us this day a little Child is born, * and His name shall be called the Mighty God, alleluia, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dóminus dixit * ad me: Fílius meus es tu, ego hódie génui te.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord hath said unto Me: * Thou art My Son, this day have I begotten thee.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Tamquam sponsus * Dóminus procédens de thálamo suo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord is as a bridegroom * coming out of his chamber.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Diffúsa est * grátia in lábiis tuis, proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Grace is poured into thy lips, * therefore God hath blessed thee for ever.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Suscépimus, * Deus, misericórdiam tuam in médio templi tui.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: We have drunk in thy loving-kindness, * O God, in the midst of thy temple.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Oriétur * in diébus Dómini abundántia pacis, et dominábitur.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: In the Lord's days * shall abundance of peace arise and flourish.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Véritas de terra * orta est, et justítia de cælo prospéxit.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Truth is sprung out of the earth, * and righteousness hath looked down from heaven.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ipse invocábit * me, allelúja: Pater meus es tu, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: He shall cry unto Me, alleluia, * Thou art My Father, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Læténtur cæli, * et exsúltet terra ante fáciem Dómini, quóniam venit.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Let the heavens rejoice, * and let the earth be glad before the Lord, for He cometh.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Notum fecit * Dóminus, allelúja, salutáre suum, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord hath made known, alleluia, * His salvation, alleluia.

Ant Vespera.ant: Rex pacíficus * magnificátus est, cujus vultum desíderat univérsa terra.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The King of Peace * is magnified, whose face the whole earth desireth.

Ant Vespera.ant: Magnificátus est * Rex pacíficus super omnes reges univérsæ terræ.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The Peaceful King * exceeded all the kings of the whole earth.

Ant Vespera.ant: Compléti sunt * dies Maríæ, ut páreret Fílium suum primogénitum.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The days of Mary * were accomplished that she should bring forth her first-born Son.

Ant Vespera.ant: Scitóte * quia prope est regnum Dei: amen dico vobis, quia non tardábit.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Know ye that the kingdom * of God is at hand? Amen, I say unto you, it will not tarry.

Ant Vespera.ant: Leváte cápita vestra: * ecce appropínquat redémptio vestra.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Lift up your heads; * behold, your redemption draweth nigh.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Tecum princípium * in die virtútis tuæ, in splendóribus sanctórum, ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: Thine shall be the dominion * in the day of thy power, amid the brightness of the saints, from the womb, before the day-star, have I begotten thee.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Redemptiónem * misit Dóminus pópulo suo: mandávit in ætérnum testaméntum suum.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: The Lord sent redemption * unto His people, He hath commanded His covenant for ever.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Exórtum est * in ténebris lumen rectis corde: miséricors, et miserátor, et justus Dóminus.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: Unto the upright there ariseth * light in the darkness; the Lord is gracious, and full of compassion, and righteous.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Apud Dóminum * misericórdia, et copiósa apud eum redémptio.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: With the Lord * there is mercy, and with Him is plenteous redemption.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: De fructu * ventris tui ponam super sedem tuam.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: Of the fruit * of thy body will I set upon thy throne.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Stéphanus autem * plenus grátia et fortitúdine, faciébat signa magna in pópulo.
Ant 1.eng: And Stephen, full of grace * and fortitude, did great signs among the people.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Stéphanus autem * plenus grátia et fortitúdine, faciébat signa magna in pópulo.
Ant 2.eng: And Stephen, full of grace * and fortitude, did great signs among the people.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Sepeliérunt Stéphanum * viri timoráti, et fecérunt planctum magnum super eum.
Ant 3.eng: Devout men buried Stephen * And made great mourning over him.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Stéphanus autem plenus grátia et fortitúdine, faciébat prodígia et signa magna in pópulo.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: And Stephen, full of grace and fortitude, did great wonders and signs among the people.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Pósitis autem génibus, clamávit voce magna, dicens: Dómine, ne státuas illis hoc peccátum. Et cum hoc dixísset, obdormívit in Dómino.
Capitulum Nona.eng: And falling on his knees, he cried with a loud voice, saying: Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleep in the Lord. And Saul was consenting to his death.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Surrexérunt autem quidam de synagóga, quæ appellátur Libertinórum, et Cyrenénsium, et Alexandrinórum, et eórum qui erant a Cilícia, et Asia, disputántes cum Stéphano: et non póterant resístere sapiéntiæ, et Spirítui qui loquebátur.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: Now there arose some of that which is called the synagogue of the Libertines, and of the Cyrenians, and of the Alexandrians, and of them that were of Cilicia and Asia, disputing with Stephen. And they were not able to resist the wisdom and the spirit that spoke.

Invit.label: Antiphon
Invit.lat: Christum natum, qui beátum hódie coronávit Stéphanum, * Veníte, adorémus.
Invit.eng: He That once a little Child, Shivering in the manger lay, Set on Stephen's blessed head, A crown that fadeth not away; * O come, let us worship Him!

Lectio Prima.label: Lectio brevis
Lectio Prima.lat: Pósitis autem génibus, clamávit voce magna, dicens: Dómine, ne státuas illis hoc peccátum. Et cum hoc dixísset, obdormívit in Dómino.
Lectio Prima.eng: And falling on his knees, he cried with a loud voice, saying: Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleep in the Lord. And Saul was consenting to his death.

Octava 1.label: Commemoratio
Octava 1.lat:
!Commemoratio Octavæ S. Stephani
Ant. Sepeliérunt Stéphanum viri timoráti, et fecérunt planctum magnum super eum.
_
V. Stéphanus vidit cælos apértos.
R. Vidit, et introívit: beátus homo, cui cæli patébant.
_
$Oremus
v. Da nobis, quǽsumus, Dómine, imitári quod cólimus: ut discámus et inimícos dilígere; quia ejus natalícia celebrámus, qui novit étiam pro persecutóribus exoráre Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum Fílium tuum:
$Qui tecum
Octava 1.eng:
!Commemoration of the Octave of St. Stephen
Ant. Devout men buried Stephen * And made great mourning over him.
_
V. Stephen saw the heavens opened:
R. He saw and entered: blessed man, to whom the heavens were opened.
_
$Oremus.
Grant us, we beseech thee, O Lord, so to imitate what we revere, that we may learn to love even our enemies; for we celebrate the heavenly birthday of him who knew how to pray for his very persecutors to our Lord:
$Qui tecum

Octava 2.label: Commemoratio
Octava 2.lat:
!Commemoratio Octavæ S. Stephani
Ant. Stéphanus autem plenus grátia et fortitúdine, faciébat signa magna in pópulo.
_
V. Sepeliérunt Stéphanum viri timoráti.
R. Et fecérunt planctum magnum super eum.
_
$Oremus
v. Da nobis, quǽsumus, Dómine, imitári quod cólimus: ut discámus et inimícos dilígere; quia ejus natalícia celebrámus, qui novit étiam pro persecutóribus exoráre Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum Fílium tuum:
$Qui tecum
Octava 2.eng:
