Versum 1.label: Versicle
Versum 1.lat: ℣. Glória et honóre coronásti eum, Dómine.
Versum 1.latR: ℟. Et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.
Versum 1.eng: ℣. Thou hast crowned him with glory and honour, O Lord.
Versum 1.engR: ℟. And madest him to have dominion over the works of thy hands.

Versum 2.label: Versicle
Versum 2.latR: ℟. Et fecérunt planctum magnum super eum.
Versum 2.eng: ℣. Devout men buried Stephen.
Versum 2.engR: ℟. And made great mourning over him.

Versum 3.label: Versicle
Versum 3.lat: ℣. Stéphanus vidit cælos apértos.
Versum 3.latR: ℟. Vidit, et introívit: beátus homo, cui cæli patébant.
Versum 3.eng: ℣. Stephen saw the heavens opened.
Versum 3.engR: ℟. He saw and entered: blessed man, to whom the heavens were opened.

Ant Laudes.ant: Lapidavérunt Stéphanum, * et ipse invocábat Dóminum, dicens: Ne státuas illis hoc peccátum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: They stoned Stephen, * calling upon God, and saying: Lay not this sin to their charge.

Ant Laudes.ant: Lápides torréntis * illi dulces fuérunt: ipsum sequúntur omnes ánimæ justæ.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The stones of the brook * were sweet to him; all the souls of the righteous follow him.

Ant Laudes.ant: Adhǽsit ánima mea * post te, quia caro mea lapidáta est pro te, Deus meus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O my God, my soul followeth hard after thee, * for my flesh hath been stoned for thy sake.

Ant Laudes.ant: Stéphanus vidit * cælos apértos, vidit, et introívit: beátus homo, cui cæli patébant.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Stephen saw the heavens opened; * he saw and entered in; blessed is he unto whom the heavens were opened.

Ant Laudes.ant: Ecce vídeo * cælos apértos, et Jesum stantem a dextris virtútis Dei.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Behold, I see * the heavens opened, and Jesus standing on the right hand of the power of God.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Tecum princípium * in die virtútis tuæ, in splendóribus sanctórum, ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: Thine shall be the dominion * in the day of thy power, amid the brightness of the saints, from the womb, before the day-star, have I begotten thee.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Redemptiónem * misit Dóminus pópulo suo: mandávit in ætérnum testaméntum suum.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: The Lord sent redemption * unto His people, He hath commanded His covenant for ever.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Exórtum est * in ténebris lumen rectis corde: miséricors, et miserátor, et justus Dóminus.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: Unto the upright there ariseth * light in the darkness; the Lord is gracious, and full of compassion, and righteous.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Apud Dóminum * misericórdia, et copiósa apud eum redémptio.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: With the Lord * there is mercy, and with Him is plenteous redemption.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: De fructu * ventris tui ponam super sedem tuam.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: Of the fruit * of thy body will I set upon thy throne.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Iste est Joánnes, * qui supra pectus Dómini in cena recúbuit: beátus Apóstolus, cui reveláta sunt secréta cæléstia.
Ant 1.eng: This is John * who leaned at supper on the bosom of the Lord. Blessed Apostle, to whom heavenly secrets were revealed.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Iste est Joánnes, * qui supra pectus Dómini in cena recúbuit: beátus Apóstolus, cui reveláta sunt secréta cæléstia.
Ant 2.eng: This is John * who leaned at supper on the bosom of the Lord. Blessed Apostle, to whom heavenly secrets were revealed.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Exiit * sermo inter fratres, quod discípulus ille non móritur; et non dixit Jesus, Non móritur: sed, Sic eum volo manére, donec véniam.
Ant 3.eng: A saying * went abroad among the brethren, that that disciple should not die; and Jesus did not say that he should not die, but so will I have him remain till I come.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Qui timet Deum, fáciet bona: et qui cóntinens est justítiæ, apprehéndet illam, et obviábit illi quasi mater honorificáta.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: He that feareth God, will do good: and he that possesseth justice, shall lay hold on her, and she will meet him as an honourable mother.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: In médio Ecclésiæ apéruit os ejus, et implévit illum Dóminus spíritu sapiéntiæ et intelléctus, et stolam glóriæ índuit eum.
Capitulum Nona.eng: And in the midst of the church she shall open his mouth, and shall fill him with the spirit of wisdom and understanding, and shall clothe him with a robe of glory.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Cibávit illum pane vitæ et intelléctus, et aqua sapiéntiæ salutáris potávit illum Dóminus, Deus noster.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: With the bread of life and understanding, she shall feed him, and give him the water of wholesome wisdom to drink; God, our Lord.

Lectio Prima.label: Lectio brevis

Lectio Prima.eng: And in the midst of the church she shall open his mouth, and shall fill him with the spirit of wisdom and understanding, and shall clothe him with a robe of glory.

Hymnus Laudes.label: Hymn
Hymnus Laudes.title: Salvéte, flores Mártyrum
Hymnus Laudes.lat:
Salvéte, flores Mártyrum,
Quos lucis ipso in límine
Christi insecútor sústulit,
Ceu turbo nascéntes rosas.

Vos prima Christi víctima,
Grex immolatórum tener,
Aram sub ipsam símplices
Palma et corónis lúditis.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
Hymnus Laudes.eng:
All hail, ye little Martyr flowers,
Sweet rosebuds cut in dawning hours!
When Herod sought the Christ to find
Ye fell as bloom before the wind.

First victims of the Martyr bands,
With crowns and palms in tender hands,
Around the very altar, gay
And innocent, ye seem to play.

All honor, laud, and glory be,
O Jesu, Virgin-born to thee;
All glory, as is ever meet
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.

Hymnus Matutinum.label: Hymn
Hymnus Matutinum.title: Audit tyránnus ánxius
Hymnus Matutinum.lat:
Audit tyránnus ánxius
Adésse regum Príncipem,
Qui nomen Israël regat,
Teneátque David régiam.

Exclámat amens núntio:
Succéssor instat, péllimur:
Satélles, i, ferrum rape,
Perfúnde cunas sánguine.

Quid próficit tantum nefas?
Quid crimen Heródem juvat?
Unus tot inter fúnera
Impúne Christus tóllitur.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
Hymnus Matutinum.eng:
With terror doth the tyrant hear
The King of kings hath come to dwell
Where David's court shall widely rear
A sceptered reign o'er Israel.

Then cries out, raging, at the word:
“He comes to stand where we have stood:
Hence, soldier, and with ruthless sword
Deluge the cradles deep with blood!”

What profiteth a crime so dread?
What hope shall Herod's bosom sway?
Alone amidst the thronging dead,
The Christ is safely borne away!

All glory for this blessed morn
To God the Father ever be;
All praise to thee, Virgin-born,
All praise, Holy Ghost, to thee.
Amen.

Hymnus Laudes.label: Hymn
Hymnus Laudes.title: Salvéte, flores Mártyrum
Hymnus Laudes.lat:
Salvéte, flores Mártyrum,
Quos lucis ipso in límine
Christi insecútor sústulit,
Ceu turbo nascéntes rosas.

Vos prima Christi víctima,
Grex immolatórum tener,
Aram sub ipsam símplices
Palma et corónis lúditis.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
Hymnus Laudes.eng:
All hail, ye little Martyr flowers,
Sweet rosebuds cut in dawning hours!
When Herod sought the Christ to find
Ye fell as bloom before the wind.

First victims of the Martyr bands,
With crowns and palms in tender hands,
Around the very altar, gay
And innocent, ye seem to play.

All honor, laud, and glory be,
O Jesu, Virgin-born to thee;
All glory, as is ever meet
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.

Hymnus Matutinum.label: Hymn
Hymnus Matutinum.title: Audit tyránnus ánxius
Hymnus Matutinum.lat:
Audit tyránnus ánxius
Adésse regum Príncipem,
Qui nomen Israël regat,
Teneátque David régiam.

Exclámat amens núntio:
Succéssor instat, péllimur:
Satélles, i, ferrum rape,
Perfúnde cunas sánguine.

Quid próficit tantum nefas?
Quid crimen Heródem juvat?
Unus tot inter fúnera
Impúne Christus tóllitur.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
Hymnus Matutinum.eng:
With terror doth the tyrant hear
The King of kings hath come to dwell
Where David's court shall widely rear
A sceptered reign o'er Israel.

Then cries out, raging, at the word:
“He comes to stand where we have stood:
Hence, soldier, and with ruthless sword
Deluge the cradles deep with blood!”

What profiteth a crime so dread?
What hope shall Herod's bosom sway?
Alone amidst the thronging dead,
The Christ is safely borne away!

All glory for this blessed morn
To God the Father ever be;
All praise to thee, Virgin-born,
All praise, Holy Ghost, to thee.
Amen.

Ant Vespera.ant: Tecum princípium * in die virtútis tuæ, in splendóribus sanctórum, ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Thine shall be the dominion * in the day of thy power, amid the brightness of the saints, from the womb, before the day-star, have I begotten thee.

Ant Vespera.ant: Redemptiónem * misit Dóminus pópulo suo: mandávit in ætérnum testaméntum suum.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The Lord sent redemption * unto His people, He hath commanded His covenant for ever.

Ant Vespera.ant: Exórtum est * in ténebris lumen rectis corde: miséricors, et miserátor, et justus Dóminus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Unto the upright there ariseth * light in the darkness; the Lord is gracious, and full of compassion, and righteous.

Ant Vespera.ant: Apud Dóminum * misericórdia, et copiósa apud eum redémptio.
Ant Vespera.antEng: With the Lord * there is mercy, and with Him is plenteous redemption.

Ant Vespera.ant: De fructu * ventris tui ponam super sedem tuam.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Of the fruit * of thy body will I set upon thy throne.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Tuam ipsíus ánimam * (ait ad Maríam Símeon) pertransíbit gládius.
Ant 1.eng: Simeon said unto Mary: * Yea, a sword shall pierce through thine own soul also.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Cum vidísset Jesus * matrem stantem juxta crucem, et discípulum quem diligébat, dicit matri suæ: Múlier, ecce fílius tuus. Deínde dicit discípulo: Ecce Mater tua.
Ant 2.eng: When Jesus saw His Mother, * and the disciple whom He loved, standing by the Cross, He saith unto His Mother: Woman, behold thy Son! Then saith He to the disciple: Behold thy Mother!

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Cum vidísset Jesus * matrem stantem juxta crucem, et discípulum quem diligébat, dicit matri suæ: Múlier, ecce fílius tuus. Deínde dicit discípulo: Ecce Mater tua.
Ant 3.eng: When Jesus saw His Mother, * and the disciple whom He loved, standing by the Cross, He saith unto His Mother: Woman, behold thy Son! Then saith He to the disciple: Behold thy Mother!

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Quis crédidit audítui nostro? et bráchium Dómini cui revelátum est? Et ascéndet sicut virgúltum coram eo, et sicut radix de terra sitiénti.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Who hath believed our report? and to whom is the arm of the Lord revealed? And he shall grow up as a tender plant before him, and as a root out of a thirsty ground.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Generatiónem ejus quis enarrábit, quia abscíssus est de terra vivéntium; propter scelus pópuli mei percússi eum.
Capitulum Nona.eng: Who shall declare his generation? because he is cut oh out of the land of the living: for the wickedness of my people have I struck him.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Ipse vulnerátus est propter iniquitátes nostras, attrítus est propter scélera nostra: disciplína pacis nostræ super eum, et livóre ejus sanáti sumus.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: But he was wounded for our iniquities, he was bruised for our sins: the chastisement of our peace was upon him, and by his bruises we are healed.

Doxology.lat:
Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui passus es pro sérvulis,
Cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

Hymnus Laudes.label: Hymn
Hymnus Laudes.title: Virgo vírginum præclára
Hymnus Laudes.lat:
Virgo vírginum præclára,
Mihi jam non sis amára,
Fac me tecum plángere.

Fac ut portem Christi mortem,
Passiónis fac consórtem,
Et plagas recólere.

Fac me plagis vulnerári,
Fac me cruce inebriári,
Et cruóre Fílii.

Flammis ne urar succénsus,
Per te Virgo sim defénsus
In die judícii.

Christe, cum sit hinc exíre,
Da per Matrem me veníre
Ad palmam victóriæ.

Quando corpus moriétur,
Fac ut ánimæ donétur
Paradísi glória.
Amen.
Hymnus Laudes.eng:
Virgin of all virgins blest!
Listen to my fond request:
Let me share thy grief divine;

Let me, to my latest breath,
In my body bear the death
Of that dying Son of thine.

Wounded with his every wound,
Steep my soul till it hath swooned
In his very blood away;

Be to me, O Virgin, nigh,
Lest in flames I burn and die,
In that awful judgement day.

Christ, when thou shalt call me hence,
Be thy Mother my defence,
Be thy cross my victory;

While my body here decays,
May my soul thy goodness praise,
Safe in Paradise with thee.
Amen.

Hymnus Matutinum.label: Hymn
Hymnus Matutinum.title: Sancta Mater, istud agas
Hymnus Matutinum.lat:
Sancta Mater, istud agas,
Crucifíxi fige plagas
Cordi meo válide:

Tui nati vulneráti,
Tam dignáti pro me pati,
Pœnas mecum dívide.

Fac me tecum pie flere,
Crucifíxo condolére,
Donec ego víxero:

Juxta crucem tecum stare,
Et me tibi sociáre
In planctu desídero.
Amen.
Hymnus Matutinum.eng:
Holy Mother! pierce me through;
In my heart each wound renew
Of my Saviour crucified:

Let me share with thee his pain,
Who for all my sins was slain,
Who for me in torments died.

Let me mingle tears with thee,
Mourning him who mourned for me,
All the days that I may live:

By the cross with thee to stay;
There with thee to weep and pray;
Is all I ask of thee to give.
Amen.

Hymnus Vespera.label: Hymn
Hymnus Vespera.title: Stabat Mater dolorósa
Hymnus Vespera.lat:
Stabat Mater dolorósa
Juxta crucem lacrimósa,
Dum pendébat Fílius.

Cujus ánimam geméntem,
Contristátam et doléntem,
Pertransívit gládius.

O quam tristis et afflícta
Fuit illa benedícta
Mater Unigéniti!

Quæ mœrébat, et dolébat,
Pia Mater dum vidébat
Nati pœnas ínclyti.

Quis est homo qui non fleret,
Matrem Christi si vidéret
In tanto supplício?

Quis non posset contristári,
Christi Matrem contemplári
Doléntem cum Fílio?

Pro peccátis suæ gentis
Vidit Jesum in torméntis,
Et flagéllis súbditum.

Vidit suum dulcem natum,
Moriéndo desolátum,
Dum emísit spíritum.

Eja, Mater, fons amóris,
Me sentíre vim dolóris
Fac, ut tecum lúgeam:

Fac ut árdeat cor meum
In amándo Christum Deum,
Ut sibi compláceam.
Amen.
Hymnus Vespera.eng:
At the cross her station keeping,
Stood the mournful Mother weeping,
Close to Jesus to the last:

Through her heart, his sorrow sharing,
All his bitter anguish bearing,
Now at length the sword had passed.

Oh, how sad and sore distressed
Was that Mother highly blest
Of the sole-begotten One!

Christ above in torment hangs;
She beneath beholds the pangs
Of her dying glorious Son.

Is there one who would not weep,
Whelmed in miseries so deep
Christ's dear Mother to behold?

Can the human heart refrain
From partaking in her pain,
In that Mother's pain untold?

Bruised, derided, cursed, defiled,
She beheld her tender Child
All with bloody scourges rent;

For the sins of his own nation,
Saw him hang in desolation,
Till his Spirit forth he sent.

O thou Mother! fount of love!
Touch my spirit from above,
Make my heart with thine accord:

Make me feel as thou hast felt;
Make my soul to glow and melt
With the love of Christ my Lord.
Amen.

Invit.label: Antiphon
Invit.lat: Dolóres gloriósæ recoléntes Vírginis, Dóminum pro nobis passum * Veníte adorémus.
Invit.eng: When we remember the sorrows of the most glorious Virgin, * O come, let us worship the Lord, Who suffered for us.

Lectio Prima.label: Lectio brevis
Lectio Prima.lat: Generatiónem ejus quis enarrábit, quia abscíssus est de terra vivéntium; propter scelus pópuli mei percússi eum.
Lectio Prima.eng: He was taken away from distress, and from judgment: who shall declare his generation? because he is cut oh out of the land of the living: for the wickedness of my people have I struck him.

Nocturn 1 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 1 Versum.eng: ℣. He hath made me desolate.
Nocturn 1 Versum.engR: ℟. And faint with sorrow all the day.

Nocturn 2 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 2 Versum.lat: ℣. Fácies mea intúmuit a fletu.
Nocturn 2 Versum.eng: ℣. My face is swollen with weeping.
Nocturn 2 Versum.engR: ℟. And on mine eyelids is the shadow (of death.

Nocturn 3 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 3 Versum.latR: ℟. Posuísti lácrimas meas in conspéctu tuo.
Nocturn 3 Versum.eng: ℣. O God, I have declared my life unto thee.
Nocturn 3 Versum.engR: ℟. Thou hast put my tears in thy sight.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, in cujus passióne, secúndum Simeónis prophetíam, dulcíssimam ánimam gloriósæ Vírginis et Matris Maríæ dolóris gládius pertransívit: concéde, propítius; ut qui transfixiónem ejus et passiónem venerándo recólimus, gloriósis méritis et précibus ómnium Sanctórum cruci fidéliter astántium intercedéntibus, passiónis tuæ efféctum felícem consequámur:
Oratio.eng: O God, at Whose Passion, according to the prophecy of Simeon, a sword of sorrow pierced through the gentle soul of the glorious Maiden and Mother Mary, mercifully grant to as many as do ever remember with awe how that her soul was pierced and Thou didst suffer, even for all such be Thou entreated, for the sake and by the prayers of all thy glorious and holy servants who stood so loyally by thy Cross, and grant unto the same, that for them thy life-giving Death may not have been in vain.

Responsory Breve Nona.label: Responsorium Breve
Responsory Breve Nona.lat:
℟.br. Deus vitam meam * Annuntiávi tibi.
℣. Posuísti lácrimas meas in conspéctu tuo.
℟. Annuntiávi tibi.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Deus vitam meam * Annuntiávi tibi.
Responsory Breve Nona.eng:
℟.br. O God, * I have declared my life unto thee.
℣. Thou hast put my tears in thy sight.
℟. I have declared my life unto thee.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. O God, * I have declared my life unto thee.

Responsory Breve Sexta.label: Responsorium Breve
Responsory Breve Sexta.lat:
℟.br. Fácies mea * Intúmuit a fletu.
℣. Et pálpebræ meæ caligavérunt.
℟. Intúmuit a fletu.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Fácies mea * Intúmuit a fletu.
Responsory Breve Sexta.eng:
℟.br. My face is * swollen with weeping.
℣. And on my eyelids is the shadow (of death.)
℟. Swollen with weeping.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. My face is * swollen with weeping.

Responsory Breve Tertia.label: Responsorium Breve
Responsory Breve Tertia.lat:
℟.br. Pósuit me * Desolátam.
℣. Tota die mæróre conféctam.
℟. Desolátam.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Pósuit me * Desolátam.
Responsory Breve Tertia.eng:
℟.br. He hath made me * desolate.
℣. And faint with sorrow all the day.
℟. Desolate.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. He hath made me * desolate.

Psalmi Dominica
Antiphonas horas
9 lectiones
Gloria responsory

Versum 1.label: Versicle
Versum 1.eng: ℣. Pray for us, O Virgin most sorrowful.
Versum 1.engR: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

Versum 2.latR: ℟. Ut digni efficiámur promissiónibus Christi.
Versum 2.eng: ℣. Pray for us, O Virgin most sorrowful.
Versum 2.engR: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

Versum 3.latR: ℟. Ut digni efficiámur promissiónibus Christi.
Versum 3.eng: ℣. Pray for us, O Virgin most sorrowful.
Versum 3.engR: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

Versum Nona.label: Versicle
Versum Nona.eng: ℣. Pray for us, O Virgin most sorrowful.
Versum Nona.engR: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

Versum Prima.label: Antiphon
Versum Prima.lat: Qui passus es propter nostram salútem.

Versum Sexta.label: Versicle

Versum Sexta.engR: ℟. Thou hast put my tears in thy sight.

Ant Laudes.ant: Vadam ad montem * myrrhæ et ad collem thuris.
Ant Laudes.antEng: I will get me to the mountain of myrrh, * and to the hill of frankincense.

Ant Laudes.ant: Diléctus meus * cándidus et rubicúndus: comæ cápitis ejus sicut púrpura regis vincta canálibus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: My beloved * is white and ruddy the hair of his head is like kingly purple, bound in tresses.

Ant Laudes.ant: Quo ábiit * diléctus tuus, o pulchérrima mulíerum? quo diléctus tuus declinávit.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Whither is thy beloved gone, * O thou fairest among women? Whither is thy beloved turned aside?

Ant Laudes.ant: Fascículus myrrhæ * diléctus meus mihi inter úbera mea commorábitur.
Ant Laudes.antEng: A bundle of myrrh is my well-beloved unto me; he shall lie betwixt my breasts.

Ant Laudes.ant: Fulcíte me flóribus * stipáte me malis, quia amóre lángueo.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Revive me with flowers, * stay me up with apples, for I am swooning with love.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Astitérunt reges terræ, * et príncipes convenérunt in unum advérsus Dóminum, et advérsus Christum ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together against the Lord, and against His Anointed.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Voce mea * ad Dóminum clamávi, et exaudívit me de monte sancto suo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I cried unto the Lord with my voice, and He heard me out of His holy hill.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Factum est cor meum * tamquam cera liquéscens in médio ventris mei.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: My heart is like melting wax in the midst of my bowels.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Inimíci mei * dixérunt mala mihi: Quando moriétur, et períbit nomen ejus?
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Mine enemies speak evil of me When shall he die, and his name perish.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Deus, vitam meam * annuntiávi tibi: posuísti lácrimas meas in conspéctu tuo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O God, I have declared my life unto thee, Thou hast put my tears in thy sight.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Fílii hóminum, * dentes eórum arma et sagíttæ: et lingua eórum gládius acútus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: As for the sons of men, their teeth are spears and arrows, and their tongue a sharp sword.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Intendérunt arcum, * rem amáram, ut sagíttent in occúltis immaculátum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: They bend their bow, even bitter words, that they may shoot in secret at the perfect.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Factus sum * sicut homo sine adjutório, inter mórtuos liber.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I am as a man that hath no strength, lying nerveless among the dead.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Replévit me amaritúdine, * inebriávit me absýnthio.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: He hath filled me with bitterness, he hath made me drunken with wormwood.

Ant Vespera.ant: Vadam ad montem * myrrhæ et ad collem thuris.
Ant Vespera.antEng: I will get me to the mountain of myrrh, * and to the hill of frankincense.

Ant Vespera.ant: Diléctus meus * cándidus et rubicúndus: comæ cápitis ejus sicut púrpura regis vincta canálibus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: My beloved * is white and ruddy; the hair of his head is like kingly purple, bound in tresses.

Ant Vespera.ant: Quo ábiit * diléctus tuus, o pulchérrima mulíerum? quo diléctus tuus declinávit.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Whither is thy beloved gone, * O thou fairest among women? Whither is thy beloved turned aside?

Ant Vespera.ant: Fascículus myrrhæ * diléctus meus mihi inter úbera mea commorábitur.
Ant Vespera.antEng: A bundle of myrrh is my well-beloved unto me; he shall lie betwixt my breasts.

Ant Vespera.ant: Fulcíte me flóribus * stipáte me malis, quia amóre lángueo.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Revive me with flowers, * stay me up with apples, for I am swooning with love.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Sapiéntia * ædificávit sibi domum, excídit colúmnas septem, súbdidit sibi gentes, superbórum et sublímium colla própria virtúte calcávit.
Ant 1.eng: Wisdom * hath builded her house, she hath hewn out her seven pillars, she hath broken the nations under her in the greatness of her strength, she hath trodden under her feet the necks of such as be haughty and proud.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Ego in altíssimis * hábito: et thronus meus in colúmna nubis.
Ant 1.eng: I dwell in the highest * places, and my throne is in a cloudy pillar.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Omnis sapiéntia * a Dómino Deo est, et cum illo fuit semper, et est ante ævum.
Ant 1.eng: All wisdom * is of the Lord God, and was with Him from everlasting, yea before time was.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Sapiéntia * clámitat in platéis: Si quis díligit sapiéntiam, ad me declínet, et eam invéniet: et, cum invénerit, beátus erit si tenúerit eam.
Ant 1.eng: Wisdom * crieth in the streets: If any man love wisdom, let him come unto me, and he shall find her and when once he hath found her, blessed shall he be if he hold her.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Obsérva, fili, * præcépta patris tui, et ne dimíttas legem matris tuæ, sed liga eam semper in corde tuo.
Ant 1.eng: My son, keep thy fathers commandment * and forsake not the law of thy mother, but bind them continually upon thy heart.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Cum audísset Job * nuntiórum verba, sustínuit patiénter, et ait: Si bona suscépimus de manu Dómini, mala autem quare non sustineámus? In ómnibus his non peccávit Job lábiis suis, neque stultum áliquid contra Deum locútus est.
Ant 1.eng: When Job heard the words * of the messengers, he suffered it patiently, and said: What! shall we receive good at the hand of the Lord, and shall we not receive evil? In all this did not Job sin with his lips, nor charged God foolishly.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: In ómnibus his * non peccávit Job lábiis suis neque stultum áliquid contra Deum locútus est.
Ant 1.eng: In all these things Job sinned not * with his lips, nor charged God with foolishness.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Ne reminiscáris, * Dómine, delícta mea vel paréntum meórum, neque vindíctam sumas de peccátis meis.
Ant 1.eng: Remember not, Lord * mine offences, nor the offences of my forefathers, neither take Thou vengeance of my sins.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Hoc genus * dæmoniórum in nullo potest exíre, nisi in oratióne et jejúnio.
Ant 2.eng: This kind of devils * can come forth by nothing but by prayer and fasting.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Hoc genus * dæmoniórum in nullo potest exíre, nisi in oratióne et jejúnio.
Ant 3.eng: This kind of devils * can come forth by nothing but by prayer and fasting.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Misericórdiæ tuæ remédiis, quǽsumus, Dómine, fragílitas nostra subsístat: ut, quæ sua conditióne attéritur, tua cleméntia reparétur.
Oratio.eng: We pray thee, O Lord, that the healing power of thy mercy may give strength to our weakness, that those things which do pass away by their own frailty, may be renewed again by thy clemency.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Múlier, * quæ erat in civitáte peccátrix, stans retro secus pedes Dómini, lácrimis cœpit rigáre pedes ejus et capíllis cápitis sui tergébat, et deosculabátur pedes ejus et unguénto ungébat.
Ant 2.eng: A woman in the city which was a sinner stood at the Lord's Feet behind Him, * and began to wash His Feet with tears, and did wipe them with the hairs of her head, and kissed His Feet, and anointed them with the ointment.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Múlier, * quæ erat in civitáte peccátrix, stans retro secus pedes Dómini, lácrimis cœpit rigáre pedes ejus et capíllis cápitis sui tergébat, et deosculabátur pedes ejus et unguénto ungébat.
Ant 3.eng: A woman in the city which was a sinner stood at the Lord's Feet behind Him, * and began to wash His Feet with tears, and did wipe them with the hairs of her head, and kissed His Feet, and anointed them with the ointment.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut observatiónes sacras ánnua devotióne recoléntes, et córpore tibi placeámus, et mente.
Oratio.eng: Grant, we beseech thee, O Almighty God, that we who every year do earnestly renew the sacred observance of this Fast, may please thee both in body and in soul.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Illúmina, Dómine, * sedéntes in ténebris et umbra mortis, et dírige pedes nostros in viam pacis.
Ant 2.eng: Give light, O Lord, to them that sit in darkness, * and guide our feet into the way of peace, O Thou the God of Israel.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui per continéntiam salutárem corpóribus medéris et méntibus: majestátem tuam súpplices exorámus; ut pia jejunántium deprecatióne placátus, et præséntia nobis subsídia tríbuas, et futúra.
Oratio.eng: O God, Who hast chosen healthy fasting, as a mean to do good both to bodies and to souls, we humbly implore thy Majesty, that the godly prayer of such as be fasting this day may turn away thy wrath, and may be effectual to gain for us thy blessing in time and in eternity.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Adonái, Dómine, * Deus magne et mirábilis, qui dedísti salútem in manu féminæ, exáudi preces servórum tuórum.
Ant 1.eng: O Adonai, O Lord God, * Thou art great and glorious, Who hast given salvation into the hand of a woman, graciously hear the prayers of thy servants.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Dómine Rex omnípotens, * in dicióne tua cuncta sunt pósita, et non est qui possit tuæ resístere voluntáti.
Ant 1.eng: O my Lord, the King Almighty, * all things are in thy power, and there is no man that can gainsay thy will.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Adapériat Dóminus * cor vestrum in lege sua et in præcéptis suis et fáciat pacem Dóminus Deus noster.
Ant 1.eng: The Lord open your hearts * in His law and commandments, and may the Lord our God send peace.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Refúlsit sol * in clípeos áureos, et resplenduérunt montes ab eis: et fortitúdo géntium dissipáta est.
Ant 1.eng: The sun shone * upon the shields of gold, and the mountains glistened therewith, and the army of the heathens was spread abroad.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Lugébat autem Judam * Israël planctu magno et dicébat: Quómodo cecidísti, potens in prǽlio, qui salvum faciébas pópulum Dómini?
Ant 1.eng: Moreover, all Israel made great lamentation * for Judas, saying How art thou fallen, thou valiant man of war, that didst deliver the Lord's people

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Exáudiat Dóminus * oratiónes vestras et reconciliétur vobis: nec vos déserat in témpore malo Dóminus, Deus noster.
Ant 1.eng: The Lord, even the Lord our God * hear your prayers, and be at one with you, and never forsake you in time of trouble.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Tua est poténtia, * tuum regnum, Dómine: tu es super omnes Gentes: da pacem, Dómine, in diébus nostris.
Ant 1.eng: Thine, O Lord, is the power * the kingdom is thine. Thou art high above all the heathen grant peace in our time, O Lord.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Vidi Dóminum * sedéntem super sólium excélsum, et plena erat omnis terra majestáte ejus: et ea, quæ sub ipso erant, replébant templum.
Ant 1.eng: I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne high and lifted up, * and the whole earth was full of His glory, and His train filled the Temple.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Aspice Dómine, * quia facta est desoláta cívitas plena divítiis, sedet in tristítia dómina Géntium: non est qui consolétur eam, nisi tu, Deus noster.
Ant 1.eng: Consider, O Lord, how that the city that was full with grace became desolate * she sedeth in great grief, there is none to comfort her: but you Lord, our God

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Muro tuo * inexpugnábili circumcínge nos, Dómine, et armis tuæ poténtiæ prótege nos semper.
Ant 1.eng: Hedge us about * with thy wall that cannot be broken down, O Lord, and shield us continually with the arms of thy might.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Qui cælórum * cóntines thronum, et abýssos intuéris, Dómine, Rex regum, montes pónderas, terram palmo conclúdis: exáudi nos, Dómine, in gemítibus nostris.
Ant 1.eng: O Lord, the King of kings, That containest the circuit of the heavens and beholdest the depths, That weighest the mountains, and holdest the earth in thine hand, * hear us, O Lord, when we cry unto thee.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Super muros tuos, * Jerúsalem, constítui custódes; tota die et nocte non tacébunt laudáre nomen Dómini.
Ant 1.eng: I have set watchmen upon thy walls, O Jerusalem, * which shall never hold their peace day nor night, praising the Name of the Lord.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Ecce nomen Dómini * venit de longínquo, et cláritas ejus replet orbem terrárum.
Ant 1.eng: Behold, the name of the Lord * cometh from far, and the whole earth is full of His glory.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Spíritus Sanctus * in te descéndet, María: ne tímeas, habébis in útero Fílium Dei, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, * O Mary; fear not, thou shalt bear in thy womb the Son of God. Alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Ne tímeas, María, * invenísti enim grátiam apud Dóminum: ecce concípies, et páries fílium, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: Fear not, Mary, * for thou hast found grace with the Lord; behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son. Alleluia.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Fratres: Hora est jam nos de somno súrgere: nunc enim própior est nostra salus, quam cum credídimus.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: And that knowing the season; that it is now the hour for us to rise from sleep. For now our salvation is nearer than when we believed.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Sicut in die honéste ambulémus, non in comessatiónibus et ebrietátibus, non in cubílibus et impudicítiis, non in contentióne et æmulatióne; sed induímini Dóminum Jesum Christum.
Capitulum Nona.eng: Let us walk honestly, as in the day: not in rioting and drunkenness, not in chambering and impurities, not in contention and envy: But put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Nox præcéssit, dies autem appropinquávit. Abiciámus ergo ópera tenebrárum, et induámur arma lucis. Sicut in die honéste ambulémus.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: The night is passed, and the day is at hand. Let us therefore cast off the works of darkness, and put on the armour of light. Let us walk honestly, as in the day.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Excita, quǽsumus, Dómine, poténtiam tuam, et veni: ut ab imminéntibus peccatórum nostrórum perículis, te mereámur protegénte éripi, te liberánte salvári:
Oratio.eng: Stir up, O Lord, we pray thee, thy strength, and come among us, that whereas through our sins and wickedness we do justly apprehend thy wrathful judgments hanging over us, thy bountiful grace and mercy may speedily help and deliver us;

Versum 1.label: Versicle
Versum 1.lat: ℣. Roráte, cæli, désuper, et nubes pluant justum.
Versum 1.eng: ℣. Drop down dew, ye heavens, from above, and let the clouds rain the Just.
Versum 1.engR: ℟. Let the earth be opened, and bud forth the Saviour.

Ant Laudes.ant: In illa die * stillábunt montes dulcédinem, et colles fluent lac et mel, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: In that day * the mountains shall drop down sweet wine, and the hills shall flow with milk and honey. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Jucundáre, * fília Sion, et exsúlta satis, fília Jerúsalem, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Sing, O daughter of Zion, * and rejoice with all the heart, O daughter of Jerusalem. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Ecce Dóminus véniet, * et omnes Sancti ejus cum eo: et erit in die illa lux magna, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Behold, the Lord shall come, * and all His saints with Him; and it shall come to pass in that day that the light shall be great. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Omnes sitiéntes, * veníte ad aquas: quǽrite Dóminum, dum inveníri potest, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Lo, every one that thirsteth * come ye to the waters: seek ye the Lord while He may be found. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Ecce véniet * Prophéta magnus, et ipse renovábit Jerúsalem, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Behold, a great Prophet * shall arise, and He shall build up a new Jerusalem. Alleluia.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Angelus Dómini * nuntiávit Maríæ, et concépit de Spíritu Sancto, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: The angel of the Lord * announced unto Mary, and she conceived of the Holy Ghost. Alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Leva, Jerúsalem, * óculos tuos, et vide poténtiam regis: ecce Salvátor venit sólvere te a vínculo.
Ant 3.eng: Lift up thine eyes, * O Jerusalem, and see that thy King is mighty behold, thy Saviour shall come and loose thee from thy chain.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Angelus Dómini * nuntiávit Maríæ, et concépit de Spíritu Sancto, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: The angel of the Lord * announced unto Mary, and she conceived of the Holy Ghost. Alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Leva, Jerúsalem, * óculos tuos, et vide poténtiam regis: ecce Salvátor venit sólvere te a vínculo.
Ant 3.eng: Lift up thine eyes, * O Jerusalem, and see that thy King is mighty behold, thy Saviour shall come and loose thee from thy chain.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Antequam convenírent, * invénta est María habens in útero de Spíritu Sancto, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: Before they came together, * Mary was found with child of the Holy Ghost. Alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Quǽrite Dóminum, * dum inveníri potest: invocáte eum, dum prope est, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: Seek ye the Lord * while He may be found; call ye upon Him while He is near. Alleluia.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Antequam convenírent, * invénta est María habens in útero de Spíritu Sancto, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: Before they came together, * Mary was found with child of the Holy Ghost. Alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Quǽrite Dóminum, * dum inveníri potest: invocáte eum, dum prope est, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: Seek ye the Lord * while He may be found; call ye upon Him while He is near. Alleluia.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: De Sion * exíbit lex, et verbum Dómini de Jerúsalem.
Ant 2.eng: Out of Zion * shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Véniet * fórtior me post me, cujus non sum dignus sólvere corrígiam calceamentórum.
Ant 3.eng: There cometh One mightier * than I after me, the latchet of Whose shoes I am not worthy to unloose.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: De Sion * exíbit lex, et verbum Dómini de Jerúsalem.
Ant 2.eng: Out of Zion * shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Véniet * fórtior me post me, cujus non sum dignus sólvere corrígiam calceamentórum.
Ant 3.eng: There cometh One mightier * than I after me, the latchet of Whose shoes I am not worthy to unloose.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Benedícta * tu in muliéribus, et benedíctus fructus ventris tui.
Ant 2.eng: Blessed art thou * among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Exspectábo * Dóminum Salvatórem meum, et præstolábor eum dum prope est, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: I will wait * upon the Lord my Saviour, and come before Him when He is near, alleluia.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Benedícta * tu in muliéribus, et benedíctus fructus ventris tui.
Ant 2.eng: Blessed art thou * among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Exspectábo * Dóminum Salvatórem meum, et præstolábor eum dum prope est, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: I will wait * upon the Lord my Saviour, and come before Him when He is near, alleluia.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Ecce véniet * Deus et homo de domo David sedére in throno, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: He that is both God and man * shall come of the house of David and sit in David's seat. Alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Ex Ægýpto * vocávi Fílium meum: véniet, ut salvet pópulum suum.
Ant 3.eng: Out of Egypt * have I called My Son; He shall come to save His people.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Ecce véniet * Deus et homo de domo David sedére in throno, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: He that is both God and man * shall come of the house of David and sit in David's seat. Alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Ex Ægýpto * vocávi Fílium meum: véniet, ut salvet pópulum suum.
Ant 3.eng: Out of Egypt * have I called My Son; He shall come to save His people.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Sion, noli timére, * ecce Deus tuus véniet, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: Fear not * Zion, behold, thy God cometh, Alleluia.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Sion, noli timére, * ecce Deus tuus véniet, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: Fear not * Zion, behold, thy God cometh, Alleluia.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Veni, Dómine, * visitáre nos in pace, ut lætémur coram te corde perfécto.
Ant 1.eng: Come, O Lord, * visit us in peace, that we may rejoice before thee with all our heart.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Joánnes autem * cum audísset in vínculis ópera Christi, mittens duos ex discípulis suis, ait illi: Tu es qui ventúrus es, an álium exspectámus?
Ant 2.eng: Now when John * had heard in the prison the works of Christ, he sent two of his disciples and said unto Him: Art Thou He That should come, or do we look for another?

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Tu es, qui ventúrus es, * an álium exspectámus? Dícite Joánni quæ vidístis: Ad lumen rédeunt cæci, mórtui resúrgunt, páuperes evangelizántur, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: Art thou he that art to come * or look we for another? Go and relate to John what you have seen: the blind see, the dead rise again, to the poor the gospel is preached. Alleluia.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Fratres: Quæcúmque scripta sunt, ad nostram doctrínam scripta sunt: ut per patiéntiam, et consolatiónem Scripturárum spem habeámus.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Brothers: For what things soever were written, were written for our learning: that through patience and the comfort of the scriptures, we might have hope.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Deus autem spei répleat vos omni gáudio et pace in credéndo: ut abundétis in spe, et in virtúte Spíritus Sancti.
Capitulum Nona.eng: Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing; that you may abound in hope, and in the power of the Holy Ghost.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Deus autem patiéntiæ, et solácii det vobis idípsum sápere in altérutrum secúndum Jesum Christum: ut unánimes uno ore honorificétis Deum, et Patrem Dómini nostri Jesu Christi.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: Now the God of patience and of comfort grant you to be of one mind one towards another, according to Jesus Christ:That with one mind, and with one mouth, you may glorify God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Excita, Dómine, corda nostra ad præparándas Unigéniti tui vias: ut, per ejus advéntum, purificátis tibi méntibus servíre mereámur:
Oratio.eng: Stir up our hearts, O Lord, to make ready the ways of thine Only-begotten Son, that by His coming our minds being purified, we may the more worthily give up ourselves to thy service:

Ant Laudes.ant: Ecce in núbibus cæli * Dóminus véniet cum potestáte magna, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Behold, the Lord * cometh in the clouds of heaven with great power. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Urbs fortitúdinis * nostræ Sion, Salvátor ponétur in ea murus et antemurále: aperíte portas, quia nobíscum Deus, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Our Zion is a strong city, * the Saviour will God appoint in her for walls and bulwarks; open ye the gates, for God is with us. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Ecce apparébit * Dóminus, et non mentiétur: si moram fécerit, exspécta eum, quia véniet, et non tardábit, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Behold, the Lord * shall appear and not lie though He tarry, wait for Him, because He will come and will not tarry. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Montes et colles * cantábunt coram Deo laudem, et ómnia ligna silvárum plaudent mánibus: quóniam véniet Dominátor Dóminus in regnum ætérnum, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The mountains and the hills * shall break forth before God into singing, and all the trees of the wood shall clap their hands for the Lord the Ruler cometh, and He shall reign for ever and ever. Alleluia, Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Ecce Dóminus * noster cum virtúte véniet, et illuminábit óculos servórum suórum, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Behold, our Lord * cometh with power, and He shall lighten the eyes of His servants. Alleluia.

Ant Vespera.ant: Ecce in núbibus cæli * Dóminus véniet cum potestáte magna, allelúja.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Behold, the Lord * cometh in the clouds of heaven with great power. Alleluia.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Veni, Dómine, * visitáre nos in pace, ut lætémur coram te corde perfécto.
Ant 1.eng: Come, O Lord, * visit us in peace, that we may rejoice before thee with all our heart.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Joánnes autem * cum audísset in vínculis ópera Christi, mittens duos ex discípulis suis, ait illi: Tu es qui ventúrus es, an álium exspectámus?
Ant 2.eng: Now when John * had heard in the prison the works of Christ, he sent two of his disciples and said unto Him: Art Thou He That should come, or do we look for another?

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Tu es, qui ventúrus es, * an álium exspectámus? Dícite Joánni quæ vidístis: Ad lumen rédeunt cæci, mórtui resúrgunt, páuperes evangelizántur, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: Art thou he that art to come * or look we for another? Go and relate to John what you have seen: the blind see, the dead rise again, to the poor the gospel is preached. Alleluia.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Fratres: Quæcúmque scripta sunt, ad nostram doctrínam scripta sunt: ut per patiéntiam, et consolatiónem Scripturárum spem habeámus.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Brothers: For what things soever were written, were written for our learning: that through patience and the comfort of the scriptures, we might have hope.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Deus autem spei répleat vos omni gáudio et pace in credéndo: ut abundétis in spe, et in virtúte Spíritus Sancti.
Capitulum Nona.eng: Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing; that you may abound in hope, and in the power of the Holy Ghost.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Deus autem patiéntiæ, et solácii det vobis idípsum sápere in altérutrum secúndum Jesum Christum: ut unánimes uno ore honorificétis Deum, et Patrem Dómini nostri Jesu Christi.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: Now the God of patience and of comfort grant you to be of one mind one towards another, according to Jesus Christ:That with one mind, and with one mouth, you may glorify God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Excita, Dómine, corda nostra ad præparándas Unigéniti tui vias: ut, per ejus advéntum, purificátis tibi méntibus servíre mereámur:
Oratio.eng: Stir up our hearts, O Lord, to make ready the ways of thine Only-begotten Son, that by His coming our minds being purified, we may the more worthily give up ourselves to thy service:

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: De cælo véniet * Dominátor Dóminus, et in manu ejus honor et impérium.
Ant 2.eng: The Lord the Ruler * cometh from heaven, and in His hand are honour and dominion.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Ecce véniet Rex * Dóminus terræ, et ipse áuferet jugum captivitátis nostræ.
Ant 3.eng: Behold, the Lord cometh * the King of all the earth, to take off from us the yoke of our captivity.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Super te, * Jerúsalem, oriétur Dóminus, et glória ejus in te vidébitur.
Ant 2.eng: The Lord shall arise * upon thee, O Jerusalem, and His glory shall be seen upon thee.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Vox clamántis * in desérto, Paráte viam Dómini, rectas fácite sémitas Dei nostri.
Ant 3.eng: The voice * of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make His paths straight.

Ant 3.eng: The voice * of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make His paths straight.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Ecce ego mitto * Angelum meum, qui præparábit viam meam ante fáciem tuam.
Ant 2.eng: Behold I send My angel * which shall prepare My way before thy face.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Sion, renováberis, * et vidébis justum tuum, qui ventúrus est in te.
Ant 3.eng: Thou shalt yet be built anew, * O Zion, and thou shalt see thy Righteous One, Who shall come in thee.

Ant 3.eng: Thou shalt yet be built anew, * O Zion, and thou shalt see thy Righteous One, Who shall come in thee.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Tu es qui ventúrus es, * Dómine, quem exspectámus, ut salvum fácias pópulum tuum.
Ant 2.eng: O Lord, Thou art He That should come, * for Whom we look, that Thou shouldest save thy people.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Qui post me véniet, * ante me factus est: cujus non sum dignus calceaménta sólvere.
Ant 3.eng: He it is * Who, coming after me, is preferred before me, Whose shoe's latchet I am not worthy to unloose.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Dícite: Pusillánimes, * confortámini: ecce Dóminus Deus noster véniet.
Ant 2.eng: Say: * Ye that are of a fearful heart, be strong; behold, the Lord our God will come.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Cantáte Dómino * cánticum novum: laus ejus ab extrémis terræ.
Ant 3.eng: Sing unto the Lord * a new song; from the end of the earth, let the voice of praise be heard.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Levábit Dóminus signum, * in natiónibus, et congregábit dispérsos Israël.
Ant 2.eng: The Lord shall lift up a standard * unto the nations, and shall gather together the outcasts of Israel.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Levábit Dóminus signum, * in natiónibus, et congregábit dispérsos Israël.
Ant 2.eng: The Lord shall lift up a standard * unto the nations, and shall gather together the outcasts of Israel.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Ante me * non est formátus Deus, et post me non erit: quia mihi curvábitur omne genu, et confitébitur omnis lingua.
Ant 1.eng: Before Me * there was no god formed, neither shall there be after Me; for unto Me every knee shall bow, and every tongue shall swear.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Super sólium * David, et super regnum ejus sedébit in ætérnum, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: He shall sit * upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom for ever. Alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Beáta es, María, * quæ credidísti Dómino: perficiéntur in te, quæ dicta sunt tibi a Dómino, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: Blessed art thou, * O Mary, who hast believed the Lord, for there shall be a performance of those things which were told thee from the Lord. Alleluia.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Fratres: Gaudéte in Dómino semper: íterum dico, gaudéte. Modéstia vestra nota sit ómnibus homínibus: Dóminus enim prope est.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Brothers: Rejoice in the Lord always; again, I say, rejoice. Let your modesty be known to all men. The Lord is nigh.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Et pax Dei, quæ exsúperat omnem sensum, custódiat corda vestra, et intellegéntias vestras in Christo Jesu Dómino nostro.
Capitulum Nona.eng: And the peace of God, which surpasseth all understanding, keep your hearts and minds in Christ Jesus.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Nihil sollíciti sitis: sed in omni oratióne, et obsecratióne cum gratiárum actióne, petitiónes vestræ innotéscant apud Deum.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: Be nothing solicitous; but in every thing, by prayer and supplication, with thanksgiving, let your petitions be made known to God.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Aurem tuam, quǽsumus, Dómine, précibus nostris accómmoda: et mentis nostræ ténebras, grátia tuæ visitatiónis illústra:
Oratio.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee, mercifully incline thine ears unto our prayers, and lighten the darkness of our minds by the grace of thy heavenly visitation.

Ant Laudes.ant: Véniet Dóminus, * et non tardábit, et illuminábit abscóndita tenebrárum, et manifestábit se ad omnes gentes, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Lord will come, * and will not tarry; He both will bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and will make Himself manifest to all people. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Jerúsalem, gaude * gáudio magno, quia véniet tibi Salvátor, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Rejoice greatly, O Jerusalem, * for thy Saviour cometh unto thee. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dabo in Sion * salútem, et in Jerúsalem glóriam meam, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: I will place salvation in Zion, * and My glory in Jerusalem. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Montes et omnes colles * humiliabúntur: et erunt prava in dirécta, et áspera in vias planas: veni, Dómine, et noli tardáre, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Every mountain and hill * shall be made low, and the crooked shall be made straight, and the rough places plain; O Lord, come and make no tarrying. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Juste et pie * vivámus, exspectántes beátam spem, et advéntum Dómini.
Ant Laudes.antEng: We should live * righteously and godly, looking for that blessed hope and the coming of the Lord.

Ant Vespera.ant: Véniet Dóminus, * et non tardábit, et illuminábit abscóndita tenebrárum, et manifestábit se ad omnes gentes, allelúja.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The Lord will come, * and will not tarry; He both will bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and will make Himself manifest to all people. Alleluia.

Ant Vespera.ant: Jerúsalem, gaude * gáudio magno, quia véniet tibi Salvátor, allelúja.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Rejoice greatly, O Jerusalem, * for thy Saviour cometh unto thee. Alleluia.

Ant Vespera.ant: Dabo in Sion * salútem, et in Jerúsalem glóriam meam, allelúja.
Ant Vespera.antEng: I will place salvation in Zion, * and My glory in Jerusalem. Alleluia.

Ant Vespera.ant: Montes et omnes colles * humiliabúntur: et erunt prava in dirécta, et áspera in vias planas: veni, Dómine, et noli tardáre, allelúja.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Every mountain and hill * shall be made low, and the crooked shall be made straight, and the rough places plain; O Lord, come and make no tarrying. Alleluia.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Egrediétur * virga de radíce Jesse, et replébitur omnis terra glória Dómini: et vidébit omnis caro salutáre Dei.
Ant 2.eng: There shall come forth a rod * out of the stem of Jesse, and the whole earth shall be filled with the glory of the Lord, and all flesh shall see the salvation of God.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Beátam me dicent * omnes generatiónes, quia ancíllam húmilem respéxit Deus.
Ant 3.eng: All generations shall call me blessed, * for God hath regarded the lowliness of His hand-maiden.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Tu Béthlehem * terra Juda, non eris mínima: ex te enim éxiet Dux, qui regat pópulum meum Israël.
Ant 2.eng: Thou, Bethlehem, * in the land of Judah, shalt not be the least (among the princes of Judah) for out of thee shall come a Ruler, That shall rule my people Israel.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Eleváre, eleváre, * consúrge Jerúsalem: solve víncula colli tui, captíva fília Sion.
Ant 3.eng: Awake, awake, * arise, O Jerusalem: loose thyself from the bands of thy neck, O captive daughter of Zion.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Missus est Gábriel * Angelus ad Maríam Vírginem desponsátam Joseph.
Ant 2.eng: The angel Gabriel * was sent to Mary, a virgin espoused to Joseph.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Ecce ancílla Dómini: * fiat mihi secúndum verbum tuum.
Ant 3.eng: Behold the handmaid * of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut redemptiónis nostræ ventúra solémnitas et præséntis nobis vitæ subsídia cónferat, et ætérnæ beatitúdinis prǽmia largiátur.
Oratio.eng: Grant, we beseech thee, Almighty God, that the solemn Feast of our redemption, which is now at hand, may both help us in the life which now is, and further us toward the attaining of thine eternal joy in that which is to come.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Vigiláte * ánimo, in próximo est Dóminus Deus noster.
Ant 2.eng: Let your soul watch, * the Lord our God is nigh at hand.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Lætámini * cum Jerúsalem, et exsultáte in ea, omnes qui dilígitis eam, in ætérnum.
Ant 3.eng: Rejoice ye with Jerusalem, * and be glad with her, all ye that love her for ever.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Ex quo facta est * vox salutatiónis tuæ in áuribus meis, exsultávit in gáudio infans in útero meo, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: As soon as the voice of thy salutation * sounded in mine ears, the babe leaped in my womb for joy. Alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Hoc est testimónium, * quod perhíbuit Joánnes: Qui post me venit, ante me factus est.
Ant 3.eng: John bare witness of Him, * saying He That cometh after me is preferred before me.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Excita, quǽsumus, Dómine, poténtiam tuam, et veni: ut hi, qui in tua pietáte confídunt, ab omni cítius adversitáte liberéntur:
Oratio.eng: Stir up, O Lord, we pray thee, thy might, and come among us; that we, trusting only in thy mercy, may by thee be speedily delivered from all adversity.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Quómodo fiet istud, * Angele Dei, quóniam virum non cognósco? Audi, María Virgo: Spíritus Sanctus supervéniet in te, et virtus Altíssimi obumbrábit tibi.
Ant 2.eng: O thou Angel of God, * how shall this be, seeing I know not a man? Hear, O Virgin Mary! the Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee!

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui cónspicis, quia ex nostra pravitáte afflígimur: concéde propítius; ut ex tua visitatióne consolémur:
Oratio.eng: O God, Who seest that by reason of our sins we are sorely afflicted, mercifully grant unto us by thy visitation effectually to be comforted.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Ave, María, * grátia plena: Dóminus tecum: benedícta tu in muliéribus, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: Hail, Mary, full of grace, * the Lord is with thee; blessed art thou among women. Alleluia.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Fratres: Sic nos exístimet homo ut minístros Christi, et dispensatóres mysteriórum Dei. Hic jam quǽritur inter dispensatóres, ut fidélis quis inveniátur.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Brothers: Let a man so account of us as of the ministers of Christ, and the dispensers of the mysteries of God. Here now it is required among the dispensers, that a man be found faithful.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Itaque nolíte ante tempus judicáre, quoadúsque véniat Dóminus: qui et illuminábit abscóndita tenebrárum, et manifestábit consília córdium: et tunc laus erit unicuíque a Deo.
Capitulum Nona.eng: Therefore judge not before the time; until the Lord come, who both will bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts; and then shall every man have praise from God.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Mihi autem pro mínimo est, ut a vobis júdicer, aut ab humáno die: sed neque meípsum júdico.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: But to me it is a very small thing to be judged by you, or by man's day; but neither do I judge my own self.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Excita, quǽsumus, Dómine, poténtiam tuam, et veni: et magna nobis virtúte succúrre; ut per auxílium grátiæ tuæ, quod nostra peccáta præpédiunt, indulgéntia tuæ propitiatiónis accéleret:
Oratio.eng: Stir up, we beseech thee, O Lord, thy power, and come; make haste to our aid with thy great might; that, by the help of thy grace, that which is hindered by our sins may be hastened by thy merciful forgiveness.

Ant Laudes.antEng: Blow ye the trumpet * in Zion, for the day of the Lord is nigh at hand: behold, He cometh to save us! Alleluia, Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Ecce véniet * desiderátus cunctis géntibus: et replébitur glória domus Dómini, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Behold, the desire * of all nations shall come; and the house of the Lord shall be filled with glory. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Erunt prava * in dirécta, et áspera in vias planas: veni, Dómine, et noli tardáre, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The crooked * shall be made straight, and the rough places plain; O Lord, come, and make no tarrying. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dóminus véniet, * occúrrite illi, dicéntes: Magnum princípium, et regni ejus non erit finis: Deus, Fortis, Dominátor, Princeps pacis, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Lord cometh! * Go ye out to meet Him, and say: How great is His dominion, and of His kingdom there shall be no end! He is the mighty God, the Ruler, the Prince of Peace. Alleluia, Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Omnípotens Sermo tuus, * Dómine, a regálibus sédibus véniet, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Thine Almighty Word, * O Lord, shall leap down out of thy royal throne. Alleluia.

Ant 2.eng: Awake, awake, * put on strength, O arm of the Lord!

Doxology.lat:
Jesu, tuis obédiens
Qui factus es paréntibus,
Cum Patre summo ac Spíritu
Semper tibi sit glória.
Amen.

Hymnus Laudes.label: Hymn
Hymnus Laudes.title: O gente felix hóspita
Hymnus Laudes.lat:
O gente felix hóspita,
Augústa sedes Názaræ,
Quæ fovit alma Ecclésiæ
Et prótulit primórdia.

Sol, qui perérrat áureo
Terras jacéntes lúmine,
Nil grátius per sǽcula
Hac vidit æde, aut sánctius.

Ad hanc frequéntes cónvolant
Cæléstis aulæ núntii,
Virtútis hoc sacrárium
Visunt, revísunt, éxcolunt.

Qua mente Jesus, qua manu,
Optáta patris pérficit!
Quo Virgo gestit gáudio
Matérna obíre múnera!

Adest amóris párticeps
Curǽque Joseph cónjugi,
Quos mille jungit néxibus
Virtútis auctor grátia.

Hi diligéntes ínvicem
In Jesu amórem cónfluunt,
Utríque Jesus mútuæ
Dat caritátis prǽmia.

Sic fiat, ut nos cáritas
Jungat perénni fœ́dere,
Pacémque alens domésticam
Amára vitæ témperet!

Jesu, tuis obédiens
Qui factus es paréntibus,
Cum Patre summo ac Spíritu
Semper tibi sit glória.
Amen.
Hymnus Laudes.eng:
O house of Nazareth the blest,
Fair hostess of the Lord,
The Church was nurtured at Thy breast
And shared thy scanty hoard.

In all the spreading lands of earth
The wandering sun may see
No dearer spot, no ampler worth
Than erst was found in thee!

We know thy humble tenement
Was heaven’s hermitage:
Celestial heralds came and went
In endless embassage.

There, whatsoever Joseph asks
Christ hastens to fulfill;
While Mary loves the household tasks
That wait her joyous will.

There, Joseph toileth at her side
Her joys and griefs to share,
With thousand ties knit to his bride,
Of love and work and prayer.

Yet how their bosoms constant burn
And deeper ardors prove
In love of Christ, whose eyes return
Tokens of mutual love.

O then, in all the homes of earth,
Be Love the bond of life:
May it enthrone at every hearth
The peace that husheth strife.

All praise to Thee, O Jesus,
who parents dost obey;
Praise to the sovereign Father
and Paraclete for aye.
Amen.

Hymnus Matutinum.label: Hymn
Hymnus Matutinum.title: Sacra jam splendent decoráta lychnis
Hymnus Matutinum.lat:
Sacra jam splendent decoráta lychnis
Templa, jam sertis redimítur ara,
Et pio fumant redoléntque acérræ
Thuris honóre.

Num juvet Summo Géniti Parénte
Régios ortus celebráre cantu?
Num domus David, décora et vetústæ
Nómina gentis?

Grátius nobis memoráre parvum
Názaræ tectum, tenuémque cultum;
Grátius Jesu tácitam reférre
Cármine vitam.

Nili ab extrémis peregrínus oris,
Angeli ductu, própere remígrat
Multa perpéssus Puer, et patérno
Límine sospes,

Arte, qua Joseph, húmili excoléndus
Abdito Jesus juvenéscit ævo,
Seque fabrílis sócium labóris
Adicit ultro.

Irriget sudor mea membra, dixit,
Antequam sparso mádeant cruóre:
Hæc quoque humáno géneri expiándo
Pœna luátur.

Assidet Nato pia Mater almo,
Assidet Sponso bona nupta, felix
Si potest curas releváre fessis
Múnere amíco.

O neque expértes óperæ et labóris,
Nec mali ignári, míseros juváte,
Quos reluctántes per acúta rerum
Urget egéstas.

Démite his fastus, quibus ampla splendet
Fáustitas, mentem date rebus æquam:
Quotquot implórant cólumen, benígno
Cérnite vultu.

Sit tibi, Jesu, decus atque virtus,
Sancta qui vitæ documénta præbes,
Quique cum summo Genitóre et almo
Flámine regnas.
Amen.
Hymnus Matutinum.eng:
A thousand lights their glory shed
On shrines and altars garlanded;
While swinging censers dusk the air
With perfumed prayer.

And shall we sing the ancestry
Of Jesus, Son of God most High?
Or the heroic names retrace
Of David’s race?

Sweeter is lowly Nazareth,
Where Jesus drew His childish breath—
Sweeter the singing that endears
His hidden years.

An Angel leads the pilgrim band
From Egypt to their native land,
Where Jesus clings to Joseph’s arm,
Secure from harm.

“And the Child grew in wisdom’s ken
And years and grace with God and men;”
And in His father’s humble art
Took share and part.

“With toil”, saith He, “my limbs are wet,
Prefiguring the Bloody Sweat:”
Ah! how He bears our chastisement
With sweet content!

At Joseph’s bench, at Jesus’ side,
The Mother sits, the Virgin-Bride;
Happy, if she may cheer their hearts
With loving arts.

O Blessed Three! who felt the sting
Of want and toil and suffering,
Pity the needy and obscure
Lot of the poor.

Banish the “pride of life” from all
Whom ampler wealth and joys befall:
Be every heart with love repaid
That seeks your aid.

Glory to Thee, Jesu dear,
Model of holy living here!
Who reign’st, with Sire and Holy Ghost,
O’er heaven’s host.
Amen.

Hymnus Vespera.label: Hymn
Hymnus Vespera.title: O lux beáta cǽlitum
Hymnus Vespera.lat:
O lux beáta cǽlitum
Et summa spes mortálium,
Jesu, o cui doméstica
Arrísit orto cáritas:

María, dives grátia,
O sola quæ casto potes
Fovére Jesum péctore,
Cum lacte donans óscula:

Tuque ex vetústis pátribus
Delécte custos Vírginis
Dulci patris quem nómine
Divína Proles ínvocat:

De stirpe Jesse nóbili
Nati in salútem géntium,
Audíte nos qui súpplices
Vestras ad aras sístimus.

Dum sol redux ad vésperum
Rebus nitórem détrahit,
Nos hic manéntes íntimo
Ex corde vota fúndimus.

Qua vestra sedes flóruit
Virtútis omnis grátia,
Hanc detur in domésticis
Reférre posse móribus.

Jesu, tuis obédiens
Qui factus es paréntibus,
Cum Patre summo ac Spíritu
Semper tibi sit glória.
Amen.
Hymnus Vespera.eng:
O highest hope of mortals,
Blest Light of Saints above,
O Jesu, on whose boyhood
Home smiled with kindly love;

And thou whose bosom nursed him,
O Mary, highly graced,
Whose breast gave milk to Jesus,
Whose arms thy God embraced;

And thou of all men chosen
To guard the Virgin’s fame,
To whom God’s Son refused not
A Father’s gracious name;

Born for the nation’s healing,
Of Jesse’s lineage high,
Behold the suppliants kneeling,
O hear the sinners’ cry!

The sun returned to evening,
Dusks all the twilight air:
We, lingering here before you,
Pour out our heartfelt prayer.

Your home was as a garden
Made glad with fairest flowers;
May life thus blossom sweetly
In every home of ours.

All praise to Thee, O Jesus,
who parents dost obey;
Praise to the sovereign Father
and Paraclete for aye.
Amen.

Nocturn 1 Versum.lat: ℣. Propter nos egénus factus est cum esset dives.
Nocturn 1 Versum.latR: ℟. Ut illíus inópia nos dívites essémus.
Nocturn 1 Versum.eng: ℣. He was rich, yet for our sakes he became poor.
Nocturn 1 Versum.engR: ℟. That we through his poverty might be rich.

Nocturn 2 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 2 Versum.lat: ℣. Dóminus vias suas docébit nos.
Nocturn 2 Versum.eng: ℣. The Lord shall teach us of his ways.
Nocturn 2 Versum.engR: ℟. And we will walk in his paths.

Nocturn 3 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 3 Versum.lat: ℣. Pauper sum ego, et in labóribus a juventúte mea.
Nocturn 3 Versum.latR: ℟. Exaltátus autem humiliátus sum, et conturbátus.
Nocturn 3 Versum.eng: ℣. I am poor and needy, and in agony from my youth up.
Nocturn 3 Versum.engR: ℟. Thy terrors have I suffered with a troubled mind.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Dómine Jesu Christe, qui, Maríæ et Joseph súbditus, domésticam vitam ineffabílibus virtútibus consecrásti: fac nos, utriúsque auxílio, Famíliæ sanctæ tuæ exémplis ínstrui; et consórtium cónsequi sempitérnum:
Oratio.eng: Lord Jesus Christ, who subject to Mary and Joseph, didst consecrate family life by thy unspeakable virtues, aid us by their united intercession to profit by the examples of thy Holy Family, and attain to their everlasting companionship:

Responsory Breve Nona.label: Responsorium Breve
Responsory Breve Nona.lat:
℟.br. Pauper sum ego, * Et in labóribus a juventúte mea.
℣. Exaltátus autem, humiliátus sum et conturbátus.
℟. Et in labóribus a juventúte mea.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Pauper sum ego, * Et in labóribus a juventúte mea.
Responsory Breve Nona.eng:
℟.br. I am poor, and in labours * from my youth.
℣. And being exalted have been humbled and troubled.
℟. From my youth.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. I am poor, and in labours * from my youth.

Responsory Breve Sexta.label: Responsorium Breve
Responsory Breve Sexta.lat:
℟.br. Dóminus vias suas * Docébit nos.
℣. Et ambulábimus in sémitis ejus.
℟. Docébit nos.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Dóminus vias suas * Docébit nos.
Responsory Breve Sexta.eng:
℟.br. The Lord * Will teach us his ways.
℣. And we will walk in his paths.
℟. Will teach us his ways.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. The Lord * Will teach us his ways.

Responsory Breve Tertia.label: Responsorium Breve
Responsory Breve Tertia.lat:
℟.br. Propter nos egénus factus est * Cum esset dives.
℣. Ut illíus inópia nos dívites essémus.
℟. Cum esset dives.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Propter nos egénus factus est * Cum esset dives.
Responsory Breve Tertia.eng:
℟.br. For our sake he became poor, * Being rich.
℣. That through his poverty we might be rich.
℟. Being rich.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. For our sake he became poor, * Being rich.

Ant Laudes.ant: Post tríduum * invenérunt Jesum in templo sedéntem in médio doctórum, audiéntem illos, et interrogántem eos.
Ant Laudes.antEng: After three days, * they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the doctors, hearing them, and asking them questions.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dixit mater Jesu * ad illum: Fili, quid fecísti nobis sic? Ecce pater tuus et ego doléntes quærebámus te.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The mother of Jesus said * to him: Son, why hast thou done so to us? Behold thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing.

Ant Laudes.ant: Descéndit Jesus * cum eis, et venit Názareth, et erat súbditus illis.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Jesus went down * with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subject to them.

Ant Laudes.ant: Et Jesus proficiébat * sapiéntia, et ætáte, et grátia apud Deum et hómines.
Ant Laudes.antEng: And Jesus advanced * in wisdom, and age, and grace with God and men.

Ant Laudes.ant: Et dicébant: * Unde huic sapiéntia hæc, et virtútes? Nonne hic est fabri fílius?
Ant Laudes.antEng: And they said: * How came this man by this wisdom and miracles? Is not this the carpenter's son?

Ant Matutinum.ant: Cum indúcerent * púerum Jesum paréntes ejus, accépit eum Símeon in ulnas suas, et benedíxit Deum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: When his parents * brought the Child Jesus, then Simeon took him up in his arms, and blessed God.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ut perfecérunt * ómnia secúndum legem Dómini, revérsi sunt in Galilǽam in civitátem suam Názareth.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: When they had performed * all things according to the Law of the Lord, they returned into Galilee, to their own city Nazareth.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Puer autem * crescébat, et confortabátur plenus sapiéntia, et grátia Dei erat in illo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: And the Child grew, * and waxed strong in spirit, filled with wisdom, and the grace of God was upon him.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Consúrgens Joseph * accépit púerum et matrem ejus nocte, et secéssit in Ægýptum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: When Joseph arose, * he took the young Child and his Mother by night, and departed into Egypt.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Angelus Dómini * appáruit in somnis Joseph in Ægýpto, dicens: Surge et áccipe púerum et matrem ejus, et vade in terram Israël.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: And the Angel of the Lord * said in a dream to Joseph in Egypt, Arise, and take the young Child and his Mother, and go into the land of Israel.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Et véniens * habitávit Názareth, ut adimplerétur quod dictum est per Prophétas: Quóniam Nazarǽus vocábitur.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: And he came * and dwelt in a city called Nazareth, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Prophets: He shall be called a Nazarene.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ibant paréntes Jesu * per omnes annos in Jerúsalem in die solémni Paschæ.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Now the parents of Jesus * went to Jerusalem every year at the Feast of the Passover.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Cum redírent, * remánsit puer Jesus in Jerúsalem, et non cognovérunt paréntes ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: And when they returned, * the Child Jesus tarried behind in Jerusalem, and his parents knew not of it.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Non inveniéntes Jesum * regréssi sunt in Jerúsalem, requiréntes eum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: But when they found him not, * they turned back again to Jerusalem, seeking him.

Ant Vespera.ant: Jacob autem * génuit Joseph virum Maríæ; de qua natus est Jesus, qui vocátur Christus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: And Jacob * begot Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.

Ant Vespera.ant: Angelus Dómini * appáruit in somnis Joseph, dicens: Joseph, fili David, noli timére accípere Maríam cónjugem tuam; quod enim in ea natum est, de Spíritu Sancto est.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The angel of the Lord * appeared to Joseph in his sleep, saying: Joseph, son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife, for that which is conceived in her, is of the Holy Ghost.

Ant Vespera.ant: Pastóres venérunt * festinántes, et invenérunt Maríam, et Joseph, et Infántem pósitum in præsépio.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The shepherds came * with haste; and they found Mary and Joseph, and the infant lying in the manger.

Ant Vespera.ant: Magi, intrántes domum, * invenérunt Púerum cum María, matre ejus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The Magi, entering into the house, * found the child with Mary his mother.

Ant Vespera.ant: Erat Pater ejus * et Mater mirántes super his quæ dicebántur de illo.
Ant Vespera.antEng: His father * and mother were wondering at those things which were spoken concerning him.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Post tríduum * invenérunt Jesum in templo sedéntem in médio doctórum, audiéntem illos, et interrogántem eos.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: After three days, * they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the doctors, hearing them, and asking them questions.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Dixit mater Jesu * ad illum: Fili, quid fecísti nobis sic? Ecce pater tuus et ego doléntes quærebámus te.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: The mother of Jesus said * to him: Son, why hast thou done so to us? Behold thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Descéndit Jesus * cum eis, et venit Názareth, et erat súbditus illis.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: Jesus went down * with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subject to them.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Et Jesus proficiébat * sapiéntia, et ætate, et grátia apud Deum et hómines.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: And Jesus advanced * in wisdom, and age, and grace with God and men.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Et dicébant: * Unde huic sapiéntia hæc, et virtútes? Nonne hic est fabri fílius?
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: And they said: * How came this man by this wisdom and miracles? Is not this the carpenter's son?

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Remánsit puer Jesus * in Jerúsalem, et non cognovérunt paréntes ejus existimántes illum esse in comitátu: et requirébant eum inter cognátos et notos.
Ant 1.eng: The child Jesus * remained in Jerusalem; and his parents knew it not. And thinking that he was in the company, they came a day's journey, and sought him among their kinsfolks and acquaintance.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Remánsit puer Jesus * in Jerúsalem, et non cognovérunt paréntes ejus existimántes illum esse in comitátu: et requirébant eum inter cognátos et notos.
Ant 2.eng: The child Jesus * remained in Jerusalem; and his parents knew it not. And thinking that he was in the company, they came a day's journey, and sought him among their kinsfolks and acquaintance.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Fili, quid fecísti * nobis sic? Ego et pater tuus doléntes quærebámus te. Quid est quod me quærebátis? nesciebátis quia in iis, quæ Patris mei sunt, opórtet me esse?
Ant 3.eng: Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? Behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing. How is it that ye sought me? Wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Fratres: Obsécro vos per misericórdiam Dei, ut exhibeátis córpora vestra hóstiam vivéntem, sanctam, Deo placéntem, rationábile obséquium vestrum.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Brethren: I Beseech you, by the mercy of God, that you present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, pleasing unto God, your reasonable service

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Sicut enim in uno córpore multa membra habémus ómnia autem membra non eundem actum habent: ita multi unum corpus sumus in Christo sínguli autem alter altérius membra in Christo Jesu Dómino nostro.
Capitulum Nona.eng: For as in one body we have many members, but all the members have not the same office: So we being many, are one body in Christ, and every one members one of another.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Dico enim per grátiam quæ data est mihi ómnibus qui sunt inter vos non plus sápere quam opórtet sápere sed sápere ad sobrietátem unicuíque sicut Deus divísit mensúram fídei.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: For I say, by the grace that is given me, to all that are among you, not to be more wise than it behoveth to be wise, but to be wise unto sobriety, and according as God hath divided to every one the measure of faith

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Vota, quǽsumus, Dómine, supplicántis pópuli cælésti pietáte proséquere: ut et quæ agénda sunt, vídeant, et ad implénda quæ víderint, convaléscant.
Oratio.eng: Attend, O Lord, we beseech thee, of thy heavenly mercy, to the desires of thy suppliant people; and grant that they may both perceive what they ought to do, and may have strength to fulfill the same.
