Doxology.lat:
Jesu, tuis obédiens
Qui factus es paréntibus,
Cum Patre summo ac Spíritu
Semper tibi sit glória.
Amen.

Hymnus Laudes.label: Hymn
Hymnus Laudes.title: O gente felix hóspita
Hymnus Laudes.lat:
O gente felix hóspita,
Augústa sedes Názaræ,
Quæ fovit alma Ecclésiæ
Et prótulit primórdia.

Sol, qui perérrat áureo
Terras jacéntes lúmine,
Nil grátius per sǽcula
Hac vidit æde, aut sánctius.

Ad hanc frequéntes cónvolant
Cæléstis aulæ núntii,
Virtútis hoc sacrárium
Visunt, revísunt, éxcolunt.

Qua mente Jesus, qua manu,
Optáta patris pérficit!
Quo Virgo gestit gáudio
Matérna obíre múnera!

Adest amóris párticeps
Curǽque Joseph cónjugi,
Quos mille jungit néxibus
Virtútis auctor grátia.

Hi diligéntes ínvicem
In Jesu amórem cónfluunt,
Utríque Jesus mútuæ
Dat caritátis prǽmia.

Sic fiat, ut nos cáritas
Jungat perénni fœ́dere,
Pacémque alens domésticam
Amára vitæ témperet!

Jesu, tuis obédiens
Qui factus es paréntibus,
Cum Patre summo ac Spíritu
Semper tibi sit glória.
Amen.
Hymnus Laudes.eng:
O house of Nazareth the blest,
Fair hostess of the Lord,
The Church was nurtured at Thy breast
And shared thy scanty hoard.

In all the spreading lands of earth
The wandering sun may see
No dearer spot, no ampler worth
Than erst was found in thee!

We know thy humble tenement
Was heaven’s hermitage:
Celestial heralds came and went
In endless embassage.

There, whatsoever Joseph asks
Christ hastens to fulfill;
While Mary loves the household tasks
That wait her joyous will.

There, Joseph toileth at her side
Her joys and griefs to share,
With thousand ties knit to his bride,
Of love and work and prayer.

Yet how their bosoms constant burn
And deeper ardors prove
In love of Christ, whose eyes return
Tokens of mutual love.

O then, in all the homes of earth,
Be Love the bond of life:
May it enthrone at every hearth
The peace that husheth strife.

All praise to Thee, O Jesus,
who parents dost obey;
Praise to the sovereign Father
and Paraclete for aye.
Amen.

Hymnus Matutinum.label: Hymn
Hymnus Matutinum.title: Sacra jam splendent decoráta lychnis
Hymnus Matutinum.lat:
Sacra jam splendent decoráta lychnis
Templa, jam sertis redimítur ara,
Et pio fumant redoléntque acérræ
Thuris honóre.

Num juvet Summo Géniti Parénte
Régios ortus celebráre cantu?
Num domus David, décora et vetústæ
Nómina gentis?

Grátius nobis memoráre parvum
Názaræ tectum, tenuémque cultum;
Grátius Jesu tácitam reférre
Cármine vitam.

Nili ab extrémis peregrínus oris,
Angeli ductu, própere remígrat
Multa perpéssus Puer, et patérno
Límine sospes,

Arte, qua Joseph, húmili excoléndus
Abdito Jesus juvenéscit ævo,
Seque fabrílis sócium labóris
Adicit ultro.

Irriget sudor mea membra, dixit,
Antequam sparso mádeant cruóre:
Hæc quoque humáno géneri expiándo
Pœna luátur.

Assidet Nato pia Mater almo,
Assidet Sponso bona nupta, felix
Si potest curas releváre fessis
Múnere amíco.

O neque expértes óperæ et labóris,
Nec mali ignári, míseros juváte,
Quos reluctántes per acúta rerum
Urget egéstas.

Démite his fastus, quibus ampla splendet
Fáustitas, mentem date rebus æquam:
Quotquot implórant cólumen, benígno
Cérnite vultu.

Sit tibi, Jesu, decus atque virtus,
Sancta qui vitæ documénta præbes,
Quique cum summo Genitóre et almo
Flámine regnas.
Amen.
Hymnus Matutinum.eng:
A thousand lights their glory shed
On shrines and altars garlanded;
While swinging censers dusk the air
With perfumed prayer.

And shall we sing the ancestry
Of Jesus, Son of God most High?
Or the heroic names retrace
Of David’s race?

Sweeter is lowly Nazareth,
Where Jesus drew His childish breath—
Sweeter the singing that endears
His hidden years.

An Angel leads the pilgrim band
From Egypt to their native land,
Where Jesus clings to Joseph’s arm,
Secure from harm.

“And the Child grew in wisdom’s ken
And years and grace with God and men;”
And in His father’s humble art
Took share and part.

“With toil”, saith He, “my limbs are wet,
Prefiguring the Bloody Sweat:”
Ah! how He bears our chastisement
With sweet content!

At Joseph’s bench, at Jesus’ side,
The Mother sits, the Virgin-Bride;
Happy, if she may cheer their hearts
With loving arts.

O Blessed Three! who felt the sting
Of want and toil and suffering,
Pity the needy and obscure
Lot of the poor.

Banish the “pride of life” from all
Whom ampler wealth and joys befall:
Be every heart with love repaid
That seeks your aid.

Glory to Thee, Jesu dear,
Model of holy living here!
Who reign’st, with Sire and Holy Ghost,
O’er heaven’s host.
Amen.

Hymnus Vespera.label: Hymn
Hymnus Vespera.title: O lux beáta cǽlitum
Hymnus Vespera.lat:
O lux beáta cǽlitum
Et summa spes mortálium,
Jesu, o cui doméstica
Arrísit orto cáritas:

María, dives grátia,
O sola quæ casto potes
Fovére Jesum péctore,
Cum lacte donans óscula:

Tuque ex vetústis pátribus
Delécte custos Vírginis
Dulci patris quem nómine
Divína Proles ínvocat:

De stirpe Jesse nóbili
Nati in salútem géntium,
Audíte nos qui súpplices
Vestras ad aras sístimus.

Dum sol redux ad vésperum
Rebus nitórem détrahit,
Nos hic manéntes íntimo
Ex corde vota fúndimus.

Qua vestra sedes flóruit
Virtútis omnis grátia,
Hanc detur in domésticis
Reférre posse móribus.

Jesu, tuis obédiens
Qui factus es paréntibus,
Cum Patre summo ac Spíritu
Semper tibi sit glória.
Amen.
Hymnus Vespera.eng:
O highest hope of mortals,
Blest Light of Saints above,
O Jesu, on whose boyhood
Home smiled with kindly love;

And thou whose bosom nursed him,
O Mary, highly graced,
Whose breast gave milk to Jesus,
Whose arms thy God embraced;

And thou of all men chosen
To guard the Virgin’s fame,
To whom God’s Son refused not
A Father’s gracious name;

Born for the nation’s healing,
Of Jesse’s lineage high,
Behold the suppliants kneeling,
O hear the sinners’ cry!

The sun returned to evening,
Dusks all the twilight air:
We, lingering here before you,
Pour out our heartfelt prayer.

Your home was as a garden
Made glad with fairest flowers;
May life thus blossom sweetly
In every home of ours.

All praise to Thee, O Jesus,
who parents dost obey;
Praise to the sovereign Father
and Paraclete for aye.
Amen.

Nocturn 3 Versum.eng: ℣. I am poor and needy, and in agony from my youth up.
Nocturn 3 Versum.engR: ℟. Thy terrors have I suffered with a troubled mind.

Oratio.lat: Dómine Jesu Christe, qui, Maríæ et Joseph súbditus, domésticam vitam ineffabílibus virtútibus consecrásti: fac nos, utriúsque auxílio, Famíliæ sanctæ tuæ exémplis ínstrui; et consórtium cónsequi sempitérnum:
Oratio.eng: Lord Jesus Christ, who subject to Mary and Joseph, didst consecrate family life by thy unspeakable virtues, aid us by their united intercession to profit by the examples of thy Holy Family, and attain to their everlasting companionship:

Responsory Breve Tertia.label: Responsorium Breve

℟. For our sake he became poor, * Being rich.

Ant Laudes.ant: Post tríduum * invenérunt Jesum in templo sedéntem in médio doctórum, audiéntem illos, et interrogántem eos.
Ant Laudes.antEng: After three days, * they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the doctors, hearing them, and asking them questions.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dixit mater Jesu * ad illum: Fili, quid fecísti nobis sic? Ecce pater tuus et ego doléntes quærebámus te.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The mother of Jesus said * to him: Son, why hast thou done so to us? Behold thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing.

Ant Laudes.ant: Descéndit Jesus * cum eis, et venit Názareth, et erat súbditus illis.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Jesus went down * with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subject to them.

Ant Laudes.ant: Et Jesus proficiébat * sapiéntia, et ætáte, et grátia apud Deum et hómines.
Ant Laudes.antEng: And Jesus advanced * in wisdom, and age, and grace with God and men.

Ant Laudes.ant: Et dicébant: * Unde huic sapiéntia hæc, et virtútes? Nonne hic est fabri fílius?
Ant Laudes.antEng: And they said: * How came this man by this wisdom and miracles? Is not this the carpenter's son?

Ant Matutinum.ant: Cum indúcerent * púerum Jesum paréntes ejus, accépit eum Símeon in ulnas suas, et benedíxit Deum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: When his parents * brought the Child Jesus, then Simeon took him up in his arms, and blessed God.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ut perfecérunt * ómnia secúndum legem Dómini, revérsi sunt in Galilǽam in civitátem suam Názareth.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: When they had performed * all things according to the Law of the Lord, they returned into Galilee, to their own city Nazareth.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Puer autem * crescébat, et confortabátur plenus sapiéntia, et grátia Dei erat in illo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: And the Child grew, * and waxed strong in spirit, filled with wisdom, and the grace of God was upon him.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Consúrgens Joseph * accépit púerum et matrem ejus nocte, et secéssit in Ægýptum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: When Joseph arose, * he took the young Child and his Mother by night, and departed into Egypt.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Angelus Dómini * appáruit in somnis Joseph in Ægýpto, dicens: Surge et áccipe púerum et matrem ejus, et vade in terram Israël.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: And the Angel of the Lord * said in a dream to Joseph in Egypt, Arise, and take the young Child and his Mother, and go into the land of Israel.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Et véniens * habitávit Názareth, ut adimplerétur quod dictum est per Prophétas: Quóniam Nazarǽus vocábitur.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: And he came * and dwelt in a city called Nazareth, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Prophets: He shall be called a Nazarene.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ibant paréntes Jesu * per omnes annos in Jerúsalem in die solémni Paschæ.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Now the parents of Jesus * went to Jerusalem every year at the Feast of the Passover.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Cum redírent, * remánsit puer Jesus in Jerúsalem, et non cognovérunt paréntes ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: And when they returned, * the Child Jesus tarried behind in Jerusalem, and his parents knew not of it.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Non inveniéntes Jesum * regréssi sunt in Jerúsalem, requiréntes eum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: But when they found him not, * they turned back again to Jerusalem, seeking him.

Ant Vespera.ant: Jacob autem * génuit Joseph virum Maríæ; de qua natus est Jesus, qui vocátur Christus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: And Jacob * begot Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.

Ant Vespera.ant: Angelus Dómini * appáruit in somnis Joseph, dicens: Joseph, fili David, noli timére accípere Maríam cónjugem tuam; quod enim in ea natum est, de Spíritu Sancto est.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The angel of the Lord * appeared to Joseph in his sleep, saying: Joseph, son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife, for that which is conceived in her, is of the Holy Ghost.

Ant Vespera.ant: Pastóres venérunt * festinántes, et invenérunt Maríam, et Joseph, et Infántem pósitum in præsépio.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The shepherds came * with haste; and they found Mary and Joseph, and the infant lying in the manger.

Ant Vespera.ant: Magi, intrántes domum, * invenérunt Púerum cum María, matre ejus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The Magi, entering into the house, * found the child with Mary his mother.

Ant Vespera.ant: Erat Pater ejus * et Mater mirántes super his quæ dicebántur de illo.
Ant Vespera.antEng: His father * and mother were wondering at those things which were spoken concerning him.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Jacob autem * génuit Joseph virum Maríæ; de qua natus est Jesus, qui vocátur Christus.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: And Jacob * begot Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Angelus Dómini * appáruit in somnis Joseph, dicens: Joseph, fili David, noli timére accípere Maríam cónjugem tuam; quod enim in ea natum est, de Spíritu Sancto est.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: The angel of the Lord * appeared to Joseph in his sleep, saying: Joseph, son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife, for that which is conceived in her, is of the Holy Ghost.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Pastóres venérunt * festinántes, et invenérunt Maríam, et Joseph, et Infántem pósitum in præsépio.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: The shepherds came * with haste; and they found Mary and Joseph, and the infant lying in the manger.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Magi, intrántes domum, * invenérunt Púerum cum María, matre ejus.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: The Magi, entering into the house, * found the child with Mary his mother.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Erat Pater ejus * et Mater mirántes super his quæ dicebántur de illo.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: His father * and mother were wondering at those things which were spoken concerning him.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Suscépit Deus * Israël, púerum suum: sicut locútus est ad Abraham, et semen ejus usque in sǽculum.
Ant 1.eng: God hath received * Israel his servant, as he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed for ever.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon

Oratio.eng: Almighty and eternal God, as thou govern all things in heaven and on earth; in thy mercy hear the supplication of thy people, and grant thy peace in our times.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Cum descendísset Jesus * de monte, ecce leprósus véniens adorábat eum, dicens: Dómine, si vis, potes me mundáre: et exténdens manum, tétigit eum, dicens: Volo, mundáre.
Ant 2.eng: When Jesus was come down from the mountain, * behold, there came a leper, and worshipped Him, saying: Lord, if Thou wilt, Thou canst make me clean. And Jesus put forth His Hand, and touched him, saying: I will; be thou clean.

Ant 3.eng: Lord, if Thou wilt, * Thou canst make me clean; and Jesus saith to him: I will; be thou clean.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Ascendénte Jesu * in navículam, ecce motus magnus factus est in mari: et suscitavérunt eum discípuli ejus, dicéntes: Dómine, salva nos, perímus.
Ant 2.eng: When Jesus was entered into a ship, * there arose a great tempest in the sea and His disciples awoke Him, saying: Lord, save us; we perish.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Dómine, salva nos, * perímus: ímpera, et fac, Deus, tranquillitátem.
Ant 3.eng: Lord, save us: * we perish; give the word, O God, and let there be a great calm!

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui nos in tantis perículis constitútos, pro humána scis fragilitáte non posse subsístere: da nobis salútem mentis et córporis; ut ea, quæ pro peccátis nostris pátimur, te adjuvánte vincámus.
Oratio.eng: O God, Who knowest us to be set in the midst of so many and great dangers, that, by reason of the frailty of our nature, we cannot always stand upright; grant to us such health of mind and body, that by thy strength and protection we may overcome all evils, whereby for our sins we are justly afflicted.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Dómine, * nonne bonum semen seminásti in agro tuo? unde ergo habet zizánia? Et ait illis: Hoc fecit inimícus homo.
Ant 2.eng: Sir, didst not thou sow good seed in thy field? * From whence then hath it tares? And he saith unto them: An enemy hath done this.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Collígite * primum zizánia, et alligáte ea in fascículos ad comburéndum: tríticum autem congregáte in hórreum meum, dicit Dóminus.
Ant 3.eng: The master saith: Gather ye together first the tares, * and bind them in bundles to burn them; but gather the wheat into my barn.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Famíliam tuam, quǽsumus, Dómine, contínua pietáte custódi: ut, quæ in sola spe grátiæ cœléstis innítitur, tua semper protectióne muniátur.
Oratio.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee to keep thy family continually in godliness, that they who do lean only upon the hope of thine heavenly grace, may evermore be defended by thy mighty power.

Ant 2.lat: Símile est * regnum cælórum grano sinápis, quod mínimum est ómnibus semínibus: cum autem créverit, majus est ómnibus oléribus.
Ant 2.eng: The kingdom of heaven * is like to a grain of mustard-seed, which is the least of all seeds, but, when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Símile est * regnum cælórum ferménto, quod accéptum múlier abscóndit in farínæ satis tribus, donec fermentátum est totum.
Ant 3.eng: The kingdom of heaven * is like unto leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal till the whole was leavened.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Dum médium siléntium * tenérent ómnia, et nox in suo cursu médium iter perágeret, omnípotens Sermo tuus, Dómine, a regálibus sédibus venit, allelúja.
Ant 1.eng: While all things were in quiet silence * and that night was in the midst of her swift course, thine Almighty Word, O Lord, leapt down out of thy Royal Throne.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Dum médium siléntium * tenérent ómnia, et nox in suo cursu médium iter perágeret, omnípotens Sermo tuus, Dómine, a regálibus sédibus venit, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: While all things were in quiet silence * and that night was in the midst of her swift course, thine Almighty Word, O Lord, leapt down out of thy Royal Throne.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Puer Jesus * proficiébat ætáte et sapiéntia coram Deo et homínibus.
Ant 3.eng: And Jesus advanced in wisdom * and age, and grace with God and men.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Fratres: Quanto témpore heres párvulus est, nihil differt a servo, cum sit dóminus ómnium: sed sub tutóribus et actóribus est usque ad præfínitum tempus a patre.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Brothers: As long as the heir is a child, he differeth nothing from a servant, though he be lord of all; But is under tutors and governors until the time appointed by the father.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Itaque jam non est servus, sed fílius: quod si fílius, et hæres per Deum.
Capitulum Nona.eng: Therefore now he is not a servant, but a son. And if a son, an heir also through God.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: At ubi venit plenitúdo témporis, misit Deus Fílium suum factum ex mulíere, factum sub lege, ut eos, qui sub lege erant, redímeret, ut adoptiónem filiórum reciperémus.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent his Son, made of a woman, made under the law: That he might redeem them who were under the law: that we might receive the adoption of sons.

Lectio Prima.label: Lectio brevis
Lectio Prima.lat: Itaque jam non est servus, sed fílius: quod si fílius, et hæres per Deum.
Lectio Prima.eng: Therefore now he is not a servant, but a son. And if a son, an heir also through God.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, dírige actus nostros in beneplácito tuo: ut in nómine dilécti Fílii tui mereámur bonis opéribus abundáre:
Oratio.eng: O Almighty and everlasting God, do Thou order all our actions in conformity with thy good pleasure, that through the name of thy well-beloved Son, we may worthily abound in all good works.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Fecit * mihi magna qui potens est, et sanctum Nomen ejus, allelúja.
Ant 1.eng: He That is mighty * hath done to me great things, and holy is His Name, alleluia.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Dedit se, * ut liberáret pópulum, et acquíreret sibi nomen ætérnum, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: He gave Himself * to deliver His people, and to get Himself an everlasting Name. Alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Vocábis * nomen ejus Jesum; ipse enim salvum fáciet pópulum suum a peccátis eórum, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: Thou shalt call His Name Jesus, * for He shall save His people from their sins, alleluia.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Fratres: Christus humiliávit semetípsum, factus obédiens usque ad mortem, mortem autem crucis. Propter quod et Deus exaltávit illum, et donávit illi nomen, quod est super omne nomen, ut in nómine Jesu omne genu flectátur.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: He humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death, even to the death of the cross. For which cause God also hath exalted him, and hath given him a name which is above all names: That in the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those that are in heaven, on earth, and under the earth.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Omne quodcúmque fácitis in verbo, aut in ópere: ómnia in nómine Dómini Jesu Christi fácite, grátias agéntes Deo et Patri per ipsum.
Capitulum Nona.eng: All whatsoever you do in word or in work, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, giving thanks to God and the Father by him.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: In nómine Jesu omne genu flectátur cæléstium, terréstrium, et infernórum: et omnis lingua confiteátur, quia Dóminus Jesus Christus in glória est Dei Patris.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: That in the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those that are in heaven, on earth, and under the earth: And that every tongue should confess that the Lord Jesus Christ is in the glory of God the Father.

Hymnus Laudes.label: Hymn
Hymnus Laudes.title: Jesu decus angélicum
Hymnus Laudes.lat:
Jesu decus angélicum,
In aure dulce cánticum,
In ore mel miríficum,
In corde nectar cǽlicum.

Qui te gustant, esúriunt;
Qui bibunt, adhuc sítiunt;
Desideráre nésciunt,
Nisi Jesum, quem díligunt.

O Jesu mi dulcíssime,
Spes suspirántis ánimæ!
Te quærunt piæ lácrimæ,
Te clamor mentis íntimæ.

Mane nobíscum, Dómine,
Et nos illústra lúmine;
Pulsa mentis calígine,
Mundum reple dulcédine.

Jesu, flos Matris Vírginis,
Amor nostræ dulcédinis,
Tibi laus, honor nóminis,
Regnum beatitúdinis.
Amen.
Hymnus Laudes.eng:
O Jesu, Thou the Beauty art
Of Angel worlds above;
Thy name is music to the heart,
Enchanting it with love.

Celestial Sweetness unalloyed!
Who eat thee hunger still;
Who drink of thee still feel a void,
Which naught but Thou can fill.

O my sweet Jesu! hear the sigh,
Which unto thee I send;
To thee mine inmost spirit cries
My being's hope and end!

Stay with us, Lord, and with thy light
Illume the soul's abyss;
Scatter the darkness of our night,
And fill the world with bliss.

O Jesu, spotless Virgin flower,
Our life and joy: to thee
Be praise, beatitude, and power,
Through all eternity.
Amen.

Hymnus Matutinum.label: Hymn
Hymnus Matutinum.title: Jesu, Rex admirábilis
Hymnus Matutinum.lat:
Jesu, Rex admirábilis,
Et triumphátor nóbilis,
Dulcédo ineffábilis,
Totus desiderábilis.

Quando cor nostrum vísitas,
Tunc lucet ei véritas,
Mundi viléscit vánitas,
Et intus fervet cáritas.

Jesu, dulcédo córdium,
Fons vivus, lumen méntium,
Excédens omne gáudium,
Et omne desidérium.

Jesum omnes agnóscite,
Amórem ejus póscite:
Jesum ardénter quǽrite,
Quæréndo inardéscite.

Te nostra, Jesu, vox sonet,
Nostri te mores éxprimant,
Te corda nostra díligant,
Et nunc, et in perpétuum.
Amen.
Hymnus Matutinum.eng:
O Jesu, King most wonderful
Thou conqueror renowned,
Thou sweetness most ineffable,
In whom all joys are found!

When once Thou visitest the heart,
Then truth begins to shine;
Then earthly vanities depart;
Then kindles love divine.

O Jesu, light of all below,
Thou fount of life and fire,
Surpassing all the joys we know,
And all we can desire:

May every heart confess thy Name,
And ever thee adore;
And, seeking thee, itself inflame
To seek thee more and more.

Thee may our tongues forever bless;
Thee may we love alone;
And ever in our lives express
The image of thine own.
Amen.

Hymnus Vespera.label: Hymn
Hymnus Vespera.title: Jesu, dulcis memória
Hymnus Vespera.lat:
Jesu, dulcis memória,
Dans vera cordis gáudia:
Sed super mel, et ómnia,
Ejus dulcis præséntia.

Nil cánitur suávius,
Nil audítur jucúndius,
Nil cogitátur dúlcius,
Quam Jesus Dei Fílius.

Jesu, spes pœniténtibus,
Quam pius es peténtibus!
Quam bonus te quæréntibus!
Sed quid inveniéntibus?

Nec lingua valet dícere,
Nec líttera exprímere:
Expértus potest crédere,
Quid sit Jesum dilígere.

Sis, Jesu, nostrum gáudium,
Qui es futúrus prǽmium:
Sit nostra in te glória,
Per cuncta semper sǽcula.
Amen.
Hymnus Vespera.eng:
Jesu, the very thought of thee
With sweetness fills my breast;
But sweeter far thy face to see,
And in thy presence rest.

Nor voice can sing, nor heart can frame,
Nor can the memory find,
A sweeter sound than thy blest Name,
O Saviour of mankind!

O Hope of every contrite heart,
O Joy of all the meek,
To those who fall, how kind Thou art!
How good to those who seek!

But what to those who find? Ah! this
Nor tongue nor pen can show:
The love of Jesus, what it is
None but his loved ones know.

Jesu, our only joy be Thou,
As Thou our prize wilt be;
Jesu, be Thou our glory now,
And through eternity.
Amen.

Invit.label: Antiphon
Invit.lat: Admirábile nomen Jesu, quod est super omne nomen, * Veníte, adorémus.
Invit.eng: The Name which shall be called Wonderful, the Name of Jesus is the Name which is above every name. * O come, let us worship Him.

Lectio Prima.label: Lectio brevis
Lectio Prima.lat: Omne quodcúmque fácitis in verbo, aut in ópere: ómnia in nómine Dómini Jesu Christi fácite, grátias agéntes Deo et Patri per ipsum.
Lectio Prima.eng: All whatsoever you do in word or in work, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, giving thanks to God and the Father by him.

Nocturn 1 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 1 Versum.lat: ℣. Propter nomen tuum, Dómine, propitiáberis peccáto meo.
Nocturn 1 Versum.eng: ℣. For thy Name's sake, O Lord, pardon mine iniquity.
Nocturn 1 Versum.engR: ℟. For it is great.

Nocturn 2 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 2 Versum.lat: ℣. Propter glóriam nóminis tui, Dómine, líbera nos.
Nocturn 2 Versum.latR: ℟. Et propítius esto peccátis nostris propter nomen tuum.
Nocturn 2 Versum.eng: ℣. For the glory of thy Name, deliver us, O Lord.
Nocturn 2 Versum.engR: ℟. And forgive our sins, for thy Name's sake.

Nocturn 3 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 3 Versum.latR: ℟. Afférte Dómino glóriam nómini ejus.
Nocturn 3 Versum.eng: ℣. Give unto the Lord glory and honour.
Nocturn 3 Versum.engR: ℟. Give unto the Lord the glory due unto His Name.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui unigénitum Fílium tuum constituísti humáni géneris Salvatórem, et Jesum vocári jussísti: concéde propítius; ut, cujus sanctum nomen venerámur in terris, ejus quoque aspéctu perfruámur in cælis.
Oratio.eng: O God, Who hast appointed thine Only-begotten Son to be the Saviour of mankind, and hast commanded that His Name should be called Jesus, mercifully grant that we who here on earth do worship that most Holy Name may be made glad in heaven by His Presence.

℟.br. O magnify the Lord with me, * Alleluia, alleluia.

℟. Alleluia, alleluia.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. O magnify the Lord with me, * Alleluia, alleluia.

℟. Afférte Dómino glóriam et honórem, * Allelúja, allelúja.

℟.br. Give unto the Lord glory and honour, * Alleluia, alleluia.
℣. Give unto the Lord the glory due unto His Name.
℟. Alleluia, alleluia.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. Give unto the Lord glory and honour, * Alleluia, alleluia.

Responsory Breve Tertia.label: Responsorium Breve
Responsory Breve Tertia.lat:
℟.br. Sit nomen Dómini benedíctum, * Allelúja, allelúja.
℣. Ex hoc nunc et usque in sǽculum.
℟. Allelúja, allelúja.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Sit nomen Dómini benedíctum, * Allelúja, allelúja.

℟. Blessed be the Name of the Lord, * Alleluia, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Oleum effúsum * nomen tuum, ídeo adolescéntulæ dilexérunt te.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Thy Name is as oil * poured forth, therefore do the virgins love thee.

Ant Laudes.ant: Scitóte, * quia Dóminus ipse est Deus, cujus nomen in ætérnum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Know ye that the Lord He is God, * and His Name endureth for ever.

Ant Laudes.ant: Sitívit * ánima mea ad nomen sanctum tuum, Dómine.
Ant Laudes.antEng: My soul thirsteth * for thy Holy Name, O Lord.

Ant Laudes.ant: Benedíctum * nomen glóriæ tuæ sanctum, et laudábile, et superexaltátum in sǽcula.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Blessed * is the Holy Name of thy glory, and worthy to be praised, and exalted above all for ever.

Ant Laudes.ant: Júvenes et vírgines, * senes cum junióribus laudáte nomen Dómini, quia exaltátum est nomen ejus solíus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Young men and maidens, * old men and children, praise the Name of the Lord, for His Name alone is exalted.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O Lord our Lord, * how admirable is thy name in the whole earth!

Ant Matutinum.ant: In nómine Jesu * omne genu flectátur cæléstium, terréstrium, et infernórum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: At the Name of Jesus, * let every knee bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Confitémini * Dómino, et invocáte nomen ejus: mementóte, quóniam excélsum est nomen ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Praise the Lord, * and call upon His Name; remember that His Name is exalted.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Mémores erunt * nóminis tui, Dómine, in omni generatióne et generatiónem.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: They shall be mindful * of thy Name, O Lord, unto all generations.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Magnificáte * Dóminum mecum, et exaltémus nomen ejus in idípsum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O magnify * the Lord with me, and let us exalt His Name together.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Omnes gentes, * quascúmque fecísti, vénient, et adorábunt coram te, Dómine, et glorificábunt nomen tuum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: All nations * whom Thou hast made, shall come and worship before thee, O Lord, and shall glorify thy Name.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Cantáte Dómino * et benedícite nómini ejus: annuntiáte de die in diem salutáre ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Sing unto the Lord, * and bless His Name show forth His salvation from day to day.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Secúndum nomen tuum, * Deus, sic et laus tua in fines terræ: justítia plena est déxtera tua.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: According to thy Name, O God, * so is thy praise unto the ends of the earth; thy right hand is full of righteousness.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Cantáte Deo, * psalmum dícite nómini ejus: iter fácite ei, qui ascéndit super occásum, Dóminus nomen illi.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Sing unto God, * sing praises to His Name; spread a path before Him That rideth upon the heavens the Lord is His Name.

Ant Vespera.ant: Omnis * qui invocáverit nomen Dómini, salvus erit.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Whosoever shall call * on the name of the Lord shall be saved.

Ant Vespera.ant: Sanctum et terríbile * nomen ejus, inítium sapiéntiæ timor Dómini.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Holy and terrible * is His Name; the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.

Ant Vespera.ant: Ego autem * in Dómino gaudébo, et exsultábo in Deo Jesu meo.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Yet will I rejoice * in the Lord I will joy in the God of my salvation.

Ant Vespera.ant: A solis ortu * usque ad occásum laudábile nomen Dómini.
Ant Vespera.antEng: From the rising of the sun * unto the going down of the same the Lord's Name is to be praised.

Ant Vespera.ant: Sacrificábo * hóstiam laudis, et nomen Dómini invocábo.
Ant Vespera.antEng: I will offer * the sacrifice of thanksgiving, and will call upon the Name of the Lord.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Fecit * mihi magna qui potens est, et sanctum Nomen ejus, allelúja.
Ant 1.eng: He That is mighty * hath done to me great things, and holy is His Name, alleluia.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Dedit se, * ut liberáret pópulum, et acquíreret sibi nomen ætérnum, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: He gave Himself * to deliver His people, and to get Himself an everlasting Name. Alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Vocábis * nomen ejus Jesum; ipse enim salvum fáciet pópulum suum a peccátis eórum, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: Thou shalt call His Name Jesus, * for He shall save His people from their sins, alleluia.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Fratres: Christus humiliávit semetípsum, factus obédiens usque ad mortem, mortem autem crucis. Propter quod et Deus exaltávit illum, et donávit illi nomen, quod est super omne nomen, ut in nómine Jesu omne genu flectátur.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: He humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death, even to the death of the cross. For which cause God also hath exalted him, and hath given him a name which is above all names: That in the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those that are in heaven, on earth, and under the earth.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Omne quodcúmque fácitis in verbo, aut in ópere: ómnia in nómine Dómini Jesu Christi fácite, grátias agéntes Deo et Patri per ipsum.
Capitulum Nona.eng: All whatsoever you do in word or in work, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, giving thanks to God and the Father by him.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: In nómine Jesu omne genu flectátur cæléstium, terréstrium, et infernórum: et omnis lingua confiteátur, quia Dóminus Jesus Christus in glória est Dei Patris.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: That in the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those that are in heaven, on earth, and under the earth: And that every tongue should confess that the Lord Jesus Christ is in the glory of God the Father.

Hymnus Laudes.label: Hymn
Hymnus Laudes.title: Jesu decus angélicum
Hymnus Laudes.lat:
Jesu decus angélicum,
In aure dulce cánticum,
In ore mel miríficum,
In corde nectar cǽlicum.

Qui te gustant, esúriunt;
Qui bibunt, adhuc sítiunt;
Desideráre nésciunt,
Nisi Jesum, quem díligunt.

O Jesu mi dulcíssime,
Spes suspirántis ánimæ!
Te quærunt piæ lácrimæ,
Te clamor mentis íntimæ.

Mane nobíscum, Dómine,
Et nos illústra lúmine;
Pulsa mentis calígine,
Mundum reple dulcédine.

Jesu, flos Matris Vírginis,
Amor nostræ dulcédinis,
Tibi laus, honor nóminis,
Regnum beatitúdinis.
Amen.
Hymnus Laudes.eng:
O Jesu, Thou the Beauty art
Of Angel worlds above;
Thy name is music to the heart,
Enchanting it with love.

Celestial Sweetness unalloyed!
Who eat thee hunger still;
Who drink of thee still feel a void,
Which naught but Thou can fill.

O my sweet Jesu! hear the sigh,
Which unto thee I send;
To thee mine inmost spirit cries
My being's hope and end!

Stay with us, Lord, and with thy light
Illume the soul's abyss;
Scatter the darkness of our night,
And fill the world with bliss.

O Jesu, spotless Virgin flower,
Our life and joy: to thee
Be praise, beatitude, and power,
Through all eternity.
Amen.

Psalm5 Vespera=115

Versum 1.label: Versicle
Versum 1.latR: ℟. Ex hoc nunc et usque in sǽculum, allelúja.
Versum 1.eng: ℣. Blessed be the Name of the Lord, alleluia.
Versum 1.engR: ℟. From this time forth, and for evermore, alleluia.

Versum 2.label: Versicle
Versum 2.latR: ℟. Qui fecit cælum et terram.
Versum 2.eng: ℣. Our help is in the Name of the Lord.
Versum 2.engR: ℟. Who made heaven and earth.

Versum 3.label: Versicle
Versum 3.lat: ℣. Sit nomen Dómini benedíctum, allelúja.
Versum 3.latR: ℟. Ex hoc nunc et usque in sǽculum, allelúja.
Versum 3.eng: ℣. Blessed be the Name of the Lord, alleluia.
Versum 3.engR: ℟. From this time forth, and for evermore, alleluia.

Versum Nona.label: Versicle
Versum Nona.lat: ℣. Adjutórium nostrum in nómine Dómini, allelúja.
Versum Nona.latR: ℟. Qui fecit cælum et terram, allelúja.
Versum Nona.eng: ℣. Our help is in the Name of the Lord, alleluia.
Versum Nona.engR: ℟. Who made heaven and earth, alleluia.

Versum Sexta.label: Versicle
Versum Sexta.latR: ℟. Et exaltémus nomen ejus in idípsum, allelúja.
Versum Sexta.eng: ℣. O magnify the Lord with me, alleluia.
Versum Sexta.engR: ℟. And let us exalt His Name together, alleluia.

Versum Tertia.label: Versicle
Versum Tertia.lat: ℣. Afférte Dómino glóriam et honórem, allelúja.
Versum Tertia.latR: ℟. Afférte Dómino glóriam nómini ejus, allelúja.
Versum Tertia.eng: ℣. Give unto the Lord glory and honour, alleluia.
Versum Tertia.engR: ℟. Give unto the Lord the glory due unto His Name, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Oleum effúsum * nomen tuum, ídeo adolescéntulæ dilexérunt te.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Thy Name is as oil * poured forth, therefore do the virgins love thee.

Ant Laudes.ant: Scitóte, * quia Dóminus ipse est Deus, cujus nomen in ætérnum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Know ye that the Lord He is God, * and His Name endureth for ever.

Ant Laudes.ant: Sitívit * ánima mea ad nomen sanctum tuum, Dómine.
Ant Laudes.antEng: My soul thirsteth * for thy Holy Name, O Lord.

Ant Laudes.ant: Benedíctum * nomen glóriæ tuæ sanctum, et laudábile, et superexaltátum in sǽcula.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Blessed * is the Holy Name of thy glory, and worthy to be praised, and exalted above all for ever.

Ant Laudes.ant: Júvenes et vírgines, * senes cum junióribus laudáte nomen Dómini, quia exaltátum est nomen ejus solíus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Young men and maidens, * old men and children, praise the Name of the Lord, for His Name alone is exalted.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O Lord our Lord, * how admirable is thy name in the whole earth!

Ant Matutinum.ant: In nómine Jesu * omne genu flectátur cæléstium, terréstrium, et infernórum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: At the Name of Jesus, * let every knee bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Confitémini * Dómino, et invocáte nomen ejus: mementóte, quóniam excélsum est nomen ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Praise the Lord, * and call upon His Name; remember that His Name is exalted.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Mémores erunt * nóminis tui, Dómine, in omni generatióne et generatiónem.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: They shall be mindful * of thy Name, O Lord, unto all generations.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Magnificáte * Dóminum mecum, et exaltémus nomen ejus in idípsum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O magnify * the Lord with me, and let us exalt His Name together.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Omnes gentes, * quascúmque fecísti, vénient, et adorábunt coram te, Dómine, et glorificábunt nomen tuum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: All nations * whom Thou hast made, shall come and worship before thee, O Lord, and shall glorify thy Name.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Cantáte Dómino * et benedícite nómini ejus: annuntiáte de die in diem salutáre ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Sing unto the Lord, * and bless His Name show forth His salvation from day to day.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Secúndum nomen tuum, * Deus, sic et laus tua in fines terræ: justítia plena est déxtera tua.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: According to thy Name, O God, * so is thy praise unto the ends of the earth; thy right hand is full of righteousness.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Cantáte Deo, * psalmum dícite nómini ejus: iter fácite ei, qui ascéndit super occásum, Dóminus nomen illi.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Sing unto God, * sing praises to His Name; spread a path before Him That rideth upon the heavens the Lord is His Name.

Ant Vespera.ant: Omnis * qui invocáverit nomen Dómini, salvus erit.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Whosoever shall call * on the name of the Lord shall be saved.

Ant Vespera.ant: Sanctum et terríbile * nomen ejus, inítium sapiéntiæ timor Dómini.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Holy and terrible * is His Name; the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.

Ant Vespera.ant: Ego autem * in Dómino gaudébo, et exsultábo in Deo Jesu meo.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Yet will I rejoice * in the Lord I will joy in the God of my salvation.

Ant Vespera.ant: A solis ortu * usque ad occásum laudábile nomen Dómini.
Ant Vespera.antEng: From the rising of the sun * unto the going down of the same the Lord's Name is to be praised.

Ant Vespera.ant: Sacrificábo * hóstiam laudis, et nomen Dómini invocábo.
Ant Vespera.antEng: I will offer * the sacrifice of thanksgiving, and will call upon the Name of the Lord.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Hódie * Christus natus est: hódie Salvátor appáruit: hódie in terra canunt Angeli, lætántur Archángeli: hódie exsúltant justi, dicéntes: Glória in excélsis Deo, allelúja.
Ant 1.eng: This day the Christ is born this day the Saviour is appeared; * this day the Angels sing praise in the earth and the Archangels rejoice; this day the righteous are glad and say: Glory to God in the highest. Alleluia.

Versum 1.label: Versicle
Versum 1.eng: ℣. The Lord hath made known, alleluia.
Versum 1.engR: ℟. His salvation, alleluia.

Versum 2.label: Versicle
Versum 2.latR: ℟. Salutáre suum, allelúja.
Versum 2.eng: ℣. The Lord hath made known, alleluia.
Versum 2.engR: ℟. His salvation, alleluia.

Ant Vespera.ant: Tecum princípium * in die virtútis tuæ, in splendóribus sanctórum, ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Thine shall be the dominion * in the day of thy power, amid the brightness of the saints, from the womb, before the day-star, have I begotten thee.

Ant Vespera.ant: Redemptiónem * misit Dóminus pópulo suo: mandávit in ætérnum testaméntum suum.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The Lord sent redemption * unto His people, He hath commanded His covenant for ever.

Ant Vespera.ant: Exórtum est * in ténebris lumen rectis corde: miséricors, et miserátor, et justus Dóminus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Unto the upright there ariseth * light in the darkness; the Lord is gracious, and full of compassion, and righteous.

Ant Vespera.ant: Apud Dóminum * misericórdia, et copiósa apud eum redémptio.
Ant Vespera.antEng: With the Lord * there is mercy, and with Him is plenteous redemption.

Ant Vespera.ant: De fructu * ventris tui ponam super sedem tuam.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Of the fruit * of thy body will I set upon thy throne.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Véspere autem sábbati * quæ lucéscit in prima sábbati, venit María Magdaléne, et áltera María, vidére sepúlcrum, allelúja.
Ant 1.eng: And in the end of the sabbath * when it began to dawn towards the first day of the week, came Mary Magdalen and the other Mary, to see the sepulchre, alleluia.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Et valde mane * una sabbatórum véniunt ad monuméntum, orto jam sole, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: And very early in the morning * the first day of the week, they come to the sepulchre, the sun being now risen, alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Et respiciéntes * vidérunt revolútum lápidem: erat quippe magnus valde, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: And looking * they saw the stone rolled back, for it was very great, alleluia.

Ant 41.label: Antiphon
Ant 41.lat: Véspere autem sábbati * quæ lucéscit in prima sábbati, venit María Magdaléne, et áltera María, vidére sepúlcrum, allelúja.
Ant 41.eng: And in the end of the sabbath, when it began to dawn towards the first day of the week, came Mary Magdalen and the other Mary, to see the sepulchre, alleluia.

Ant 43.label: Antiphon
Ant 43.lat:
Allelúja, allelúja, allelúja, allelúja.
Hæc dies * quam fecit Dóminus: exsultémus et lætémur in ea.
Ant 43.eng:
Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia.
This is the day * which the Lord hath made: let us be glad and rejoice therein.

Invit.label: Antiphon
Invit.lat: Surréxit Dóminus vere, * Allelúja.
Invit.eng: The Lord is risen, indeed, * Alleluia.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui hodiérna die per Unigénitum tuum æternitátis nobis áditum devícta morte reserásti: vota nostra, quæ præveniéndo aspíras, étiam adjuvándo proséquere.
Oratio.eng: God, who on this day, through thy Only-begotten Son, overcame death, and opened to us the gate of everlasting life: as by thy anticipating grace, thou breathest good desires into our hearts, so also, by thy gracious help, bring them to good effect.

Versum 2.label: Antiphon
Versum 2.lat: Hæc dies * quam fecit Dóminus: exsultémus et lætémur in ea.
Versum 2.eng: This is the day * which the Lord hath made: let us be glad and rejoice therein.

Ant Laudes.ant: Angelus autem Dómini * descéndit de cælo, et accédens revólvit lápidem, et sedébat super eum, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: For an angel of the Lord * descended from heaven and coming rolled back the stone and sat upon it, alleluia, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Et ecce terræmótus * factus est magnus: Angelus enim Dómini descéndit de cælo, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: There was a great earthquake; * For an angel of the Lord descended from heaven, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Erat autem * aspéctus ejus sicut fulgur, vestiménta autem ejus sicut nix, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: And his countenance * was as lightning and his raiment as snow, alleluia, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Præ timóre autem ejus * extérriti sunt custódes, et facti sunt velut mórtui, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: And for fear of him * the guards were struck with terror and became as dead men, alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Respóndens autem Angelus, * dixit muliéribus: Nolíte timére: scio enim quod Jesum quǽritis, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: And the angel answering * said to the women: Fear not you: for I know that you seek Jesus, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ego sum qui sum, * et consílium meum non est cum ímpiis, sed in lege Dómini volúntas mea est, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I am who I am * and my counsel is not with the ungodly, my will is in the law of God, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Postulávi Patrem meum, * allelúja: dedit mihi gentes, allelúja, in hereditátem, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I asked my Father, * alleluia, and he gave me nations, alleluia, as inheritance, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ego dormívi, * et somnum cepi: et exsurréxi, quóniam Dóminus suscépit me, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I have slept * and have taken my rest: and I have risen up, because the Lord hath protected me, alleluia, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.r: Qui pro nobis pepéndit in ligno, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.vEng: The Lord is risen from the sepulcher, alleluia.
Ant Matutinum.rEng: He, who hangeth on the tree, alleluia.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Jesus junxit se * discípulis suis in via, et ibat cum illis: óculi autem eórum tenebántur, ne eum agnóscerent: et increpávit eos, dicens: O stulti et tardi corde ad credéndum in his, quæ locúti sunt Prophétæ, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: While they walked * Jesus drew near, and went with His disciples: but their eyes were holden that they should not know Him: and He rebuked them, saying: O fools, and slow of heart to believe all that the Prophets have spoken! Alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Qui sunt hi sermónes * quos confértis ad ínvicem ambulántes, et estis tristes? allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: What manner of communications are these * that ye have one to another, as ye walk, and are sad? Alleluia.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui solemnitáte pascháli, mundo remédia contulísti: pópulum tuum, quǽsumus, cælésti dono proséquere; ut et perféctam libertátem cónsequi mereátur, et ad vitam profíciat sempitérnam.
Oratio.eng: O God, Who dost heal the sick world by the solemn gladness of the Passover, continue, we beseech thee, to pour forth thine heavenly gifts upon thy people, till the same shall bring them into perfect liberty, and finally avail them unto life everlasting.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Stetit Jesus * in médio discipulórum suórum, et dixit eis: Pax vobis, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: Jesus stood in the midst of His disciples * and said unto them: Peace be unto you, alleluia, alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Vidéte manus meas * et pedes meos, quia ego ipse sum, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: Behold My Hands * and my Feet, that it is I myself, alleluia, alleluia.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui Ecclésiam tuam novo semper fœtu multíplicas: concéde fámulis tuis; ut sacraméntum vivéndo téneant, quod fide percepérunt.
Oratio.eng: O God, Who art ever multiplying the Children of thy Church, grant unto the same thy servants that they may lead the rest of their lives according to this beginning wherein Thou hast given them faith to receive the Sacrament of the New Birth.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Míttite in déxteram * navígii rete, et inveniétis, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: Cast the net on the right side of the ship, * and ye shall find, alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Dixit Jesus * discípulis suis: Afférte de píscibus, quos prendidístis nunc. Ascéndit autem Simon Petrus, et traxit rete in terram plenum magnis píscibus, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: Jesus saith * unto His disciples: Bring of the fish which ye have now caught. Simon Peter went up, and drew the net to land, full of great fishes, alleluia.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui nos resurrectiónis Domínicæ ánnua solemnitáte lætíficas: concéde propítius; ut per temporália festa quæ ágimus, perveníre ad gáudia ætérna mereámur.
Oratio.eng: O God, Who dost every year fill us with holy gladness for the rising-again of the Lord, mercifully grant that these Feast-days which we are now keeping here in time, may be to us a mean whereby in the end we may worthily attain unto those pleasures which are at thy right hand for evermore.

Ant Matutinum.vEng: The disciples therefore were glad, alleluia.
Ant Matutinum.rEng: When they saw the Lord, alleluia.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: María stabat * ad monuméntum plorans, et vidit duos Angelos in albis, sedéntes, et sudárium quod fúerat super caput Jesu, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: Mary stood without at the Sepulchre weeping, * and saw two Angels in white, sitting, and the napkin that had been about the Head of Jesus, alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Tulérunt Dóminum meum, * et néscio ubi posuérunt eum: si tu sustulísti eum, dícito mihi, allelúja: et ego eum tollam, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: They have taken away my Lord, * and I know not where they have laid Him: if thou have borne Him hence, tell me, alleluia, and I will take Him away, alleluia.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui diversitátem géntium in confessióne tui nóminis adunásti: da, ut renátis fonte baptísmatis una sit fides méntium et píetas actiónum.
Oratio.eng: O God, Who dost make all nations, how diverse soever they be, to become one family in giving of praise to thy Name, grant unto all them that are born again in the fountain of baptism to live ever in oneness of faith, and godliness of works.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Undecim discípuli * in Galilǽa vidéntes Dóminum adoravérunt, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: When the eleven disciples * saw the Lord in Galilee, they worshipped Him, alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Data est mihi * omnis potéstas in cælo et in terra, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: All power is given unto Me * in heaven and in earth, alleluia.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui paschále sacraméntum in reconciliatiónis humánæ fœ́dere contulísti: da méntibus nostris; ut quod professióne celebrámus, imitémur efféctu.
Oratio.eng: Almighty and eternal God, in the Easter sacrament thou instituted the covenant, whereby thou forgavest mankind; grant to our souls, that what we outwardly profess we may show forth in our deeds.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ego sum qui sum, * et consílium meum non est cum ímpiis, sed in lege Dómini volúntas mea est, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I am who I am * and my counsel is not with the ungodly, my will is in the law of God, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.antEng: I asked my Father, * alleluia, and he gave me nations, alleluia, as inheritance, alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ego dormívi, * et somnum cepi: et exsurréxi, quóniam Dóminus suscépit me, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I have slept * and have taken my rest: and I have risen up, because the Lord hath protected me, alleluia, alleluia.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Currébant duo simul, * et ille álius discípulus præcucúrrit cítius Petro, et venit prior ad monuméntum, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: They ran both together, * and that other disciple did outrun Peter, and came first to the Sepulchre, alleluia.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Concéde, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui festa paschália venerándo égimus, per hæc contíngere ad gáudia ætérna mereámur.
Oratio.eng: Grant, we beseech thee, O Almighty God, that we who have kept worshipfully the Easter solemnities, may at last worthily pass from keeping Feasts unto thee here to the everlasting jubilation hereafter.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Cum esset sero * die illa una sabbatórum, et fores essent clausæ, ubi erant discípuli congregáti in unum, stetit Jesus in médio, et dixit eis: Pax vobis, allelúja.
Ant 1.eng: Now when it was late * the same day, the first of the week, and the doors were shut, where the disciples were gathered together, for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in the midst and said to them: Peace be to you, alleluia.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Cum esset sero * die illa una sabbatórum, et fores essent clausæ, ubi erant discípuli congregáti in unum, stetit Jesus in médio, et dixit eis: Pax vobis, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: Now when it was late * the same day, the first of the week, and the doors were shut, where the disciples were gathered together, for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in the midst and said to them: Peace be to you, alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Post dies octo * jánuis clausis ingréssus Dóminus dixit eis: Pax vobis, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: After eight days * came the Lord, the doors being shut, and said unto them: Peace be unto you, alleluia, alleluia.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Caríssimi: Omne, quod natum est ex Deo, vincit mundum: et hæc est victória, quæ vincit mundum, fides nostra.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: My beloved: For whatsoever is born of God, overcometh the world: and this is the victory which overcometh the world, our faith.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Si testimónium hóminum accípimus, testimónium Dei majus est: quóniam hoc est testimónium Dei, quod majus est, quóniam testificátus est de Fílio suo. Qui credit in Fílium Dei, habet testimónium Dei in se.
Capitulum Nona.eng: If we receive the testimony of men, the testimony of God is greater. For this is the testimony of God, which is greater, because he hath testified of his Son. He that believeth in the Son of God, hath the testimony of God in himself.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Quis est autem qui vincit mundum, nisi qui credit quóniam Jesus est Fílius Dei? hic est, qui venit per aquam et sánguinem, Jesus Christus: non in aqua solum, sed in aqua et sánguine.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: Who is he that overcometh the world, but he that believeth that Jesus is the Son of God? This is he that came by water and blood, Jesus Christ: not by water only, but by water and blood.

Invit.label: Antiphon
Invit.lat: Surréxit Dóminus vere, * Allelúja.
Invit.eng: The Lord is risen, indeed, * Alleluia.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut qui paschália festa perégimus, hæc, te largiénte, móribus et vita teneámus.
Oratio.eng: Grant, we beseech Thee, almighty God, that we who have celebrated the Paschal Feast, may, by Thy bounty, retain its fruits in our daily habits and behaviour.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Surgens Jesus * mane prima sábbati, appáruit primo Maríæ Magdalénæ, de qua ejécerat septem dæmónia, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: He rising * early the first day of the week, appeared first to Mary Magdalen; out of whom he had cast seven devils, alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Pax vobis, * ego sum, allelúja: nolíte timére, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: Peace be with you, * it is I, alleluia: do not be afraid, alleluia.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Præcédam vos * in Galilǽam, ibi me vidébitis, sicut dixi vobis, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: I go before you into Galilee, * there shall ye see Me, as I said unto you. Alleluia, Alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Mitte manum tuam, * et cognósce loca clavórum, allelúja: et noli esse incrédulus, sed fidélis, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: Reach hither thine hand * and feel the print of the nails. Alleluia. And be not faithless but believing. Alleluia.

Ant 3.lat: Quia vidísti me, * Thoma, credidísti: beáti qui non vidérunt, et credidérunt, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: Thomas because thou hast seen Me, thou hast believed * blessed are they that have not seen and yet have believed. Alleluia.

Ant 2.eng: Mine heart is on fire: * I would that I might see my Lord: I seek Him, and know not where they have laid Him. Alleluia, Alleluia.

Ant 2.eng: Mary Magdalene and the other Mary * came to see the Sepulchre. Alleluia.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Ego sum pastor óvium: * ego sum via, véritas, et vita: ego sum pastor bonus, et cognósco oves meas, et cognóscunt me meæ, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant 1.eng: I am the Shepherd of the Sheep: * I am the Way, the Truth, and the Life: I am the Good Shepherd, and know My Sheep, and am known of Mine. Alleluia, Alleluia.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Ego sum pastor óvium: * ego sum via, véritas, et vita: ego sum pastor bonus, et cognósco oves meas, et cognóscunt me meæ, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: I am the Shepherd of the Sheep: * I am the Way, the Truth, and the Life: I am the Good Shepherd, and know My Sheep, and am known of Mine. Alleluia, Alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Ego sum pastor bonus, * qui pasco oves meas, et pro óvibus meis pono ánimam meam, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: I am the Good Shepherd, * Who feed My sheep: and I lay down My life for My sheep. Alleluia.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Caríssimi: Christus passus est pro nobis, vobis relínquens exémplum ut sequámini vestígia ejus. Qui peccátum non fecit, nec invéntus est dolus in ore ejus.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: My beloved: Christ also suffered for us, leaving you an example that you should follow his steps. Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Erátis enim sicut oves errántes, sed convérsi estis nunc ad pastórem et epíscopum animárum vestrárum.
Capitulum Nona.eng: For you were as sheep going astray; but you are now converted to the shepherd and bishop of your souls.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Tradébat autem judicánti se injúste: qui peccáta nostra ipse pértulit in córpore suo super lignum: ut peccátis mórtui, justítiæ vivámus: cujus livóre sanáti sumus.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: He delivered himself to him that judged him unjustly. Who his own self bore our sins in his body upon the tree: that we, being dead to sins, should live to justice: by whose stripes you were healed.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui in Fílii tui humilitáte jacéntem mundum erexísti: fidélibus tuis perpétuam concéde lætítiam; ut, quos perpétuæ mortis eripuísti cásibus, gáudiis fácias pérfrui sempitérnis.
Oratio.eng: O God, Whose Son hath humbled Himself, and Who hast through Him raised up the whole world, grant to thy faithful people everlasting joy; and as Thou hast delivered them from the bitter pains of eternal death, make them to be glad for ever in thy presence.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Eúntes in mundum, * allelúja: docéte omnes gentes, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: Go * into the whole world, alleluia: and teach all the nations, alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Pastor bonus * ánimam suam ponit pro óvibus suis, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: The good shepherd * gives his life to his sheep, alleluia.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Eúntes in mundum, * docéte omnes gentes, baptizántes eos in nómine Patris, et Fílii, et Spíritus Sancti, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: Going therefore * teach ye all nations; baptising them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost, alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Mercenárius autem, * cujus non sunt oves própriæ, videt lupum veniéntem, et dimíttit oves, et fugit, et lupus rapit, et dispérgit oves, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: But the hireling * and he that is not the shepherd, whose own the sheep are not, seeth the wolf coming, and leaveth the sheep, and flieth: and the wolf catcheth, and scattereth the sheep, alleluia.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Cum esset desponsáta * Mater Jesu María Joseph, ántequam convenírent, invénta est in útero habens de Spíritu Sancto.
Ant 1.eng: When as Mary * the Mother of Jesus, was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost. Alleluia.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Joseph, fili David, * noli timére accípere Maríam cónjugem tuam; quod enim in ea natum est, de Spíritu Sancto est, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: Joseph, thou Son of David, * fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife; for That Which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Fili, quid fecísti * nobis sic? Ecce pater tuus et ego doléntes quærebámus te, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: Son * why hast Thou thus dealt with us? Behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing. Alleluia.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Benedictiónes patris tui confortátæ sunt benedictiónibus patrum ejus, donec veníret Desidérium cóllium æternórum: fiant in cápite Joseph, et in vértice Nazarǽi inter fratres suos.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: The blessings of thy father are strengthened with the blessings of his fathers: until the desire of the everlasting hills should come; may they be upon the head of Joseph, and upon the crown of the Nazarite among his brethren

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Fílius accréscens Joseph, fílius accréscens, et decórus aspéctu: fíliæ discurrérunt super murum.
Capitulum Nona.eng: Joseph is a fruitful bough, a fruitful bough and comely to look upon, whose branches run over the wall.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Deus patris tui erit adjútor tuus, et Omnípotens benedícet tibi benedictiónibus cæli désuper.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: The blessings of thy father are strengthened with the blessings of his fathers: until the desire of the everlasting hills should come; may they be upon the head of Joseph, and upon the crown of the Nazarite among his brethren.

Hymnus Laudes.label: Hymn
Hymnus Laudes.title: Cǽlitum Joseph, decus atque nostræ
Hymnus Laudes.lat:
Cǽlitum Joseph, decus atque nostræ
Certa spes vitæ, columénque mundi,
Quas tibi læti cánimus, benígnus
Súscipe laudes.

Te Sator rerum státuit pudícæ
Vírginis sponsum, voluítque Verbi
Te patrem dici, dedit et minístrum
Esse salútis.

Tu Redemptórem stábulo jacéntem,
Quem chorus Vatum cécinit futúrum,
Aspicis gaudens, humilísque natum
Numen adóras.

Rex Deus regum, Dominátor orbis,
Cujus ad nutum tremit inferórum
Turba, cui pronus famulátur æther,
Se tibi subdit.

Laus sit excélsæ Tríadi perénnis,
Quæ tibi præbens súperos honóres,
Det tuis nobis méritis beátæ
Gáudia vitæ.
Amen.
Hymnus Laudes.eng:
Joseph, the praise and glory of the heavens,
Sure pledge of life, and safety of the wide world,
As in our joy we sing to thee, in kindness
List to our praises.

Thou by the world's Creator wert appointed
Spouse of the Virgin: thee he willed to honour
Naming thee father of the Word, and guardian
Of our salvation.

Thou thy Redeemer, lying in a stable,
Whom long ago foretold the choir of prophets,
Sawest rejoicing, and thy God adoredst
Humble in childhood.

God, King of kings, and Governor of the ages,
He at whose word the powers of hell do tremble,
He whom the adoring heavens ever worship
Called the protector.

Grant us, great Trinity, for Joseph's holy sake,
In highest bliss and love, above the stars to reign,
That we in joy with him may praise our loving God,
And sing our glad eternal strain.
Amen.

Hymnus Matutinum.label: Hymn
Hymnus Matutinum.title: Te, Joseph, célebrent ágmina cǽlitum
Hymnus Matutinum.lat:
Te, Joseph, célebrent ágmina cǽlitum,
Te cuncti résonent christíadum chori,
Qui clarus méritis, junctus est ínclitæ
Casto fœ́dere Vírgini.

Almo cum túmidam gérmine cónjugem
Admírans, dúbio tángeris ánxius,
Afflátu súperi Fláminis Angelus
Concéptum Púerum docet.

Tu natum Dóminum stringis, ad éxteras
Ægýpti prófugum tu séqueris plagas;
Amíssum Sólymis quæris, et ínvenis,
Miscens gáudia flétibus.

Post mortem réliquos sors pia cónsecrat,
Palmámque eméritos glória súscipit:
Tu vivens, Súperis par, frúeris Deo,
Mira sorte beátior.

Nobis, summa Trias, parce precántibus,
Da Joseph méritis sídera scándere:
Ut tandem líceat nos tibi pérpetim
Gratum prómere cánticum.
Amen.
Hymnus Matutinum.eng:
Let angels chant thy praise, pure spouse of purest bride,
While Christendom's sweet choirs the gladsome strains repeat,
To tell thy wondrous fame, to raise the pealing hymn,
Wherewith we all thy glory greet.

When doubts and bitter fears thy heavy heart oppressed,
And filled thy righteous soul with sorrow and dismay,
An angel quickly came, the wondrous secret told,
And drove thy anxious griefs away.

Thy arms thy new-born Lord, with tender joy embrace;
Him then to Egypt's land thy watchful care doth bring;
Him in the temple's courts once lost thou dost regain,
And 'mid thy tears dost greet thy King.

Not till death's pangs are o'er do others gain their crown,
But, Joseph, unto thee the blessed lot was given
While life did yet endure, thy God to see and know,
As do the saints above in heaven.

Grant us, great Trinity, for Joseph's holy sake,
In highest bliss and love, above the stars to reign,
That we in joy with him may praise our loving God,
And sing our glad eternal strain.
Amen.

Invit.label: Antiphon
Invit.lat: Laudémus Deum nostrum * In veneratióne beáti Joseph, protectóris nostri, allelúja.
Invit.eng: In worshipful remembrance of our blessed Defender Joseph, * let us praise our God.

Lectio Prima.label: Lectio brevis
Lectio Prima.lat: Fílius accréscens Joseph, fílius accréscens, et decórus aspéctu: fíliæ discurrérunt super murum.
Lectio Prima.eng: Joseph is a fruitful bough, a fruitful bough and comely to look upon, whose branches run over the wall.

Nocturn 1 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 1 Versum.latR: ℟. Quóniam adjútor et protéctor factus es mihi, allelúja.
Nocturn 1 Versum.eng: ℣. I will give praise unto thy Name, Alleluia.
Nocturn 1 Versum.engR: ℟. For Thou hast been mine Helper and Defender, Alleluia.

Nocturn 2 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 2 Versum.lat: ℣. Réspice de cælo, et vide, et vísita víneam istam, allelúja.
Nocturn 2 Versum.eng: ℣. Look down from heaven, and behold, and visit this vine, Alleluia.
Nocturn 2 Versum.engR: ℟. And protect that (thy right hand hath planted.) Alleluia.

Nocturn 3 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 3 Versum.lat: ℣. Invocávi Dóminum, Patrem Dómini mei, allelúja.
Nocturn 3 Versum.latR: ℟. Ut non derelínquat me in die tribulatiónis, allelúja.
Nocturn 3 Versum.eng: ℣. I called upon the Lord, the Father of my Lord, Alleluia.
Nocturn 3 Versum.engR: ℟. That He would not leave me in the days of my trouble. Alleluia.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui ineffábili providéntia beátum Joseph sanctíssimæ Genitrícis tuæ sponsum elígere dignátus es: præsta, quǽsumus; ut quem protectórem venerámur in terris, intercessórem habére mereámur in cælis:
Oratio.eng: God, Who in thine unspeakable foreknowledge didst choose thy blessed servant Joseph to be the husband of thine Own most holy Mother; mercifully grant that now that he is in heaven with thee, we who on earth do reverence him for our Defender, may worthily be holpen by the succour of his prayers to thee on our behalf;

Responsory Breve Nona.label: Responsorium Breve
Responsory Breve Nona.lat:
℟.br. Justus germinábit sicut lílium, * Allelúja, allelúja.
℣. Et florébit in ætérnum ante Dóminum.
℟. Allelúja, allelúja.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Justus germinábit sicut lílium, * Allelúja, allelúja.
Responsory Breve Nona.eng:
℟.br. The righteous shall grow as the lily. * Alleluia, Alleluia.
℣. Yea, he shall flourish for ever in the presence of the Lord.
℟. Alleluia, Alleluia.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. The righteous shall grow as the lily. Alleluia, Alleluia.

Responsory Breve Sexta.lat:
℟.br. Confitébor nómini tuo, * Allelúja, allelúja.
℣. Quóniam adjútor et protéctor factus es mihi.
℟. Allelúja, allelúja.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Confitébor nómini tuo, * Allelúja, allelúja.

℟. I will give praise unto thy Name. Alleluia, Alleluia.

Responsory Breve Tertia.lat:
℟.br. Constítuit eum dóminum domus suæ, * Allelúja, allelúja.
℣. Et príncipem omnis possessiónis suæ.
℟. Allelúja, allelúja.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Constítuit eum dóminum domus suæ, * Allelúja, allelúja.

℣. And ruler of all His substance.
℟. Alleluia, Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Jacob autem * génuit Joseph, virum Maríæ, de qua natus est Jesus, qui vocátur Christus, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: And Jacob begat Joseph, * the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, Who is called Christ. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Missus est * Ángelus Gábriel a Deo in civitátem Galilǽæ, cui nomen Názareth, ad Vírginem desponsátam viro, cui nomen erat Joseph, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Angel Gabriel * was sent from God, unto a city of Galilee, named Nazareth, to a Virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Ascéndit autem * Joseph a Galilǽa de civitáte Názareth in Judǽam, in civitátem David, quæ vocátur Béthlehem, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: And Joseph also went up * from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, unto Judea, unto the city of David, which is called Bethlehem. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Et venérunt festinántes, * et invenérunt Maríam, et Joseph, et Infántem pósitum in præsépio, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: And they came with haste, * and found Mary and Joseph, and the Babe lying in a manger. Alleluia.

Ant Laudes.ant: Et ipse Jesus * erat incípiens quasi annórum trigínta, ut putabátur, fílius Joseph, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: And Jesus Himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the Son of Joseph. Alleluia.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ángelus Dómini * appáruit in somnis Joseph, dicens: Surge, et áccipe Púerum et Matrem ejus, et fuge in Ægýptum, et esto ibi usque dum dicam tibi, allelúja
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Angel of the Lord appeareth to Joseph in a dream, saying Arise, and take the young Child and His Mother, and flee into Egypt, and be thou there until I bring thee word. Alleluia

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ángelus Dómini * appáruit in somnis Joseph, dicens: Surge, et áccipe Púerum et Matrem ejus, et vade in terram Israël: defúncti sunt enim qui quærébant ánimam Púeri, allelúja
Ant Matutinum.antEng: An Angel of the Lord appeareth in a dream to Joseph (in Egypt) saying Arise, and take the young Child and His Mother, and go into the land of Israel for they are dead which sought the young Child's life. Alleluia

Ant Matutinum.ant: Consúrgens Joseph, * accépit Púerum et Matrem ejus, et venit in terram Israël: et habitávit in civitáte quæ vocátur Názareth, allelúja
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Joseph arose, and took the young Child and His Mother, and came into the land of Israel, and dwelt in a city called Nazareth. Alleluia

Ant Vespera.ant: Jacob autem * génuit Joseph, virum Maríæ, de qua natus est Jesus, qui vocátur Christus, allelúja.
Ant Vespera.antEng: And Jacob begat Joseph, * the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, Who is called Christ. Alleluia.

Ant Vespera.ant: Missus est * Ángelus Gábriel a Deo in civitátem Galilǽæ, cui nomen Názareth, ad Vírginem desponsátam viro, cui nomen erat Joseph, allelúja.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The Angel Gabriel * was sent from God, unto a city of Galilee, named Nazareth, to a Virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph. Alleluia.

Ant Vespera.ant: Ascéndit autem * Joseph a Galilǽa de civitáte Názareth in Judǽam, in civitátem David, quæ vocátur Béthlehem, allelúja.
Ant Vespera.antEng: And Joseph also went up * from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, unto Judea, unto the city of David, which is called Bethlehem. Alleluia.

Ant Vespera.ant: Et venérunt festinántes, * et invenérunt Maríam, et Joseph, et Infántem pósitum in præsépio, allelúja.
Ant Vespera.antEng: And they came with haste, * and found Mary and Joseph, and the Babe lying in a manger. Alleluia.

Ant Vespera.ant: Et ipse Jesus * erat incípiens quasi annórum trigínta, ut putabátur, fílius Joseph, allelúja.
Ant Vespera.antEng: And Jesus Himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the Son of Joseph. Alleluia.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Ite, nuntiáte * frátribus meis, allelúja: ut eant in Galilǽam, allelúja: ibi me vidébunt, allelúja, allelúja, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: Go, tell my brethren alleluia * that they go into Galilee, alleluia, there they shall see me, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Sicut novit me Pater, * et ego cognósco Patrem, et ánimam meam pono pro óvibus meis, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: As the Father * knoweth me, and I know the Father: and I lay down my life for my sheep. alleluia.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Módicum * et non vidébitis me, dicit Dóminus: íterum módicum, et vidébitis me, quia vado ad Patrem, allelúja, allelúja.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Caríssimi: Obsecro vos tamquam ádvenas et peregrínos abstinére vos a carnálibus desidériis, quæ mílitant advérsus ánimam.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Dearly beloved, I beseech you as strangers and pilgrims, to refrain yourselves from carnal desires which war against the soul.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Servi, súbditi estóte in omni timóre dóminis, non tantum bonis et modéstis, sed étiam dýscolis. Hæc est enim grátia in Christo Jesu Dómino nostro.
Capitulum Nona.eng: Servants, be subject to your masters with all fear, not only to the good and gentle, but also to the froward. For this is thankworthy, if for conscience towards God, a man endure sorrows, suffering wrongfully.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Subjécti ígitur estóte omni humánæ creatúræ propter Deum: sive regi quasi præcellénti: sive dúcibus tamquam ab eo missis ad vindíctam malefactórum, laudem vero bonórum.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: Be ye subject therefore to every human creature for God's sake: whether it be to the king as excelling; Or to governors as sent by him for the punishment of evildoers, and for the praise of the good.

Hymnus Laudes.label: Hymn
Hymnus Laudes.title: Cǽlitum Joseph, decus atque nostræ
Hymnus Laudes.lat:
Cǽlitum Joseph, decus atque nostræ
Certa spes vitæ, columénque mundi,
Quas tibi læti cánimus, benígnus
Súscipe laudes.

Te Sator rerum státuit pudícæ
Vírginis sponsum, voluítque Verbi
Te patrem dici, dedit et minístrum
Esse salútis.

Tu Redemptórem stábulo jacéntem,
Quem chorus Vatum cécinit futúrum,
Aspicis gaudens, humilísque natum
Numen adóras.

Rex Deus regum, Dominátor orbis,
Cujus ad nutum tremit inferórum
Turba, cui pronus famulátur æther,
Se tibi subdit.

Laus sit excélsæ Tríadi perénnis,
Quæ tibi præbens súperos honóres,
Det tuis nobis méritis beátæ
Gáudia vitæ.
Amen.
Hymnus Laudes.eng:
Joseph, the praise and glory of the heavens,
Sure pledge of life, and safety of the wide world,
As in our joy we sing to thee, in kindness
List to our praises.

Thou by the world's Creator wert appointed
Spouse of the Virgin: thee he willed to honour
Naming thee father of the Word, and guardian
Of our salvation.

Thou thy Redeemer, lying in a stable,
Whom long ago foretold the choir of prophets,
Sawest rejoicing, and thy God adoredst
Humble in childhood.

God, King of kings, and Governor of the ages,
He at whose word the powers of hell do tremble,
He whom the adoring heavens ever worship
Called the protector.

Grant us, great Trinity, for Joseph's holy sake,
In highest bliss and love, above the stars to reign,
That we in joy with him may praise our loving God,
And sing our glad eternal strain.
Amen.

Hymnus Matutinum.label: Hymn
Hymnus Matutinum.title: Te, Joseph, célebrent ágmina cǽlitum
Hymnus Matutinum.lat:
Te, Joseph, célebrent ágmina cǽlitum,
Te cuncti résonent christíadum chori,
Qui clarus méritis, junctus est ínclitæ
Casto fœ́dere Vírgini.

Almo cum túmidam gérmine cónjugem
Admírans, dúbio tángeris ánxius,
Afflátu súperi Fláminis Angelus
Concéptum Púerum docet.

Tu natum Dóminum stringis, ad éxteras
Ægýpti prófugum tu séqueris plagas;
Amíssum Sólymis quæris, et ínvenis,
Miscens gáudia flétibus.

Post mortem réliquos sors pia cónsecrat,
Palmámque eméritos glória súscipit:
Tu vivens, Súperis par, frúeris Deo,
Mira sorte beátior.

Nobis, summa Trias, parce precántibus,
Da Joseph méritis sídera scándere:
Ut tandem líceat nos tibi pérpetim
Gratum prómere cánticum.
Amen.
Hymnus Matutinum.eng:
Let angels chant thy praise, pure spouse of purest bride,
While Christendom's sweet choirs the gladsome strains repeat,
To tell thy wondrous fame, to raise the pealing hymn,
Wherewith we all thy glory greet.

When doubts and bitter fears thy heavy heart oppressed,
And filled thy righteous soul with sorrow and dismay,
An angel quickly came, the wondrous secret told,
And drove thy anxious griefs away.

Thy arms thy new-born Lord, with tender joy embrace;
Him then to Egypt's land thy watchful care doth bring;
Him in the temple's courts once lost thou dost regain,
And 'mid thy tears dost greet thy King.

Not till death's pangs are o'er do others gain their crown,
But, Joseph, unto thee the blessed lot was given
While life did yet endure, thy God to see and know,
As do the saints above in heaven.

Grant us, great Trinity, for Joseph's holy sake,
In highest bliss and love, above the stars to reign,
That we in joy with him may praise our loving God,
And sing our glad eternal strain.
Amen.

Invit.eng: In worshipful remembrance of our blessed Defender Joseph, * let us praise our God.

Nocturn 1 Versum.eng: ℣. I will give praise unto thy Name, Alleluia.
Nocturn 1 Versum.engR: ℟. For Thou hast been mine Helper and Defender, Alleluia.

Nocturn 2 Versum.eng: ℣. Look down from heaven, and behold, and visit this vine, Alleluia.
Nocturn 2 Versum.engR: ℟. And protect that (thy right hand hath planted.) Alleluia.

Nocturn 3 Versum.eng: ℣. I called upon the Lord, the Father of my Lord, Alleluia.
Nocturn 3 Versum.engR: ℟. That He would not leave me in the days of my trouble. Alleluia.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui ineffábili providéntia beátum Joseph sanctíssimæ Genitrícis tuæ sponsum elígere dignátus es: præsta, quǽsumus; ut quem protectórem venerámur in terris, intercessórem habére mereámur in cælis:
Oratio.eng: God, Who in thine unspeakable foreknowledge didst choose thy blessed servant Joseph to be the husband of thine Own most holy Mother; mercifully grant that now that he is in heaven with thee, we who on earth do reverence him for our Defender, may worthily be holpen by the succour of his prayers to thee on our behalf;
