Ant Laudes.ant: Veníte ad me * omnes qui laborátis et oneráti estis et ego refíciam vos.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Come unto me, * all ye that travail and are heavy laden, and I will refresh you.

Ant Laudes.ant: Fili, * præbe mihi cor tuum, et óculi tui custódiant vias meas.
Ant Laudes.antEng: My son, * give me thine heart, and let thine eyes observe my ways.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Cogitatiónes * Cordis ejus in generatióne et generatiónem.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The thoughts of his Heart * shall endure from generation to generation.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Apud te * est fons vitæ; torrénte voluptátis tuæ potábis nos, Dómine.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: For with thee * is the well of life, O Lord; and thou shalt give them drink of thy pleasures.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Homo * pacis meæ, qui edébat panes meos, magnificávit super me supplantatiónem.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Even mine own familiar friend * who did eat of my Bread, hath laid great wait for me.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Rex omnis terræ * Deus; regnábit super gentes.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: God is King * upon all the earth: he reigneth over the heathen.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dum anxiarétur * Cor meum, in petra exaltásti me.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: When my Heart * was in heaviness, thou didst set me up upon a rock.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Secúndum multitúdinem * dolórum meórum in Corde meo, consolatiónes tuæ lætificavérunt ánimam meam.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: In the multitude * of the sorrows that I had in my Heart, thy comforts have given joy to my soul.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Qui dilígitis Dóminum, * confitémini memóriæ sanctificatiónis ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O ye that love the Lord, * give thanks for a remembrance of his holiness.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Vidérunt * omnes términi terræ salutáre Dei nostri.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: All the ends of the world * have seen the salvation of our God.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Psallam tibi * in natiónibus, quia magna est super cælos misericórdia tua.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I will sing praises unto thee * among the nations, for thy mercy is greater than the heavens.

Ant Vespera.ant: Suávi jugo tuo * domináre, Dómine, in médio inimicórum tuórum.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Put thy easy yoke * upon all mankind, O Lord, and be thou ruler, even in the midst of thine enemies.

Ant Vespera.ant: Miséricors * et miserátor Dóminus: escam dedit timéntibus se.
Ant Vespera.antEng: This merciful * and gracious Lord hath given Meat unto them that fear him.

Ant Vespera.ant: Exórtum est * in ténebris lumen rectis; miséricors et miserátor Dóminus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Unto the godly * there ariseth up light in the darkness, even the Lord merciful and gracious.

Ant Vespera.ant: Quid retríbuam * Dómino pro ómnibus quæ retríbuit mihi?
Ant Vespera.antEng: What reward shall I give * unto the Lord for all the benefits that he hath done unto me?

Ant Vespera.ant: Apud Dóminum * propitiátio est et copiósa apud eum redémptio.
Ant Vespera.antEng: With the Lord * there is mercy, and with him is plenteous redemption.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Unus mílitum * láncea latus ejus apéruit et contínuo exívit sanguis et aqua.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: One of the soldiers * with a spear pierced his side, and forthwith came there out Blood and Water.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Stans Jesus * clamábat dicens: Si quis sitit, véniat ad me et bibat.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: Jesus stood * and cried, saying, If any man thirst, let him come unto me and drink.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: In caritáte perpétua * diléxit nos Deus, ídeo, exaltátus a terra, attráxit nos ad Cor suum, míserans.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: With an everlasting love * hath God loved us, and from the day that he was lifted up over the earth, he hath drawn us with loving-kindness unto his Heart.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Veníte ad me * omnes qui laborátis et oneráti estis et ego refíciam vos.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: Come unto me, * all ye that travail and are heavy laden, and I will refresh you.

Ant Vespera 3.ant: Fili, * præbe mihi cor tuum, et óculi tui custódiant vias meas.
Ant Vespera 3.antEng: My son, * give me thine heart, and let thine eyes observe my ways.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Impropérium exspectávit cor meum * et misériam: et sustínui qui simul contristarétur, et non fuit; et qui consolarétur, et non invéni.
Ant 1.eng: My heart hath looked for * reproach and bitterness and I looked for some to take pity on me, and there was none and for comforters, and I found none.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Vulnerátus est propter iniquitátes nostras * attrítus est propter scélera nostra: disciplína pacis nostræ super eum, et livóre ejus sanáti sumus.
Ant 2.eng: He was wounded * for our transgressions. He was bruised for our iniquities the chastisement of our peace was upon Him, and with His stripes we are healed.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Ad Jesum autem cum veníssent * ut vidérunt eum jam mórtuum, non fregérunt ejus crura: sed unus mílitum láncea latus ejus apéruit, et contínuo exívit sanguis et aqua.
Ant 3.eng: But when they came to Jesus * and saw that He was dead already, they brake not His Legs but one of the soldiers with a spear pierced His Side, and forthwith came thereout Blood and Water.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Ecce Deus Salvátor meus, fiduciáliter agam, et non timébo: quia fortitúdo mea et laus mea Dóminus, et factus est mihi in salútem. Hauriétis aquas in gáudio de fóntibus Salvatóris.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Behold, God is my saviour, I will deal confidently, and will not fear: O because the Lord is my strength, and my praise, and he is become my salvation. You shall draw waters with joy out of the saviour's fountains:

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Cantáte Dómino quóniam magnífice fecit, annuntiáte hoc in univérsa terra. Exsúlta et lauda habitátio Sion, quia magnus in médio tui sanctus Israël.
Capitulum Nona.eng: Sing ye to the Lord, for he hath done great things: show this forth in all the earth. Rejoice, and praise, O thou habitation of Sion: for great is he that is in the midst of thee, the Holy One of Israel.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Dicétis in die illa: Confitémini Dómino, et invocáte nomen ejus: et mementate quóniam excélsum est nomen ejus.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: And you shall say in that day: Praise ye the Lord, and call upon his name: make his works known among the people: remember that his name is high.

Hymnus Laudes.label: Hymn
Hymnus Laudes.title: Cor, arca legem cóntinens
Hymnus Laudes.lat:
Cor, arca legem cóntinens
Non servitútis véteris,
Sed grátiæ, sed véniæ,
Sed et misericórdiæ.

Cor, sanctuárium novi
Intemerátum fœ́deris,
Templum vetústo sánctius,
Velúmque scisso utílius.

Te vulnerátum cáritas
Ictu paténti vóluit,
Amóris invisíbilis
Ut venerémur vúlnera.

Hoc sub amóris sýmbolo
Passus cruénta et mýstica,
Utrúmque sacrifícium
Christus sacérdos óbtulit.

Quis non amántem rédamet?
Quis non redémptus díligat,
Et Corde in isto séligat
Ætérna tabernácula?

Decus Parénti, et Fílio,
Sanctóque sit Spirítui,
Quibus potéstas, glória,
Regnúmque in omne est sǽculum.
Amen.
Hymnus Laudes.eng:
Jesus, behind thy temple's veil,
Hid in an ark of gold,
On stones engraven, lay the law
thy finger wrote of old.

But in thy body's temple new,
thy life-blood's throbbing shrine,
Held, upon fleshly tables graved,
The law of love divine.

And when that heart in death was stilled,
Each temple's veil was riven:
And lo, within thy love's red shrine,
To us to look was given.

There make us gaze and see the love
Which drew thee, for our sake,
O great high-priest, thyself to God
A sacrifice to make.

Thou, Saviour, cause that every soul
Which thou hast loved so well,
May will within thine open heart
In life and death to dwell.

Grant it, O Father, only Son,
And Spirit, God of grace,
To whom all worship shall be done,
In every time and place.
Amen.

Hymnus Matutinum.label: Hymn
Hymnus Matutinum.title: En, ut supérba críminum
Hymnus Matutinum.lat:
En, ut supérba críminum
Et sæva nostrórum cohors
Cor sauciávit ínnocens
Meréntis haud tale Dei!

Vibrántis hastam mílitis
Peccáta nostra dírigunt,
Ferrúmque diræ cúspidis
Mortále crimen ácuit.

Ex Corde scisso Ecclésia,
Christo jugáta, náscitur:
Hoc óstium arcæ in látere est
Genti ad salútem pósitum.

Ex hoc perénnis grátia,
Ceu septifórmis flúvius,
Stolas ut illic sórdidas
Lavémus Agni in sánguine.

Turpe est redíre ad crímina,
Quæ Cor beátum lácerent:
Sed æmulémur córdibus
Flammas amóris índices.

Hoc Christe nobis, hoc Pater,
Hoc sancte dona Spiritus,
Quibus potéstas, glória,
Regnúmque in omne est sǽculum.
Amen.
Hymnus Matutinum.eng:
Lo, how the savage crew
Of our proud sins hath rent
The heart of our all-gracious God,
That heart so innocent.

The soldier's quivering lance
Our guilt it was that drave,
Our wicked deeds that to its point
Such cruel sharpness gave.

O wounded heart, whence sprang
The Church, the Saviour's bride;
Thou door of our salvation's ark
Set in its mystic side.

Thou holy fount, whence flows
The sacred sevenfold flood,
Where we our filthy robes may cleanse
In the Lamb's saving blood:

By sorrowful relapse,
thee will we rend no more;
But like the flames, those types of love,
Strive heavenward to soar.

Hoc Christe nobis, hoc Pater,
Hoc sancte dona Spiritus,
Quibus potéstas, glória,
Regnúmque in omne est sǽculum.
Amen.

Hymnus Vespera.label: Hymn
Hymnus Vespera.title: Auctor beáte sǽculi
Hymnus Vespera.lat:
Auctor beáte sǽculi,
Christe, Redémptor ómnium,
Lumen Patris de lúmine,
Deúsque verus de Deo.

Amor coégit te tuus
Mortále corpus súmere,
Ut novus Adam rédderes,
Quod vetus ille abstúlerat.

Ill[e] amor, almus ártifex
Terræ marísqu[e], et síderum,
Erráta patrum míserans,
Et nostra rumpens víncula.

Non Corde discédat tuo
Vis ill[a] amóris íncliti:
Hoc fonte gentes háuriant
Remissiónis grátiam.

Percúss[um] ad hoc est láncea,
Passúmqu[e] ad hoc est vúlnera:
Ut nos laváret sórdibus,
Unda fluént[e], et sánguine.

Decus Parénti, et Fílio,
Sanctóque sit Spirítui,
Quibus potéstas, glória,
Regnúmque in omne est sǽculum.
Amen.
Hymnus Vespera.eng:
O Christ, the world's Creator bright,
Who didst mankind from sin redeem,
Light from the Father's glorious light,
True God of God, in bliss supreme.

Thy love compelled thee to assume
A mortal body, man to save;
Reversing the old Adam's doom;
Our ransom the new Adam gave.

That love which gloriously framed all
The earth, the stars, and wondrous sea
Took pity on our parents' fall,
Broke all our bonds and set us free.

O Saviour, let thy potent love
Flow ever from thy bounteous heart;
To nations that pure fount above
The grace of pardon will impart.

His heart for this was opened wide,
And wounded by the soldier's spear,
That freely from his sacred side
Might flow the streams our souls to clear.

Decus Parénti, et Fílio,
Sanctóque sit Spirítui,
Quibus potéstas, glória,
Regnúmque in omne est sǽculum.
Amen.

Invit.label: Antiphon
Invit.lat: Christum pro nobis passum, * Veníte adorémus.
Invit.eng: Christ suffered for us, * O come, let us worship Him

Lectio Prima.label: Lectio brevis
Lectio Prima.lat: Cantáte Dómino quóniam magnífice fecit, annuntiáte hoc in univérsa terra. Exsúlta et lauda habitátio Sion, quia magnus in médio tui sanctus Israël.
Lectio Prima.eng: Sing ye to the Lord, for he hath done great things: show this forth in all the earth. Rejoice, and praise, O thou habitation of Sion: for great is he that is in the midst of thee, the Holy One of Israel.

Nocturn 1 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 1 Versum.latR: ℟. Omnia enim ópera nostra operátus es nobis.
Nocturn 1 Versum.eng: ℣. Lord, Thou wilt ordain peace for us
Nocturn 1 Versum.engR: ℟. For Thou hast also wrought all our works for us.

Nocturn 2 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 2 Versum.lat: ℣. Convérsus est furor tuus.
Nocturn 2 Versum.eng: ℣. thine anger is turned away.
Nocturn 2 Versum.engR: ℟. And Thou comforteest me.

Nocturn 3 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 3 Versum.latR: ℟. Deus noster maniféste véniet.
Nocturn 3 Versum.eng: ℣. Out of Zion, the Perfection of beauty
Nocturn 3 Versum.engR: ℟. Our God shall come manifestly.

Oratio 1.label: Oratio
Oratio 1.lat: Concéde quǽsumus omnípotens Deus: ut, qui in sanctíssimo dilécti Fílii tui Corde gloriántes, præcípua in nos caritátis ejus benefícia recólimus; eórum páriter et actu delectémur et fructu.
Oratio 1.eng: O God, the Protector of all them that trust in thee, without Whom nothing is strong, nothing is Holy increase and multiply upon us thy mercy, that Thou being our ruler and guide, we may so pass through things temporal, that we finally lose not the things eternal.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Concéde quǽsumus omnípotens Deus: ut, qui in sanctíssimo dilécti Fílii tui Corde gloriántes, præcípua in nos caritátis ejus benefícia recólimus: eórum páriter et actu delectémur et fructu.
Oratio 2.eng: Almighty God, grant, we beseech thee, that all we who do make our boast in the most Holy Heart of thy well-beloved Son, and do tell of the wondrous works of His love to us-ward, may be blessed in knowing both what He hath wrought for us and also what He is able and willing to work in us.

Responsory Breve Nona.label: Responsorium Breve
Responsory Breve Nona.lat:
℟.br. Dirupísti Dómine, * Víncula mea.
℣. Tibi sacrificábo hóstiam laudis.
℟. Víncula mea
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Dirupísti Dómine, * Víncula mea.
Responsory Breve Nona.eng:
℟.br. O Lord, Thou hast loosed my bonds.
℣. I will offer to thee the sacrifice of thanksgiving.
℟. Thou hast loosed my bonds.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. O Lord, Thou hast loosed my bonds.

Responsory Breve Sexta.label: Responsorium Breve
Responsory Breve Sexta.lat:
℟.br. Pósuit * Fines tuos pacem.
℣. Et ádipe fruménti sátiat te.
℟. Fines tuos paces
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Pósuit * Fines tuos pacem.
Responsory Breve Sexta.eng:
℟.br. He maketh peace in thy borders.
℣. And filleth thee with the finest of the wheat.
℟. Peace in thy borders.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. He maketh peace in thy borders.

Responsory Breve Tertia.label: Responsorium Breve
Responsory Breve Tertia.lat:
℟.br. Vere * Languóres nostros ipse tulit.
℣. Et dolóres nostros ipse portávit.
℟. Languóres nostros ipse tulit.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Vere * Languóres nostros ipse tulit.
Responsory Breve Tertia.eng:
℟.br. Surely He hath borne our griefs.
℣. And carried our sorrows.
℟. He hath borne our griefs.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. Surely He hath borne our griefs.

Ant Laudes.ant: Díscite a me, * quia mitis sum et húmilis corde.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Learn of Me, * for I am meek and lowly in Heart.

Ant Laudes.ant: Sanctificávi locum * istum, ut sit nomen meum ibi in sempitérnum, et permáneant óculi mei et cor meum ibi cunctis diébus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: I have sanctified this place, * that My Name may be there for ever, and Mine eyes, and Mine heart shall be there perpetually.

Ant Laudes.ant: Et dixi: * Ergo sine causa justificávi cor meum, et lavi inter innocéntes manus meas, et fui flagellátus tota die.
Ant Laudes.antEng: And I said: Then have I cleansed my heart * in vain, and washed my hands in innocency, for all the day long have I been plagued.

Ant Laudes.ant: Secúndum multitúdinem * dolórum meórum in corde meo, consolatiónes tuæ lætificavérunt ánimam meam.
Ant Laudes.antEng: In the multitude of the sorrows * within my heart, thy comforts delight my soul.

Ant Laudes.ant: Pone me * ut signáculum super cor tuum, ut signáculum super bráchium tuum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Set me as a seal upon thine heart, * as a seal upon thine arm.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Quid est homo * quia magníficas eum, aut quid appónis erga eum cor tuum?
Ant Matutinum.antEng: What is man, that Thou shouldest magnify him? and that Thou shouldest set thine Heart upon him?

Ant Matutinum.ant: Meditátio * cordis mei in conspéctu tuo sempe.r
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Let the meditation of my heart be acceptable in thy sight for ever

Ant Matutinum.ant: Elevámini * portæ æternáles, et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Be ye lift up, ye everlasting doors, and the King of glory shall come in

Ant Matutinum.ant: Afferéntur * in lætítia et exsultatióne: adducéntur in templum Regis.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: With gladness and rejoicing shall they be brought; they shall enter into the King's palace

Ant Matutinum.ant: Sanctificávit * tabernáculum suum Altíssimus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Most High hath hallowed His Tabernacle

Ant Matutinum.ant: Sicut lætántium * ómnium habitátio est in te.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: All they that dwell in thee are in gladness

Ant Matutinum.ant: Annuntiáte * de die in diem salutáre ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Show forth His salvation from day to day

Ant Matutinum.ant: Adoráte eum * omnes Angeli ejus: audívit, et lætáta est Sion.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Worship Him, all ye His Angels Zion heard, and was glad

Ant Matutinum.ant: Vidérunt omnes * términi terræ salutáre Dei nostri.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God

Ant Vespera.ant: Díscite a me, * quia mitis sum et húmilis corde
Ant Vespera.antEng: Learn of Me, * for I am meek and lowly in Heart

Ant Vespera.ant: Sanctificávi locum * istum, ut sit nomen meum ibi in sempitérnum, et permáneant óculi mei et cor meum ibi cunctis diébus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: I have sanctified this place, * that My Name may be there for ever, and Mine eyes, and Mine heart shall be there perpetually

Ant Vespera.ant: Et dixi: * Ergo sine causa justificávi cor meum, et lavi inter innocéntes manus meas, et fui flagellátus tota die
Ant Vespera.antEng: And I said: Then have I cleansed my heart * in vain, and washed my hands in innocence, for all the day long have I been plagued

Ant Vespera.ant: Secúndum multitúdinem * dolórum meórum in corde meo, consolatiónes tuæ lætificavérunt ánimam meam
Ant Vespera.antEng: In the multitude of the sorrows * within my heart, thy comforts delight my soul

Ant Vespera.ant: Pone me * ut signáculum super cor tuum, ut signáculum super bráchium tuum
Ant Vespera.antEng: Set me as a seal upon thine heart, * as a seal upon thine arm

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Cognovérunt omnes * a Dan usque Bersabée, quod fidélis Sámuel prophéta esset Dómini.
Ant 1.eng: And they all knew, * from Dan even unto Beersheba, that Samuel was established to be a Prophet of the Lord.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Quis ex vobis * homo, qui habet centum oves et, si perdíderit unam ex illis, nonne dimíttit nonagínta novem in desérto et vadit ad illam quæ períerat, donec invéniat eam? Allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: What man of you * that hath an hundred sheep, and if he shall lose one of them, doth he not leave the ninety-nine in the desert and go after that which was lost, until he find it? Alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Quæ múlier * habens drachmas decem, et si perdíderit drachmam unam, nonne accéndit lucérnam et evérrit domum et quærit diligénter, donec invéniat?
Ant 3.eng: What woman * having ten pieces of silver, if she lose one piece, doth not light a candle, and sweep the house, and seek diligently till she find it?

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Caríssimi, humiliámini sub poténti manu Dei, ut vos exáltet in témpore visitatiónis; omnem sollicitúdinem vestram proiciéntes in eum, quóniam ipsi cura est de vobis.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Dearly beloved, humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time: casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Deus autem omnis grátiæ, qui vocávit nos in ætérnam suam glóriam in Christo Jesu, módicum passos ipse perfíciet, confirmábit solidabítque. Ipsi glória et impérium in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
Capitulum Nona.eng: Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil goeth about as a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour; whom resist stedfast in the Faith, knowing that the same afflictions are accomplished in your brethren that are in the world.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Sóbrii estóte, et vigiláte: quia adversárius vester diábolus tamquam leo rúgiens círcuit, quærens quem dévoret: cui resístite fortes in fide, sciéntes eámdem passiónem ei, quæ in mundo est, vestræ fraternitáti fíeri.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: Sóbrii estóte, et vigiláte: quia adversárius vester diábolus tamquam leo rúgiens círcuit, quærens quem dévoret: cui resístite fortes in fide, sciéntes eámdem passiónem ei, quæ in mundo est, vestræ fraternitáti fíeri.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Protéctor in te sperántium, Deus, sine quo nihil est válidum, nihil sanctum; multíplica super nos misericórdiam tuam; ut, te rectóre, te duce, sic transeámus per bona temporália, ut non amittámus ætérna.
Oratio.eng: O God, the protector of all them that trust in thee, without whom nothing is strong, nothing is holy; increase and multiply upon us thy mercy, that thou being our ruler and guide, we may so pass through things temporal, that we finally lose not the things eternal.

Versum 2.latR: ℟. Quia mitis sum et húmilis Corde.
Versum 2.eng: ℣. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me.
Versum 2.engR: ℟. For I am meek and lowly in Heart.

Versum 3.label: Versicle

Versum 3.latR: ℟. Escam dedit timéntibus se.
Versum 3.eng: ℣. The merciful Lord hath instituted a memorial of his wondrous deeds.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Cognovérunt omnes * a Dan usque Bersabée, quod fidélis Sámuel prophéta esset Dómini.
Ant 1.eng: And they all knew, * from Dan even unto Beersheba, that Samuel was established to be a Prophet of the Lord.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Quis ex vobis * homo, qui habet centum oves et, si perdíderit unam ex illis, nonne dimíttit nonagínta novem in desérto et vadit ad illam quæ períerat, donec invéniat eam? Allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: What man of you * that hath an hundred sheep, and if he shall lose one of them, doth he not leave the ninety-nine in the desert and go after that which was lost, until he find it? Alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Quæ múlier * habens drachmas decem, et si perdíderit drachmam unam, nonne accéndit lucérnam et evérrit domum et quærit diligénter, donec invéniat?
Ant 3.eng: What woman * having ten pieces of silver, if she lose one piece, doth not light a candle, and sweep the house, and seek diligently till she find it?

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Protéctor in te sperántium, Deus, sine quo nihil est válidum, nihil sanctum; multíplica super nos misericórdiam tuam; ut, te rectóre, te duce, sic transeámus per bona temporália, ut non amittámus ætérna.
Oratio.eng: O God, the protector of all them that trust in thee, without whom nothing is strong, nothing is holy; increase and multiply upon us thy mercy, that thou being our ruler and guide, we may so pass through things temporal, that we finally lose not the things eternal.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Præváluit David * in Philisthǽum in funda et lápide in nómine Dómini.
Ant 1.eng: So David prevailed * over the Philistine with a sling, and with a stone, in the name of the Lord.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Ascéndens Jesus * in navim, et sedens docébat turbas, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: Jesus entered into the ship, * and sat down, and taught the people, alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Præcéptor, * per totam noctem laborántes nihil cépimus; in verbo autem tuo laxábo rete.
Ant 3.eng: Master, we have toiled all night, * and have taken nothing; nevertheless at thy word I will let down the net.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Da nobis, quǽsumus, Dómine: ut et mundi cursus pacífice nobis tuo órdine dirigátur; et Ecclésia tua tranquílla devotióne lætétur.
Oratio.eng: Grant, O Lord, we beseech thee, that the course of this world may be so peaceably ordered by thy governance, that thy Church may joyfully serve thee in all godly quietness.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Montes Gélboë, * nec ros nec plúvia véniant super vos: quia in te abjéctus est clípeus fórtium, clípeus Saul, quasi non esset unctus óleo. Quómodo cecidérunt fortes in bello? Jónathas in excélsis interféctus est: Saul et Jónathas, amábiles et decóri valde in vita sua, in morte quoque non sunt divísi.
Ant 1.eng: Ye mountains of Gilboa, * let there be no dew, neither let there be rain upon you; for there the shield of the mighty is vilely cast away, the shield of Saul, as though he had not been anointed with oil. How are the mighty fallen in the midst of the battle! Jonathan is slain upon the high places; Saul and Jonathan were lovely and pleasant in their lives, and in their death they were not divided.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Audístis * quia dictum est antíquis: Non occídes; qui autem occíderit, reus erit judício.
Ant 2.eng: Ye have heard that it was said * by them of old time: Thou shalt not kill; and whosoever shall kill shall be in danger of the judgment.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Si offers * munus tuum ad altáre et recordátus fúeris quia frater tuus habet áliquid advérsus te, relínque ibi munus tuum ante altáre, et vade prius reconciliári fratri tuo, et tunc véniens ófferes munus tuum, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: If thou bring thy gift to the Altar, * and there rememberest that thy brother hath aught against thee, leave there thy gift before the Altar, and go thy way; first be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift. Alleluia.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui diligéntibus te bona invisibília præparásti: infúnde córdibus nostris tui amóris afféctum; ut te in ómnibus et super ómnia diligéntes, promissiónes tuas, quæ omne desidérium súperant, consequámur.
Oratio.eng: O God, Who hast prepared for them that love thee such good things as pass man's understanding; pour into our hearts such love toward thee, that we, loving thee in all things and above all things, may obtain thy promises, which exceed all that we can desire.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Obsecro, Dómine, * aufer iniquitátem servi tui, quia insipiénter egi.
Ant 1.eng: I beseech thee, * O Lord, do away the iniquity of thy servant, for I have done very foolishly.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Cum turba multa * esset cum Jesu nec habérent quod manducárent, convocátis discípulis, ait illis: Miséreor super turbam, quia ecce jam tríduo sústinent me nec habent quod mandúcent, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: The multitude being very great, * and having nothing to eat, Jesus called His disciples unto Him, and saith unto them: I have compassion on the multitude, because they have now been with Me three days, and have nothing to eat. Alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Miséreor * super turbam, quia ecce jam tríduo sústinent me nec habent quod mandúcent, et, si dimísero eos jejúnos, defícient in via, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: I have compassion on the multitude, * because they have now been with Me three days, and have nothing to eat; and if I send them away fasting, they will faint by the way. Alleluia.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus virtútum, cujus est totum quod est óptimum: ínsere pectóribus nostris amórem tui nóminis, et præsta in nobis religiónis augméntum; ut, quæ sunt bona, nútrias, ac pietátis stúdio, quæ sunt nutríta, custódias.
Oratio.eng: Lord of all power and might, Who art the Author and Giver of all good things, graft in our hearts the love of thy Name, increase in us true religion, nourish us with all goodness, and, of thy great mercy, keep us in the same.

Rule.lat:

Symbolum Athanasium

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Unxérunt Salomónem * Sadoc sacérdos et Nathan prophéta, regem in Gihon et ascendéntes læti dixérunt: Vivat rex in ætérnum.
Ant 1.eng: Nathan the Prophet * anointed Solomon King in Gihon, and they went up with joy, and cried, saying: May the King live for ever.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Atténdite * a falsis prophétis, qui véniunt ad vos in vestiméntis óvium, intrínsecus autem sunt lupi rapáces; a frúctibus eórum cognoscétis eos, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: Beware of false prophets, * which come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves. Ye shall know them by their fruits. Alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Non potest arbor * bona fructus malos fácere, nec arbor mala fructus bonos fácere. Omnis arbor quæ non facit fructum bonum, excidétur, et in ignem mittétur, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, * neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit. Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit, is hewn down and cast into the fire. Alleluia.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, cujus providéntia in sui dispositióne non fállitur: te súpplices exorámus; ut nóxia cuncta submóveas, et ómnia nobis profutúra concédas.
Oratio.eng: O God, Whose never-failing Providence ordereth all things both in heaven and earth, we humbly beseech thee to put away from us all hurtful things, and to give us those things which be profitable for us.

Rule.lat:
9 lectiones
Psalmi Dominica
Antiphonas horas
Symbolum Athanasium

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Exaudísti, Dómine, * oratiónem servi tui, ut ædificárem templum nómini tuo.
Ant 1.eng: O Lord, Thou hast hearkened unto the prayer of thy servant, * that I might build a temple unto thy Name.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Ait dóminus víllico: * Quid hoc áudio de te? redde ratiónem villicatiónis tuæ, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: The lord said unto his steward: * How is it that I hear this of thee? Give an account of thy stewardship. Alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Quid fáciam, * quia dóminus meus aufert a me villicatiónem? Fódere non váleo, mendicáre erubésco. Scio quid fáciam, ut, cum amótus fúero a villicatióne, recípiant me in domos suas.
Ant 3.eng: What shall I do? * For my lord taketh away from me the stewardship. I cannot dig, to beg I am ashamed. I am resolved what to do, that, when I am put out of the stewardship, they may receive me into their houses.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Largíre nobis, quǽsumus, Dómine, semper spíritum cogitándi quæ recta sunt, propítius et agéndi: ut, qui sine te esse non póssumus, secúndum te vívere valeámus.
Oratio.eng: Grant to us, Lord, we beseech thee, the spirit to think and do always such things as be rightful, that we, who cannot do anything that is good without thee, may by thee be enabled to live according to thy will.

Rule.lat:
9 lectiones
Psalmi Dominica
Antiphonas horas
Symbolum Athanasium

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Dum tólleret Dóminus * Elíam per túrbinem in cælum, Eliséus clamábat: Pater mi, currus Israël et auríga ejus.
Ant 1.eng: When the Lord would take up * Elijah into heaven by a whirlwind, Elisha cried, and said: My father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Cum appropinquáret * Dóminus Jerúsalem videns civitátem flevit super illam, et dixit: Quia si cognovísses et tu, quia vénient dies in te, et circúmdabunt te inimíci tui vallo et circúmdabunt te et coangustábunt te úndique et ad terram prostérnent te: eo quod non cognovísti tempus visitatiónis tuæ, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: When the Lord was come near to Jerusalem, He beheld the city, and wept * over it, saying: If thou hadst known, even thou! For the days shall come upon thee, that thine enemies shall cast a trench about thee, and compass thee round, and keep thee in on every side and shall lay thee even with the ground because thou knewest not the time of thy visitation, alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Scriptum est enim: * Quia domus mea domus oratiónis est cunctis géntibus; vos autem fecístis illam spelúncam latrónum. Et erat cotídie docens in templo.
Ant 3.eng: It is written: My house is the house of prayer * for all nations but ye have made it a den of thieves. And He taught daily in the Temple.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Páteant aures misericórdiæ tuæ, Dómine, précibus supplicántium: et, ut peténtibus desideráta concédas; fac eos, quæ tibi sunt plácita, postuláre.
Oratio.eng: Let thy merciful ears, O Lord, be open to the prayers of thy humble servants; and, that they may obtain their petitions, make them to ask such things as shall please thee.

Rule.lat:
9 lectiones
Psalmi Dominica
Antiphonas horas
Symbolum Athanasium

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Fecit Joas * rectum coram Dómino cunctis diébus, quibus dócuit eum Jójada sacérdos.
Ant 1.eng: And Joas did * that which was right before the Lord all the days that Joiada, the priest, taught him.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Stans a longe * publicánus, nolébat óculos ad cælum leváre, sed percutiébat pectus suum dicens: Deus, propítius esto mihi peccatóri.
Ant 2.eng: The publican, standing afar off, * would not lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven, but smote upon his breast, saying: God, be merciful to me, a sinner.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Descéndit * hic justificátus in domum suam ab illo; quia omnis qui se exáltat, humiliábitur, et, qui se humíliat, exaltábitur.
Ant 3.eng: This man went down to his house * justified rather than the other, for every one that exalteth himself shall be abased, and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui omnipoténtiam tuam parcéndo máxime et miserándo maniféstas: multíplica super nos misericórdiam tuam; ut, ad tua promíssa curréntes, cæléstium bonórum fácias esse consórtes.
Oratio.eng: O God, Who declarest thine Almighty power most chiefly in showing mercy and pity, mercifully grant unto us such a measure of thy grace, that we, running the way of thy commandments, may obtain thy gracious promises, and be made partakers of thy heavenly treasure.

Rule.lat:
9 lectiones
Psalmi Dominica
Antiphonas horas
Symbolum Athanasium

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Obsécro, Dómine: * meménto, quæso, quómodo ambuláverim coram te in veritáte et in corde perfécto et quod plácitum est coram te, fécerim.
Ant 1.eng: I beseech thee, O Lord, * remember now how I have walked before thee in truth and with a perfect heart, and have done that which is good in thy sight.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Cum transísset Dóminus * fines Tyri, surdos fecit audíre et mutos loqui.
Ant 2.eng: When the Lord had departed from the coasts of Tyre, * He made both the deaf to hear and the dumb to speak.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Bene ómnia fecit * et surdos fecit audíre et mutos loqui.
Ant 3.eng: He hath done all things well, * He maketh both the deaf to hear and the dumb to speak.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui, abundántia pietátis tuæ, et mérita súpplicum excédis et vota: effúnde super nos misericórdiam tuam; ut dimíttas quæ consciéntia métuit, et adícias quod orátio non præsúmit.
Oratio.eng: Almighty and everlasting God, Who art always more ready to hear than we to pray, and art wont to give more than either we desire or deserve, pour down upon us the abundance of thy mercy, forgiving us those things whereof our conscience is afraid, and giving us those good things which we are not worthy to ask.

Rule.lat:
9 lectiones
Psalmi Dominica
Antiphonas horas
Symbolum Athanasium

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Magíster, * quid faciéndo vitam ætérnam possidébo? At ille dixit ad eum: In lege quid scriptum est? quómodo legis? Díliges Dóminum Deum tuum ex toto corde tuo, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: Master, what shall I do * to inherit eternal life? He said unto him: What is written in the law? How readest thou? And he, answering, said: Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Homo quidam * descendébat ab Jerúsalem in Jéricho et íncidit in latrónes, qui étiam despoliavérunt eum et, plagis impósitis, abiérunt semivívo relícto.
Ant 3.eng: A certain man went down from Jerusalem * to Jericho, and fell among thieves, which stripped him of his raiment, and wounded him, and departed, leaving him half dead.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Omnípotens et miséricors Deus, de cujus múnere venit, ut tibi a fidélibus tuis digne et laudabíliter serviátur: tríbue, quǽsumus, nobis; ut ad promissiónes tuas sine offensióne currámus.
Oratio.eng: Almighty and merciful God, of Whose only gift it cometh that thy faithful people do unto thee true and laudable service, grant, we beseech thee, that we may so faithfully serve thee in this life, that we fail not finally to attain thy heavenly promises.

Rule.lat:
9 lectiones
Psalmi Dominica
Antiphonas horas
Symbolum Athanasium

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Cum transíret Jesus * quoddam castéllum, occurrérunt ei decem viri leprósi, qui stetérunt a longe et levavérunt vocem dicéntes: Jesu præcéptor, miserére nostri.
Ant 2.eng: As Jesus passed through * a certain village, there met Him ten men that were lepers, which stood afar off; and they lifted up their voices, and said: “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us.”

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Unus autem * ex illis, ut vidit quod mundátus est, regréssus est cum magna voce magníficans Deum, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: And one of them, * when he saw that he was healed, turned back, and with a loud voice glorified God, alleluia.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, da nobis fídei, spei et caritátis augméntum: et, ut mereámur ássequi quod promíttis, fac nos amáre quod prǽcipis.
Oratio.eng: Almighty and everlasting God, give unto us the increase of faith, hope, and charity, and that we may worthily obtain that which Thou dost promise, make us to love that which Thou dost command.

Rule.lat:
9 lectiones
Psalmi Dominica
Antiphonas horas
Symbolum Athanasium

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Nolíte sollíciti esse * dicéntes: Quid manducábimus aut quid bibémus? scit enim Pater vester quid vobis necésse sit, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: Take no thought, saying: What shall we eat? * or: What shall we drink? For your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Quǽrite primum * regnum Dei et justítiam ejus, et hæc ómnia adiciéntur vobis, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: Seek ye first the kingdom of God * and His righteousness, and all these things shall be added unto you, alleluia.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Custódi, Dómine, quǽsumus, Ecclésiam tuam propitiatióne perpétua: et quia sine te lábitur humána mortálitas; tuis semper auxíliis et abstrahátur a nóxiis et ad salutária dirigátur.
Oratio.eng: Keep, we beseech thee, O Lord, thy Church with thy perpetual mercy, and because the frailty of man without thee cannot but fall, keep us ever by thy help from all things hurtful, and lead us to all things profitable to our salvation.

Rule.lat:
9 lectiones
Psalmi Dominica
Antiphonas horas
Symbolum Athanasium

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Ibat Jesus * in civitátem, quæ vocátur Naim: et ecce defúnctus efferebátur fílius únicus matris suæ.
Ant 2.eng: Jesus went into a city called Nain * and, behold, there was a dead man carried out, the only son of his mother.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Prophéta magnus * surréxit in nobis, et quia Deus visitávit plebem suam.
Ant 3.eng: A great prophet is risen up among us * and God hath visited His people.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Ecclésiam tuam, Dómine, miserátio continuáta mundet et múniat: et quia sine te non potest salva consístere; tuo semper múnere gubernétur.
Oratio.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee, let thy continual pity cleanse and defend thy Church, and because it cannot continue in safety without thy succour, preserve it evermore by thy help and goodness.

Rule.lat:
9 lectiones
Psalmi Dominica
Antiphonas horas
Symbolum Athanasium

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Cum intráret Jesus * in domum cujúsdam príncipis pharisæórum sábbato manducáre panem, ecce homo quidam hydrópicus erat ante illum: ipse vero apprehénsum sanávit eum, ac dimísit.
Ant 2.eng: As Jesus went into the house * of one of the chief Pharisees, to eat bread on the Sabbath Day, behold, there was a certain man before Him which had the dropsy and He took him, and healed him, and let him go.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Cum vocátus fúeris * ad núptias, recúmbe in novíssimo loco, ut dicat tibi qui te invitávit: Amíce, ascénde supérius. Et erit tibi glória coram simul discumbéntibus, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: When thou art bidden * of any man to a wedding, go and sit down in the lowest room, that he that bade thee may say: Friend, go up higher, then shalt thou have worship in the presence of them that sit at meat with thee, alleluia.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Tua nos, quǽsumus, Dómine, grátia semper et prævéniat et sequátur: ac bonis opéribus júgiter præstet esse inténtos.
Oratio.eng: Lord, we pray thee, that thy grace may always prevent and follow us, and make us continually to be given to all good works.

Rule.lat:
9 lectiones
Psalmi Dominica
Antiphonas horas
Symbolum Athanasium

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Magíster, * quod est mandátum magnum in lege? Ait illi Jesus: Díliges Dóminum Deum tuum ex toto corde tuo, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: Master, which is the great commandment * in the law? Jesus said unto him: Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Quid vobis * vidétur de Christo? cujus fílius est? Dicunt ei omnes: David. Dicit eis Jesus: Quómodo David in spíritu vocat eum Dóminum dicens: Dixit Dóminus Dómino meo: Sede a dextris meis?
Ant 3.eng: What think ye of Christ? Whose Son is He? * They say all unto Him: The Son of David. Jesus saith unto them: How then doth David in spirit call Him Lord, saying: The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit Thou at My right hand?

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Da, quǽsumus, Dómine, pópulo tuo diabólica vitáre contágia: et te solum Deum pura mente sectári.
Oratio.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee, grant thy people grace to withstand the temptations of the devil, and with pure hearts to follow thee the only God.

Rule.lat:
9 lectiones
Psalmi Dominica
Antiphonas horas
Symbolum Athanasium

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Dixit Dóminus * paralýtico: Confíde, fili, remittúntur tibi peccáta tua.
Ant 2.eng: The Lord said unto the sick * of the palsy: Son, be of good cheer, thy sins be forgiven thee.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Tulit ergo * paralýticus lectum suum, in quo jacébat, magníficans Deum: et omnis plebs, ut vidit, dedit laudem Deo.
Ant 3.eng: And immediately, he that had been sick of the palsy arose, * and took up his bed whereon he lay, glorifying God and all the people, when they saw it, gave praise to God.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Dírigat corda nostra, quǽsumus, Dómine, tuæ miseratiónis operátio: quia tibi sine te placére non póssumus.
Oratio.eng: Mercifully grant, O Lord, that thine effectual goodness may in all things direct our hearts, forasmuch as without thee we are not able to please thee.

Rule.lat:
9 lectiones
Psalmi Dominica
Antiphonas horas
Symbolum Athanasium

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Dícite invitátis: * Ecce prándium meum parávi, veníte ad núptias, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: Tell them which are bidden: * Behold, I have prepared my dinner; Come unto the marriage. Alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Intrávit autem rex * ut vidéret discumbéntes, et vidit ibi hóminem non vestítum veste nuptiáli et ait illi: Amíce, quómodo huc intrásti non habens vestem nuptiálem?
Ant 3.eng: And the King came in * to see the guests, and he saw there a man which had not on a wedding garment. And he saith unto him: Friend, how camest thou in hither, not having a wedding garment?

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Omnípotens et miséricors Deus, univérsa nobis adversántia propitiátus exclúde: ut mente et córpore páriter expedíti, quæ tua sunt, líberis méntibus exsequámur.
Oratio.eng: O Almighty and most merciful God, of thy bountiful goodness keep us, we beseech thee, from all things that may hurt us; that we, being ready both in body and soul, may cheerfully accomplish those things that Thou wouldest have done.

Rule.lat:
9 lectiones
Psalmi Dominica
Antiphonas horas
Symbolum Athanasium

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Erat quidam régulus, * cujus fílius infirmabátur Caphárnaum. Hic cum audísset quod Jesus veníret in Galilǽam, rogábat eum ut sanáret fílium ejus.
Ant 2.eng: There was a certain nobleman whose son was sick * at Capernaum. When he heard that Jesus was come into Galilee, he besought Him that He would heal his son.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Cognóvit autem pater * quia illa hora erat, in qua dixit Jesus: Fílius tuus vivit; et crédidit ipse et domus ejus tota.
Ant 3.eng: So the father knew * that it was at the same hour in which Jesus said “Thy son liveth.” And he himself believed, and his whole house.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Largíre, quǽsumus, Dómine, fidélibus tuis indulgéntiam placátus et pacem: ut páriter ab ómnibus mundéntur offénsis, et secúra tibi mente desérviant.
Oratio.eng: Grant, we beseech thee, O Lord, to thy faithful people pardon and peace, that they may be cleansed from all their sins, and serve thee with a quiet mind.

Rule.lat:
9 lectiones
Psalmi Dominica
Antiphonas horas
Symbolum Athanasium

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Dixit autem * dóminus servo: Redde quod debes. Prócidens autem servus ille rogábat eum, dicens: Patiéntiam habe in me, et ómnia reddam tibi.
Ant 2.eng: The lord said unto his servant: Pay me * that thou owest. But the servant fell down and besought him, saying: Have patience with me, and I will pay thee all.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Serve nequam, * omne débitum dimísi tibi, quóniam rogásti me: nonne ergo opórtuit et te miseréri consérvi tui, sicut et ego tui misértus sum, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: O thou wicked servant, I forgave thee all * that debt, because thou desiredst me. Shouldest not thou also have had compassion on thy fellow-servant, even as I had pity on thee, alleluia.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Famíliam tuam, quǽsumus, Dómine, contínua pietáte custódi: ut a cunctis adversitátibus te protegénte, sit líbera; et in bonis áctibus tuo nómini sit devóta.
Oratio.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee to keep thine household in continual godliness, that, through thy protection, it may be free from all adversities, and devoutly given to serve thee in good works, to the glory of thy Name.

Rule.lat:
9 lectiones
Psalmi Dominica
Antiphonas horas
Symbolum Athanasium

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Magíster, * scimus quia verax es et viam Dei in veritáte doces, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: Master, we know that Thou art true, * and teachest the way of God in truth, alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Réddite ergo * quæ sunt Cǽsaris Cǽsari, et quæ sunt Dei Deo, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: Render therefore unto Caesar the things which are Caesar's, * and unto God the things that are God's, alleluia.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, refúgium nostrum et virtus: adésto piis Ecclésiæ tuæ précibus, auctor ipse pietátis, et præsta; ut, quod fidéliter pétimus, efficáciter consequámur.
Oratio.eng: O God, our Refuge and Strength, Who art the author of all godliness, be ready, we beseech thee, to hear the devout prayers of thy Church, and grant that those things which we ask faithfully, we may obtain effectually.

Rule.lat:
9 lectiones
Psalmi Dominica
Antiphonas horas
Symbolum Athanasium

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Dicébat enim * intra se: Si tetígero fímbriam vestiménti ejus tantum, salva ero.
Ant 2.eng: For she said within herself: * If I may but touch the hem of His garment, I shall be whole.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: At Jesus convérsus * et videns eam dixit: Confíde, fília, fides tua te salvam fecit, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: But Jesus turned Him about, * and when He saw her, He said: Daughter, be of good comfort; thy faith hath made thee whole, alleluia.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Absólve, quǽsumus, Dómine, tuórum delícta populórum: ut a peccatórum néxibus, quæ pro nostra fragilitáte contráximus, tua benignitáte liberémur.
Oratio.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee, absolve thy people from their offences, that through thy bountiful goodness we may all be delivered from the bands of those sins, which by our frailty we have committed.

Rule.lat:
9 lectiones
Psalmi Dominica
Antiphonas horas
Symbolum Athanasium

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Dicébat enim * intra se: Si tetígero fímbriam vestiménti ejus tantum, salva ero.
Ant 2.eng: For she said within herself: * If I may but touch the hem of His garment, I shall be whole.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: At Jesus convérsus * et videns eam dixit: Confíde, fília, fides tua te salvam fecit, allelúja.
Ant 3.eng: But Jesus turned Him about, * and when He saw her, He said: Daughter, be of good comfort; thy faith hath made thee whole, alleluia.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Absólve, quǽsumus, Dómine, tuórum delícta populórum: ut a peccatórum néxibus, quæ pro nostra fragilitáte contráximus, tua benignitáte liberémur.
Oratio.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee, absolve thy people from their offences, that through thy bountiful goodness we may all be delivered from the bands of those sins, which by our frailty we have committed.

Rule.lat:
3 lectiones
Symbolum Athanasium
No prima vespera

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Cum vidéritis * abominatiónem desolatiónis quæ dicta est a Daniéle prophéta, stantem in loco sancto: qui legit, intéllegat.
Ant 2.eng: When ye shall see the abomination of desolation, * spoken of by Daniel the Prophet, stand in the Holy Place, (whoso readeth, let him understand.)

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Amen dico vobis * quia non præteríbit generátio hæc, donec ómnia fiant: cælum et terra transíbunt, verba autem mea non transíbunt, dicit Dóminus.
Ant 3.eng: Amen, I say unto you, this generation shall not pass till all these things be fulfilled; * heaven and earth shall pass away, but My words shall not pass away, saith the Lord.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Excita, quǽsumus, Dómine, tuórum fidélium voluntátes: ut, divíni óperis fructum propénsius exsequéntes; pietátis tuæ remédia majóra percípiant.
Oratio.eng: Stir up, we beseech thee, Lord, the wills of thy faithful people, that they, plenteously bringing forth the fruit of good works, may of thee be plenteously rewarded.

Rule.lat:
9 lectiones
Psalmi Dominica
Antiphonas horas
Symbolum Athanasium

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Tunc invocábis, * et Dóminus exáudiet: clamábis, et dicet: Ecce adsum.
Ant 1.eng: Then shalt thou call, * and the Lord shall answer; thou shalt cry, and He shall say: Here I am.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Ductus est Jesus * in desértum a Spíritu, ut tentarétur a diábolo: et cum jejunásset quadragínta diébus et quadragínta nóctibus, póstea esúriit.
Ant 2.eng: Jesus was led up of the Spirit into the wilderness, * to be tempted of the devil and when He had fasted forty days and forty nights, He was afterward hungry.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Ecce nunc tempus * acceptábile, ecce nunc dies salútis: in his ergo diébus exhibeámus nosmetípsos sicut Dei minístros in multa patiéntia, in jejúniis, in vigíliis, et in caritáte non ficta.
Ant 3.eng: Behold, now is the accepted time * behold, now is the day of salvation; in these days therefore let us approve ourselves as the ministers of God, in much patience, in fastings, in watchings, and in love unfeigned.

Ant Nona.label: Antiphon
Ant Nona.lat: Dóminum Deum tuum * adorábis, et illi soli sérvies.
Ant Nona.eng: Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, * and Him only shalt thou serve.

Ant Prima.label: Antiphon
Ant Prima.lat: Jesus autem * cum jejunásset quadragínta diébus et quadragínta nóctibus, póstea esúriit.
Ant Prima.eng: When Jesus had fasted forty days * and forty nights, He was afterward hungry.

Ant Sexta.label: Antiphon
Ant Sexta.lat: Non in solo pane * vivit homo, sed in omni verbo, quod procédit de ore Dei.
Ant Sexta.eng: Man shall not live by bread alone, * but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.

Ant Tertia.label: Antiphon
Ant Tertia.lat: Tunc assúmpsit * eum diábolus in sanctam civitátem, et státuit eum supra pinnáculum templi, et dixit ei: Si Fílius Dei es, mitte te deórsum.
Ant Tertia.eng: Then the devil taketh Him up into the holy city, * and setteth Him on a pinnacle of the temple, and saith unto Him: If Thou be the Son of God, cast thyself down.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Fratres: Hortámur vos, ne in vácuum grátiam Dei recipiátis. Ait enim: Témpore accépto exaudívi te, et in die salútis adjúvi te.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Brothers, we exhort you, that you receive not the grace of God in vain. For he saith: In an accepted time have I heard thee; and in the day of salvation have I helped thee.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Ut castigáti, et non mortificáti: quasi tristes, semper autem gaudéntes: sicut egéntes, multos autem locupletántes tamquam nihil habéntes, et ómnia possidéntes.
Capitulum Nona.eng: As dying, and behold we live; as chastised, and not killed; as sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as needy, yet enriching many; as having nothing, and possessing all things.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Ecce nunc tempus acceptábile, ecce nunc dies salútis: némini dantes ullam offensiónem, ut non vituperétur ministérium nostrum.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: For he saith: In an accepted time have I heard thee; and in the day of salvation have I helped thee. Behold, now is the acceptable time; behold, now is the day of salvation, giving no offense to any man, that our ministry be not blamed.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui Ecclésiam tuam ánnua quadragesimáli observatióne puríficas: præsta famíliæ tuæ; ut, quod a te obtinére abstinéndo nítitur, hoc bonis opéribus exsequátur.
Oratio.eng: O God, Who dost every year purge thy Church by the Fast of Forty Days, grant unto this thy family, that what things soever they strive to obtain at thy hand by abstaining from meats, they may ever turn to profit by good works.

Versum 1.label: Versicle
Versum 1.lat: ℣. Ángelis suis Deus mandávit de te.
Versum 1.latR: ℟. Ut custódiant te in ómnibus viis tuis.
Versum 1.eng: ℣. God hath given His Angels charge over thee.
Versum 1.engR: ℟. To keep thee in all thy ways.

Versum 2.label: Versicle
Versum 2.lat: ℣. Ángelis suis Deus mandávit de te.
Versum 2.latR: ℟. Ut custódiant te in ómnibus viis tuis.
Versum 2.eng: ℣. God hath given His Angels charge over thee.
Versum 2.engR: ℟. To keep thee in all thy ways.

Versum 3.label: Versicle
Versum 3.lat: ℣. Ángelis suis Deus mandávit de te.
Versum 3.latR: ℟. Ut custódiant te in ómnibus viis tuis.
Versum 3.eng: ℣. God hath given His Angels charge over thee.
Versum 3.engR: ℟. To keep thee in all thy ways.

Ant Laudes.ant: Cor mundum * crea in me Deus, et spíritum rectum ínnova in viscéribus meis.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Create in me a clean heart, * O God, and renew a right spirit within me.

Ant Laudes.ant: O Dómine, * salvum me fac; o Dómine, bene prosperáre.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Save me now, O Lord; * O Lord, send Thou prosperity.

Ant Laudes.ant: Sic benedícam * te in vita mea, Dómine: et in nómine tuo levábo manus meas.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Thus will I bless thee, * O Lord, while I live; and will lift up my hands in thy Name.

Ant Laudes.ant: In spíritu humilitátis, * et in ánimo contríto suscipiámur, Dómine, a te: et sic fiat sacrifícium nostrum, ut a te suscipiátur hódie, et pláceat tibi, Dómine Deus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: In an humble spirit * and a contrite heart may we be accepted by thee, O Lord; and so let our sacrifice be this day, that it may be acceptable and pleasant in thy sight, O Lord our God!

Ant Laudes.ant: Laudáte Deum * cæli cælórum, et aquæ omnes.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Praise God, * ye heavens of heavens, and all ye waters.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Veníte, benedícti * Patris mei, percípite regnum, quod vobis parátum est ab orígine mundi.
Ant 2.eng: Come, ye blessed of My Father, * inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Quod uni * ex mínimis meis fecístis, mihi fecístis, dicit Dóminus.
Ant 3.eng: As long as you did it to one * of these my least brethren, you did it to me, said the Lord.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Convérte nos, Deus, salutáris noster: et, ut nobis jejúnium quadragesimále profíciat, mentes nostras cæléstibus ínstrue disciplínis.
Oratio 2.eng: Turn us, O God of our salvation, and that the Fast of these Forty Days may profit us, do Thou order all our thoughts according to thy heavenly teaching.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Absólve, quǽsumus, Dómine, nostrórum víncula peccatórum: et, quidquid pro eis merémur, propitiátus avérte.
Oratio 3.eng: Loose us, O Lord, we beseech thee, from all bonds of our sins, and in thy mercy turn away from us all pains which for the same we do justly deserve.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Intrávit Jesus * in templum Dei, et eiciébat omnes vendéntes et eméntes: et mensas nummulariórum, et cáthedras vendéntium colúmbas evértit.
Ant 2.eng: Jesus went into * the temple of God, * and cast out all them that sold and bought, and overthrew the tables of the money-changers, and the seats of them that sold doves.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Scriptum est enim, * quia domus mea, domus oratiónis est cunctis géntibus: vos autem fecístis illam spelúncam latrónum: et erat cotídie docens in templo.
Ant 3.eng: For it is written * that My house is the house of prayer * for all nations but ye have made it a den of thieves and He was daily teaching in the temple.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Réspice, Dómine, famíliam tuam, et præsta: ut apud te mens nostra tuo desidério fúlgeat, quæ se carnis maceratióne castígat.
Oratio 2.eng: Look down, O Lord, on this thy family, and grant that our minds, which, by the chastening of the body, we seek to purify, may ever more and more shine in thy sight by strong hungering after thee.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Ascéndant ad te, Dómine, preces nostræ: et ab Ecclésia tua cunctam repélle nequítiam.
Oratio 3.eng: O Lord, may our prayers come up before thy presence, and do Thou mercifully rid thy Church of all wickedness.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Generátio * hæc prava et pervérsa signum quærit: et signum non dábitur ei, nisi signum Jonæ prophétæ.
Ant 2.eng: This evil and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign; * and there shall no sign be given to it, but the sign of the Prophet Jonas.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Sicut fuit Jonas * in ventre ceti tribus diébus et tribus nóctibus, ita erit Fílius hóminis in corde terræ.
Ant 3.eng: As Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale's belly, * so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Preces nostras, quǽsumus, Dómine, cleménter exáudi: et contra cuncta nobis adversántia déxteram tuæ majestátis exténde.
Oratio 2.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee mercifully to hear our prayers, and to stretch forth the right hand of thy power against all things that fight against us.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Mentes nostras, quǽsumus, Dómine, lúmine tuæ claritátis illústra: ut vidére possímus quæ agénda sunt; et, quæ recta sunt, ágere valeámus.
Oratio 3.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee to cast thy bright beams of light upon our mind, that we may clearly see whatsoever things Thou wouldst have us to do, and have strength to do always that which is pleasing in thy sight.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Egréssus Jesus * secéssit in partes Tyri et Sidónis: et ecce múlier Chananǽa a fínibus illis egréssa, clamábat dicens: Miserére mei, Fili David.
Ant 2.eng: And Jesus went from thence * and retired into the coasts of Tyre and Sidon. And behold a woman of Canaan who came out of those coasts, crying out, said to him: Have mercy on me, O thou Son of David.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: O múlier, * magna est fides tua: fiat tibi sicut petísti.
Ant 3.eng: O woman * great is thy faith; be it unto thee even as thou wilt.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Devotiónem pópuli tui, quǽsumus, Dómine, benígnus inténde: ut, qui per abstinéntiam macerántur in córpore, per fructum boni óperis reficiántur in mente.
Oratio 2.eng: We beseech thee, O Lord, look with favor upon the devotion of Thy people, that they who mortify the body by abstinence, may be refreshed in mind by the fruit of good works.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Da, quǽsumus, Dómine, pópulis christiánis: et, quæ profiténtur, agnóscere, et cæléste munus dilígere, quod frequéntant.
Oratio 3.eng: Grant, O Lord, we beseech thee, unto all Christian people, that what they now believe they may one day know and may see in love unchecked, that heavenly gift whereof now they are the worshippers and the partakers.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Angelus Dómini * descendébat de cælo, et movebátur aqua, et sanabátur unus.
Ant 2.eng: The Angel of the Lord * came down from heaven and the water was troubled, and one was made whole.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Qui me sanum fecit * ille mihi præcépit: tolle grabátum tuum, et ámbula in pace.
Ant 3.eng: He that made me whole, * the same said unto me: Take up thy bed, and walk in peace.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Esto, Dómine, propítius plebi tuæ: et, quam tibi facis esse devótam, benígno réfove miserátus auxílio.
Oratio 2.eng: Be gracious unto thy people, O Lord, and in thy mercy help all such as Thou hast called to be thine.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Exáudi nos, miséricors Deus: et méntibus nostris grátiæ tuæ lumen osténde.
Oratio 3.eng: Hear us, O merciful God, and cause the bright beams of thy grace to shine upon our souls.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Assúmpsit Jesus * discípulos suos, et ascéndit in montem, et transfigurátus est ante eos.
Ant 2.eng: Jesus took His disciples, * and went up into a mountain, and was transfigured before them.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Pópulum tuum, quǽsumus, Dómine, propítius réspice: atque ab eo flagélla tuæ iracúndiæ cleménter avérte.
Oratio 2.eng: Look down mercifully, O Lord, we beseech thee, upon thy people, and graciously turn away from them the scourges of thy wrath.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Visiónem quam vidístis, * némini dixéritis, donec a mórtuis resúrgat Fílius hóminis.
Ant 1.eng: Tell the vision that ye have seen to no man, * until the Son of man be risen again from the dead.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Assúmpsit Jesus * discípulos suos, et ascéndit in montem, et transfigurátus est ante eos.
Ant 2.eng: Jesus took His disciples, * and went up into a mountain, and was transfigured before them.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Visiónem quam vidístis, * némini dixéritis, donec a mórtuis resúrgat Fílius hóminis.
Ant 3.eng: Tell the vision that ye have seen to no man, * until the Son of man be risen again from the dead.

Ant Nona.label: Antiphon
Ant Nona.lat: Visiónem quam vidístis, * némini dixéritis, donec a mórtuis resúrgat Fílius hóminis.
Ant Nona.eng: Tell the vision that ye have seen to no man, * until the Son of man be risen again from the dead.

Ant Prima.label: Antiphon
Ant Prima.lat: Dómine, * bonum est nos hic esse: si vis, faciámus hic tria tabernácula; tibi unum, Móysi unum, et Elíæ unum.
Ant Prima.eng: Lord, it is good for us to be here; * if Thou wilt, let us make here three tabernacles, one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.

Ant Sexta.label: Antiphon
Ant Sexta.lat: Faciámus hic * tria tabernácula; tibi unum, Móysi unum, et Elíæ unum.
Ant Sexta.eng: Let us make here three tabernacles, * one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.

Ant Tertia.label: Antiphon
Ant Tertia.lat: Dómine, * bonum est nos hic esse: si vis, faciámus hic tria tabernácula; tibi unum, Móysi unum, et Elíæ unum.
Ant Tertia.eng: Lord, it is good for us to be here; * if Thou wilt, let us make here three tabernacles, one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Fratres: Rogámus vos, et obsecrámus in Dómino Jesu: ut, quemádmodum accepístis a nobis, quómodo vos opórteat ambuláre, et placére Deo, sic et ambulétis, ut abundétis magis.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: For the rest therefore, brethren, we pray and beseech you in the Lord Jesus, that as you have received from us, how you ought to walk, and to please God, so also you would walk, that you may abound the more.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Non enim vocávit nos Deus in immundítiam, sed in sanctificatiónem, in Christo Jesu Dómino nostro.
Capitulum Nona.eng: For God hath not called us unto uncleanness, but unto sanctification in Christ Jesus our Lord.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Hæc est enim volúntas Dei, sanctificátio vestra: ut abstineátis vos a fornicatióne, ut sciat unusquísque vestrum vas suum possidére in sanctificatióne et honóre.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: For this is the will of God, your sanctification; that you should abstain from fornication, that every one of you should know how to possess his vessel in sanctification and honour.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui cónspicis omni nos virtúte destítui: intérius exteriúsque custódi; ut ab ómnibus adversitátibus muniámur in córpore, et a pravis cogitatiónibus mundémur in mente.
Oratio.eng: O God, Who seest that we have no power of ourselves to help ourselves, keep us both outwardly in our bodies, and inwardly in our souls, that we may be defended from all adversities which may happen to the body, and from all evil thoughts which may assault and hurt the soul.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dómine, * lábia mea apéries, et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O Lord, open Thou my lips, * and my mouth shall show forth thy praise.

Ant Laudes.ant: Déxtera Dómini * fecit virtútem: déxtera Dómini exaltávit me.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The right hand of the Lord * hath done valiantly, the right hand of the Lord hath exalted me.

Ant Laudes.ant: Factus est * adjútor meus, Deus meus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: My God * hath been my help.

Ant Laudes.ant: Trium puerórum * cantémus hymnum, quem cantábant in camíno ignis, benedicéntes Dóminum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Let us sing the Song of the Three Children, * even the Song that they sang when they blessed the Lord in the burning fiery furnace.

Ant Laudes.ant: Státuit ea * in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.
Ant Laudes.antEng: He hath established them * for ever and ever: He hath made a decree which shall not pass.

Ant 2.eng: Jesus took His disciples, * and went up into a mountain, and was transfigured before them.

Ant Tertia.eng: Lord, it is good for us to be here; * if Thou wilt, let us make here three tabernacles, one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.
