Ant Laudes.antEng: O Lord, open Thou my lips, * and my mouth shall show forth thy praise.

Ant Laudes.ant: Déxtera Dómini * fecit virtútem: déxtera Dómini exaltávit me.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The right hand of the Lord * hath done valiantly, the right hand of the Lord hath exalted me.

Ant Laudes.ant: Factus est * adjútor meus, Deus meus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: My God * hath been my help.

Ant Laudes.ant: Trium puerórum * cantémus hymnum, quem cantábant in camíno ignis, benedicéntes Dóminum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Let us sing the Song of the Three Children, * even the Song that they sang when they blessed the Lord in the burning fiery furnace.

Ant Laudes.ant: Státuit ea * in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.
Ant Laudes.antEng: He hath established them * for ever and ever: He hath made a decree which shall not pass.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Ego princípium, * qui et loquor vobis.
Ant 2.eng: The beginning, * who also speak unto you.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Qui me misit * mecum est, et non relíquit me solum; quia quæ plácita sunt ei, fácio semper.
Ant 3.eng: He That sent Me is with Me, * and hath not left Me alone, for I do always those things that please Him.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut família tua, quæ se, affligéndo carnem, ab aliméntis ábstinet, sectándo justítiam, a culpa jejúnet.
Oratio 2.eng: Almighty God, grant, we beseech thee, unto this thy family, that as they do abstain from meals to afflict the flesh, so by following after righteousness they may fast from sin.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Adésto supplicatiónibus nostris, omnípotens Deus: et, quibus fidúciam sperándæ pietátis indúlges; consuétæ misericórdiæ tríbue benígnus efféctum.
Oratio 3.eng: Graciously hear our prayers, O Almighty God, and as Thou dost give us to look with confidence for thy favour for which we hope, so grant us, in thy goodness, the manifestation of thine accustomed mercy.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Unus est * enim magíster vester, qui in cælis est, Christus Dóminus.
Ant 2.eng: For One is your Master, * Which is in heaven, even Christ the Lord.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Omnes autem * vos fratres estis: et patrem nolíte vocáre vobis super terram: unus est enim Pater vester, qui in cælis est: nec vocémini magístri, quia magíster vester unus est Christus.
Ant 3.eng: And all ye are brethren, * and call no man your father upon earth, for One is your Father, Which is in heaven; neither be ye called masters, for One is your Master, even Christ.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Pérfice, quǽsumus, Dómine, benígnus in nobis observántiæ sanctæ subsídium: ut, quæ te auctóre faciénda cognóvimus, te operánte impleámus.
Oratio 2.eng: Enable us, O Lord, we beseech thee, to carry to a perfect end this holy and helpful observance, that what we know we have to do by thine ordinance we may be helped to do by thy strength.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Propitiáre, Dómine, supplicatiónibus nostris, et animárum nostrárum medére languóribus: ut, remissióne percépta, in tua semper benedictióne lætémur.
Oratio 3.eng: Tend thy merciful ears, O Lord, we beseech thee, unto our supplications, and heal the sickness of our souls, that we, receiving thy pardon, may rejoice for ever in thy blessing.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Ecce ascéndimus * Jerosólymam: et Fílius hóminis tradétur ad crucifigéndum.
Ant 2.eng: Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, * and the Son of man shall be betrayed to be crucified.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Tradétur enim géntibus * ad illudéndum, et flagellándum, et crucifigéndum.
Ant 3.eng: For He shall be delivered to the Gentiles, * to mock, and to scourge, and to crucify.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Pópulum tuum, quǽsumus, Dómine, propítius réspice: et quos ab escis carnálibus prǽcipis abstinére, a nóxiis quoque vítiis cessáre concéde.
Oratio 2.eng: Look down in mercy upon thy people, O Lord, we beseech thee, and grant unto them, whom Thou commandest to abstain from fleshly meats, power to abstain also from the corruption of sin.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Deus, innocéntiæ restitútor et amátor, dírige ad te tuórum corda servórum: ut, spíritus tui fervóre concépto, et in fide inveniántur stábiles, et in ópere efficáces.
Oratio 3.eng: God, the Renewer and Lover of innocency, turn the hearts of all thy servants to thyself, that so they, being enkindled with the fire of thy Spirit, may be found ever rooted in faith, and fruitful in works.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Fili, recordáre, * quia recepísti bona in vita tua, et Lázarus simíliter mala.
Ant 2.eng: Son, remember * that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Dives ille * guttam aquæ pétiit, qui micas panis Lázaro negávit.
Ant 3.eng: That rich man * who had refused Lazarus bread-crumbs, cried for a drop of water.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Præsta nobis, quǽsumus, Dómine, auxílium grátiæ tuæ: ut, jejúniis et oratiónibus conveniénter inténti, liberémur ab hóstibus mentis et córporis.
Oratio 2.eng: Grant unto us, O Lord, we beseech thee, the help of thy grace, that we, who are now bent on fasting and prayer, may be freed from enemies both of our bodies and of our souls.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Adésto, Dómine, fámulis tuis, et perpétuam benignitátem largíre poscéntibus: ut iis, qui te auctóre et gubernatóre gloriántur, et congregáta restáures et restauráta consérves.
Oratio 3.eng: O Lord, help thy servants, and grant unto their prayers this abiding effect of thy mercy that as they do make their boast in thee, that it is Thou which hast created and dost govern them, so Thou wilt renew in them the gifts wherewith Thou didst bountifully endow them, and wilt preserve what Thou hast renewed.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Malos male perdet, * et víneam suam locábit áliis agrícolis, qui reddant ei fructum tempóribus suis.
Ant 2.eng: He will miserably destroy * those wicked men, and will let out His vineyard unto other husbandmen, which shall render Him the fruits in their seasons.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Quæréntes eum tenére, * timuérunt turbam, quia sicut prophétam eum habébant.
Ant 3.eng: When they sought * to lay hands on Him, they feared the multitude, because they took Him for a Prophet.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Da, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, sacro nos purificánte jejúnio, sincéris méntibus ad sancta ventúra fácias perveníre.
Oratio 2.eng: O Almighty God, grant, we beseech thee, that the Sacred Fast may so cleanse us that thereby Thou mayest make us to come with clean hearts unto those holy ordinances which are now before us.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Da, quǽsumus, Dómine, pópulo tuo salútem mentis et córporis: ut, bonis opéribus inhæréndo, tuæ semper virtútis mereátur protectióne deféndi.
Oratio 3.eng: Grant unto thy people, O Lord, we beseech thee, soundness both of mind and body, that they, cleaving ever unto good works, may evermore worthily be defended by the shield of thine Almighty arm.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Vadam ad Patrem meum * et dicam ei: Pater, fac me sicut unum ex mercenáriis tuis.
Ant 2.eng: I will arise and go to my father, * and will say unto him: Make me as one of thine hired servants.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Dixit autem pater * ad servos suos: Cito proférte stolam primam, et indúite illum, et date ánulum in manu ejus, et calceaménta in pédibus ejus.
Ant 3.eng: But the father said * to his servants: Bring forth quickly the first robe, and put it on him, and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Da, quǽsumus, Dómine, nostris efféctum jejúniis salutárem: ut castigátio carnis assúmpta, ad nostrárum vegetatiónem tránseat animárum.
Oratio 2.eng: Grant, O Lord, we beseech thee, that our Fasts may bring forth their fruit unto salvation, that so the affliction which we lay upon our bodies may quicken our souls unto spiritual increase.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus, vota humílium réspice: atque ad defensiónem nostram, déxteram tuæ majestátis exténde.
Oratio 3.eng: We beeseech thee, almighty God, look upon the hearty desires of thy humble servants, and stretch forth the right hand of thy Majesty to be our defense against all our enemies.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Dixit autem pater * ad servos suos: Cito proférte stolam primam, et indúite illum, et date ánulum in manu ejus, et calceaménta in pédibus ejus.
Ant 1.eng: But the father said to his servants: * Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him, and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Cum fortis armátus * custódit átrium suum, in pace sunt ómnia quæ póssidet.
Ant 2.eng: When a strong man armed keepeth his palace, * his goods are in peace.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Extóllens vocem * quædam múlier de turba, dixit: Beátus venter qui te portávit, et úbera quæ suxísti. At Jesus ait illi: Quinímmo beáti, qui áudiunt verbum Dei, et custódiunt illud.
Ant 3.eng: A certain woman of the company lifted up her voice and said: * Blessed is the womb that bare thee, and the paps which Thou hast sucked. But Jesus said unto her: Yea, rather, blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it.

Ant Nona.label: Antiphon
Ant Nona.lat: Cum immúndus spíritus * exíerit ab hómine, ámbulat per loca inaquósa, quærens réquiem et non ínvenit.
Ant Nona.eng: When the unclean spirit * is gone out of a man, he walketh through dry places, seeking rest, and finding none.

Ant Prima.label: Antiphon
Ant Prima.lat: Et cum ejecísset Jesus * dæmónium, locútus est mutus, et admirátæ sunt turbæ.
Ant Prima.eng: When Jesus had cast out the devil, * the dumb spake, and the people wondered.

Ant Sexta.label: Antiphon
Ant Sexta.lat: Qui non cólligit mecum * dispérgit, et qui non est mecum, contra me est.
Ant Sexta.eng: He that gathereth not with Me scattereth, * and he that is not with Me is against Me.

Ant Tertia.label: Antiphon
Ant Tertia.lat: Si in dígito Dei * eício dæmónia, profécto pervénit in vos regnum Dei.
Ant Tertia.eng: If I with the finger of God * cast out devils, no doubt the kingdom of God is come upon you.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Fratres: Estóte imitatóres Dei, sicut fílii caríssimi: et ambuláte in dilectióne, sicut et Christus diléxit nos, et trádidit semetípsum pro nobis oblatiónem et hóstiam Deo in odórem suavitátis.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Be ye, therefore, followers of God, as most dear children; And walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us, and hath delivered himself for us, an oblation and a sacrifice to God for an odour of sweetness.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Erátis enim aliquándo ténebræ, nunc autem lux in Dómino: ut fílii lucis ambuláte: fructus enim lucis est in omni bonitáte, et justítia, et veritáte.
Capitulum Nona.eng: For you were heretofore darkness, but now light in the Lord. Walk then as children of the light. For the fruit of the light is in all goodness, and justice, and truth.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Hoc enim scitóte intellegéntes, quod omnis fornicátor, aut immúndus, aut avarus, quod est idolórum sérvitus, non habet hereditátem in regno Christi et Dei.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: For know you this and understand, that no fornicator, or unclean, or covetous person (which is a serving of idols), hath inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and of God.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus, vota humílium réspice: atque ad defensiónem nostram, déxteram tuæ majestátis exténde.
Oratio.eng: We beeseech thee, almighty God, look upon the hearty desires of thy humble servants, and stretch forth the right hand of thy Majesty to be our defense against all our enemies.

Ant Laudes.ant: Fac benígne * in bona voluntáte tua, ut ædificéntur, Dómine, muri Jerúsalem.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O Lord, do good in thy good pleasure * unto Zion; to build the walls of Jerusalem.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dóminus * mihi adjútor est, non timébo quid fáciat mihi homo.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Lord is on my side; * I will not fear what can man do unto me.

Ant Laudes.ant: Adhǽsit ánima mea * post te, Deus meus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O my God, my soul cleaveth fast * after thee, O God.

Ant Laudes.ant: Vim virtútis suæ * oblítus est ignis: ut púeri tui liberaréntur illǽsi.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The fire forgot his strength * that thy children might be delivered therefrom.

Ant Laudes.ant: Sol et luna * laudáte Deum: quia exaltátum est nomen ejus solíus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Praise God, O ye sun and moon, * for His Name alone is exalted!

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Amen dico vobis, * quia nemo prophéta accéptus est in pátria sua.
Ant 2.eng: Amen I say unto you, * no Prophet is accepted in his own country.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Jesus autem, tránsiens * per médium illórum, ibat.
Ant 3.eng: But Jesus, * passing through the midst of them, went His way.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Córdibus nostris, quǽsumus, Dómine, grátiam tuam benígnus infúnde: ut, sicut ab escis carnálibus abstinémus; ita sensus quoque nostros a nóxiis retrahámus excéssibus.
Oratio 2.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee mercifully to shed abroad thy grace into our hearts, that we who are now denying carnal meats to our bodily cravings, may have power likewise to withhold from the same all yielding to the deathful lusts of sin.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Subvéniat nobis, Dómine, misericórdia tua: ut ab imminéntibus peccatórum nostrórum perículis te mereámur protegénte éripi, te liberánte salvári.
Oratio 3.eng: Let our help, O Lord, be in thy mercy, that we over whom thy wrath doth most justly hang because of our sins, may in all dangers worthily be shielded by thy protection and delivered by thy salvation.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Si duo ex vobis * consénserint super terram: de omni re quamcúmque petíerint, fiet illis a Patre meo, dicit Dóminus.
Ant 2.eng: If two of you shall agree on earth * as touching anything that they shall ask, it shall be done for them of My Father, saith the Lord.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Ubi duo vel tres * congregáti fúerint in nómine meo, in médio eórum sum, dicit Dóminus.
Ant 3.eng: Where two or three are gathered together in My Name, * there am I in the midst of them, saith the Lord.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Exáudi nos, omnípotens et miséricors Deus: et continéntiæ salutáris propítius nobis dona concéde.
Oratio 2.eng: Graciously hear us, O Almighty and merciful God, and in thy goodness enable us to reap the fruit of this our healthful Fasting.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Tua nos, Dómine, protectióne defénde: et ab omni semper iniquitáte custódi.
Oratio 3.eng: O Lord, shield us by thy protection, and keep us ever from all iniquity.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Audíte et intellégite * traditiónes, quas Dóminus dedit nobis.
Ant 2.eng: Hear and understand * the traditions which the Lord hath given unto us.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Non lotis mánibus * manducáre, non coínquinat hóminem.
Ant 3.eng: To eat * with unwashen hands, defileth not a man.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Præsta nobis, quǽsumus, Dómine: ut salutáribus jejúniis erudíti, a nóxiis quoque vítiis abstinéntes, propitiatiónem tuam facílius impetrémus.
Oratio 2.eng: Grant unto us, O Lord, we beseech thee, that we, being purged by healthful Fasting, and mortified to all sinful lusts, may the more speedily obtain of thee forgiveness.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Concéde, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui protectiónis tuæ grátiam quǽrimus, liberáti a malis ómnibus, secúra tibi mente serviámus.
Oratio 3.eng: Grant unto us, we beseech thee, O Almighty God, that we who seek the shelter of thy protection, being defended from all evils, may serve thee in peace and quietness of spirit.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Audíte et intellégite * traditiónes, quas Dóminus dedit nobis.
Ant 2.eng: Hear and understand * the traditions which the Lord hath given unto us.

Oratio 2.eng: Grant unto us, O Lord, we beseech thee, that we, being purged by healthful Fasting, and mortified to all sinful lusts, may the more speedily obtain of thee forgiveness.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Concéde, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui protectiónis tuæ grátiam quǽrimus, liberáti a malis ómnibus, secúra tibi mente serviámus.
Oratio 3.eng: Grant unto us, we beseech thee, O Almighty God, that we who seek the shelter of thy protection, being defended from all evils, may serve thee in peace and quietness of spirit.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Exíbant autem dæmónia * a multis clamántia, et dicéntia, Quia tu es Christus Fílius Dei: et íncrepans non sinébat ea loqui, quia sciébant ipsum esse Christum.
Ant 2.eng: And devils also came out of many, * crying out and saying: Thou art Christ, the Son of God. And He, rebuking them, suffered them not to speak, for they knew that He was Christ.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Omnes qui habébant infírmos, * ducébant illos ad Jesum, et sanabántur.
Ant 3.eng: All they that had * any sick brought them unto Jesus, and He healed them.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Magníficet te, Dómine, sanctórum tuórum Cosmæ et Damiáni beáta solémnitas: qua et illis glóriam sempitérnam, et opem nobis ineffábili providéntia contulísti.
Oratio 2.eng: Praise be to thee, O Lord, for the blessed and solemn victory of thine holy servants Cosmas and Damian, whereby Thou, in thine unspeakable Providence, wast pleased to give unto them everlasting glory, and unto us a shield and succour.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Subjéctum tibi pópulum, quǽsumus, Dómine, propitiátio cæléstis amplíficet: et tuis semper fáciat servíre mandátis.
Oratio 3.eng: Lord, we beseech thee that thine heavenly Peace-Offering may so effectually work for all thy people, which are now bowing themselves down before thee, that they may ever continue in meek obedience to thy commandments.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Exíbant autem dæmónia * a multis clamántia, et dicéntia, Quia tu es Christus Fílius Dei: et íncrepans non sinébat ea loqui, quia sciébant ipsum esse Christum.

Oratio 3.eng: Lord, we beseech thee that thine heavenly Peace-Offering may so effectually work for all thy people, which are now bowing themselves down before thee, that they may ever continue in meek obedience to thy commandments.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Aquam, quam ego dédero, * si quis bíberit ex ea, non sítiet in ætérnum.
Ant 2.eng: Whosoever drinketh * of the water that I shall give him, shall never thirst.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Dómine, * ut vídeo, prophéta es tu: patres nostri in monte hoc adoravérunt.
Ant 3.eng: Sir, I perceive * that Thou art a prophet: our fathers worshipped in this mountain.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Jejúnia nostra, quǽsumus, Dómine, benígno favóre proséquere: ut, sicut ab aliméntis abstinémus in córpore; ita a vítiis jejunémus in mente.
Oratio 2.eng: Lord, we beseech thee graciously to bless this our Fast, that we who are now outwardly denying meats to our bodies, may have power inwardly to keep our souls fasting from all sin.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui in tua protectióne confídimus, cuncta nobis adversántia te adjuvánte vincámus.
Oratio 3.eng: Grant, we beseech thee, O Almighty God, that we whose trust is under the shadow of thy wings, may, through the help of thy power, overcome all evils that rise up against us.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Aquam, quam ego dédero, * si quis bíberit ex ea, non sítiet in ætérnum.
Ant 2.eng: Whosoever drinketh * of the water that I shall give him, shall never thirst.

Oratio 2.eng: Lord, we beseech thee graciously to bless this our Fast, that we who are now outwardly denying meats to our bodies, may have power inwardly to keep our souls fasting from all sin.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui in tua protectióne confídimus, cuncta nobis adversántia te adjuvánte vincámus.
Oratio 3.eng: Grant, we beseech thee, O Almighty God, that we whose trust is under the shadow of thy wings, may, through the help of thy power, overcome all evils that rise up against us.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Inclinávit se Jesus, * et scribébat in terra: Si quis sine peccáto est, mittat in eam lápidem.
Ant 2.eng: Jesus stooped down, * and wrote on the ground: He that is without sin, let him cast a stone at her.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui se, affligéndo carnem, ab aliméntis ábstinent; sectándo justítiam a culpa jejúnent.
Oratio 2.eng: O Almighty God, grant, we beseech thee, that as many as, to afflict the body, do abstain from meats, may, by following after righteousness, fast from sin.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Inclinávit se Jesus, * et scribébat in terra: Si quis sine peccáto est, mittat in eam lápidem.
Ant 2.eng: Jesus stooped down, * and wrote on the ground: He that is without sin, let him cast a stone at her.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui se, affligéndo carnem, ab aliméntis ábstinent; sectándo justítiam a culpa jejúnent.
Oratio 2.eng: O Almighty God, grant, we beseech thee, that as many as, to afflict the body, do abstain from meats, may, by following after righteousness, fast from sin.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Nemo te condemnávit, múlier? * Nemo, Dómine. Nec ego te condemnábo: jam ámplius noli peccáre.
Ant 1.eng: Woman, hath no man condemned thee? * No man, Lord. Neither do I condemn thee; go, and sin no more.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Cum sublevásset óculos * Jesus, et vidísset máximam multitúdinem veniéntem ad se, dixit ad Philíppum: Unde emémus panes, ut mandúcent hi? Hoc autem dicébat tentans eum: ipse enim sciébat quid esset factúrus.
Ant 2.eng: When Jesus lifted up His Eyes, * and saw a great company come unto Him, He saith unto Philip: Whence shall we buy bread that these may eat? And this He said to prove him; for He Himself knew what He would do.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Súbiit ergo, * in montem Jesus, et ibi sedébat cum discípulis suis.
Ant 3.eng: And Jesus went up into a mountain, * and there He sat with His disciples.

Ant Nona.label: Antiphon
Ant Nona.lat: Illi ergo * hómines, cum vidíssent quod fécerat Jesus signum, intra se dicébant: quia hic est vere Prophéta, qui ventúrus est in mundum.
Ant Nona.eng: Then those men, * when they had seen the miracle that Jesus did, said amongst themselves: This is of a truth that Prophet that should come into the world.

Ant Prima.label: Antiphon
Ant Prima.lat: Accépit ergo * Jesus panes, et, cum grátias egísset, distríbuit discumbéntibus.
Ant Prima.eng: And Jesus took the loaves, * and when He had given thanks, He distributed to them that were set down.

Ant Sexta.label: Antiphon
Ant Sexta.lat: Satiávit Dóminus * quinque míllia hóminum de quinque pánibus et duobus píscibus.
Ant Sexta.eng: With five loaves and two fishes * did the Lord satisfy five thousand men.

Ant Tertia.label: Antiphon
Ant Tertia.lat: De quinque pánibus * et duobus píscibus satiávit Dóminus quinque míllia hóminum.
Ant Tertia.eng: With five loaves and two fishes * did the Lord satisfy five thousand men.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Fratres: Scriptum est, quóniam Abraham duos fílios hábuit: unum de ancílla, et unum de líbera: sed qui de ancílla, secúndum carnem natus est: qui autem de líbera, per repromissiónem: quæ sunt per allegoríam dicta.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Brothers: For it is written that Abraham had two sons: the one by a bondwoman, and the other by a free woman. But he who was of the bondwoman, was born according to the flesh: but he of the free woman, was by promise, which things are said by an allegory.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Itaque, fratres, non sumus ancíllæ fílii, sed líberæ: qua libertáte Christus nos liberávit.
Capitulum Nona.eng: So then, brethren, we are not the children of the bondwoman, but of the free: by the freedom wherewith Christ has made us free.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Lætáre, stérilis, quæ non paris: erúmpe et clama, quæ non párturis: quia multi fílii desértæ, magis quam ejus, quæ habet virum.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: For it is written: Rejoice, thou barren, that bearest not: break forth and cry, thou that travailest not: for many are the children of the desolate, more than of her that hath a husband.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Concéde, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui ex mérito nostræ actiónis afflígimur, tuæ grátiæ consolatióne respirémus.
Oratio.eng: Grant, we beseech thee, Almighty God, that we who for our evil deeds are worthily punished, may, by the comfort of thy grace, mercifully be relieved.

Ant Laudes.ant: Tunc acceptábis * sacrifícium justítiæ, si avérteris fáciem tuam a peccátis meis.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Then shalt Thou be pleased * with the sacrifices of righteousness, when Thou hast hidden thy face from my sins.

Ant Laudes.ant: Bonum est * speráre in Dómino, quam speráre in princípibus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: It is better to trust * in the Lord, than to trust in princes.

Ant Laudes.ant: Me suscépit * déxtera tua, Dómine.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Thy right hand hath * received me, O Lord.

Ant Laudes.ant: Potens es, Dómine, * erípere nos de manu forti: líbera nos, Deus noster.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O Lord, Thou art mighty * to save us; with a strong hand deliver us, O our God.

Ant Laudes.ant: Reges terræ * et omnes pópuli, laudáte Deum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Kings of the earth, * and all people, praise God.

Ant Laudes.antEng: Kings of the earth, * and all people, praise God.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Auférte ista hinc, * dicit Dóminus: et nolíte fácere domum Patris mei domum negotiatiónis.
Ant 2.eng: Thus saith the Lord: * Take these things hence; make not My Father's house an house of merchandise.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Sólvite templum hoc, * dicit Dóminus; et post tríduum reædificábo illud: hoc autem dicébat de templo córporis sui.
Ant 3.eng: Thus saith the Lord: * Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. But He spoke of the temple of His Body.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut observatiónes sacras ánnua devotióne recoléntes, et córpore tibi placeámus, et mente.
Oratio 2.eng: Grant, we beseech thee, O Almighty God, that we who year by year do prayerfully renew the holy observance of this thy great Fast, may be acceptable in thy sight, as touching both our bodies and our souls.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Deprecatiónem nostram, quǽsumus, Dómine, benígnus exáudi: et, quibus supplicándi præstas afféctum, tríbue defensiónis auxílium.
Oratio 3.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee graciously to hear our supplications, and evermore help and defend all them to whom Thou hast given the mind to pray.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Quid me quǽritis * interfícere, hóminem qui vera locútus sum vobis?
Ant 2.eng: Why go ye about to kill Me, * a Man that hath told you the truth?

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Nemo in eum misit manum: * quia nondum vénerat hora ejus.
Ant 3.eng: No man laid hands on Him; * because His hour was not yet come.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Sacræ nobis, quǽsumus, Dómine, observatiónis jejúnia: et piæ conversatiónis augméntum, et tuæ propitiatiónis contínuum præstent auxílium.
Oratio 2.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee, that the observance of this holy fast may avail us both to the increase of godliness in our conversation, and the stablishing upon us of the help of thy mercy.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Miserére, Dómine, pópulo tuo: et contínuis tribulatiónibus laborántem propítius respiráre concéde.
Oratio 3.eng: O Lord, have mercy upon thy people, and be graciously pleased to grant relief unto the same, who are ever toiling amid the storms of diverse tribulations.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Quid me quǽritis * interfícere, hóminem qui vera locútus sum vobis?
Ant 2.eng: Why go ye about to kill Me, * a Man that hath told you the truth?

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Nemo in eum misit manum: * quia nondum vénerat hora ejus.
Ant 3.eng: No man laid hands on Him; * because His hour was not yet come.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Sacræ nobis, quǽsumus, Dómine, observatiónis jejúnia: et piæ conversatiónis augméntum, et tuæ propitiatiónis contínuum præstent auxílium.
Oratio 2.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee, that the observance of this holy fast may avail us both to the increase of godliness in our conversation, and the stablishing upon us of the help of thy mercy.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Miserére, Dómine, pópulo tuo: et contínuis tribulatiónibus laborántem propítius respiráre concéde.
Oratio 3.eng: O Lord, have mercy upon thy people, and be graciously pleased to grant relief unto the same, who are ever toiling amid the storms of diverse tribulations.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Rabbi, quid peccávit * homo iste, quod cæcus natus est? Respóndit Jesus, et dixit: Neque hic peccávit, neque paréntes ejus: sed ut manifesténtur ópera Dei in illo.
Ant 2.eng: Rabbi, who did sin, this man, or his parents, * that he was born blind? Jesus answered, and said: Neither hath this man sinned, nor his parents; but that the works of God shall be made manifest in him.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Ille homo * qui dícitur Jesus, lutum fecit ex sputo, et linívit óculos meos, et modo vídeo.
Ant 3.eng: The Man that is called Jesus * made clay of His Spittle, and anointed mine eyes, and now I do see.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Deus, qui et justis prǽmia meritórum, et peccatóribus per jejúnium véniam præbes: miserére supplícibus tuis; ut reátus nostri conféssio indulgéntiam váleat percípere delictórum.
Oratio 2.eng: O God, Who by mean of fasting dost give unto the righteous the reward of their good works, and unto sinners pardon; have mercy upon us, we beseech thee, and grant that we, humbly confessing our guiltiness, may so be enabled to obtain thy forgiveness.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Páteant aures misericórdiæ tuæ, Dómine, précibus supplicántium: et, ut peténtibus desideráta concédas, fac eos, quæ tibi sunt plácita, postuláre.
Oratio 3.eng: Let thy merciful ears, O Lord, be open unto the prayers of all them that entreat thee, and that Thou mayest grant us ever such things as we ask, teach us ever to ask such things as are pleasing in thy sight.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Rabbi, quid peccávit * homo iste, quod cæcus natus est? Respóndit Jesus, et dixit: Neque hic peccávit, neque paréntes ejus: sed ut manifesténtur ópera Dei in illo.
Ant 2.eng: Rabbi, who did sin, this man, or his parents, * that he was born blind? Jesus answered, and said: Neither hath this man sinned, nor his parents; but that the works of God shall be made manifest in him.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Ille homo * qui dícitur Jesus, lutum fecit ex sputo, et linívit óculos meos, et modo vídeo.
Ant 3.eng: The Man that is called Jesus * made clay of His Spittle, and anointed mine eyes, and now I do see.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Deus, qui et justis prǽmia meritórum, et peccatóribus per jejúnium véniam præbes: miserére supplícibus tuis; ut reátus nostri conféssio indulgéntiam váleat percípere delictórum.
Oratio 2.eng: O God, Who by mean of fasting dost give unto the righteous the reward of their good works, and unto sinners pardon; have mercy upon us, we beseech thee, and grant that we, humbly confessing our guiltiness, may so be enabled to obtain thy forgiveness.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Páteant aures misericórdiæ tuæ, Dómine, précibus supplicántium: et, ut peténtibus desideráta concédas, fac eos, quæ tibi sunt plácita, postuláre.
Oratio 3.eng: Let thy merciful ears, O Lord, be open unto the prayers of all them that entreat thee, and that Thou mayest grant us ever such things as we ask, teach us ever to ask such things as are pleasing in thy sight.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Ibat Jesus * in civitátem, quæ vocátur Naim: et ecce defúnctus efferebátur fílius únicus matris suæ.
Ant 2.eng: Jesus went * into a city that is called Naim: and behold, a dead man was being carried out, the only son of his mother.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Prophéta magnus * surréxit in nobis, et quia Deus visitávit plebem suam.
Ant 3.eng: A great Prophet * is risen up among us, and God hath visited His people.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, quos jejúnia votíva castígant, ipsa quoque devótio sancta lætíficet; ut, terrénis afféctibus mitigátis, facílius cæléstia capiámus.
Oratio 2.eng: O Almighty God, grant, we beseech thee, that we who are chastened by this hallowed fast, may be gladdened by holy earnestness, and that as earthly attractions grow dimmer, things heavenly may grow clearer.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Pópuli tui, Deus, institútor et rector: peccáta, quibus impugnátur, expélle; ut semper tibi plácitus, et tuo munímine sit secúrus.
Oratio 3.eng: O God, the Teacher and Shepherd of all thy people, free the same from all sins which do assail them, that so they may ever be pleasing in thy sight and safe under thy shelter.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Lázarus amícus noster * dormit: eámus, et a somno excitémus eum.
Ant 2.eng: Our friend Lazarus sleepeth; * let us go and awake him out of sleep.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Dómine, * si fuísses hic, Lázarus non esset mórtuus: ecce jam fœtet quatriduánus in monuménto.
Ant 3.eng: Lord, if Thou hadst been here * Lazarus had not died; behold, by this time he stinketh, for he hath lain in the grave four days already.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Deus, qui ineffabílibus mundum rénovas sacraméntis: præsta, quǽsumus; ut Ecclésia tua et ætérnis profíciat institútis, et temporálibus non destituátur auxíliis.
Oratio 2.eng: O God, who dost quicken the whole world anew by thine unspeakable Sacraments, grant, we beseech thee, that thy Church may both profit by whatsoever Thou hast ordained touching the things which are eternal, nor be comfortless of such help as is needful unto her touching the things which are temporal.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Da nobis, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui infirmitátis nostræ cónscii, de tua virtúte confídimus, sub tua semper pietáte gaudeámus.
Oratio 3.eng: Grant, we beseech thee, O Almighty God, unto all us who know that we are weak, and who trust in thee, because we know that Thou art strong, the gladsome help of thy loving-kindness, both here in time and hereafter in eternity.

Ant 2.eng: Our friend Lazarus sleepeth; * let us go and awake him out of sleep.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Da nobis, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui infirmitátis nostræ cónscii, de tua virtúte confídimus, sub tua semper pietáte gaudeámus.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Qui séquitur me, * non ámbulat in ténebris: sed habébit lumen vitæ, dicit Dóminus.
Ant 2.eng: Thus saith the Lord: * He that followeth Me walketh not in darkness, but shall have the Light of life.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Ego sum * qui testimónium perhíbeo de meípso: et testimónium pérhibet de me, qui misit me, Pater.
Ant 3.eng: I am One * That bear witness of Myself, and the Father That sent Me beareth witness of Me.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Fiat, Dómine, quǽsumus, per grátiam tuam fructuósus nostræ devotiónis afféctus: quia tunc nobis próderunt suscépta jejúnia, si tuæ sint plácita pietáti.
Oratio 2.eng: O Lord, we pray thee, that thy grace may make fruitful the toil of this our godly exercise, since it shall nothing avail us to have fasted, if our Fast be not pleasing in thy most gracious sight.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus, famíliam tuam propítius réspice: ut, te largiénte, regátur in córpore; et, te servánte, custodiátur in mente.
Oratio 3.eng: We beseech thee, Almighty God, mercifully to look upon this thy family, that by thy great goodness they may be governed and preserved evermore, both in body and soul.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Qui séquitur me, * non ámbulat in ténebris: sed habébit lumen vitæ, dicit Dóminus.
Ant 2.eng: Thus saith the Lord: * He that followeth Me walketh not in darkness, but shall have the Light of life.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Ego sum * qui testimónium perhíbeo de meípso: et testimónium pérhibet de me, qui misit me, Pater.

Oratio 3.eng: We beseech thee, Almighty God, mercifully to look upon this thy family, that by thy great goodness they may be governed and preserved evermore, both in body and soul.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Ego sum * qui testimónium perhíbeo de meípso: et testimónium pérhibet de me, qui misit me, Pater.
Ant 1.eng: I am One * That bear witness of Myself, and the Father That sent Me beareth witness of Me.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Dicébat Jesus * turbis Judæórum, et princípibus sacerdótum: Qui ex Deo est, verba Dei audit: proptérea vos non audítis, quia ex Deo non estis.
Ant 2.eng: Jesus said * unto the multitudes of the Jews and unto the Chief Priests: He that is of God heareth God's words; ye, therefore, hear them not, because ye are not of God.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Abraham pater vester * exsultávit ut vidéret diem meum: vidit, et gavísus est.
Ant 3.eng: Your father Abraham rejoiced to see My day * and he saw it, and was glad.

Ant Nona.label: Antiphon
Ant Nona.lat: Tulérunt lápides * Judǽi, ut jácerent in eum: Jesus autem abscóndit se, et exívit de templo.
Ant Nona.eng: Then took the Jews up stones * to cast at Him, but Jesus hid Himself, and went out of the temple.

Ant Prima.label: Antiphon
Ant Prima.lat: Ego dæmónium non hábeo, * sed honorífico Patrem meum, dicit Dóminus.
Ant Prima.eng: I have not a devil; * but I honour My Father, and ye do dishonour Me, saith the Lord.

Ant Sexta.label: Antiphon
Ant Sexta.lat: Amen, amen, dico vobis: * si quis sermónem meum serváverit, mortem non gustábit in ætérnum.
Ant Sexta.eng: Amen, Amen, * I say unto you: If a man keep My saying, he shall never see death.

Ant Tertia.label: Antiphon
Ant Tertia.lat: Ego glóriam meam * non quæro: est qui quærat, et júdicet.
Ant Tertia.eng: I seek not Mine Own glory; * there is One That seeketh and judgeth.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Fratres: Christus assístens Póntifex futurórum bonórum, per ámplius et perféctius tabernáculum non manu factum, id est, non hujus creatiónis: neque per sánguinem hircórum aut vitulórum, sed per próprium sánguinem introívit semel in Sancta, ætérna redemptióne invénta.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: But Christ, being come an high priest of the good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle not made with hand, that is, not of this creation: Neither by the blood of goats, or of calves, but by his own blood, entered once into the holies, having obtained eternal redemption.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Et ídeo novi testaménti mediátor est: ut, morte intercedénte, in redemptiónem eárum prævaricatiónum, quæ erant sub prióri testaménto, repromissiónem accípiant, qui vocáti sunt ætérnæ hereditátis in Christo Jesu, Dómino nostro.
Capitulum Nona.eng: And therefore he is the mediator of the new testament: that by means of his death, for the redemption of those trangressions, which were under the former testament, they that are called may receive the promise of eternal inheritance.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Si enim sanguis hircórum, et taurórum, et cinis vítulæ aspérsus inquinátos sanctíficat ad emundatiónem carnis: quanto magis sanguis Christi, qui per Spíritum Sanctum semetípsum óbtulit immaculátum Deo, emundábit consciéntiam nostram ab opéribus mórtuis, ad serviéndum Deo vivénti?
Capitulum Sexta.eng: For if the blood of goats and of oxen, and the ashes of an heifer being sprinkled, sanctify such as are defiled, to the cleansing of the flesh: How much more shall the blood of Christ, who by the Holy Ghost offered himself unspotted unto God, cleanse our conscience from dead works, to serve the living God?

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus, famíliam tuam propítius réspice: ut, te largiénte, regátur in córpore; et, te servánte, custodiátur in mente.
Oratio.eng: We beseech thee, Almighty God, mercifully to look upon this thy family, that by thy great goodness they may be governed and preserved evermore, both in body and soul.

Ant Laudes.ant: Vide, Dómine, * afflictiónem meam, quóniam eréctus est inimícus meus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O Lord, behold my affliction; * for the enemy hath magnified himself.

Ant Laudes.ant: In tribulatióne * invocávi Dóminum, et exaudívit me in latitúdine.
Ant Laudes.antEng: I called upon the Lord * in my distress; and He answered me, and set me at large.

Ant Laudes.ant: Judicásti, Dómine, * causam ánimæ meæ, defénsor vitæ meæ, Dómine Deus meus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O Lord, Thou hast pleaded the cause of my soul; * Thou hast redeemed my life, O Lord my God.

Ant Laudes.ant: Pópule meus, * quid feci tibi, aut quid moléstus fui? Respónde mihi.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O My people, what have I done unto thee? * or wherein have I wearied thee? testify against Me.

Ant Laudes.ant: Numquid rédditur * pro bono malum, quia fodérunt fóveam ánimæ meæ.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Shall evil be recompensed for good? * for they have digged a pit for My soul.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: In die magno * festivitátis stabat Jesus, et clamábat dicens: Si quis sitit, véniat ad me, et bibat.
Ant 2.eng: In the last day, that great day of the Feast, * Jesus stood and cried, saying: If any man thirst, let Him come unto Me, and drink.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Si quis sitit, * véniat ad me, et bibat: et de ventre ejus fluent aquæ vivæ, dicit Dóminus.
Ant 3.eng: If any man thirst, let him come unto Me, * and drink, and out of his belly shall flow living water, saith the Lord.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Sanctífica, quǽsumus, Dómine, nostra jejúnia: et cunctárum nobis indulgéntiam propítius largíre culpárum.
Oratio 2.eng: Hallow, O Lord, we beseech thee, this our Fast, and mercifully grant us forgiveness of all our trespasses.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Da, quǽsumus, Dómine, pópulo tuo salútem mentis et córporis: ut bonis opéribus inhæréndo, tua semper mereátur protectióne deféndi.
Oratio 3.eng: Grant unto thy people, we beseech thee, O Lord, health both of mind and body, that they, ever cleaving unto good works, may under thy shadow be ever worthily defended.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Tempus meum * nondum advénit, tempus autem vestrum semper est parátum.
Ant 2.eng: My time is not yet come * but your time is always ready.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Vos ascéndite * ad diem festum hunc: ego autem non ascéndam, quia tempus meum nondum advénit.
Ant 3.eng: Go ye up unto this Feast; * I go not up (yet) unto this Feast, for My time is not yet full come.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Nostra tibi, Dómine, quǽsumus, sint accépta jejúnia: quæ nos et expiándo, grátia tua dignos effíciant, et ad remédia perdúcant ætérna.
Oratio 2.eng: Lord, we beseech thee, that this our Fast may be acceptable in thy sight, and may, through thy blessing, effectually work in us, making us meet here to receive thy grace and hereafter the everlasting glory which Thou hast promised.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Da nobis, quǽsumus, Dómine, perseverántem in tua voluntáte famulátum: ut in diébus nostris et mérito et número pópulus tibi sérviens augeátur.
Oratio 3.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee to give us grace to endure to the end in doing of thy will, that in our days thy people which serve thee may have increase, both as touching bettering of their works, and multiplying of their numbers.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Tempus meum * nondum advénit, tempus autem vestrum semper est parátum.
Ant 2.eng: My time is not yet come * but your time is always ready.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Vos ascéndite * ad diem festum hunc: ego autem non ascéndam, quia tempus meum nondum advénit.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Da nobis, quǽsumus, Dómine, perseverántem in tua voluntáte famulátum: ut in diébus nostris et mérito et número pópulus tibi sérviens augeátur.
Oratio 3.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee to give us grace to endure to the end in doing of thy will, that in our days thy people which serve thee may have increase, both as touching bettering of their works, and multiplying of their numbers.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Oves meæ * vocem meam áudiunt: et ego Dóminus agnósco eas.
Ant 2.eng: My sheep hear My voice, * and I, the Lord, know them.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Multa bona ópera * operátus sum vobis: propter quod opus vultis me occídere?
Ant 3.eng: Many good works have I wrought * among you, and for them ye go about to kill Me?

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Sanctificáto hoc jejúnio Deus, tuórum corda fidélium miserátor illústra: et, quibus devotiónis præstas afféctum, præbe supplicántibus pium benígnus audítum.
Oratio 2.eng: O God, be mercifully pleased, through the hallowing of this Fast, to shed light upon the hearts of thy faithful people, and since Thou hast given them the mind to pray, let thy pitiful ears be opened graciously to hear their supplications.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Adésto supplicatiónibus nostris, omnípotens Deus: et quibus fidúciam sperándæ pietátis indúlges, consuétæ misericórdiæ tríbue benígnus efféctum.
Oratio 3.eng: Graciously hear our prayers, O Almighty God, and as Thou dost give us to look with confidence for thy favour for which we hope, so grant us, in thy goodness, the manifestation of thine accustomed mercy.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Oves meæ * vocem meam áudiunt: et ego Dóminus agnósco eas.
Ant 2.eng: My sheep hear My voice, * and I, the Lord, know them.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Multa bona ópera * operátus sum vobis: propter quod opus vultis me occídere?
Ant 3.eng: Many good works have I wrought * among you, and for them ye go about to kill Me?

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Magíster dicit: * Tempus meum prope est, apud te fácio Pascha cum discípulis meis.
Ant 2.eng: The Master saith: My time is at hand; * I will keep the Passover at thy house with My disciples.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Desidério desiderávi * hoc Pascha manducáre vobíscum, ántequam pátiar.
Ant 3.eng: With desire I have desired * to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut dígnitas condiciónis humánæ per immoderántiam sauciáta, medicinális parsimóniæ stúdio reformétur.
Oratio 2.eng: Grant, we beseech thee, O Almighty God, that the honour of man's nature, which gluttony hath degraded, may be seasonably renewed by strictness in keeping of this healthful Fast.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Esto, quǽsumus, Dómine, propítius plebi tuæ: ut, quæ tibi non placent, respuéntes, tuórum pótius repleántur delectatiónibus mandatórum.
Oratio 3.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee deal mercifully with thy people, and fill plentifully with the rich things of thy commandments all them who at this time do, to fulfill thy will, turn away from that which displeaseth thee.

Ant 1.lat: Tuam ipsíus ánimam * (ait ad Maríam Símeon) pertransíbit gládius.
Ant 1.eng: Simeon said unto Mary: * Yea, a sword shall pierce through thine own soul also.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Cum vidísset Jesus * matrem stantem juxta crucem, et discípulum quem diligébat, dicit matri suæ: Múlier, ecce fílius tuus. Deínde dicit discípulo: Ecce Mater tua.
Ant 2.eng: When Jesus saw His Mother, * and the disciple whom He loved, standing by the Cross, He saith unto His Mother: Woman, behold thy Son! Then saith He to the disciple: Behold thy Mother!

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Quis crédidit audítui nostro? et bráchium Dómini cui revelátum est? Et ascéndet sicut virgúltum coram eo, et sicut radix de terra sitiénti.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Who hath believed our report? and to whom is the arm of the Lord revealed? And he shall grow up as a tender plant before him, and as a root out of a thirsty ground.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Generatiónem ejus quis enarrábit, quia abscíssus est de terra vivéntium; propter scelus pópuli mei percússi eum.
Capitulum Nona.eng: Who shall declare his generation? because he is cut oh out of the land of the living: for the wickedness of my people have I struck him.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Ipse vulnerátus est propter iniquitátes nostras, attrítus est propter scélera nostra: disciplína pacis nostræ super eum, et livóre ejus sanáti sumus.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: But he was wounded for our iniquities, he was bruised for our sins: the chastisement of our peace was upon him, and by his bruises we are healed.

Commemoratio 1.label: Commemoratio
Commemoratio 1.lat:
!Commemoratio Feriæ Quintæ
Ant. Desidério desiderávi * hoc Pascha manducáre vobíscum, ántequam pátiar.
_
V. Eripe me Dómine ab hómine malo.
R. A viro iníquo éripe me.
_
$Oremus
Esto, quǽsumus Dómine, propítius plebi tuæ: ut, quæ tibi non placent, respuéntes, tuórum pótius repleántur delectatiónibus mandatórum.
$Per Dominum.
Commemoratio 1.eng:
!Commemoration of Thursday of Passion Week
Ant. With desire I have desired * to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.
_
V. Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man.
R. Preserve me from the wicked man.
_
$Oremus
O Lord, we beseech thee deal mercifully with thy people, and fill plentifully with the rich things of thy commandments all them who at this time do, to fulfill thy will, turn away from that which displeaseth thee.
$Per Dominum

Commemoratio 2.label: Commemoratio
Commemoratio 2.lat:
!Commemoratio Feria Sexta
Ant. Appropinquábat autem * dies festus Judæórum: et quærébant príncipes sacerdótum quómodo Jesum interfícerent, sed timébant plebem.
_
V. Eripe me de inimícis meis Deus meus.
R. Et ab insurgéntibus in me líbera me.
_
$Oremus
Córdibus nostris, quǽsumus, Dómine, grátiam tuam benígnus infúnde: ut peccáta nostra castigatióne voluntária cohibéntes, temporáliter pótius macerémur, quam supplíciis deputémur ætérnis.
$Per Dominum
Commemoratio 2.eng:
!Commemoration of Friday of Passion Week
Ant. Now the Jews' Feastday was at hand, and the chief Priests sought how they might kill Jesus; but they feared the people.
_
V. Deliver me from mine enemies, O my God.
R. And defend me from them that rise up against me.
_
$Oremus.
We beseech thee, O Lord, pour thy grace into our hearts, that all we who of our own will do check our sins with the curb of mortification, may suffer here, and escape condemnation to eternal punishment hereafter.
$Per Dominum

Commemoratio 3.label: Commemoratio
Commemoratio 3.lat:
!Commemoratio Feriæ Sextæ
Ant. Príncipes sacerdótum * consílium fecérunt ut Jesum occíderent: dicébant autem: Non in die festo, ne forte tumúltus fíeret in pópulo.
_
V. Eripe me de inimícis meis Deus meus.
R. Et ab insurgéntibus in me líbera me.
_
$Oremus
Concéde, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut qui protectiónis tuæ grátiam quǽrimus, liberáti a malis ómnibus, secúra tibi mente serviámus.
$Per Dominum
Commemoratio 3.eng:
!Commemoration of Friday of Passion Week
Ant. The chief Priests consulted that they might kill Jesus, but they said Not on the Feast-day, lest there be an uproar among the people.
_
V. Deliver me from mine enemies, O my God.
R. And defend me from them that rise up against me.
_
$Oremus
Grant, we beseech thee, O Almighty God, that we who seek the grace of thy protection, being delivered from all evils, may serve thee ever in peace and quietness of spirit.
$Per Dominum

Doxology.lat:
Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui passus es pro sérvulis,
Cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

Hymnus Laudes.label: Hymn
Hymnus Laudes.title: Virgo vírginum præclára
Hymnus Laudes.lat:
Virgo vírginum præclára,
Mihi jam non sis amára,
Fac me tecum plángere.

Fac ut portem Christi mortem,
Passiónis fac consórtem,
Et plagas recólere.

Fac me plagis vulnerári,
Fac me cruce inebriári,
Et cruóre Fílii.

Flammis ne urar succénsus,
Per te Virgo sim defénsus
In die judícii.

Christe, cum sit hinc exíre,
Da per Matrem me veníre
Ad palmam victóriæ.

Quando corpus moriétur,
Fac ut ánimæ donétur
Paradísi glória.
Amen.
Hymnus Laudes.eng:
Virgin of all virgins blest!
Listen to my fond request:
Let me share thy grief divine;

Let me, to my latest breath,
In my body bear the death
Of that dying Son of thine.

Wounded with his every wound,
Steep my soul till it hath swooned
In his very blood away;

Be to me, O Virgin, nigh,
Lest in flames I burn and die,
In that awful judgement day.

Christ, when thou shalt call me hence,
Be thy Mother my defence,
Be thy cross my victory;

While my body here decays,
May my soul thy goodness praise,
Safe in Paradise with thee.
Amen.

Hymnus Matutinum.label: Hymn
Hymnus Matutinum.title: Sancta Mater, istud agas
Hymnus Matutinum.lat:
Sancta Mater, istud agas,
Crucifíxi fige plagas
Cordi meo válide:

Tui nati vulneráti,
Tam dignáti pro me pati,
Pœnas mecum dívide.

Fac me tecum pie flere,
Crucifíxo condolére,
Donec ego víxero:

Juxta crucem tecum stare,
Et me tibi sociáre
In planctu desídero.
Amen.
Hymnus Matutinum.eng:
Holy Mother! pierce me through;
In my heart each wound renew
Of my Saviour crucified:

Let me share with thee his pain,
Who for all my sins was slain,
Who for me in torments died.

Let me mingle tears with thee,
Mourning him who mourned for me,
All the days that I may live:

By the cross with thee to stay;
There with thee to weep and pray;
Is all I ask of thee to give.
Amen.

Hymnus Vespera.label: Hymn
Hymnus Vespera.title: Stabat Mater dolorósa
Hymnus Vespera.lat:
Stabat Mater dolorósa
Juxta crucem lacrimósa,
Dum pendébat Fílius.

Cujus ánimam geméntem,
Contristátam et doléntem,
Pertransívit gládius.

O quam tristis et afflícta
Fuit illa benedícta
Mater Unigéniti!

Quæ mœrébat, et dolébat,
Pia Mater dum vidébat
Nati pœnas ínclyti.

Quis est homo qui non fleret,
Matrem Christi si vidéret
In tanto supplício?

Quis non posset contristári,
Christi Matrem contemplári
Doléntem cum Fílio?

Pro peccátis suæ gentis
Vidit Jesum in torméntis,
Et flagéllis súbditum.

Vidit suum dulcem natum,
Moriéndo desolátum,
Dum emísit spíritum.

Eja, Mater, fons amóris,
Me sentíre vim dolóris
Fac, ut tecum lúgeam:

Fac ut árdeat cor meum
In amándo Christum Deum,
Ut sibi compláceam.
Amen.
Hymnus Vespera.eng:
At the cross her station keeping,
Stood the mournful Mother weeping,
Close to Jesus to the last:

Through her heart, his sorrow sharing,
All his bitter anguish bearing,
Now at length the sword had passed.

Oh, how sad and sore distressed
Was that Mother highly blest
Of the sole-begotten One!

Christ above in torment hangs;
She beneath beholds the pangs
Of her dying glorious Son.

Is there one who would not weep,
Whelmed in miseries so deep
Christ's dear Mother to behold?

Can the human heart refrain
From partaking in her pain,
In that Mother's pain untold?

Bruised, derided, cursed, defiled,
She beheld her tender Child
All with bloody scourges rent;

For the sins of his own nation,
Saw him hang in desolation,
Till his Spirit forth he sent.

O thou Mother! fount of love!
Touch my spirit from above,
Make my heart with thine accord:

Make me feel as thou hast felt;
Make my soul to glow and melt
With the love of Christ my Lord.
Amen.

Invit.label: Antiphon
Invit.lat: Dolóres gloriósæ recoléntes Vírginis, Dóminum pro nobis passum * Veníte adorémus.
Invit.eng: When we remember the sorrows of the most glorious Virgin, * O come, let us worship the Lord, Who suffered for us.

Lectio Prima.label: Lectio brevis
Lectio Prima.lat: Generatiónem ejus quis enarrábit, quia abscíssus est de terra vivéntium; propter scelus pópuli mei percússi eum.
Lectio Prima.eng: He was taken away from distress, and from judgment: who shall declare his generation? because he is cut oh out of the land of the living: for the wickedness of my people have I struck him.

Nocturn 1 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 1 Versum.eng: ℣. He hath made me desolate.
Nocturn 1 Versum.engR: ℟. And faint with sorrow all the day.

Nocturn 2 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 2 Versum.lat: ℣. Fácies mea intúmuit a fletu.
Nocturn 2 Versum.eng: ℣. My face is swollen with weeping.
Nocturn 2 Versum.engR: ℟. And on mine eyelids is the shadow (of death.

Nocturn 3 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 3 Versum.latR: ℟. Posuísti lácrimas meas in conspéctu tuo.
Nocturn 3 Versum.eng: ℣. O God, I have declared my life unto thee.
Nocturn 3 Versum.engR: ℟. Thou hast put my tears in thy sight.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, in cujus passióne, secúndum Simeónis prophetíam, dulcíssimam ánimam gloriósæ Vírginis et Matris Maríæ dolóris gládius pertransívit: concéde, propítius; ut qui transfixiónem ejus et passiónem venerándo recólimus, gloriósis méritis et précibus ómnium Sanctórum cruci fidéliter astántium intercedéntibus, passiónis tuæ efféctum felícem consequámur:
Oratio.eng: O God, at Whose Passion, according to the prophecy of Simeon, a sword of sorrow pierced through the gentle soul of the glorious Maiden and Mother Mary, mercifully grant to as many as do ever remember with awe how that her soul was pierced and Thou didst suffer, even for all such be Thou entreated, for the sake and by the prayers of all thy glorious and holy servants who stood so loyally by thy Cross, and grant unto the same, that for them thy life-giving Death may not have been in vain.

Responsory Breve Nona.label: Responsorium Breve
Responsory Breve Nona.lat:
℟.br. Deus vitam meam * Annuntiávi tibi.
℣. Posuísti lácrimas meas in conspéctu tuo.
℟. Annuntiávi tibi.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Deus vitam meam * Annuntiávi tibi.
Responsory Breve Nona.eng:
℟.br. O God, * I have declared my life unto thee.
℣. Thou hast put my tears in thy sight.
℟. I have declared my life unto thee.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. O God, * I have declared my life unto thee.

Responsory Breve Sexta.label: Responsorium Breve
Responsory Breve Sexta.lat:
℟.br. Fácies mea * Intúmuit a fletu.
℣. Et pálpebræ meæ caligavérunt.
℟. Intúmuit a fletu.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Fácies mea * Intúmuit a fletu.
Responsory Breve Sexta.eng:
℟.br. My face is * swollen with weeping.
℣. And on my eyelids is the shadow (of death.)
℟. Swollen with weeping.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. My face is * swollen with weeping.

Responsory Breve Tertia.label: Responsorium Breve
Responsory Breve Tertia.lat:
℟.br. Pósuit me * Desolátam.
℣. Tota die mæróre conféctam.
℟. Desolátam.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Pósuit me * Desolátam.
Responsory Breve Tertia.eng:
℟.br. He hath made me * desolate.
℣. And faint with sorrow all the day.
℟. Desolate.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. He hath made me * desolate.

Ant Laudes.ant: Vadam ad montem * myrrhæ et ad collem thuris.
Ant Laudes.antEng: I will get me to the mountain of myrrh, * and to the hill of frankincense.

Ant Laudes.ant: Diléctus meus * cándidus et rubicúndus: comæ cápitis ejus sicut púrpura regis vincta canálibus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: My beloved * is white and ruddy the hair of his head is like kingly purple, bound in tresses.

Ant Laudes.ant: Quo ábiit * diléctus tuus, o pulchérrima mulíerum? quo diléctus tuus declinávit.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Whither is thy beloved gone, * O thou fairest among women? Whither is thy beloved turned aside?

Ant Laudes.ant: Fascículus myrrhæ * diléctus meus mihi inter úbera mea commorábitur.
Ant Laudes.antEng: A bundle of myrrh is my well-beloved unto me; he shall lie betwixt my breasts.

Ant Laudes.ant: Fulcíte me flóribus * stipáte me malis, quia amóre lángueo.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Revive me with flowers, * stay me up with apples, for I am swooning with love.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Astitérunt reges terræ, * et príncipes convenérunt in unum advérsus Dóminum, et advérsus Christum ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together against the Lord, and against His Anointed.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Voce mea * ad Dóminum clamávi, et exaudívit me de monte sancto suo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I cried unto the Lord with my voice, and He heard me out of His holy hill.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Factum est cor meum * tamquam cera liquéscens in médio ventris mei.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: My heart is like melting wax in the midst of my bowels.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Inimíci mei * dixérunt mala mihi: Quando moriétur, et períbit nomen ejus?
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Mine enemies speak evil of me When shall he die, and his name perish.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Deus, vitam meam * annuntiávi tibi: posuísti lácrimas meas in conspéctu tuo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O God, I have declared my life unto thee, Thou hast put my tears in thy sight.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Fílii hóminum, * dentes eórum arma et sagíttæ: et lingua eórum gládius acútus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: As for the sons of men, their teeth are spears and arrows, and their tongue a sharp sword.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Intendérunt arcum, * rem amáram, ut sagíttent in occúltis immaculátum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: They bend their bow, even bitter words, that they may shoot in secret at the perfect.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Factus sum * sicut homo sine adjutório, inter mórtuos liber.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I am as a man that hath no strength, lying nerveless among the dead.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Replévit me amaritúdine, * inebriávit me absýnthio.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: He hath filled me with bitterness, he hath made me drunken with wormwood.

Ant Vespera.ant: Vadam ad montem * myrrhæ et ad collem thuris.
Ant Vespera.antEng: I will get me to the mountain of myrrh, * and to the hill of frankincense.

Ant Vespera.ant: Diléctus meus * cándidus et rubicúndus: comæ cápitis ejus sicut púrpura regis vincta canálibus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: My beloved * is white and ruddy; the hair of his head is like kingly purple, bound in tresses.

Ant Vespera.ant: Quo ábiit * diléctus tuus, o pulchérrima mulíerum? quo diléctus tuus declinávit.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Whither is thy beloved gone, * O thou fairest among women? Whither is thy beloved turned aside?

Ant Vespera.ant: Fascículus myrrhæ * diléctus meus mihi inter úbera mea commorábitur.
Ant Vespera.antEng: A bundle of myrrh is my well-beloved unto me; he shall lie betwixt my breasts.

Ant Vespera.ant: Fulcíte me flóribus * stipáte me malis, quia amóre lángueo.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Revive me with flowers, * stay me up with apples, for I am swooning with love.

Ant 2.lat: Appropinquábat autem * dies festus Judæórum: et quærébant príncipes sacerdótum quómodo Jesum interfícerent, sed timébant plebem.
Ant 2.eng: Now the Jews' Feastday * was at hand, and the chief Priests sought how they might kill Jesus; but they feared the people.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Príncipes sacerdótum * consílium fecérunt ut Jesum occíderent: dicébant autem: Non in die festo, ne forte tumúltus fíeret in pópulo.
Ant 3.eng: The chief Priests * consulted that they might kill Jesus, but they said: Not on the Feast-day, lest there be an uproar among the people.

Oratio 2 Commemoratio.lat:

Ant. Cum vidísset Jesus * matrem stantem juxta crucem, et discípulum quem diligébat, dicit matri suæ: Múlier, ecce fílius tuus. Deínde dicit discípulo: Ecce Mater tua.
_
V. Ora pro nobis, Virgo dolorosíssima.
R. Ut digni efficiámur promissiónibus Christi.
_
$Oremus
v. Deus, in cujus passióne, secúndum Simeónis prophetíam, dulcíssimam ánimam gloriósæ Vírginis et Matris Maríæ dolóris gládius pertransívit: concéde, propítius; ut qui transfixiónem ejus et passiónem venerándo recólimus, gloriósis méritis et précibus ómnium Sanctórum cruci fidéliter astántium intercedéntibus, passiónis tuæ efféctum felícem consequámur:
Oratio 2 Commemoratio.eng:
!Commemoration of the Seven Sorrows of the Blessed Virgin Mary
Ant. When Jesus saw His Mother, * and the disciple whom He loved, standing by the Cross, He saith unto His Mother: Woman, behold thy Son! Then saith He to the disciple: Behold thy Mother!
_
V. Pray for us, O Virgin most sorrowful.
R. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.
_
$Oremus
v. O God, at Whose Passion, according to the prophecy of Simeon, a sword of sorrow pierced through the gentle soul of the glorious Maiden and Mother Mary, mercifully grant to as many as do ever remember with awe how that her soul was pierced and Thou didst suffer, even for all such be Thou entreated, for the sake and by the prayers of all thy glorious and holy servants who stood so loyally by thy Cross, and grant unto the same, that for them thy life-giving Death may not have been in vain.

Oratio 3.eng: Grant, we beseech thee, O Almighty God, that we who seek the grace of thy protection, being delivered from all evils, may serve thee ever in peace and quietness of spirit.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Clarífica me, Pater, * apud temetípsum claritáte, quam hábui priúsquam mundus fíeret.
Ant 2.eng: Father, glorify Thou Me * with thine Own Self, with the glory which I had with thee before the world was.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Profíciat, quǽsumus, Dómine, plebs tibi dicáta, piæ devotiónis afféctu: ut sacris actiónibus erudíta, quanto majestáti tuæ fit grátior, tanto donis potióribus augeátur.
Oratio 2.eng: Grant, O Lord, that thy people, which are consecrated to thy service may continually increase in all godly affections: that they being duly instructed in all holy learning, may both be made the more acceptable unto thy divine majesty, and prospered more abundantly in the gifts of thy bounty.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Pater juste, * mundus te non cognóvit: ego autem novi te, quia tu me misísti.
Ant 1.eng: O just Father, * the world has not known thee: I however have known thee, for thou hast sent me.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Turba multa, * quæ convénerat ad diem festum, clamábat Dómino: Benedíctus qui venit in nómine Dómini: Hosánna in excélsis.
Ant 2.eng: Much people that were come to the Feast, cried * unto the Lord: Blessed is He That cometh in the Name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Scriptum est enim: * Percútiam pastórem, et dispergéntur oves gregis: postquam autem resurréxero, præcédam vos in Galilǽam: ibi me vidébitis, dicit Dóminus.
Ant 3.eng: It is written: I will smite the Shepherd, * and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered abroad, but after I am risen again, I will go before you into Galilee: there shall ye see Me, saith the Lord.

Ant Nona.label: Antiphon
Ant Nona.lat: Invocábo * nomen tuum, Dómine: ne avértas fáciem tuam a clamóre meo.
Ant Nona.eng: I will call * upon thy Name, O Lord: hide not thy face at my cry.

Ant Prima.label: Antiphon
Ant Prima.lat: Púeri Hebræórum * tolléntes ramos olivárum, obviavérunt Dómino clamántes et dicéntes: Hosánna in excélsis.
Ant Prima.eng: The Hebrew children took branches of olive-trees, * and went forth to meet the Lord, crying and saying: Hosanna in the highest!

Ant Sexta.label: Antiphon
Ant Sexta.lat: Tibi revelávi * causam meam, defénsor vitæ meæ, Dómine, Deus meus.
Ant Sexta.eng: Unto thee have I opened my cause, * O Lord my God, Which art the Redeemer of my life.

Ant Tertia.label: Antiphon
Ant Tertia.lat: Púeri Hebræórum * vestiménta prosternébant in via, et clamábant, dicéntes: Hosánna Fílio David: benedíctus qui venit in nómine Dómini.
Ant Tertia.eng: The Hebrew children spread their garments in the way, * and cried, saying: Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is He that cometh in the Name of the Lord!

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Fratres: Hoc enim sentíte in vobis, quod et in Christo Jesu: qui, cum in forma Dei esset, non rapínam arbitrátus est esse se æquálem Deo: sed semetípsum exinanívit, formam servi accípiens, in similitúdinem hóminum factus, et hábitu invéntus ut homo.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Brothers: For let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus: Who being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God: But emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men, and in habit found as a man.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: In nómine Jesu omne genu flectátur cæléstium, terréstrium, et infernórum: et omnis lingua confiteátur, quia Dóminus Jesus Christus in glória est Dei Patris.
Capitulum Nona.eng: That in the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those that are in heaven, on earth, and under the earth: And that every tongue should confess that the Lord Jesus Christ is in the glory of God the Father.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Humiliávit semetípsum factus obédiens usque ad mortem, mortem autem crucis. Propter quod et Deus exaltávit illum, et donávit illi nomen, quod est super omne nomen.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: He humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death, even to the death of the cross. For which cause God also hath exalted him, and hath given him a name which is above all names:

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui humáno géneri, ad imitándum humilitátis exémplum, Salvatórem nostrum carnem súmere, et crucem subíre fecísti: concéde propítius; ut et patiéntiæ ipsíus habére documénta, et resurrectiónis consórtia mereámur.
Oratio.eng: Almighty and everlasting God, Who, of thy tender love towards mankind, hast sent thy Son our Saviour Jesus Christ to take upon Him our flesh and to suffer death upon the Cross, that all mankind should follow the example of His great humility; mercifully grant, that we may both follow the example of His patience, and also be made partakers of His resurrection.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dóminus Deus * auxiliátor meus: et ídeo non sum confúsus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Lord God will help me * and therefore I am not confounded.

Ant Laudes.ant: Circumdántes * circumdedérunt me: et in nómine Dómini vindicábor in eis.
Ant Laudes.antEng: They compassed me about, * yea, they compassed me about but in the Name of the Lord! I will destroy them.

Ant Laudes.ant: Júdica causam meam: * defénde, quia potens es, Dómine.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Judge Thou my cause, * and redeem me, O Lord, for Thou art mighty to save.

Ant Laudes.ant: Cum Angelis * et púeris fidéles inveniámur, triumphatóri mortis clamántes: Hosánna in excélsis.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Fare we with Angels and men in faith to meet the Redeemer, * hailing the Slayer of death with joyful shouts of “Hosanna in the highest!”

Ant Laudes.ant: Confundántur * qui me persequúntur, et non confúndar ego, Dómine, Deus meus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Let them be confounded that persecute me; * but let not me be confounded, O Lord my God.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Clarífica me, Pater, * apud temetípsum claritáte, quam hábui priúsquam mundus fíeret.
Ant 2.eng: And now, O Father, glorify Thou Me * with thine Own Self, with the glory which I had with thee before the world was.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Non habéres * in me potestátem, nisi désuper tibi datum fuísset.
Ant 3.eng: Thou couldest have no power * at all against Me, except it were given thee from above.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Da, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui in tot advérsis ex nostra infirmitáte defícimus; intercedénte unigéniti Fílii tui passióne respirémus:
Oratio 2.eng: O Almighty God, Which knowest that we be set in such straits that we have no power of ourselves to help ourselves, we pray thee mercifully to relieve us, for whom continually pleadeth the suffering of thine Only Begotten Son.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Adjuva nos, Deus, salutáris noster: et ad benefícia recolénda, quibus nos instauráre dignátus es, tríbue veníre gaudéntes.
Oratio 3.eng: Help us, O God of our salvation, and grant us grace to draw near with joy to the memorial of thy great mercies whereby Thou wast pleased to make us new creatures.

Ant Laudes.ant: Fáciem meam * non avérti ab increpántibus, et conspuéntibus in me.
Ant Laudes.antEng: I hid not my face * from shame and spitting.

Ant Laudes.ant: Frámea, suscitáre * advérsus eos, qui dispérgunt gregem meum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Awake, O sword, * against them that scatter my flock.

Ant Laudes.ant: Appendérunt * mercédem meam trigínta argénteis: quibus appretiátus sum ab eis.
Ant Laudes.antEng: They took the thirty pieces of silver, * my price, that I was prized at of them.

Ant Laudes.ant: Inundavérunt aquæ * super caput meum: dixi, Périi: invocábo nomen tuum, Dómine Deus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Waters flowed over mine head; * I said I am cut off; I will call upon thy Name, O Lord God.

Ant Laudes.ant: Lábia insurgéntium, * et cogitatiónes eórum vide, Dómine.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O Lord, behold the lips * of those that rose up against me, and their device.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Ante diem festum * Paschæ, sciens Jesus quia venit hora ejus, cum dilexísset suos, in finem diléxit eos.
Ant 2.eng: Now, before the Feast of the Passover, as Jesus knew that His hour was come, * having loved His Own which were in the world, He loved them unto the end.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Potestátem hábeo * ponéndi ánimam meam, et íterum suméndi eam.
Ant 3.eng: I have power * to lay down my life: and to take it up again.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus: da nobis ita Domínicæ passiónis sacraménta perágere; ut indulgéntiam percípere mereámur.
Oratio 2.eng: O Almighty and everlasting God, give us grace so to use the solemn and mysterious memorial of the Lord's Suffering, that the same may be unto us a mean whereby worthily to win thy forgiveness.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Tua nos misericórdia, Deus, et ab omni subreptióne vetustátis expúrget: et capáces sanctæ novitátis effíciat.
Oratio 3.eng: May thy mercy, O God, cleanse us from the deceits of our old nature, and enable us to be formed anew unto holiness.

Ant Laudes.ant: Vide, Dómine, * et consídera, quóniam tríbulor: velóciter exáudi me.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Behold, O Lord, and see, * for I am in trouble; hear me speedily.

Ant Laudes.ant: Discérne causam meam, * Dómine: ab hómine iníquo et dolóso éripe me.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Plead my cause, * O Lord; deliver me from the unjust and deceitful man.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dum tribulárer, * clamávi ad Dóminum de ventre ínferi, et exaudívit me.
Ant Laudes.antEng: I cried by reason of mine affliction unto the Lord, * and He heard me out of the belly of hell.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dómine, vim pátior, * respónde pro me: quia néscio quid dicam inimícis meis.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O Lord, I am oppressed, * undertake Thou for me; for I know not what to say unto mine enemies.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dixérunt ímpii: * Opprimámus virum justum, quóniam contrárius est opéribus nostris.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The ungodly said Let us oppress the righteous man, * because he is clean contrary to our doings.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Simon, dormis? * non potuísti una hora vigiláre mecum?
Ant 2.eng: Simon, do you sleep? * Could you not watch one hour with me?

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Ancílla dixit * Petro: Vere tu ex illis es: nam et loquéla tua maniféstum te facit.
Ant 3.eng: The handmaid said to Peter: * Surely thou also art one of them; for even thy speech doth discover thee.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui nostris excéssibus incessánter afflígimur, per unigéniti Fílii tui passiónem liberémur:
Oratio 2.eng: O Almighty God, we beseech Thee that we whose transgressions do unceasingly harm us, may find freedom in the Suffering of Thine Only-begotten Son.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Réspice, quǽsumus, Dómine, super hanc famíliam tuam, pro qua Dóminus noster Jesus Christus non dubitávit mánibus tradi nocéntium, et crucis subíre torméntum:
Oratio 3.eng: O Lord, we beseech Thee, behold this Thy family, for which our Lord Jesus Christ was contented to be betrayed, and given up into the hands of wicked men, and to suffer death upon the Cross.

Ant Laudes.ant: Líbera me * de sanguínibus, Deus, Deus meus: et exsultábit lingua mea justítiam tuam.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Deliver me * from blood, O God, thou God of my salvation: and my tongue shall extol thy justice.

Ant Laudes.ant: Contumélias * et terróres passus sum ab eis: et Dóminus mecum est tamquam bellátor fortis.
Ant Laudes.antEng: I received * injuries and terrors from them: but the Lord is with me as a strong warrior.

Ant Laudes.ant: Tu autem, Dómine, * scis omne consílium eórum advérsum me in mortem.
Ant Laudes.antEng: But thou, O Lord, * knowest all their plans to put me to death.

Ant Laudes.ant: Omnes inimíci mei * audiérunt malum meum: Dómine, lætáti sunt, quóniam tu fecísti.
Ant Laudes.antEng: All my enemies have heard of my evil, * they have rejoiced that thou, O Lord, hast done it.

Ant Laudes.ant: Fac, Dómine, * judícium injúriam patiéntibus: et vias peccatórum dispérde.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Lord helpeth them * to right that suffer wrong, but as for the way of the ungodly, he turneth it upside down.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon

Ant Laudes.ant: Justificéris, Dómine, * in sermónibus tuis, et vincas cum judicáris.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O Lord, Thou shalt be justified * when Thou speakest, and be clear when Thou art judged.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dóminus * tamquam ovis ad víctimam ductus est, et non apéruit os suum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Lord was brought as a lamb * to the slaughter, and He opened not His mouth.

Ant Laudes.ant: Contrítum est * cor meum in médio mei, contremuérunt ómnia ossa mea.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Mine heart is broken within me * all my bones tremble.

Ant Laudes.ant: Exhortátus es * in virtúte tua, et in refectióne sancta tua, Dómine.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O Lord, Thou hast spoken unto us * in thy strength, and in thy Holy Banquet.

Ant Laudes.ant: Oblátus est * quia ipse vóluit, et peccáta nostra ipse portávit.
Ant Laudes.antEng: He was offered up because He willed it * and He bore our sins.
