Ant Laudes.ant: Próprio * Fílio suo non pepércit Deus, sed pro nobis ómnibus trádidit illum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: God spared not His Own Son * but delivered Him up for us all.

Ant Laudes.ant: Anxiátus est super me * spíritus meus, in me turbátum est cor meum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: My spirit is overwhelmed within me; * my heart within me is troubled.

Ant Laudes.ant: Ait latro ad latrónem: * Nos quidem digna factis recípimus, hic autem quid fecit? Meménto mei, Dómine, dum véneris in regnum tuum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: One thief said unto the other: * We indeed receive the due reward of our deeds, but what hath this man done? Lord, remember me, when thou comest into thy kingdom.

Ant Laudes.ant: Cum conturbáta fúerit * ánima mea, Dómine, misericórdiæ memor eris.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Lord, when my soul is troubled, * thou wilt remember mercy.

Ant Laudes.ant: Meménto mei, * Dómine, dum véneris in regnum tuum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Lord, remember me * when thou comest into thy kingdom.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Astitérunt reges terræ, * et príncipes convenérunt in unum, advérsus Dóminum, et advérsus Christum ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The kings of the earth set themselves, * and the rulers take counsel together, against the Lord, and against His Anointed.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Divisérunt sibi * vestiménta mea, et super vestem meam misérunt sortem.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: They part my garments among them, * and cast lots upon my vesture.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Insurrexérunt in me * testes iníqui, et mentíta est iníquitas sibi.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: False witnesses are risen up against me, * and iniquity hath belied itself.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Vim faciébant, * qui quærébant ánimam meam.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: They that sought after my life * have used violence again me.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Confundántur * et revereántur, qui quærunt ánimam meam, ut áuferant eam.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Let them be ashamed and confounded * together that seek after my soul, to destroy it.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Aliéni * insurrexérunt in me, et fortes quæsiérunt ánimam meam.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Strangers are risen up against me, * and oppressors seek after my soul.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ab insurgéntibus in me * líbera me, Dómine, quia occupavérunt ánimam meam.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O Lord, defend me from them that rise up against me, * for they lie in wait for my life.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Longe fecísti * notos meos a me: tráditus sum, et non egrediébar.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Thou hast put away mine acquaintance far from me; * I am shut up, and cannot come forth.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Captábunt * in ánimam justi, et sánguinem innocéntem condemnábunt.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: They gather themselves together * against the soul of the righteous, and condemn the innocent blood.

Ant Vespera.ant: Cálicem * salutáris accípiam et nomen Dómini invocábo.
Ant Vespera.antEng: I will take the cup of salvation; * and call upon the Name of the Lord.

Ant Vespera.ant: Cum his, * qui odérunt pacem eram pacíficus: dum loquébar illis, impugnábant me gratis.
Ant Vespera.antEng: With them * that hate peace I was peaceable; when I spoke unto them they fought against me without a cause.

Ant Vespera.ant: Ab homínibus * iníquis líbera me, Dómine.
Ant Vespera.antEng: O Lord, preserve me * from the wicked man.

Ant Vespera.ant: Custódi me * a láqueo, quem statuérunt mihi, et a scándalis operántium iniquitátem.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Keep me * from the snare which they have laid for me, and the gins of the workers of iniquity.

Ant Vespera.ant: Considerábam * ad déxteram, et vidébam, et non erat qui cognósceret me.
Ant Vespera.antEng: I looked * on my right hand and beheld: but there was no man that would know me.

Ant 2.eng: Thus saith the Lord: The kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, * which went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard.

Ant Sexta.label: Antiphon

Capitulum Laudes.eng: Brothers: Know you not that they that run in the race, all run indeed, but one receiveth the prize? So run that you may obtain.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Bibébant autem de spiritáli, consequénte eos, petra: petra autem erat Christus: sed non in plúribus eórum beneplácitum est Deo.
Capitulum Nona.eng: And all drank the same spiritual drink; and they drank of the spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ. But with most of them God was not well pleased: for they were overthrown in the desert.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Omnis autem, qui in agóne conténdit, ab ómnibus se ábstinet: et illi quidem ut corruptíbilem corónam accípiant, nos autem incorrúptam.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: And every one that striveth for the mastery, refraineth himself from all things: and they indeed that they may receive a corruptible crown; but we an incorruptible one.

Invit.label: Antiphon
Invit.lat: Præoccupémus fáciem Dómini: * Et in psalmis jubilémus ei.
Invit.eng: Let us come before the presence of the Lord * and make a joyful noise unto Him with Psalms.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Preces pópuli tui, quǽsumus, Dómine, cleménter exáudi: ut, qui juste pro peccátis nostris afflígimur, pro tui nóminis glória misericórditer liberémur.
Oratio.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee favourably to hear the prayers of thy people; that we, who are justly punished for our offences, may be mercifully delivered by thy goodness, for the glory of thy Name.

Versum 2.label: Versicle
Versum 2.latR: ℟. A generatióne et progénie.
Versum 2.eng: ℣. Lord, thou hast been our refuge.
Versum 2.engR: ℟. From generation to generation.

Ant Laudes.ant: Miserére * mei, Deus, et a delícto meo munda me: quia tibi soli peccávi.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Have mercy upon me, * O God, and cleanse me from my sin, for against thee only have I sinned.

Ant Laudes.ant: Confitébor * tibi, quóniam exaudísti me.
Ant Laudes.antEng: I will praise thee, * for thou hast heard me.

Ant Laudes.ant: Deus, Deus meus, * ad te de luce vígilo, quia factus es adjútor meus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O God, Thou art my God, * early will I seek thee, because thou hast been my help.

Ant Laudes.ant: Benedíctus es * in firmaménto cæli, et laudábilis in sǽcula, Deus noster.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Blessed art thou, * O our God, in the firmament of heaven, and worthy to be praised above all for ever.

Ant Laudes.ant: Laudáte * Dóminum de cælis.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Praise ye the Lord * from the heavens.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Hi novíssimi * una hora fecérunt, et pares illos nobis fecísti, qui portávimus pondus diéi, et æstus.
Ant 3.eng: These last have wrought but one hour, * and thou hast made them equal unto us, which have borne the burden and heat of the day.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Dixit autem paterfamílias: * Amíce, non fácio tibi injúriam: nonne ex denário convenísti mecum? tolle quod tuum est, et vade.
Ant 3.eng: And the householder said: * Friend, I do thee no wrong didst not thou agree with me for a penny? Take that is thine, and go thy way.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Tolle quod tuum est, * et vade; quia ego bonus sum, dicit Dóminus.
Ant 3.eng: Take that thine is, * and go thy way; for I am good, saith the Lord.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Non licet mihi, * quod volo, fácere? an óculus tuus nequam est? quia ego bonus sum, dicit Dóminus.
Ant 3.eng: Is it not lawful for me * to do what I will? Is thine eye evil, because I am gracious?” saith the Lord.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Dixit Dóminus * ad Noë: Finis univérsæ carnis venit coram me: fac tibi arcam de lignis lævigátis, ut salvétur univérsum semen in ea.
Ant 1.eng: The Lord said unto Noah: * The end of all flesh is come before Me, make thee an ark of planed timber, that seed of all flesh may be saved therein.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Cum turba * plúrima convenírent ad Jesum, et de civitátibus properárent ad eum, dixit per similitúdinem: Exiit qui séminat, semináre semen suum.
Ant 2.eng: When much people were gathered together to Jesus, * and were come to Him out of every city, He spoke by a parable: A sower went out to sow his seed.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Vobis datum est * nosse mystérium regni Dei, céteris autem in parábolis, dixit Jesus discípulis suis.
Ant 3.eng: Jesus said to His disciples: * Unto you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God, but to others in parables.

Ant Nona.label: Antiphon
Ant Nona.lat: Si vere, fratres, * dívites esse cúpitis, veras divítias amáte.
Ant Nona.eng: If then, dearly beloved brethren, ye seek to be rich, * earnestly desire the true riches.

Ant Prima.label: Antiphon
Ant Prima.lat: Semen cécidit * in terram bonam, et áttulit fructum in patiéntia.
Ant Prima.eng: The seed fell * upon good ground, and brought forth its fruit in patience.

Ant Sexta.label: Antiphon
Ant Sexta.lat: Semen cécidit * in terram bonam, et áttulit fructum, áliud centésimum, et áliud sexagésimum.
Ant Sexta.eng: Some seed fell on good ground, * and bare fruit, some one hundred-fold, and some sixty-fold.

Ant Tertia.label: Antiphon
Ant Tertia.lat: Qui verbum Dei * rétinent corde perfécto et óptimo, fructum áfferunt in patiéntia.
Ant Tertia.eng: They who keep * the word of God with a good and perfect heart, bring forth fruit in patience.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Fratres: Libénter suffértis insipiéntes, cum sitis ipsi sapiéntes: sustinétis enim si quis vos in servitútem rédigit, si quis dévorat, si quis áccipit, si quis extóllitur, si quis in fáciem vos cædit.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: For you gladly suffer the foolish; whereas yourselves are wise. For you suffer if a man bring you into bondage, if a man devour you, if a man take from you, if a man be lifted up, if a man strike you on the face.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Libénter ígitur gloriábor in infirmitátibus meis, ut inhábitet in me virtus Christi.
Capitulum Nona.eng: And he said to me: My grace is sufficient for thee; for power is made perfect in infirmity. Gladly therefore will I glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may dwell in me.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Ter virgis cæsus sum, semel lapidátus sum: ter naufrágium feci, nocte et die in profúndo maris fui.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: Thrice was I beaten with rods, once I was stoned, thrice I suffered shipwreck, a night and a day I was in the depth of the sea.

Invit.label: Antiphon
Invit.lat: Præoccupémus fáciem Dómini: * Et in psalmis jubilémus ei.
Invit.eng: Let us come before the presence of the Lord * and make a joyful noise unto Him with Psalms.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui cónspicis, quia ex nulla nostra actióne confídimus: concéde propítius; ut, contra advérsa ómnia Doctóris géntium protectióne muniámur.
Oratio.eng: O God, Who seest that we put not our trust in anything that we do, mercifully grant that through the protection of the Teacher of the Gentiles we may be defended against all adversity.

Versum 2.label: Versicle
Versum 2.latR: ℟. A generatióne et progénie.
Versum 2.eng: ℣. Lord, thou hast been our refuge.
Versum 2.engR: ℟. From generation to generation.

Ant Laudes.ant: Secúndum magnam misericórdiam * tuam miserére mei, Deus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Have mercy upon me, O God, * after thy great mercy.

Ant Laudes.ant: Si mihi Dóminus * salvátor fúerit, non timébo, quid fáciat mihi homo.
Ant Laudes.antEng: If the Lord be my Saviour * I will not fear what man can do unto me.

Ant Laudes.ant: In velaménto * clamávi valde dilúculo: Deus, Deus meus, ad te de luce vígilo.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Within the veil I cried betimes: * O God, Thou art my God, early will I seek thee.

Ant Laudes.ant: Hymnum dicámus * Dómino Deo nostro.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Let us sing praises * to the Lord our God.

Ant Laudes.ant: In excélsis, * laudáte Deum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: In the high places, * praise ye God.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Si culmen * veri honóris quǽritis, ad illam cæléstem pátriam quantócius properáte.
Ant 3.eng: If ye would be truly honourable, * strive after our Fatherland which is in heaven.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Semen est * verbum Dei, sator autem Christus: omnis qui invénit eum, manébit in ætérnum.
Ant 3.eng: The seed is the word of God, * and the Sower is Christ; if any man find Him, he shall never be moved.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Quod autem cécidit * in terram bonam, hi sunt, qui in corde bono et óptimo fructum áfferunt in patiéntia.
Ant 3.eng: But that on the good ground * are they which in an honest and good heart bring forth fruit with patience.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Pater fídei nostræ * Abraham summus, óbtulit holocáustum super altáre pro fílio.
Ant 1.eng: The father of our faith, * the mighty Abraham, offered a burnt offering on the altar for his son.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Ecce ascéndimus * Jerosólymam, et consummabúntur ómnia quæ scripta sunt de Fílio hóminis: tradétur enim géntibus, et illudétur, et conspuétur: et postquam flagelláverint, occídent eum, et tértia die resúrget.
Ant 2.eng: Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, * and all things that are written by the Prophets concerning the Son of man shall be accomplished; for He shall be delivered unto the Gentiles, and shall be mocked and spitted on; and they shall scourge Him, and put Him to death, and the third day He shall rise again.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Stans autem Jesus, * jussit cæcum addúci ad se, et ait illi: Quid vis ut fáciam tibi? Dómine, ut vídeam. Et Jesus ait illi: Réspice, fides tua te salvum fecit. Et conféstim vidit, et sequebátur illum, magníficans Deum.
Ant 3.eng: And Jesus stood, * and commanded the blind man to be brought unto Him, and He asked him, saying: What wilt thou that I shall do unto thee? Lord, that I may receive my sight. And Jesus said unto him: Receive thy sight, thy faith hath saved thee. And immediately he received his sight, and followed Him, glorifying God.

Ant Nona.label: Antiphon
Ant Nona.lat: Cæcus magis * ac magis clamábat, ut eum Dóminus illumináret.
Ant Nona.eng: The blind man cried to the Lord * so much the more, to give him light.

Ant Prima.label: Antiphon
Ant Prima.lat: Iter faciénte * Jesu, dum appropinquáret Jericho, cæcus clamábat ad eum, ut lumen recípere mererétur.
Ant Prima.eng: As Jesus went on His way, * as He was come nigh unto Jericho, a certain blind man cried unto Him, that he might worthily receive his sight.

Ant Sexta.label: Antiphon
Ant Sexta.lat: Et qui præíbant, * increpábant eum ut tacéret: ipse vero multo magis clamábat: Miserére mei, Fili David.
Ant Sexta.eng: And they that went before rebuked him, * that he should hold his peace, but he cried so much the more: Thou Son of David, have mercy on me!

Ant Tertia.label: Antiphon
Ant Tertia.lat: Transeúnte * Dómino, clamábat cæcus ad eum: Miserére mei, Fili David.
Ant Tertia.eng: As the Lord passed by, * a certain blind man cried unto Him: Thou Son of David, have mercy on me.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Fratres: Si linguis hóminum loquar, et Angelórum, caritátem autem non hábeam, factus sum velut æs sonans, aut cýmbalum tínniens.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Brothers: If I speak with the tongues of men, and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Nunc autem manent fides, spes, cáritas, tria hæc: major autem horum est cáritas.
Capitulum Nona.eng: And now there remain faith, hope, and charity, these three: but the greatest of these is charity.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Cáritas nunquam éxcidit: sive prophetíæ evacuabúntur, sive linguæ cessábunt, sive sciéntia destruétur. Ex parte enim cognóscimus, et ex parte prophetámus.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: Charity never falleth away: whether prophecies shall be made void, or tongues shall cease, or knowledge shall be destroyed. For we know in part, and we prophesy in part.

Invit.label: Antiphon
Invit.lat: Præoccupémus fáciem Dómini: * Et in psalmis jubilémus ei.
Invit.eng: Let us come before the presence of the Lord * and make a joyful noise unto Him with Psalms.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Preces nostras, quǽsumus, Dómine, cleménter exáudi: atque, a peccatórum vínculis absolútos, ab omni nos adversitáte custódi.
Oratio.eng: O Lord, we beseech You, mercifully hear our prayers; loose us from the chains of our sins and keep us from all adversity.

Versum 2.label: Versicle
Versum 2.latR: ℟. A generatióne et progénie.
Versum 2.eng: ℣. Lord, thou hast been our refuge.
Versum 2.engR: ℟. From generation to generation.

Ant Laudes.ant: Secúndum multitúdinem * miseratiónum tuárum, Dómine, dele iniquitátem meam.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O Lord, according to the multitude of thy tender mercies, * blot out my transgressions.

Ant Laudes.ant: Deus meus es tu, * et confitébor tibi: Deus meus es tu, et exaltábo te.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Thou art my God, * and I will praise thee; Thou art my God, and I will exalt thee.

Ant Laudes.ant: Ad te de luce * vígilo, Deus, ut vídeam virtútem tuam.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O God, early will I seek thee, * to see thy power.

Ant Laudes.ant: Hymnum dícite, * et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Sing praises, * and exalt Him above all for ever.

Ant Laudes.ant: Omnes Angeli * ejus laudáte Dóminum de cælis.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Praise ye the Lord * from the heavens, all His angels.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Et qui præíbant, * increpábant eum ut tacéret: ipse vero multo magis clamábat: Miserére mei, Fili David.
Ant 3.eng: And they that went before * rebuked him, that he should hold his peace. But he cried out so much the more: “Have mercy on me, thou Son of David.”

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Miserére mei, * Fili David. Quid vis ut fáciam tibi? Dómine, ut vídeam.
Ant 3.eng: Have mercy on me, * thou Son of David. What wouldst thou that I should do unto thee? Lord, that I may receive my sight.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Cum jejunátis, * nolíte fíeri sicut hypócritæ, tristes.
Ant 2.eng: When ye fast, * be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Thesaurizáte vobis * thesáuros in cælo, ubi nec ærúgo, nec tínea demolítur.
Ant 3.eng: Lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, * where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Præsta, Dómine, fidélibus tuis: ut jejuniórum veneránda solémnia, et cóngrua pietáte suscípiant, et secúra devotióne percúrrant.
Oratio 2.eng: Grant, O Lord, to thy faithful people, that they may undertake with fitting piety the venerable solemnities of fasting, and complete them with steadfast devotion.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Inclinántes se, Dómine, majestáti tuæ, propitiátus inténde: ut, qui divíno múnere sunt refécti, cæléstibus semper nutriántur auxíliis.
Oratio 3.eng: Look graciously, O Lord, upon those who bow down before thy Divine Majesty, that they who have been refreshed by thy divine gift may always be sustained by heavenly aids.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Dómine, * puer meus jacet paralýticus in domo, et male torquétur: Amen dico tibi, ego véniam, et curábo eum.
Ant 2.eng: Lord, * my servant lieth at home sick of the palsy, and is grieviously tormented. Amen, I say unto thee, I will come and heal him.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Dómine, * non sum dignus ut intres sub tectum meum: sed tantum dic verbo, et sanábitur puer meus.
Ant 3.eng: O Lord, * I am not worthy that thou shouldst enter under my roof: but only say the word, and my servant shall be healed.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Deus, qui culpa offénderis, pæniténtia placáris: preces pópuli tui supplicántis propítius réspice; et flagélla tuæ iracúndiæ, quæ pro peccátis nostris merémur, avérte.
Oratio 2.eng: O God, whom sin doth justly move to anger, and at repentance doth turn again to forgive the same; mercifully regard the prayers of your people, and turn aside the scourges of thy wrath, which we deserve for our sins.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Parce, Dómine, parce populo tuo: ut, dignis flagellatiónibus castigátus, in tua miseratióne respíret.
Oratio 3.eng: Spare, O Lord, spare thy people, that they, being deservedly chastened, they may find solace through thy tender mercy.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Cum facis * eleemósynam nésciat sinístra tua quid fáciat déxtera tua.
Ant 2.eng: When thou dost * alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doth.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Tu autem cum oráveris, * intra in cubículum tuum: et clauso óstio, ora Patrem tuum.
Ant 3.eng: But thou when thou shalt pray, * enter into thy chamber, and having shut the door, pray to thy Father.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Inchoáta jejúnia, quǽsumus, Dómine, benígno favóre proséquere: ut observántiam, quam corporáliter exhibémus, méntibus étiam sincéris exercére valeámus.
Oratio 2.eng: Further with thy gracious favor, we beseech thee, O Lord, the fasts which we have begun, that we may be able to practice the bodily fasts which we keep, with sincere minds.

Oratio 3.label: Oratio
Oratio 3.lat: Tuére, Dómine, pópulum tuum et ab ómnibus peccátis cleménter emúnda: quia nulla ei nocébit advérsitas, si nulla ei dominétur iníquitas.
Oratio 3.eng: Guard, O Lord, thy people, and from all their sins cleanse them; for no adversity shall harm them if no iniquity dominates them.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Me étenim * de die in diem quærunt, et scire vias meas volunt.
Ant 2.eng: For they seek me * from day to day, and desire to know my ways.

Oratio 2.label: Oratio
Oratio 2.lat: Adésto, Dómine, supplicatiónibus nostris: et concéde; ut hoc solémne jejúnium, quod animábus corporibúsque curándis salúbriter institútum est, devóto servítio celebrémus.
Oratio 2.eng: Hearken, O Lord, to our supplications; and grant that we may celebrate with devout service this solemn fast, which thou hast instituted for the healing of soul and body.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Dabit illi * Dóminus Deus sedem David, patris ejus: et regnábit in domo Jacob in ætérnum, et regni ejus non erit finis, allelúja.
Ant 1.eng: The Lord God * shall give unto him the throne of David, his father: and he shall reign in the house of Jacob for ever, and of his kingdom there shall be no end, alleluia.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Fecit nos Deo * et Patri suo regnum, primogénitus mortuórum, et Princeps regum terræ, allelúja.
Ant 2.eng: He hath made us * a kingdom to God and his Father: the first begotten of the dead, and the Prince of the kings of the earth, alleluia.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Habet in vestiménto * et in fémore suo scriptum: Rex regum, et Dóminus dominántium. Ipsi glória et impérium, in sǽcula sæculórum.
Ant 3.eng: And he hath on his garment, * and on his thigh written: King of kings, and Lord of lords. To him be glory and empire for ever and ever.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Fratres: Grátias ágimus Deo Patri, qui dignos nos fecit in partem sortis sanctórum in lúmine, qui erípuit nos de potestáte tenebrárum, et tránstulit in regnum Fílii dilectiónis suæ.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Brethren: We give thanks to God the Father, who hath made us worthy to be partakers of the lot of the saints in light, who hath delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated us into the kingdom of the Son of his love.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: In ipso complácuit omnem plenitúdinem inhabitáre, et per eum reconciliáre ómnia in ipsum, pacíficans per sánguinem crucis ejus sive quæ in terris, sive quæ in cælis sunt, in Christo Jesu Dómino nostro.
Capitulum Nona.eng: In him, it hath well pleased the Father, that all fullness should dwell, and through him to reconcile all things unto himself, making peace through the blood of his cross, both as to the things that are on earth, and the things that are in heaven, in Christ Jesus our Lord.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Omnia per ipsum et in ipso creáta sunt, et ipse est ante omnes, et ómnia in ipso constant. Et ipse est caput córporis Ecclésiæ, qui est princípium, primogénitus ex mórtuis, ut sit in ómnibus ipse primátum tenens.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: LL things were created by him and in him, and he is before all, and by him all things consist. And he is the head of the body, the Church, who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, that in all things he may hold the primacy.

Doxology.lat:
Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui sceptra mundi témperas,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

Hymnus Laudes.label: Hymn
Hymnus Laudes.title: Vexílla Christus ínclita
Hymnus Laudes.lat:
Vexílla Christus ínclita
Late triúmphans éxplicat:
Gentes adéste súpplices,
Regíque regum pláudite.

Non Ille regna cládibus:
Non vi metúque súbdidit
Alto levátus stípite,
Amóre traxit ómnia.

O ter beáta cívitas
Cui rite Christus ímperat,
Quæ jussa pergit éxsequi
Edícta mundo cǽlitus!

Non arma flagrant ímpia,
Pax usque firmat fœ́dera,
Arrídet et concórdia,
Tutus stat ordo cívicus.

Servat fides connúbia,
Juvénta pubet íntegra,
Pudíca florent límina
Domésticis virtútibus.

Optáta nobis spléndeat
Lux ista, Rex dulcíssime:
Te, pace adépta cándida,
Adóret orbis súbditus.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui sceptra mundi témperas,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
Hymnus Laudes.eng:
Christ’s flag unfurled in glory raised,
Triumphing o’er the serpent’s stings;
Come humbly forward all ye lands,
Applauding the great King of kings.

No force or threat doth he need use,
Not by coersion leadeth he;
Raised on the cross he draweth all,
With love unto his fruitful tree.

O! Thrice blest city of the Lord,
Wherein Christ ruleth without dearth;
Fervently she doth execute
His heavenly edicts to the earth,

No fiery weapon can e’er harm,
The peace ’stablished by Jesus’ hand;
In happiness and unity,
The ranks of Christ secure do stand.

A marriage blessed by faith in thee,
Yields virtuous offspring from the womb;
Like seed in fertile soil doth grow,
In virtuous homes do children bloom.

We yearn and long to shine on us,
Thy light, O sweet and winsome King;
All thus submitted to thy reign,
To us, thy gift of peace do bring.

All glory be, Jesu, to thee,
Thy scepter over all that be;
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.

Hymnus Matutinum.label: Hymn
Hymnus Matutinum.title: Ætérna Imago Altíssimi
Hymnus Matutinum.lat:
Ætérna Imago Altíssimi,
Lumen, Deus, de Lúmine,
Tibi, Redémptor glória,
Honor, potéstas régia.

Tu solus ante sǽcula
Spes atque centrum témporum,
Cui jure sceptrum géntium
Pater suprémum crédidit.

Tu flos pudícæ Vírginis,
Nostræ caput propáginis,
Lapis cadúcus vértice
Ac mole terras óccupans.

Diro tyránno súbdita,
Damnáta stirps mortálium,
Per te refrégit víncula
Sibíque cælum víndicat.

Doctor, Sacérdos, Légifer
Præfers notátum sánguine
In veste « Princeps príncipum
Regúmque Rex Altíssimus ».

Tibi voléntes súbdimur,
Qui jure cunctis ímperas:
Hæc cívium beátitas
Tuis subésse légibus.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui sceptra mundi témperas,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
Hymnus Matutinum.eng:
O thou eternal Image bright
Of God most high, thou Light of Light,
To thee, Redeemer, glory be,
And might and kingly majesty.

Sole hope of all created things,
Thou art the Lord and King of kings,
Whom God, long ere creation's morn,
Had crowned to rule earth yet unborn.

Fair flower from the Virgin's breast,
Our race's Head for ever blest,
The stone that Daniel saw on high,
Which falling, o'er the world doth lie.

The race of men, condemned to lie
Beneath the direful tyrant's yoke,
By thee at length the shackles broke
And claimed the fatherland on high.

Priest, Teacher, Giver of the law,
Thy Name the rapt Apostle saw
Writ on thy vesture and thy thigh:
The King Of Kings, The Lord Most High.

Fain would we own thy blessed sway,
Whose rule all creatures must obey;
For happy is that state and throne
Whose subjects seek thy will alone.

All glory be, Jesu, to thee,
Thy scepter over all that be;
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.

Hymnus Vespera.label: Hymn
Hymnus Vespera.title: Te sæculórum Príncipem
Hymnus Vespera.lat:
Te sæculórum Príncipem,
Te, Christe, Regem géntium,
Te méntium, te córdium
Unum fatémur árbitrum.

Scelésta turba clámitat:
Regnáre Christum nólumus:
Te nos ovántes ómnium
Regem suprémum dícimus.

O Christe, Princeps Pácifer,
Mentes rebélles súbice:
Tuóque amóre dévios,
Ovíle in unum cóngrega.

Ad hoc cruénta ab árbore
Pendes apértis brácchiis,
Diráque fossum cúspide
Cor igne flagrans éxhibes.

Ad hoc in aris ábderis
Vini dapísque imágine,
Fundens salútem fíliis
Transverberáto péctore.

Te natiónum Prǽsides
Honóre tollant público,
Colant magístri, júdices,
Leges et artes éxprimant.

Submíssa regum fúlgeant
Tibi dicáta insígnia:
Mitíque sceptro pátriam
Domósque subde cívium.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui sceptra mundi témperas,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
Hymnus Vespera.eng:
To thee, O Prince of all that be,
Thou Christ, O King eternally;
O Framer of the mind and heart,
Our one true Judge we say thou art.

The wicked protest, wail and cry,
Christ Jesus’ reign they would deny;
Rejoice we at thy glorious name,
Thou Highest King we do proclaim.

O Christ! The Source of all our peace,
Make all our sinful thoughts to cease;
And still in us our loves misplaced,
As Thy one sheepfold be we embraced.

For this, hanging on cruel tree,
With arms outstretched, for all to see;
His heart is pierced by soldier’s spear,
Revealing burning love most dear.

From this the altar of the tree
Thy blood flows forth from Calvary;
As wine to us it doth appear,
To thine own heart it draws us near.

Thou Governor of all that be,
May all thy creatures honour thee;
All those who rule, O Lord renew!
Source of all precepts just and true.

To regal glory, all submit,
All crowns and honours we do remit;—
To thy scepter—so sweet and mild!
Submit we as a little child.

All glory be, Jesu, to thee,
Thy scepter over all that be;
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.

Invit.label: Antiphon
Invit.lat: Jesum Christum, Regem regum: * Veníte adorémus.
Invit.eng: Jesus Christ, the King of kings * Come, let us adore!

Lectio Prima.label: Lectio brevis
Lectio Prima.lat: In ipso complácuit omnem plenitúdinem inhabitáre, et per eum reconciliáre ómnia in ipsum, pacíficans per sánguinem crucis ejus sive quæ in terris, sive quæ in cælis sunt, in Christo Jesu Dómino nostro.
Lectio Prima.eng: In him, it hath well pleased the Father, that all fullness should dwell, and through him to reconcile all things unto himself, making peace through the blood of his cross, both as to the things that are on earth, and the things that are in heaven, in Christ Jesus our Lord.

Nocturn 1 Versum.eng: ℣. Given to me is all power.
Nocturn 1 Versum.engR: ℟. In heaven and in earth.

Nocturn 2 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 2 Versum.lat: ℣. Afférte Dómino, famíliæ populórum.
Nocturn 2 Versum.eng: ℣. Bring ye to the Lord, O ye families of the nations.
Nocturn 2 Versum.engR: ℟. Bring ye to the Lord glory and empire.

Nocturn 3 Versum.eng: ℣. They shall adore him: all kings of the earth.
Nocturn 3 Versum.engR: ℟. All nations shall serve him.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui in dilécto Fílio tuo, universórum Rege, ómnia instauráre voluísti: concéde propítius; ut cunctæ famíliæ géntium, peccáti vúlnere disgregátæ, ejus suavíssimo subdántur império:
Oratio.eng: Almighty and everlasting God, who in thy beloved Son, the King of the whole world, hast willed to restore all things: mercifully grant that all the families of nations, now kept apart by the wound of sin, may be brought under the sweet yoke of his rule.

Ant Laudes.ant: Suscitábit * Deus cæli regnum quod commínuet et consúmet univérsa regna, et ipsum stabit in ætérnum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The God of heaven * will set up a kingdom that shall break in pieces and shall consume all these kingdoms, and itself shall stand for ever.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dedit ei Dóminus * potestátem et honórem et regnum; et omnes pópuli, tribus et linguæ ipsi sérvient.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The Lord gave him * power and glory, and a kingdom; and all peoples, tribes and tongues shall serve him.

Ant Laudes.ant: Exíbunt aquæ vivæ * de Jerúsalem; et erit Dóminus Rex super omnem terram.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Living waters shall go out * from Jerusalem; and the Lord shall be king over all the earth.

Ant Laudes.ant: Magnificábitur * usque ad términos terræ, et erit iste pax.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Now shall he be magnified * even to the ends of the earth, and this man shall be our peace.

Ant Laudes.ant: Gens et regnum * quod non servíerit tibi, períbit: et gentes solitúdine vastabúntur.
Ant Laudes.antEng: The nation and the kingdom * that will not serve thee, shall perish: and the Gentiles shall be wasted with desolation.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ego autem * constitútus sum Rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum ejus, prǽdicans præcéptum ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I have been set up * as King by Him on Sion, His holy mountain, proclaiming His decree.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Glória * et honóre coronásti eum, Dómine: ómnia subjecísti sub pédibus ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Thou hast crowned him * with glory and honor, O Lord, putting all things under His feet.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Elevámini, * portæ æternáles, et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Reach up * you ancient portals, that the King of glory may come in.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Sedébit * Dóminus Rex in ætérnum: Dóminus benedícet pópulo suo in pace.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: The Lord is enthroned * as King forever; may the Lord bless his people with peace.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Virga directiónis, * virga regni tui: proptérea pópuli confitebúntur tibi in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: A tempered rod * is thy royal scepter; therefore shall nations praise thee forever and ever.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Psállite * Regi nostro, psállite: quóniam Rex magnus super omnem terram.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Sing praise to our King * sing praise; for he is the great King over all earth.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Benedicéntur in ipso * omnes tribus terræ; omnes gentes magnificábunt eum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: In Him * shall all the tribes of the earth be blessed; all the nations shall proclaim His greatness.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Et ego primogénitum * ponam illum: excélsum præ régibus terræ.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: And I will make Him * the firstborn, highest of the kings of the earth.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Thronus ejus * sicut sol in conspéctu meo: et sicut luna perfécta in ætérnum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: His throne * shall be like the sun before Me; like the moon, which remains forever.

Ant Vespera.ant: Pacíficus * vocábitur, et thronus ejus erit firmíssimus in perpétuum.
Ant Vespera.antEng: He shall be called * Peaceable, and his throne shall be most firm for ever.

Ant Vespera.ant: Regnum ejus * regnum sempitérnum est, et omnes reges sérvient ei et obédient.
Ant Vespera.antEng: His kingdom * is an everlasting kingdom, and all kings shall serve him, and shall obey him.

Ant Vespera.ant: Ecce Vir Oriens * nomen ejus: sedébit et dominábitur, et loquétur pacem géntibus.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Behold a man, the Orient * is his name: he shall sit and rule, and shall speak peace to the Gentiles.

Ant Vespera.ant: Dóminus * judex noster, Dóminus légifer noster: Dóminus Rex noster, ipse salvábit nos.
Ant Vespera.antEng: The Lord * is our judge, the Lord is our lawgiver: the Lord is our king, he will save us.

Ant Vespera.ant: Ecce dedi te * in lucem géntium, ut sis salus mea usque ad extrémum terræ.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Behold, I have given thee * to be the light of the Gentiles, that thou mayst be my salvation even to the farthest part of the earth.
